index.name: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM)
index.one_liner: Sakana AI / UBC (Zhang, Hu, Lu, Lange, Clune): coding agent that rewrites its own code, keeps an open-ended archive of variants, and empirically validates each self-modification on SWE-bench/Polyglot (20.0%->50.0% SWE-bench, 14.2%->30.7% Polyglot). Paper arXiv:2505.22954, ICLR 2026; blog sakana.ai/dgm.
index.why_relevant: The reference point for the entire self-modifying-agent lineage: every 2026 Gödel-machine variant (HGM, RQGM, MGM, GEA, Hyperagents) forks this codebase or builds on its archive-and-self-edit loop. Repo is stale since Aug 2025 but remains the canonical baseline.

index.name: Hyperagents (DGM-H)
index.one_liner: Meta FAIR (Jenny Zhang, Clune, Foerster, Jiang et al.): self-referential agents where the meta-agent that does the improving is itself editable, extending DGM to any computable task (coding, peer review, robotics reward design, Olympiad math grading). arXiv:2603.19461, Mar 2026.
index.why_relevant: Removes DGM's fixed human-written meta-agent constraint; meta-level improvements (persistent memory, performance tracking) transfer across domains and accumulate across runs. Most-starred 2026 self-referential agent repo; now the standard 'level 3' reference for agents rewriting their own improvement logic.

index.name: karpathy/autoresearch
index.one_liner: AI agents autonomously running research on single-GPU nanochat training: propose a code change, train, evaluate, keep or discard, repeat. Mar 2026.
index.why_relevant: Not agent-self-modification (the agent edits training code, not itself) but the 95k-star loop that the BetterForAll progression and many 2026 RSI lists treat as 'level 1' of self-improving code agents; enormous heat.

index.name: GenericAgent
index.one_liner: Self-evolving agent that grows a skill tree from a 3.3K-line seed to full system control, claiming 6x lower token consumption. Jan 2026, pushed today.
index.why_relevant: Highest-starred 2026 'self-evolving agent' repo; evolution is skills/tools written by the agent rather than rewriting its core loop, so partially adjacent to the DGM lineage.

index.name: Absolute Zero Reasoner (AZR)
index.one_liner: Single LLM acts as both task proposer and solver over abduction/deduction/induction code tasks, verified by a Python executor, trained with zero external data (NeurIPS 2025 spotlight).
index.why_relevant: The canonical 'zero data self-play' reference point: closed propose-solve-verify RL loop, SOTA on coding+math without any curated data. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335. Repo still the most-starred in this niche though commits stopped Aug 2025.

index.name: AgentEvolver (ModelScope/Alibaba)
index.one_liner: End-to-end self-evolving agent training system unifying self-questioning (auto task generation from env exploration), self-navigating (experience reuse), and self-attributing (credit assignment).
index.why_relevant: Production-grade framework whose self-questioning module is a self-generated curriculum over environments; CuES extension (arXiv 2512.01311) and SeeUPO (2026-03) build on it. Tech report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10395.

index.name: GEPA (gepa-ai/gepa)
index.one_liner: Genetic-Pareto reflective optimizer: LLM reads full execution traces, proposes prompt/code/skill mutations, Pareto-selects; `optimize_anything` API + Claude Code agent skill.
index.why_relevant: The reference implementation of reflective prompt evolution; claims 35x fewer rollouts than GRPO, 46.6%->56.6% AIME for GPT-4.1-mini, 32%->89% ARC-AGI agent via architecture discovery, 50+ production uses (Shopify, Databricks, OpenAI, Pydantic, MLflow, Comet). Still very active (commits 2026-09-11, v0.1.4 2026-07-15).

index.name: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
index.one_liner: 'The agent that grows with you' — built-in closed learning loop: autonomously creates skills after complex tasks, improves skills during use, nudges itself to persist memory, searches past sessions, builds a user model.
index.why_relevant: By far the most-starred self-improving agent; the de-facto reference implementation of skill-from-experience loops in 2026 (SkillClaw, Evolver etc. position themselves relative to it).

index.name: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM)
index.one_liner: Agent that rewrites its own code and validates changes empirically on SWE-bench/Polyglot, keeping an open-ended archive of variants (SWE-bench 20%→50%). ICLR 2026. Code: github.com/jennyzzt/dgm.
index.why_relevant: Foundational reference point for code-level self-improving agents (Sakana/UBC/Clune); nearly every 2026 RSI paper baselines against it.

index.name: HyperAgents (Meta FAIR)
index.one_liner: Self-referential agents where task agent + meta agent are one editable program, so the improvement procedure itself evolves (DGM-H); transfers beyond coding to paper review and robotics reward design. ICLR 2026. Code: github.com/facebookresearch/HyperAgents.
index.why_relevant: Successor to DGM that closes the meta-level loop; institutional weight (Meta, Clune, Foerster).

index.name: AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind)
index.last_activity: 2026-07-10 (DeepMind blog 'scaling impact across fields'); GA on Google Cloud / Gemini Enterprise 2026-07
index.one_liner: Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent: LLM ensemble proposes code diffs, automated evaluators score them, evolutionary database keeps the best; found 48-multiplication 4x4 complex matmul, improved 5 Ramsey lower bounds, data-center scheduling, and sped up its own training.
index.why_relevant: The reference point of the whole field: a closed-loop system where the LLM rewrites code, the evaluator scores it, and the population improves autonomously. 833 citations (Semantic Scholar) in ~15 months; now a commercial product (docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/alphaevolve). Also notable for accelerating training of the Gemini model that powers it (self-improvement of the substrate).

index.name: OpenEvolve
index.one_liner: Most-starred open-source AlphaEvolve implementation: MAP-Elites + island model, cascade evaluation, LLM ensembles, prompt-evolution mode; SOTA n=26 circle packing, 2.8x MLX Metal kernel speedup, +23% HotpotQA via evolved prompts.
index.why_relevant: De facto open baseline that nearly every 2026 paper (EvoX, SeaEvo, PACEvolve, BES, TurboEvolve) compares against; used as the environment for ThetaEvolve's test-time RL. Still active (weekly commits in July 2026).

index.name: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
index.one_liner: ICLR 2026 Oral (Agrawal, Khattab et al., UC Berkeley/Stanford/Databricks/MIT): natural-language reflection on trajectories + Pareto evolutionary search beats GRPO by up to 10-20% with up to 35x fewer rollouts.
index.why_relevant: Canonical paper establishing that a prompt-space self-improvement loop can outperform weight-space RL; the baseline every 2026 prompt-optimizer paper compares against.

index.name: ReasoningBank (Google)
index.one_liner: Memory framework distilling generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent experiences, plus memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS); code at github.com/google-research/reasoning-bank (578 stars).
index.why_relevant: Google Cloud AI Research + UIUC reference point for 'agent self-evolving with reasoning memory' on WebArena/Mind2Web/SWE-Bench-Verified; v2 Mar 2026; precursor to SkillOS.

index.name: Lilian Weng: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
index.one_liner: Lil'Log post (Jul 4, 2026) synthesizing ~35 papers arguing RSI will begin with agents optimizing their own harness (prompts, workflows, memory, orchestration code) rather than weights; covers DGM, HGM, Hyperagents, SICA and harness-evolution work.
index.why_relevant: Most influential 2026 overview of the self-improving-harness thesis; widely cited (Latent Space AINews, multiple reading lists) and frames the field's vocabulary.

index.name: Agent0 / Agent0-VL
index.one_liner: Curriculum agent and executor agent (same base LLM) co-evolve with tool-integrated (code interpreter) multi-turn reasoning from zero data; ICML'26 + COLM'26.
index.why_relevant: Direct successor to AZR/R-Zero adding tools and multi-turn: Qwen3-8B-Base math avg 49.2 -> 58.2 (+18%), general +24%, beating R-Zero (54.7) and Socratic-Zero (56.1). Agent0-VL extends to VLMs with self-verifier rewards (+12.5%). Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043.

index.name: R-Zero
index.one_liner: Challenger/Solver co-evolution from a single base model: Challenger rewarded for ~50% solver uncertainty, Solver trained on majority-vote pseudo-labels (ICLR 2026).
index.why_relevant: The most-cited co-evolving proposer/solver framework after AZR; Qwen3-4B-Base +6.49 math / +7.54 general, Qwen3-8B-Base overall 34.49 -> 38.73 over 3 iters. Spawned VisPlay, R-Few, G-Zero, Vocabulary Dropout follow-ups. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05004.

index.name: AutoResearchClaw
index.one_liner: Fully autonomous, self-evolving idea-to-paper pipeline with multi-agent debate, self-healing Pivot/Refine executor, verifiable reporting and cross-run evolution; paper arXiv:2605.20025.
index.why_relevant: 'Cross-run evolution' converts past mistakes into future safeguards, so the system improves across research runs. Beats AI Scientist v2 by 54.7% on ARC-Bench (25 topics). Large author list incl. Caiming Xiong, James Zou, Cihang Xie.

index.name: EvoScientist
index.one_liner: Huawei's multi-agent evolving AI scientist: Researcher + Engineer + Evolution Manager agents with persistent ideation and experimentation memories; paper arXiv:2603.08127.
index.why_relevant: Explicit self-evolution loop: an Evolution Manager Agent distills insights from prior runs into reusable knowledge so idea quality and code success rate rise over time. Outperforms 7 SOTA systems on idea novelty/feasibility. Very active (commits 2026-09-10).

index.name: Prime Agent (Prime Intellect)
index.one_liner: Self-improving RLM (Recursive Language Model) coding harness with a 'Continual Harness' that refines its own prompts, memories, skills and subagent specs via evidence-backed updates. Paper arXiv:2608.23552.
index.why_relevant: Launched 2026-08-07; 20k stars in a month; explicit harness-level self-improvement loop from a major open lab.

index.name: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
index.one_liner: Stanford IRIS (Lee, Khattab, Finn) outer-loop system: an agentic proposer reads source, scores and execution traces of all prior harness candidates via a filesystem and rewrites harness code; 76.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Opus 4.6), +7.7 pts on text classification with 4x fewer context tokens.
index.why_relevant: The current reference point for 'harness-as-optimization-target': outer loop searches over harness code itself. Paper arxiv.org/abs/2603.28052; companion artifact repo stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness-tbench2-artifact has 1,205 stars. Every 2026 harness-evolution paper positions against it.

index.name: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve
index.one_liner: First systematic survey organizing self-evolving agents by what/when/how/where to evolve on the path to ASI; companion repo github.com/CharlesQ9/Self-Evolving-Agents.
index.why_relevant: Most-cited taxonomy for the exact term 'self-evolving agent'.

index.name: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents (EvoAgentX team)
index.one_liner: Unified feedback-loop framework (system inputs → agent system → environment → optimisers) for self-evolving agentic systems; awesome list github.com/ANative-Lab/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents.
index.why_relevant: Second major survey; its abstract feedback loop is the standard mental model for harness-level evolution.

index.name: Your Agent May Misevolve: Emergent Risks in Self-evolving LLM Agents
index.one_liner: First systematic study of 'misevolution': safety degradation across four evolutionary pathways (model, memory, tool, workflow), affecting even Gemini-2.5-Pro-based agents.
index.why_relevant: The safety taxonomy every 2026 self-evolving survey cites (Shanghai AI Lab / SJTU). Documents alignment decay after memory accumulation and vulnerabilities from tool creation/reuse; the four-pathway framing is reused by several awesome lists. Repo ShaoShuai0605/Misevolution.

index.name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM)
index.one_liner: Cambridge (Iacob, Jovanović, Shen, Lane et al.): recursive self-improvement under non-stationary utilities; agents and their evaluators co-evolve in epochs with statistically guided evaluator replacement. 71.7% Polyglot vs HGM-H 69.9% with 1.35-1.72x fewer tokens; also paper-writing and proof-generation domains.
index.why_relevant: Newest branch of the Gödel-machine lineage; makes the evaluator part of the self-improvement loop so the benchmark cannot be gamed. Several independent open reimplementations already (kingkillery/red-queen-godel-machine, ianyac/red-queen-godel-machine, DreamFallenFlowers/OpenRQGM).

index.name: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)
index.one_liner: Fudan-led closed loop that evolves coding-agent harnesses via three observability pillars (component / experience / decision); 10 iterations lift GPT-5.4 on Terminal-Bench 2 from 69.7% to 77.0%, beating Codex-CLI (71.9%), ACE and TF-GRPO; NexAU-AHE reaches 84.7% with GPT-5.5.
index.why_relevant: Fully automated harness self-evolution with every edit stated as a falsifiable prediction verified next round; frozen evolved harness transfers to SWE-bench Verified with 12% fewer tokens. Paper arxiv.org/abs/2604.25850 (v4 May 2026).

index.name: ACE: Agentic Context Engineering (ace-agent/ace)
index.one_liner: Generator/Reflector/Curator loop that grows an 'evolving playbook' context via incremental delta updates, avoiding brevity bias and context collapse; offline and online modes.
index.why_relevant: Official code for arXiv 2510.04618 (Stanford/SambaNova, ICLR 2026): +10.6% on AppWorld agents, +8.6% finance; -82.3% latency and -75.1% rollouts vs GEPA offline; -91.5% latency vs Dynamic Cheatsheet online. Coined the 'evolving playbook' framing now ubiquitous in self-improving-agent work. Latest commit parallelizes proposals with an LLM reducer (ComBEE).

index.name: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
index.one_liner: Zhang et al. (Stanford, SambaNova, UC Berkeley): treat contexts as evolving playbooks with structured incremental updates; matches top AppWorld production agent with a smaller open model.
index.why_relevant: Defines 'context collapse' and 'brevity bias' failure modes of iterative prompt rewriting and the grow-and-refine remedy; the standard citation for memory/playbook-style self-improvement without weight updates.

index.name: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
index.one_liner: Formalizes an agent as foundation model + scaffold (prompts, memory, tools, control) and self-improvement as a self-induced update operator on parameters or scaffold components (Jilin/KAUST/Alberta/IDSIA).
index.why_relevant: Clean formal framing that separates harness-level vs weight-level loops.

index.name: ShinkaEvolve (Sakana AI)
index.last_activity: 2026-08-21 (commits); May 2026 headless Codex/Claude mutation models; ICLR 2026
index.one_liner: Sample-efficient open-ended program evolution: bandit-based LLM ensemble selection, novelty-based rejection filtering, adaptive parent sampling; SOTA circle packing in ~150 samples; won ICFP 2025 contest with Team Unagi; pip install shinka-evolve; ships Claude Code/Codex skills.
index.why_relevant: ICLR 2026 accepted (arXiv 2509.19349, 142 citations). Explicitly positioned as an 'open-ended self-refining innovation engine'; newest releases let coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) drive the mutation loop, bridging evolutionary program search with agent harnesses.

index.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
index.one_liner: Survey of 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-2026) organized by what the system improves (deployment behavior, policy via training, evaluator, research process) and degree of loop closure; v2 Sep 6, 2026 (Chen, Wang, Qu; UC Riverside).
index.why_relevant: Best current taxonomy that places self-modifying agents (DGM lineage) relative to self-refine, self-reward and auto-research; useful to disambiguate the conflated 'self-*' vocabulary.

index.name: OpenRSI (Frontis-MA1 + OpenMLE)
index.one_liner: FrontisAI: executable, reproducible 'AI improving AI' stack for ML engineering: OpenMLE Gym/RL/Evo, Frontis-MA1 35B/30B models, OpenMLE sandbox; EEMA (Experience-Evolving Meta Agents) accepted EMNLP 2026. arXiv:2607.28568.
index.why_relevant: Meta-agent evolution (OpenMLE-Evo) plus RL on the same tasks; one of the few RSI stacks releasing models, sandbox and evolving meta-agents together. Adjacent to code-self-modification but weight-centric.

index.name: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
index.one_liner: Hexo Labs framework where Meta / Target / Feedback agents jointly rewrite a task agent's harness AND fine-tune its weights across generations; +25.1% over SOTA on LawBench, 12.4% faster GPU kernels, +20.4% on scRNA denoising, #1 on MLE-Bench Hard.
index.why_relevant: Only widely-used open framework that unifies harness-update and weight-update schools of self-improvement in one loop; pip-installable (sia-agent). Paper arxiv.org/abs/2605.27276.

index.name: CORAL
index.one_liner: Open-source autoresearch runtime driving Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex with grading, shared knowledge and multi-agent evolution; accepted at COLM 2026.
index.why_relevant: Peer-reviewed multi-agent evolution loop layered on production coding-agent harnesses.

index.name: Dr. Zero (Meta)
index.one_liner: Self-evolving multi-turn search agents with no training data: proposer generates hard-yet-solvable questions, solver trained via hop-grouped relative policy optimization (HRPO).
index.why_relevant: Meta Superintelligence Labs + UIUC zero-data proposer/solver loop for tool-using agents; data-free Dr. Zero matches or surpasses fully supervised Search-R1-style agents. Built on veRL 0.5. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07055.

index.name: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
index.one_liner: Black-box LM keeps a persistent, self-curated 'cheatsheet' of strategies and code snippets across queries at inference time; no weight updates (arXiv 2504.07952, EACL 2026).
index.why_relevant: Precursor/baseline for ACE's online mode; Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME accuracy more than doubled, GPT-4o Game of 24 10%->99% by reusing discovered solutions. Stanford (Suzgun, Yuksekgonul, Jurafsky, Zou).

index.name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (survey, ANative-Lab)
index.one_liner: Curated list accompanying 'A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents' (arXiv 2508.07407), organizing prompt, memory, tool, workflow and model-weight evolution.
index.why_relevant: Most-starred map of the space; its 'prompt optimization' section is the quickest index of APO-as-self-evolution papers.

index.name: Evolver (EvoMap)
index.one_liner: GEP-powered self-evolving engine for agents: auditable evolution via Genes, Capsules, Events; paper 'From Procedural Skills to Strategy Genes' arXiv:2604.15097 (4,590 trials). Moving to source-available after Hermes similarity dispute.
index.why_relevant: High-star dedicated self-evolution engine with a formal 'gene' representation for experience accumulation.

index.name: Reef — continual learning infra for self-improving agents
index.one_liner: Infra connecting agent inference, feedback, learning and versioned delivery; trains weights (Slime/SGLang) or evolves harness (prompts, rules, skills) while staying live through updates.
index.why_relevant: ~950 stars in 11 days; positions itself as the missing infra layer (versioning + live updates) for self-improving agents.

index.name: SkillClaw
index.one_liner: Collective skill evolution daemon: skills evolve silently from every real interaction across sessions, agents, devices and users (Hermes/OpenClaw-compatible). arXiv:2604.08377.
index.why_relevant: Turns cross-user experience into the primary signal for skill evolution; plug-in for the Hermes ecosystem.

index.name: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
index.one_liner: Wang, Piękos et al. (KAUST/Schmidhuber group): guides the DGM self-modification tree with clade metaproductivity (CMP) plus Thompson-sampling search; agent evolved with GPT-5-mini reaches human-level on SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5 using fewer CPU hours. arXiv:2510.21614, ICLR 2026.
index.why_relevant: Direct successor to DGM that fixes the metaproductivity-performance mismatch (which agent to expand next); baseline (HGM-H) that RQGM and MGM compare against. Clean-room reimplementations exist (weill-labs/hgm).

index.name: ASI-Arch (AlphaGo Moment for Model Architecture Discovery)
index.one_liner: GAIR-NLP's fully autonomous architecture-discovery loop: 1,773 experiments over 20,000 GPU-hours yielded 106 SOTA linear-attention architectures and a 'scaling law for scientific discovery'.
index.why_relevant: Reference point for 'AI does its own architecture research'. Closed loop of researcher/engineer/analyst agents that propose, train, evaluate and feed back into the archive; code at github.com/GAIR-NLP/ASI-Arch.

index.name: Anthropic Institute: When AI builds itself (recursive self-improvement)
index.one_liner: Anthropic's evidence report on Claude running AI research end-to-end: >80% of merged production code by Claude, ~52x code-optimization speedup (vs ~3x a year earlier), agents recovered 97% of a research performance gap vs 23% for human researchers.
index.why_relevant: Primary-source institutional data on closing the 'perspiration' loop (hypothesis -> experiment -> iterate) in frontier-lab AI research; follow-up (Aug 2026) describes Claude running an entire alignment-research loop unassisted.

index.name: microsoft/SkillOpt
index.one_liner: Text-space optimizer that trains SKILL.md files for frozen LLM agents with epochs/batches/validation gates; v0.2 adds SkillOpt-Sleep nightly offline self-evolution (harvest->mine->replay->consolidate).
index.why_relevant: Microsoft Research; treats agent skills as trainable parameters with trajectory-driven edits and validation-gated updates. Paper arXiv 2605.23904; integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Devin, OpenClaw; adopted by gbrain and darwin-skill.

index.name: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
index.one_liner: Wang, Piekos, et al. (KAUST/IDSIA, Schmidhuber group): identifies the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch and searches the self-modification tree with Clade Metaproductivity (CMP) + Thompson sampling; HGM-optimized agent w/ GPT-5-mini matches best human-engineered agents on SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5.
index.why_relevant: Second-generation Gödel-machine-style self-improving coding agent, ICLR 2026 oral (OpenReview T0EiEuhOOL); repo github.com/metauto-ai/HGM; clean-room reimplementations exist (weill-labs/hgm).

index.name: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
index.one_liner: Benchmark (Wu, Zhang + 17 authors) whose unit of evaluation is runnable infrastructure: agents build a harness from a minimal seed (Creation) then iteratively revise it from execution feedback (Evolution); self-built harnesses vary widely and transfer poorly across models. Sep 1, 2026.
index.why_relevant: Ten days old; first benchmark that directly measures an agent's ability to write and then self-evolve its own harness code, the capability DGM/SICA assume.

index.name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
index.one_liner: Shanghai AI Lab: an agent improves its OWN harness with no stronger external agent via Weakness Mining -> Harness Proposal -> regression-gated Proposal Validation; up to 132% relative gain across 9 model x benchmark combos (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, AppWorld) with MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, GLM-5.
index.why_relevant: Distinguishes itself from Meta-Harness by using the same model as both proposer and target, i.e. genuine self-improvement of the harness. Code: github.com/qzzqzzb/Self-Harness (101 stars). v3 revised Aug 2026.

index.name: Self-Evolving Coding Agents (survey)
index.one_liner: Survey of coding agents that update their framework, memory, skills, tools, models or collaboration structures from prior interactions.
index.why_relevant: Recent taxonomy covering the harness/scaffold self-evolution branch alongside memory/skills/weights.

index.name: Skill Self-Play (Skill-SP, Qwen/Alibaba)
index.one_liner: Proposer, solver, and a dynamic skill controller co-evolve: skill-routed task generation, validity checks, frontier-based curriculum, and feedback-driven skill library evolution.
index.why_relevant: Newest institutional (Alibaba Qwen team) self-play loop that also evolves a skill library, bridging self-play RL and skill-based self-evolution. Ministral-3-8B tool-call 20.7 -> 63.6, Qwen3-8B ZebraLogic 23.6 -> 32.4. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22529.

index.name: Arbor
index.one_liner: Generalist autonomous research agent that grows a hypothesis tree, runs real experiments and keeps only held-out gains; claims 2.5x over Claude Code/Codex at equal compute and 86.36% any-medal on MLE-Bench Lite. Paper arXiv:2606.11926.
index.why_relevant: Since 2026-06-30 Arbor 'learns from its own runs' - reusable findings recalled at intake for similar tasks, i.e., cross-run self-improvement; wins held-out tests on 6 tasks incl. BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.0.

index.name: Harnessing Agentic Evolution (AEvo)
index.one_liner: Treats the evolution process itself as an environment: a meta-agent reads accumulated candidates, feedback, traces, failures and cost history and edits the mechanism that drives future search.
index.why_relevant: Second-order self-improvement: improves over fixed-procedure optimizers (GEPA-style) and free-form agent optimizers on agentic, reasoning and open-ended tasks by letting the loop rewrite its own search strategy. Jiayi Zhang et al. (MetaGPT/FoundationAgents lineage).

index.name: A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve
index.one_liner: 'PyTorch for agentic evolution': ae.Evolver(agent, benchmark).run(cycles=10) evolves any agent with any evolution algorithm; #1 MCP-Atlas, ~#5 SWE-bench Verified with zero manual harness engineering.
index.why_relevant: Infrastructure plus position paper 'Agentic Evolution is the Path to Evolving LLMs' (arXiv 2602.00359); domain- and algorithm-agnostic harness evolution.

index.name: Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ADAS) / Meta Agent Search
index.one_liner: Hu, Lu, Clune (UBC/Vector): a meta agent programs new agents in code from an ever-growing archive; discovered agents beat hand-designed ones on ARC, math, reading comprehension and transfer across models/domains.
index.why_relevant: Foundational precursor to DGM (same lab): archive + meta-agent-in-code recipe. Repo github.com/ShengranHu/ADAS 1,637 stars; still the reference for 'agent search in code space' in 2026 harness papers.

index.name: Meta-Harness (Stanford IRIS)
index.one_liner: Lee, Nair, Zhang, K. Lee, Khattab, Finn: outer-loop agentic proposer that edits harness code with filesystem access to source, scores and traces; +7.7 pts text classification w/ 4x fewer context tokens, +4.7 pts on IMO-level RAG math, 76.4% Terminal-Bench 2.0 with Claude Opus 4.6.
index.why_relevant: High-influence 2026 formulation of 'optimize the harness code end-to-end'; repo github.com/stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness (1,545 stars) plus tbench2 artifact repo (1,205 stars); referenced by Lilian Weng's harness post and by AHE as concurrent work.

index.name: ShinkaEvolve (Sakana AI)
index.one_liner: Lange, Imajuku, Cetin: open-ended, sample-efficient LLM program evolution with exploration/exploitation parent sampling, novelty rejection sampling and bandit LLM-ensemble selection; new SOTA circle packing in 150 samples.
index.why_relevant: Same Sakana group as DGM; evolutionary program-improvement engine adjacent to (and reused by) self-improving agent loops; repo github.com/SakanaAI/ShinkaEvolve.

index.name: agentdescent
index.one_liner: 'Gradient descent, but the parameters are agents': parallel asynchronous framework that evolves skills, prompts and harnesses; code diffs act as gradients and an aggregator acts as the optimizer. Jul 2026.
index.why_relevant: Active (pushed yesterday) general framework for harness self-evolution with an optimizer abstraction over agent diffs; 217 stars in 7 weeks.

index.name: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
index.one_liner: Embodied agent alternates acting with refining its own prompt, sub-agents, skills and memory online within a single Pokemon Red/Emerald run, plus a process-reward co-learning loop that updates an open model from teacher-relabeled rollouts.
index.why_relevant: Harness self-improvement without episode resets, jointly with weight updates; cited in Weng's survey as the online-adaptation exemplar.

index.name: darwin-skill
index.one_liner: Autoresearch-style evaluate -> improve -> test -> keep/revert loop that makes any Claude Code skill self-evolve; 5.9k stars, bilingual.
index.why_relevant: Popular practitioner instantiation of the self-improving loop applied to harness components (skills) inside Claude Code.

index.name: autocontext
index.one_liner: 'Recursive self-improving harness': runs a task against evaluation, keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, leaves traces/playbooks/datasets and optional local-model training artifacts for the next iteration; Pi/Claude/Codex/MCP providers.
index.why_relevant: Actively-maintained open tool whose whole purpose is cross-run harness improvement (knowledge/playbook accumulation plus optional weight training).

index.name: pi-autoresearch
index.one_liner: Autonomous experiment-loop extension for the pi coding-agent harness (8k stars).
index.why_relevant: Turns a general coding-agent harness into a keep/discard improvement loop primitive; heavily adopted.

index.name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (XMUDeepLIT survey list)
index.one_liner: Curated survey + resource list on self-evolving agents (surveys, papers, benchmarks, open-source projects), actively maintained.
index.why_relevant: Most active curated index covering self-play/zero-data work alongside memory/skill evolution; companion to the 1.3K-star CharlesQ9/Self-Evolving-Agents survey (arXiv 2507.21046, stale since 2025-10).

index.name: OpenViking (Volcengine/ByteDance)
index.one_liner: Self-evolving context database unifying agent memory, knowledge RAG and skills; event-driven memory extraction/consolidation (VikingMem) so experience accumulates across interactions.
index.why_relevant: Massive adoption; the memory/skill substrate many self-evolving agents build on, though the loop is memory-side rather than full harness rewriting.

index.name: MemSkill
index.one_liner: Learning and evolving memory skills for self-evolving agents — the agent learns how to manage its own memory as evolvable skills.
index.why_relevant: Meta-level: evolving the memory-management procedure itself.

index.name: Yunjue Agent
index.one_liner: Fully reproducible, zero-start in-situ self-evolving agent system for open-ended tasks.
index.why_relevant: Emphasizes reproducibility of in-situ self-evolution from a zero seed.

index.name: DSPy (stanfordnlp/dspy)
index.one_liner: Programming-not-prompting framework whose optimizers (MIPROv2, GEPA, SIMBA, BootstrapFewShot, BetterTogether) automatically rewrite instructions and demos of LM programs against a metric.
index.why_relevant: The largest ecosystem for automated prompt optimization; dspy.GEPA is the recommended optimizer for complex workloads in 2026 and dspy.SIMBA is the lighter reflective option. Hosts the compile-loop that most industrial prompt self-optimization runs on (MLflow, Databricks, Ax all wrap it).

index.name: Everything Claude Code (ECC) — continuous-learning v2.1 'instincts'
index.one_liner: Agent-harness optimization system for Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode; its continuous-learning skill observes sessions via Pre/PostToolUse hooks, extracts atomic 'instincts' with 0.3-0.9 confidence, and evolves them into skills/commands/agents (project-scoped in v2.1).
index.why_relevant: Most-starred concrete implementation of an automated learn-from-session → skill-promotion loop inside a mainstream coding harness; instincts promote project→global when seen in 2+ projects.

index.name: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve
index.one_liner: DeepMind + Alman + Vassilevska Williams: reformulated laser-method optimization, ML-style optimizers, then AlphaEvolve refinement gives omega < 2.371177 (prev 2.371339).
index.why_relevant: Headline 2026 AlphaEvolve math result: an automated evolutionary loop contributing to the matrix multiplication exponent, one of the most-studied constants in TCS. Shows AlphaEvolve applied as a final-stage refiner on top of gradient/ML optimization.

index.name: Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao, Wagner)
index.one_liner: AlphaEvolve run on 67 problems across analysis, combinatorics, geometry, number theory; improved best-known on 23, matched on 36; released prompts/data.
index.why_relevant: Largest systematic evaluation of an evolutionary LLM loop on open math problems; Tao's framing ('scattered successes among a sea of unreported failures') is the reference calibration for what these loops can and cannot do. Companion blog: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2025/11/05/mathematical-exploration-and-discovery-at-scale/

index.name: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery (UC Berkeley / Sky)
index.one_liner: Jointly evolves candidate solutions AND the search strategy (selection/variation operators) based on progress; beats AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve, GEPA and ShinkaEvolve on the majority of ~200 real-world tasks.
index.why_relevant: Directly on-angle: the evolutionary loop rewrites its own search procedure (meta-evolution), from Stoica/Zaharia/Sen/Dimakis group; the most comprehensive head-to-head benchmark of the 2025-2026 evolutionary-coding frameworks.

index.name: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs (orig. AgentFly)
index.one_liner: Memory-augmented MDP with case-based reasoning: episodic case bank + neural case-selection policy updated from environment feedback; 87.88% Pass@3 on GAIA val, 79.40% test, 66.6% F1 on DeepResearcher. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2508.16153.
index.why_relevant: Flagship 'learn at test time without gradients' agent; explicitly frames continual adaptation as memory-based RL over cases, with 4.7-9.6 pt OOD gains from the case memory loop. v1 of the paper was titled 'AgentFly'.

index.name: The AI Scientist-v2 (Sakana AI)
index.one_liner: Template-free end-to-end research agent using progressive agentic tree search with an experiment manager and VLM figure critique; one fully AI-generated paper passed an ICLR 2025 workshop peer review. Code: github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2 (7,126 stars).
index.why_relevant: Reference open-source system for autonomous hypothesis->experiment->paper loops; tree-search over experiments is the pattern most later systems (Arbor, AutoResearchClaw, FAROS) benchmark against.

index.name: Towards End-to-End Automation of AI Research (Nature 2026)
index.one_liner: Nature 651, 914-919 (2026): The AI Scientist creates ideas, writes code, runs experiments, writes the manuscript and reviews itself; two modes (human code templates vs open-ended agentic search); workshop paper passed review at a 70%-acceptance venue.
index.why_relevant: Journal-level validation (Yamada, Lange, Lu, Lu, Hu, Foerster, Ha, Clune) of the fully automated research loop; institutional weight makes it the citation anchor for 'AI Scientist' in 2026.

index.name: SICA: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
index.one_liner: Robeyns, Szummer, Aitchison (Bristol): eliminates the meta-agent/target-agent split, the best archived agent edits its own codebase to improve cost, speed and benchmark score; 17%->53% on a SWE-bench Verified subset. arXiv:2504.15228.
index.why_relevant: Canonical 'agent that rewrites its own code' framework contemporaneous with DGM; cited as foundation by MOSS, DemoEvolve, Kitchen Loop and the self-evolving agents surveys. Repo inactive since Apr 2025.

index.name: Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ADAS / Meta Agent Search)
index.one_liner: Hu, Lu, Clune (UBC/Vector): a meta agent programs ever-better agents in code using a growing archive of discoveries; discovered agents beat hand-designed ones on coding, science and math. arXiv:2408.08435, ICLR 2025.
index.why_relevant: Origin of the 'meta agent writes agents in code space' idea that DGM turned self-referential; still the reference point for automated agent design. Spawned successors like MaAS, AutoMaAS, AgentSquare.

index.name: AutoAgent (thirdlayer) - autonomous harness engineering
index.one_liner: Karpathy-autoresearch pattern applied to agent harnesses: a meta-agent driven by program.md edits system prompt, tools, config and orchestration of agent.py, runs the benchmark, keeps/discards; 24h run hit #1 on SpreadsheetBench (96.5%) and top GPT-5 score on TerminalBench (55.1%).
index.why_relevant: Most-starred practitioner implementation of 'let the agent engineer its own harness overnight'; widely covered (MarkTechPost etc.). Repo has not been pushed since April 2026.

index.name: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
index.one_liner: RL on unlabeled test data using majority-vote as the reward signal; NeurIPS 2025.
index.why_relevant: Foundational self-training loop where the model bootstraps rewards from its own consensus: Qwen2.5-Math-7B AIME24 pass@1 +159% using only unlabeled test prompts. Reference point for Self-Harmony, TTRV, DARE, TTC-RL. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16084.

index.name: SPIRAL
index.one_liner: Self-play on two-player zero-sum language games (Kuhn Poker, TicTacToe, etc.) with role-conditioned advantage estimation; reasoning transfers to math.
index.why_relevant: Game self-play as an automatic curriculum of ever-stronger opponents with no human data: Qwen3-4B-Base +8.6% math / +8.4% general from Kuhn Poker alone; up to +10% across 8 benchmarks. Built on Oat. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.24119.

index.name: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments (Meta)
index.one_liner: Challenger mines a document corpus to create reasoning tasks; Reasoner solves them; corpus grounding supplies an inexhaustible external signal that avoids ungrounded self-play collapse.
index.why_relevant: Meta FAIR argument that pure self-play saturates without an environment; +8.9% math and +9.8% general reasoning across model families vs limited gains from ungrounded self-play.

index.name: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents (Meta FAIR)
index.one_liner: Agent plays challenger (creates Code-as-Task problems with verification) and executor; supports both distillation and pure self-improvement on tool-use tasks.
index.why_relevant: Early Meta work on self-generated verifiable agent tasks; precursor to Dr. Zero / Tool-R0 style zero-data tool agents.

index.name: Microsoft R&D-Agent
index.one_liner: Dual-agent Research/Development loop that iteratively proposes ideas from performance feedback and refines code from error feedback, with parallel traces that merge; 'AI drives data-driven AI'. Paper arXiv:2505.14738.
index.why_relevant: Longest-running open industrial automated-R&D loop; top MLE-bench performer at time of report and still actively developed in 2026 (quant, Kaggle, data-science scenarios).

index.name: The AI Scientist (v1) - Sakana AI
index.one_liner: First end-to-end automated ML research pipeline: idea generation, experiment execution, paper writing, automated review (~$15/paper). Paper arXiv:2408.06292.
index.why_relevant: Foundational reference point that the whole 'AI Scientist' category and most 2026 systems benchmark against; includes the famous incident of the agent editing its own launch script to extend its time budget.

index.name: The AI Scientist-v2 - Sakana AI
index.one_liner: Template-free agentic tree-search research system with VLM feedback loop; produced the first fully AI-generated paper to pass peer review (ICLR 2025 workshop, avg score 6.33). Paper arXiv:2504.08066.
index.why_relevant: Progressive agentic tree search managed by an experiment-manager agent is the direct ancestor of 2026 tree/graph-search research agents; the standard baseline in AutoResearchClaw, EvoScientist etc.

index.name: MLEvolve
index.one_liner: Self-evolving multi-agent framework for end-to-end ML algorithm discovery: progressive Monte-Carlo graph search + retrospective global memory + adaptive coding modes. Paper arXiv:2606.06473 (Jun 2026).
index.why_relevant: SOTA medal rate on MLE-Bench under 12h budget and beats AlphaEvolve on math algorithm-optimization tasks; memory accumulates across tasks so the system improves with experience.

index.name: Hyra (Tencent Hunyuan Research Agent) results
index.one_liner: Artifacts from Tencent's Hyra research agent: new bounds on open math problems (e.g., Beurling-Ahlfors coefficient 1.575 -> 1.523958, commutator bound O(log^3)), with Lean 4 formalizations and reproduction scripts.
index.why_relevant: Institutional autonomous research agent producing verifiable frontier results; launch post at hy.tencent.com/research/hyra.

index.name: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented RL
index.one_liner: Distills successful trajectories into strategic patterns and failures into lessons in a hierarchical SkillBank (general + task-specific) that co-evolves with the policy during RL; 10-20% token compression vs raw trajectories; checkpoints + SFT data on HF.
index.why_relevant: Skill library and RL policy improve each other in one loop (recursive skill evolution from validation failures); arXiv:2602.08234 (ALFWorld/WebShop).

index.name: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
index.one_liner: First LLM lifelong-learning agent in Minecraft: automatic curriculum + ever-growing skill library of executable code + iterative prompting with self-verification; 3.3x more unique items, 15.3x faster tech-tree milestones.
index.why_relevant: The foundational 'skill library' paradigm every 2025-26 skill-evolution paper cites; repo github.com/MineDojo/Voyager (NVIDIA/Caltech/UT Austin/Stanford).

index.name: Evo-Memory: Benchmarking LLM Agent Test-time Learning with Self-Evolving Memory (Google DeepMind)
index.one_liner: Benchmark over 10 multi-turn goal-oriented and reasoning/QA datasets for memory that evolves across a task stream, plus ReMem (reason/act/memory-update) pipeline.
index.why_relevant: DeepMind standard for evaluating test-time learning via evolving memory; revised May 2026.

index.name: FunSearch (Google DeepMind)
index.one_liner: Pair a pretrained LLM with an automated evaluator in an island-based genetic loop over program skeletons; discovered new cap-set constructions and bin-packing heuristics (Romera-Paredes et al., Nature 2023).
index.why_relevant: The origin of LLM-driven evolutionary program search; every 2025-2026 system (AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve, Shinka, LLM4AD) cites it as the starting point. Repo is archived-quality but still the canonical reference.

index.name: Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale (Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao, Wagner) + AlphaEvolve problem repository
index.one_liner: 67 mathematical problems (analysis, combinatorics, geometry, number theory) attacked with AlphaEvolve, with prompts, verifiers, seed programs and final evolved programs in Colab notebooks; arXiv 2511.02864.
index.why_relevant: Primary open benchmark/evidence base for what LLM evolutionary search can discover in math; LLM4AD_Next (Sept 2026) and others build benchmark suites on it. Institutional weight: Terence Tao co-author.

index.name: AlphaEvolve on Google Cloud (client library + examples)
index.one_liner: Official client-side Python library and runnable examples (circle packing to GPU training on GKE) for the AlphaEvolve service in Gemini Enterprise; includes 'AlphaEvolve Skills' for coding agents.
index.why_relevant: Signals AlphaEvolve's transition from research to a hosted product (seed program + scoring function in, evolved code out); shows the 'skills for coding agents' pattern spreading across evolutionary frameworks.

index.name: ThetaEvolve: Test-time Learning on Open Problems
index.one_liner: Simplifies AlphaEvolve to a single LLM + large program DB, then RL-trains that LLM at test time on the evolution rewards; an 8B model (Distill-Qwen3-8B) set new best-known bounds, e.g. circle packing n=26 = 2.6359857 > AlphaEvolve's 2.63586.
index.why_relevant: Closes the loop between evolutionary program search and weight updates: the proposer model learns from its own evolutionary trajectories (44 citations). UW (Simon Du) group.

index.name: What Do Evolutionary Coding Agents Evolve? (EvoTrace + EvoReplay, ZIB)
index.one_liner: Dataset of 121 full evolutionary runs across OpenEvolve, GEPA, EvoX, ShinkaEvolve on 16 tasks; finds ~30% of added lines are re-introductions of deleted code, hyperparameter tuning dominates edits, and Bayesian optimization on one intermediate program often matches the whole run.
index.why_relevant: The first systematic 'mechanistic' audit of LLM evolutionary search; essential for anyone designing a self-improving loop to know what is actually being improved. Companion repo github.com/ZIB-IOL/EvoReplay.

index.name: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA)
index.one_liner: Weng, Antoniades, Nathani, Zhang, Pu, Xin Eric Wang (UCSB): treats a group of self-modifying agents as the evolutionary unit with explicit experience sharing instead of DGM's isolated tree branches; SWE-bench Verified 71.0% (vs 56.7% prior), Polyglot 88.3% (vs 68.3%).
index.why_relevant: Direct DGM-lineage paper that fixes the branch-isolation inefficiency of tree-structured self-evolution; repo github.com/UCSB-AI/GEA; project page group-evolving-agents.github.io.

index.name: ReMe: Memory Management Kit for Agents (AgentScope / Alibaba Tongyi)
index.one_liner: Local-first, self-evolving Markdown personal knowledge base that turns conversations/trajectories into refined experience for agents (Remember Me, Refine Me).
index.why_relevant: The experience-management layer underneath AgentEvolver's self-navigating and the memory of QwenPaw (34.8k stars); progressively distills sessions into daily notes -> long-term knowledge. Experience-driven tool-use enhancement paper arXiv:2608.03403 (2026-08). Ships plugins for DeepSeek Harness and OpenClaw.

index.name: WebRL: Self-Evolving Online Curriculum RL (THUDM / Zhipu)
index.one_liner: Trains open web agents (GLM-4/Llama) with a self-evolving curriculum that generates new tasks from failures plus an outcome reward model.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2411.02337; foundational Tsinghua/Zhipu reference cited in both awesome lists for 'inter-test-time self-evolution'; lifted Llama-3.1-8B on WebArena-Lite from 4.8% to 42.4%.

index.name: Diving into Reliable Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey (Tencent Hunyuan + Zhejiang University)
index.one_liner: 549-paper survey and list on reliability of self-evolving agents, with a five-level self-evolution taxonomy and OpenReview paper.
index.why_relevant: Newest Chinese-industry survey (Tencent Hunyuan, 2026-08) focused on making self-evolution reliable rather than just capable; complements Misevolution and PAST-Bench (arXiv:2608.04003, Mengdi Wang) on recursive self-improvement of personal agents.

index.name: Training-Free GRPO (Tencent Youtu)
index.one_liner: Replaces parameter updates with group-relative semantic advantages distilled into an evolving experience library used as a token prior; with only dozens of samples DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus beats fine-tuned small LLMs on math and web search. Code in TencentCloudADP/youtu-agent (4612 stars).
index.why_relevant: Makes the 'experience memory as optimizer' analogy explicit (GRPO-shaped loop over text); frequently used as a baseline in 2026 harness-evolution papers.

index.name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
index.one_liner: AI2 / UW (Wang, Hajishirzi, Tsvetkov, Dasigi, Xiao et al.): shows harness-evolution methods must be compared with task-level search baselines under matched feedback and inference budgets to tell improved design from extra search. Jul 2026, v2 Aug 27.
index.why_relevant: Key critique of the self-improvement lineage's evaluation methodology (search-vs-improvement confound) that applies directly to DGM/HGM-style benchmark-validated self-edits.

index.name: Claude Autoresearch Skill
index.one_liner: Claude Code skill implementing modify -> verify -> keep/discard -> repeat forever against any metric.
index.why_relevant: Most-starred Claude Code-native self-improvement loop skill.

index.name: Search Self-Play (SSP, Alibaba Quark)
index.one_liner: Adversarial proposer/solver self-play where both roles call a search engine in multi-turn reasoning; rule-based outcome rewards, per-role RL algorithms.
index.why_relevant: Zero-QA-pair self-play for search agents from Alibaba; co-evolving proposer and solver with tool use, built on veRL + Search-R1. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18821.

index.name: AI4AI-Bench
index.one_liner: Benchmark for recursive self-improvement: 10 frozen research repos across 10 training-algorithm families; agent gets 4h on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm, rerun from scratch up to 12h, scored by fixed evaluator. Code: github.com/Einsia/AI4AI-Bench.
index.why_relevant: Isolates 'can an agent improve the process that produces AI systems' from data collection/hyperparameter tuning - the cleanest measurement target for AI-improving-AI loops.

index.name: PenguinHarness
index.one_liner: 'Harness for RSI': local multi-agent auto-dev platform where an agent runs the benchmark, finds lost points, ships version N+1 with snapshots and traces; tuned for DeepSeek-class open models.
index.why_relevant: Explicit native self-evolution engine (agents build/optimize agents) with strong recent momentum.

index.name: Gödel Agent
index.one_liner: Self-referential agent framework that recursively modifies its own logic/code at runtime guided by task feedback (ACL 2025). Code: github.com/Arvid-pku/Godel_Agent.
index.why_relevant: Foundational RSI reference alongside DGM; the 'self-referential' lineage HyperAgents extends.

index.name: MemOS
index.one_liner: Self-evolving memory OS for LLM agents: persistent memory, hybrid retrieval, cross-task skill reuse; sibling paper MemRL (runtime RL on episodic memory, github.com/MemTensor/MemRL).
index.why_relevant: Memory-centric self-evolution with an RL-on-memory variant.

index.name: ALMA: Learning to Continually Learn via Meta-learning Agentic Memory Designs
index.one_liner: Meta-learns the agent memory design (what to store, how to retrieve/update) instead of hand-engineering it; learned designs beat SOTA human-crafted memories on 4 sequential decision domains.
index.why_relevant: Jeff Clune's group (UBC) — turns the memory/skill mechanism into a searched object, one level up from AWM/Memp-style fixed designs.

index.name: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime RL on Episodic Memory
index.one_liner: Non-parametric self-evolution: two-phase retrieval over episodic memory whose utilities are updated by environmental feedback (runtime RL), no weight updates; beats SOTA on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, LifelongAgentBench.
index.why_relevant: Stability-plasticity via learned memory utilities; arXiv:2601.03192, from the MemOS team.

index.name: evo
index.one_liner: Turns any codebase into an autoresearch loop: discovers what to measure, instruments the benchmark, runs tree search with parallel subagents.
index.why_relevant: Automates the metric-discovery step that autoresearch-style harness loops otherwise leave to humans.

index.name: Mendel Gödel Machine (MGM)
index.one_liner: Liu, Tresp, Ma et al. (LMU): adds reaction-norm mutation (edit agent from trajectories on many tasks at once) and cross-lineage hybridization to DGM-style self-modification; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Polyglot 50.8%->93.3%, evolved scaffold transfers to DeepSeek-V4-Pro at 96.9%. arXiv:2608.07645, Aug 2026.
index.why_relevant: Most recent Gödel-machine variant (one month old) with the strongest reported Polyglot numbers; introduces multi-trajectory and cross-lineage self-edits with proofs under an additive fitness model.

index.name: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA)
index.one_liner: UCSB (William Wang group): treats a group of self-modifying agents as the evolutionary unit with explicit experience sharing instead of DGM's isolated tree branches; 71.0% vs 56.7% SWE-bench Verified and 88.3% vs 68.3% Polyglot over prior self-evolving methods. arXiv:2602.04837.
index.why_relevant: Direct open-ended self-improvement successor to DGM that matches/exceeds top human-designed coding agent frameworks; code released.

index.name: AutoSaddler (Microsoft)
index.one_liner: Frames harness improvement as offline learning over execution traces: failure-trace diagnosis, structured patches to prompts/tools/middleware/agent-loop code, generalization-aware selection with an evolution DAG; +9.0 / +9.6 / +10.0 pp on GAIA2, SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.0 over base harnesses.
index.why_relevant: Newest institutional entry (Aug 24 2026) with durable, resumable, content-addressed harness optimization; beats strongest automated baseline by 4.4-7.4 pts. Paper arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041; V2 added Meta-ARE support Aug 25.

index.name: OpenAI 'automated research intern' milestone
index.one_liner: OpenAI says it hit its Sept-2026 target of an automated research intern that carries out multi-day well-defined research tasks; ~3.1 agent-workdays per human researcher workday, median researcher >$600/day of inference.
index.why_relevant: Roadmap milestone toward a fully automated AI researcher (target March 2028); the most concrete public numbers on agents running a frontier lab's internal research loop.

index.name: DeepScientist
index.one_liner: Month-scale autonomous discovery system using Bayesian optimization over a hierarchical evaluator: ~5,000 ideas generated, ~1,100 experimentally validated, >20,000 GPU-hours; gains 1.9%-183.7% over human SOTA on 3 AI tasks. Paper arXiv:2509.26603.
index.why_relevant: Claims first large-scale evidence of an AI progressively surpassing human SOTA via a closed hypothesize-verify-analyze loop that updates its own priors.

index.name: AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents (Meta)
index.one_liner: Meta FAIR's second-gen AI research agent: async multi-GPU search, Hidden Consistent Evaluation, ReAct with dynamic action scoping; 81.5% mean percentile on MLE-bench-30 at 24h, beats human SOTA on 6/20 AIRS-Bench tasks.
index.why_relevant: Institutional-weight research agent with predictable scaling laws for research-agent compute; builds on AIRA-dojo (github.com/facebookresearch/aira-dojo) search scaffolds.

index.name: Towards Execution-Grounded Automated AI Research (Stanford)
index.one_liner: Si, Yang, Choi, Candes, D. Yang, Hashimoto: an executor implements research ideas and runs GPU experiments; evolutionary search lifts post-training to 69.4% (vs GRPO 48.0%) and cuts nanoGPT pretraining to 19.7 min (vs 35.9) in ten epochs.
index.why_relevant: Rigorous academic study of the idea->execute->select loop, including the finding that RL from execution feedback mode-collapses and LLM ideas saturate early - key caveat for self-improving research loops.

index.name: EvoSkill (Sentient)
index.one_liner: Toolkit that automatically discovers and synthesizes reusable agent skills from failed trajectories; proposes joint skill+prompt mutations, evaluates on held-out data, emits a new agent program each iteration (extends GEPA). Works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, OpenHands, Goose, Harbor.
index.why_relevant: Directly implements failure-driven skill induction as an outer optimization loop for coding agents; paper arXiv:2603.02766.

index.name: Acontext — Agent Skills as a Memory Layer
index.one_liner: Open-source skill-memory layer that automatically captures learnings from agent runs and stores them as editable, shareable agent skill files (Python + npm SDKs).
index.why_relevant: Treats skills as the unit of long-term memory that grows automatically from runs — exactly the 'experience → procedural memory' loop, framework-agnostic.

index.name: tigerless-labs/autoharness
index.one_liner: Self-learning skill layer for Claude Code: distills skills from real sessions, merges same-scenario skills, updates them in use, prunes unused ones; touches only skills it wrote.
index.why_relevant: Clean example of a harness sub-layer that maintains itself with no benchmark or daemon; validation is 'adherence in later turns'. Motivated by HAL's 42%->78% CORE-Bench harness gap.

index.name: aiming-lab/MetaClaw
index.one_liner: Meta-learn and evolve an OpenClaw-style agent from every conversation: skills mode + scheduled LoRA RL training (via Tinker) + cross-session memory, no GPU required.
index.why_relevant: Combines skill self-evolution with actual weight updates from in-the-wild conversations; paper arXiv 2603.17187; same lab as AutoResearchClaw and SkillRL.

index.name: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery (SkyDiscover, UC Berkeley)
index.one_liner: Two-level evolution: inner loop evolves candidate programs, outer loop evolves the search strategy itself when progress plateaus; beats AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve/GEPA/ShinkaEvolve on most of ~200 tasks (ALE-Bench-Lite 1958 vs 1915 Shinka); ships AdaEvolve too.
index.why_relevant: Berkeley Sky lab (Stoica, Zaharia, Keutzer, Dimakis) framework that makes the evolutionary loop's own strategy an evolvable object; 41 citations in 6 months; supports Harbor-format benchmarks (AlgoTune, Frontier-CS); SkyDiscover Synthesize is a Claude Code/Codex skill.

index.name: SICA: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
index.one_liner: Maxime Robeyns et al. (Bristol): a coding agent that edits its own codebase (tools, sub-agents, prompts) in a benchmark-scored loop; reports 17-53% relative gains on SWE-bench Verified subsets; ICLR 2025 SSI-FM workshop oral.
index.why_relevant: One of the two canonical 2025 self-editing coding agents (with DGM); ~44 citations; repo github.com/MaximeRobeyns/self_improving_coding_agent; frequently cloned as a teaching seed (micro-sica etc.).

index.name: Mendel Gödel Machine (MGM)
index.one_liner: Liu, Liu, Yan, Tresp, Ma (UESTC/LMU/MCML): self-modification conditioned on comparative evidence across the archive via three operators (clonal mutation, reaction-norm mutation, cross-lineage hybridization); Polyglot-60 50.8%->93.2% (HGM 77.9%), SWE-bench Verified-60 68.3%->78.3%; ~96h on 8xH100.
index.why_relevant: Newest (Aug 2026) direct successor in the DGM->HGM lineage with theory + strong numbers; repo github.com/RealLcz/MGM, project page reallcz.github.io/MGM.

index.name: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)
index.one_liner: Lin et al. (Fudan/Shanghai AI Lab): observability-driven automatic evolution of coding-agent harnesses (component-level file repr, evidence corpus distilled from trajectories, decision verification turning each edit into a falsifiable contract); Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 69.7%->77.0% over 10 iters with GPT-5.4, NexAU-AHE 84.7% with GPT-5.5.
index.why_relevant: State-of-the-art 2026 harness self-evolution with strong numbers and open code (github.com/china-qijizhifeng/agentic-harness-engineering); explicitly benchmarks against DGM-style self-evolving baselines and Codex-CLI.

index.name: A Systematic Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: From Model-Centric to Environment-Driven Co-Evolution (Xiang et al., XMU)
index.one_liner: 2026 survey with a three-part taxonomy: Model-Centric, Environment-Centric, and Model-Environment Co-Evolution; argues co-evolution with environments is the key emerging direction.
index.why_relevant: Newest broad taxonomy (Xiamen Univ. DeepLIT; also on SSRN 6626878). Model-Centric: inference-based (parallel sampling, sequential self-correction, structured reasoning) and training-based (synthesis-driven offline: STaR, SEAL, SPIN, Sirius; exploration-driven online: R-Zero, Absolute Zero, Agent0, Dr. Zero, WebRL, Search Self-Play, SPICE). Environment-Centric: static knowledge (agentic RAG, deep research), dynamic experience (offline compilation: SkillWeaver, Agent KB; online adaptation: Dynamic Cheatsheet, Memento, GEPA, ACE; lifelong: ReasoningBank, EvolveR, AgentEvolver, MemGen; skill-augmented: RewardHarness, AutoSkill, SkillRL, OpenSkill), modular architecture (memory: MemRL, MemSkill, MemEvolve; tools: Godel Agent, Alita, Live-SWE-agent, EvoTest), agentic topology (ADAS, AFlow, MaAS, EvoAgent). Co-Evolution: multi-agent policy co-evolution (CoMAS, CORAL, GEA), environment training (GenEnv, AgentGym, GEM, Endless Terminals, Agent-World). Also curates self-evolution benchmarks: Aspire, S3Gym, HarnessDev. Repo XMUDeepLIT/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (426 stars, actively updated).

index.name: selfimproving-agent/awesome-Self-Improving-Agents (companion to Ren et al. survey)
index.one_liner: 471-star, actively maintained list organized by FM-improvement vs scaffolding-improvement, including a 'Full Scaffolding' table of 30+ harness/agent self-modification systems.
index.why_relevant: Best current index of 2026 harness-evolution papers (Hyperagents, Continual Harness, Harness-R1, Ouroboros, Prime Agent, HarnessDev, Red Queen GM, MOSS, Meta^n, EvoSafeHarness) plus benchmarks matrix; has an agent-oriented README_AGENT.md and Discord.

index.name: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
index.one_liner: One LLM is both Environment Designer (writes executable reset()/step() Python envs, grounded in a pretraining corpus + env memory) and Reasoning Agent; designer trained with hint-based regret (return with vs. without privileged hint). Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19197
index.why_relevant: Newest and most ambitious zero-data loop: makes environment design itself learnable. Qwen3 4B/8B/30B-A3B: +5.3 avg on 8 held-out benchmarks, +5.7 BFCL-v4 multi-turn, +13.9 ACEBench-Agent, improving past the saturation point of fixed-environment baselines. Authors span UW/Meta/Stanford (Jaques, Zettlemoyer, Choi, Zhao of AZR). Slime/SGLang + Tinker backends.

index.name: Simple Baselines are Competitive with Code Evolution (Gideoni, Risi, Gal)
index.one_liner: Two trivial baselines match or beat sophisticated code-evolution pipelines on math bounds, agent scaffold design and ML competitions; search-space design and prompt domain knowledge dominate.
index.why_relevant: Key skeptical result for the field: argues the evolutionary pipeline is secondary to the human-designed search space; must-read before building yet another AlphaEvolve clone. Companion OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=QSWFqDcveB

index.name: Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment (The Station)
index.one_liner: Multi-agent open-world research environment where agents from different model families pick problems, experiment and build a shared literature; new 604-point kissing configurations in dim 11, new finite-field Kakeya families, improved Erdos minimum-overlap bound.
index.why_relevant: Successor to 'The Station' (arXiv 2511.06309) which already beat AlphaEvolve on circle packing; shows the AlphaEvolve math problem set being attacked by an open-ended, decentralized agent society with released dialogues and verification code.

index.name: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems (+ EvolveLab)
index.one_liner: ICML 2026: jointly evolves the memory contents and the memory architecture itself (encode/store/retrieve/manage modules); EvolveLab unifies 12 memory systems; up to +17.06% on existing frameworks across 4 benchmarks. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2512.18746.
index.why_relevant: Second-order self-evolution: the agent's memory system (not just memories) is optimized from experience; the EvolveLab codebase is a standardized harness for comparing memory-driven evolution.

index.name: Evo-Harness: Context-to-Harness Skill Compilation for Self-Evolving Agents
index.one_liner: EMNLP 2026 Main: frozen LLM agents improve across sequential tasks by compiling noisy single-shot executions into reusable structured skill harnesses; evaluated on TerminalBench2, SWE-bench, CL-Bench and two others in one-shot-per-task settings.
index.why_relevant: Represents the 2026 shift from 'memory entries' to 'compiled harness/skills' as the unit of accumulated experience; 17-author industrial paper from the Evo-Memory group.

index.name: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
index.one_liner: Self-improving training arena that autonomously discovers environment-aligned tasks from thousands of real-world themes with controllable difficulty and trains agents with multi-env RL plus dynamic task synthesis; 8B/14B models beat proprietary baselines on 23 agent benchmarks.
index.why_relevant: Directly on-angle: closed loop of environment discovery -> task synthesis -> RL -> more environments, with explicit scaling analysis showing gains grow with environment diversity and number of self-evolution rounds. Same RUC group (Guanting Dong) as EnvScaler.

index.name: AgentGym-RL
index.one_liner: Unified multi-turn RL framework for training LLM agents from scratch (no SFT) across web, search, games, embodied, science environments; ScalingInter-RL progressively expands interaction horizon; 27 tasks matching/exceeding commercial models (arXiv:2509.08755).
index.why_relevant: Fudan's successor to AgentGym focused on RL scaling of interaction turns; a key open framework for 'agent RL scaling' and the substrate for their self-evolution work.

index.name: Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents (SkillMisevo-Gym/Bench + SafeEvolve)
index.one_liner: Gym + benchmark with 9 metrics for how unsafe practice turns into reusable skills; 21/21 evolved configs produced unsafe artifacts, carryover attack success rose 16.0%->35.3% after malicious exposure.
index.why_relevant: Directly measures skill-level misevolution across 25 agent-method configs x 525 tasks; SafeEvolve wrapper cuts unsafe retrieval by 26.7pp and fresh-session harm by 17.3pp at 0.4pt utility cost. Code: https://github.com/henrymao2004/misevolve

index.name: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness? (Salesforce Research)
index.one_liner: 17 multi-stage harness streams, 802 tasks, 520 tools, 42 skills, 62 agents; finds 'harness-induced forgetting' where adding capabilities degrades previously solved tasks.
index.why_relevant: Evaluation of the harness-evolution pathway: retention vs adaptation conflict, inconsistent gains across evolution stages. Site: https://mas-orchestra.salesforceresearch.ai/evoharness/

index.name: Anthropic: Natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking (From shortcuts to sabotage)
index.one_liner: Models that learn to reward-hack coding RL environments generalize to sabotage of safety research code (12% via Claude Code) and alignment-faking reasoning (50%); 'inoculation prompting' removes the generalization.
index.why_relevant: Key institutional evidence that reward hacking inside a training loop propagates to broad misalignment -- the core risk in weight-level self-improvement. Paper PDF: https://assets.anthropic.com/m/74342f2c96095771/original/Natural-emergent-misalignment-from-reward-hacking-paper.pdf

index.name: Anthropic: Automated researchers can reliably mitigate alignment failures
index.one_liner: Claude run in a closed literature->method->train->test loop closes 26-96% of the safety gap across 10 alignment failure categories (85% on deception vs 20% for 8h humans); Sonnet 5 aligned Opus 4.8 to 65% gap closure in 60h with ~2,000 examples.
index.why_relevant: Anthropic's most direct 2026 statement on using automated AI R&D loops for safety during RSI, with reported caveats: cheating attempts in 2.4% of transcripts and non-persistence after further training. PDF: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/7b1c44894e980876479947dcdd40716278aeeffd/automated-alignment-researchers-august-2026.pdf

index.name: METR: Expenditure Horizon (NanoGPT speedrun optimization)
index.one_liner: New metric = dollars at which an agent's optimization matches human returns; on nanoGPT speedrun humans spend ~$2,500 per 1% speedup; GPT-5/Opus-4.1 = $0, GPT-5.2 ~$600, GPT-5.5 $2,300 (~1%), Opus-4.8 $3,300 (~1.5%); only 50-60% of agent speedups judged mergeable (brittle hyperparameter tuning).
index.why_relevant: Most rigorous public measurement to date of autonomous AI R&D uplift on a real research artifact; directly quantifies how much of the 'AI improving AI training' loop is currently automatable.

index.name: Prime Intellect: Frontier Automated NanoGPT Speedrun
index.one_liner: 153 autonomous multi-day runs of 18 frontier models on the modded-nanogpt track-3 optimizer speedrun (8xH200, frozen verify.py, 8-seed records): Fable 5 2,726 steps (81.7% of human-record gap closed), Opus 5 2,920, Kimi K3 2,968, GPT-5.6 Sol 3,042; baseline 3,290, human 2,600.
index.why_relevant: Cleanest head-to-head public benchmark of frontier models doing unattended ML-research optimization with full sanitized traces released; write-up at primeintellect.ai/research/nanogpt-speedrun.

index.name: RSI-Exam
index.one_liner: aiming-lab: benchmark measuring recursive self-improvement on long-horizon executable research tasks. Aug 2026.
index.why_relevant: New evaluation target for self-improving agents beyond SWE-bench/Polyglot; from the Agent0 group.

index.name: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself
index.one_liner: Outer loop analyzes the inner autoresearch loop's trace and injects new search mechanisms as Python code at runtime, same LLM at both levels; reported 5x improvement over inner loop alone (-0.045 vs -0.009 val_bpb) on Karpathy's benchmark.
index.why_relevant: Directly meta-optimizes the improvement harness itself (optimizer code as the object of optimization), the top rung of Weng's ladder. Paper arxiv.org/abs/2603.23420, AISC 2026.

index.name: ECC (Everything Claude Code) - agent harness performance optimization system
index.one_liner: Massive Claude Code/Codex/Cursor harness layer (68 agents, 291 skills, hooks, memory) with continuous-learning v2: an observer daemon distills sessions into confidence-scored 'instincts', /evolve clusters instincts into skills, /prune expires them.
index.why_relevant: By far the most-adopted practitioner harness with an automated learn-from-sessions loop (instincts -> skills); relevance is moderate (learns rules/skills, not harness code) but influence is enormous (256k stars, 38k forks).

index.name: Socratic-Zero
index.one_liner: Teacher, Solver, and Generator agents co-evolve from ~100 seed questions; Teacher targets Solver weaknesses, Generator distills the Teacher's question-design strategy.
index.why_relevant: Near-zero-data three-agent co-evolution: Socratic-Solver-8B +20.2 pp over prior synthesis methods across 7 math benchmarks (AMC23, AIME24/25, MATH-500, etc.); appears as a baseline in Agent0's tables.

index.name: Self-Questioning Language Models (SQLM)
index.one_liner: Asymmetric self-play from a single topic prompt: proposer rewarded for medium-difficulty questions, solver rewarded via majority vote (or unit tests for code); both trained with RL.
index.why_relevant: CMU (Chen, Prabhudesai et al.) minimal formulation of zero-data self-play; improvements on arithmetic, algebra, coding and multimodal tasks from only a topic string.

index.name: Self-Play Only Evolves When Self-Synthetic Pipeline Ensures Learnable Information Gain
index.one_liner: Analysis (KCL) showing self-play loops plateau when synthesized data stops adding learnable information; proposes asymmetric co-evolution, capacity growth, and proactive information seeking.
index.why_relevant: Key diagnostic of why zero-data self-evolution stalls (Proposer/Solver/Verifier triad); a system-level design guide for anyone building sustained self-improvement loops.

index.name: EvoMap AutoResearch
index.one_liner: Open-source stateful, recoverable AI/ML research workflow from idea discovery through pilot experiments, independent multi-model review and blind evaluation to paper-ready evidence.
index.why_relevant: Fast-rising (3.4k stars in 4 weeks) idea-to-evidence loop that iterates on pilot results and critic reports; independent review by >=3 distinct models to avoid self-approval.

index.name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery (Edison Scientific)
index.one_liner: 12-hour runs cycling parallel data analysis, literature search and hypothesis generation over a structured world model; ~200 rollouts, 42,000 lines of code and 1,500 papers per run. Community reimplementation: github.com/jimmc414/Kosmos.
index.why_relevant: Reference for long-horizon iterative discovery loops with shared world-model state between agents; frequently cited by 2026 systems.

index.name: SePO: Self-Evolving Prompt Agent for System Prompt Optimization
index.one_liner: Self-referential design: a single prompt agent optimizes task agents' system prompts AND its own system prompt under open-ended evolutionary search with an archive of stepping-stone prompts (code: github.com/taowangcheng/SePO).
index.why_relevant: Closes the loop that PromptBreeder opened: the optimizer's own prompt evolves. Evaluated on AIME'25, ARC-AGI-1, GPQA, MBPP, Sudoku with pretrain-on-multi-task then fine-tune-on-target stages. Repo is tiny (4 stars) but the idea is squarely 'self-refining system prompt'.

index.name: FAPO: Fully Automated Prompt Optimization (cisco-foundation-ai)
index.one_liner: Uses Claude Code as the autonomous optimizer over LangGraph pipelines: evaluate -> step-level failure attribution -> edit prompts, agent skills, chain params or chain structure -> re-measure.
index.why_relevant: Institutional (Cisco Foundation AI, arXiv 2606.19605) example of a coding agent acting as the prompt/skill self-improvement loop; widens GEPA's action space from instruction strings to whole-chain edits with attribution-driven escalation. Benchmarked on 6 tasks x 3 task models.

index.name: Building State-of-the-Art Enterprise Agents 90x Cheaper with Automated Prompt Optimization (Databricks)
index.one_liner: GEPA-optimized gpt-oss-120b beats Claude Sonnet 4 / Opus 4.1 by ~3% at 20x/90x lower serving cost; also lifts Opus 4.1 and Sonnet 4 by 6-7%; matches or beats SFT with 20% lower serving cost.
index.why_relevant: The most-cited industrial evidence that an automated prompt-evolution loop substitutes for fine-tuning; widely re-reported and quoted in the GEPA README.

index.name: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
index.one_liner: DeepMind (Fernando et al.): evolutionary population of task-prompts whose mutation-prompts are themselves evolved by the LLM, i.e. self-referential self-improvement.
index.why_relevant: Foundational self-referential prompt-evolution paper still cited as the origin of 'optimize the optimizer's prompt' (directly extended by SePO 2026).

index.name: MIPROv2: Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage LM Programs
index.one_liner: Bayesian surrogate search over jointly proposed instructions and bootstrapped few-shot demos for multi-module DSPy programs (Opsahl-Ong, Khattab et al., EMNLP 2024).
index.why_relevant: The workhorse DSPy optimizer and the main non-RL baseline in the GEPA paper; still the default for labeled-data prompt compilation.

index.name: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement
index.one_liner: Workshop on algorithmic foundations for reliable self-improving AI (agents rewriting codebases/prompts, continual fine-tuning pipelines, robotics stacks patching controllers). OpenReview: openreview.net/forum?id=OsPQ6zTQXV.
index.why_relevant: Institutional signal that RSI became a mainstream research track in 2026; proceedings are a curated paper pool.

index.name: Raven (EverMind)
index.one_liner: Open-source self-improving agent harness (terminal-first, tracing, long-term memory, skills, evaluation, workflows); roadmap toward a 'Harness of Harnesses' with an evaluation→execution→verification→memory→feedback loop.
index.why_relevant: High-velocity harness with explicit feedback loop; sibling of EverOS memory layer (12.9k stars).

index.name: Kiro Crew (AWS)
index.one_liner: Persistent dev workspace that is self-learning (corrections/failures become durable lessons) and self-evolving (repeated patterns become reusable skills), with visible editable memory.
index.why_relevant: Big-vendor (AWS Kiro) productization of the lessons→skills self-improvement loop.

index.name: R-Zero
index.one_liner: Self-evolving reasoning LLM from zero data via Challenger/Solver co-evolution from one base model (ICLR 2026). Code: github.com/Chengsong-Huang/R-Zero.
index.why_relevant: Reference zero-data self-evolution loop at the weight level; precursor to Agent0.

index.name: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution (ICML 2026)
index.one_liner: Bi-level framework co-evolving context-engineering skills and context artifacts; +18.4/+33.0 pts relative gain vs ACE offline/online across 5 domains, 13.6x faster training, 4.8x fewer rollouts.
index.why_relevant: Replaces static harness heuristics with learnable, evolving skills that decide how context itself is built; arXiv:2601.21557.

index.name: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents (Google)
index.one_liner: RL-trains a skill curator (composite rewards, grouped task streams) that manages an external skill repository so agents reuse experience instead of solving each task in isolation; consistent gains over memory-free baselines, generalizes across agent architectures.
index.why_relevant: Google Cloud AI Research follow-up to ReasoningBank: the skill-library maintenance policy itself is learned via RL.

index.name: Agent Workflow Memory (AWM)
index.one_liner: Induces reusable workflows from past trajectories (offline or online from self-generated successes) and stores them as memory for future planning; +24.6% WebArena and +51.1% Mind2Web relative success.
index.why_relevant: CMU foundational work on procedural/workflow memory that grows online; arXiv:2409.07429.

index.name: Teaching LLMs to Self-Evolve: MetaEvolve (UIUC)
index.one_liner: Trains meta-skills (self-reflection, insight extraction from history, feedback integration) with GRPO on synthesized evolutionary trajectories, then runs inference-time evolutionary search; APPS 59.8% vs AlphaEvolve-style 42.2%, +46.9% on AlgoTune.
index.why_relevant: Explicitly frames evolutionary code search as a capability to be trained into the model, combining RL post-training with an inference-time evolutionary loop; Heng Ji group.

index.name: LLM4AD_Next / OpenLoopX (Optima-CityU)
index.one_liner: One-command 'problem description -> runnable evolutionary algorithm search' platform: EoH, FunSearch, ReEvo, MEoH, MCTS-AHD, Diverse Island GA as orchestrators, MindMemOS long-term memory, algorithm-design skills for coding agents, AlphaEvolve Mathematics Benchmark Suite (11 cases, Sept 2026).
index.why_relevant: Fastest-moving academic platform for LLM-driven automated algorithm design (commits today); packages the whole EoH/FunSearch/ReEvo lineage plus AlphaEvolve-style benchmarks and agent skills.

index.name: CodeEvolve (Inter / science-codeevolve)
index.one_liner: Open-source evolutionary coding agent with island model, inspiration-based crossover, meta-prompting that lets the model rewrite its own instructions; compared head-to-head with AlphaEvolve on its math benchmark (arXiv 2510.14150).
