index.why_relevant: 36 citations; one of the few industry (Inter bank) open frameworks that evolves both solutions and the search prompts.

index.name: Live-SWE-agent
index.one_liner: Xia, Wang, Yang, Wei, Lingming Zhang (UIUC): agent starts with minimal bash tools and evolves its own scaffold on-the-fly at runtime while solving tasks; 77.4% SWE-bench Verified, 45.8% SWE-bench Pro.
index.why_relevant: Runtime (in-task) self-evolution rather than offline archive search; repo github.com/OpenAutoCoder/live-swe-agent; listed under recursive self-modification in the Schmidhuber-group survey.

index.name: EvoAgentX
index.one_liner: Open-source framework for evolving agentic workflows (TextGrad/AFlow/MIPRO optimizers) that accompanies the Fang survey; EMNLP 2025 demo.
index.why_relevant: The survey authors' own self-evolving-ecosystem framework (arXiv:2507.03616), listed as the primary open-source framework in their awesome list.

index.name: CORAL: Towards Autonomous Multi-Agent Evolution for Open-Ended Discovery
index.one_liner: Open-source 'autoresearch' runner for Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode with grading, shared knowledge, and multi-agent evolution.
index.why_relevant: Listed by both Fang's list and XMU survey under MAS optimisation / co-evolution; practical framework for running self-evolving agent populations. Repo Human-Agent-Society/CORAL.

index.name: AlphaResearch: Accelerating New Algorithm Discovery with Language Models
index.one_liner: Autonomous research agent looping propose -> program/verify -> optimize proposal, with execution reward plus simulated peer review; beats prior systems on 6/8 open algorithmic problems and surpasses AlphaEvolve on circle packing.
index.why_relevant: Adds a 'research-proposal' level above code evolution (Yale/Tsinghua, Arman Cohan); AlphaResearchComp benchmark of 8 open problems.

index.name: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
index.one_liner: Alternates harness evolution and weight training in a joint loop (Yoonho Lee, Meta-Harness authors).
index.why_relevant: Outperforms weight-only, harness-only and Fast-Slow Training by 4.15-24.38 pp; frames the prompt/harness-vs-RL question as a joint optimization rather than either/or.

index.name: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution
index.one_liner: Che, Yang, Lin, Wang, Wang, Su: harness evolution around a frozen LLM as sample-efficient fast adaptation; uses expert demonstrations to guide the coding proposer when reward-only harness search is too sparse in long-horizon stochastic environments. May 2026.
index.why_relevant: Addresses the credit-assignment problem that limits SICA/DGM-style self-edits outside coding benchmarks; cites SICA as foundation.

index.name: auto-harness
index.one_liner: Bring-your-own-agent system that mines failures, optimizes the agent harness, and gates against regressions.
index.why_relevant: Failure-mining → harness optimization → regression gate is exactly the harness-level loop.

index.name: Gödel Agent
index.one_liner: Yin, Wang, Pan, Wan, W.Y. Wang (PKU/UCSB): LLM agent that dynamically modifies its own logic and code, including the code that analyzes and modifies itself, guided only by high-level prompted objectives. arXiv:2410.04444.
index.why_relevant: Earliest LLM-era self-referential agent implementation (pre-DGM); the 'search the full agent design space by self-modification' framing that later Gödel-machine work formalized.

index.name: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting
index.one_liner: Argues that text-mutable artifacts (skills, prompts, memory, workflow graphs) cannot reach structural failures living in code, and performs self-rewriting at the harness source level on production agentic substrates. May 2026.
index.why_relevant: Explicitly positions source-code self-modification as a Turing-complete strict superset of prompt/skill/memory evolution, i.e. the theoretical case for the self-modifying-agent lineage over text-layer self-evolution.

index.name: Sakana AI Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) Lab
index.one_liner: Tokyo lab co-founded by Llion Jones dedicated to AI redesigning the AI development process; consolidates DGM, ShinkaEvolve, Digital Red Queen (Core War coevolution with MIT) and The AI Scientist under one RSI agenda. Announced Jun 2026.
index.why_relevant: Institutional signal: the DGM originators formed a dedicated RSI lab, pitching self-improving agents as a way around the frontier-lab compute arms race.

index.name: Live-SWE-agent
index.one_liner: UIUC (Steven Xia): starts from bash-only mini-SWE-agent and synthesizes/refines its own tools and scaffold on the fly while solving tasks; 77.4% SWE-bench Verified, 45.8% SWE-bench Pro with no offline training or test-time scaling.
index.why_relevant: Runtime (within-episode) scaffold self-evolution rather than offline outer-loop search; strongest SWE-bench numbers among self-evolving scaffolds at release. Paper arxiv.org/abs/2511.13646.

index.name: Multi-Agent Evolve (MAE)
index.one_liner: One base LLM instantiates Proposer, Solver, and Judge roles trained jointly via Task-Relative REINFORCE++ in a closed propose-solve-judge loop without external supervision.
index.why_relevant: Extends the 2-role proposer/solver pattern with a learned Judge so the loop works on general (non-verifiable) reasoning; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct +4.54% avg across benchmarks. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23595.

index.name: Self-Play SWE-RL (SSR, Meta)
index.one_liner: Bug-injection agent and bug-solving agent share one model and co-evolve via RL on sandboxed repos, no human issues or tests required; pitched as a step toward 'superintelligent software agents'.
index.why_relevant: Applies the zero-data proposer/solver loop to real software engineering from Meta's CWM group; only needs repo + deps sandbox. Reference for later Socratic-SWE and self-evolving coding agent work.

index.name: Socratic-SWE
index.one_liner: Shared policy alternates Generator (repo-grounded repair task construction from solving traces) and Solver roles; self-evolving SWE agent.
index.why_relevant: Reaches 50.40% SWE-bench Verified after three self-play iterations, consistently beating other self-evolving baselines at equal compute on SWE-bench Verified/Lite/Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0; tasks target the agent's own weaknesses rather than fixed bug injection.

index.name: Self-Rewarding Language Models (Meta/NYU) + lucidrains impl
index.one_liner: Model generates its own prompts, responses, and LLM-as-a-Judge rewards, then iterates DPO on self-created preference data (arXiv 2401.10020).
index.why_relevant: Foundational 'self-rewarding' loop that most 2025-26 self-play work cites; the lucidrains implementation remains the most-starred community codebase. Follow-ups: Meta-Rewarding LMs (2407.19594), Process-based Self-Rewarding (2503.03746). Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10020.

index.name: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams (Zitnik lab)
index.one_liner: Decentralized agents self-organize into teams around hypotheses, critique before spending compute, and share successes/failures across long-running experiments.
index.why_relevant: 74.4% mean percentile on BioML-Bench, 1.9x faster to target on LM training, +12.5% protein fitness; preserves memory of failed directions so the collective improves over long horizons.

index.name: POISE: From AI Assistant to AI Scientist - Autonomous Discovery of LLM-RL Algorithms
index.one_liner: Fudan framework maintaining archives of proposals/implementations/evaluations to auto-discover policy-optimization algorithms; from GRPO, 64 candidates evaluated, best variant lifts AIME25 pass@32 from 26.7% to 43.3%.
index.why_relevant: An AI research loop that improves the training algorithm used to train LLMs - a concrete AI4AI instance with measurable gains.

index.name: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design (Meta)
index.one_liner: Two agentic neural-architecture-discovery frameworks: 11 agents produced 14 designs scaling to 3B params surpassing Llama 3.2 (54-71% faster scaling); 20 agents invented attention/optimizer variants near-SOTA on Long Range Arena.
index.why_relevant: Meta's counterpart to ASI-Arch: LLM agents autonomously discovering architectures beyond Transformers at industrial scale.

index.name: AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind)
index.one_liner: Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent: population of programs, automated evaluators, LLM mutation of top candidates; now generally available on Google Cloud.
index.why_relevant: Canonical closed evaluate-mutate-select loop that improved Spanner efficiency, broke math records and advanced neural-net building blocks; the baseline MLEvolve and others compare against.

index.name: TextGrad (zou-group/textgrad)
index.one_liner: PyTorch-like 'automatic differentiation via text': LLM-generated textual gradients backpropagated through compound AI systems to optimize prompts, code, molecules. Published in Nature (2025).
index.why_relevant: Foundational textual-gradient paradigm for self-optimizing prompts/pipelines (arXiv 2406.07496). Development has slowed (last push 2025-07) and the metaphor is now contested (see 'Textual Gradients are a Flawed Metaphor'), but it remains a core reference point.

index.name: SCOPE: Prompt Evolution for Enhancing Agent Effectiveness (JarvisPei/SCOPE)
index.one_liner: Frames context management as online optimization: synthesizes guidelines from execution traces into tactical vs strategic memory streams, with conflict resolution, subsumption pruning and perspective-driven parallel prompt evolution.
index.why_relevant: Paper arXiv 2512.15374 reports +8.2 points on SWE-bench Verified for a single coding agent from self-evolved prompts alone; pip-installable (scope-optimizer). Directly a 'self-refining system prompt' loop for agents.

index.name: RLMOpt: Adaptive Prompt Optimization via Recursive Language Models
index.one_liner: Makes the search policy itself an LLM agent (RLM) that inspects failures, proposes candidates, allocates eval budget and decides when to stop, under a deterministic harness enforcing Pareto selection and no-regression.
index.why_relevant: Newest (Aug 2026) challenger to GEPA: best held-out score on all 4 benchmarks (Chia, HotpotQA, IFBench-2025, BFCL), wins 9/11 matched seed comparisons, prompts 27-79% shorter, ~500 vs 800+ rollouts, zero regressions. Represents the shift from fixed optimizer procedures to agentic optimizers.

index.name: Automatically Learning Skills for Coding Agents (GEPA blog / ACM AIAS)
index.one_liner: gskill: GEPA evolves repository-specific skill files for Mini-SWE-Agent under 300 rollouts; resolve rate 55%->82% on Jinja and 24%->93% on Bleve; skills transfer to Claude Code (Haiku 4.5 79.3%->100% on Bleve).
index.why_relevant: Demonstrates the prompt-evolution loop applied to agent skill/context files rather than a single prompt, with concrete coding-agent numbers; later published at ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (doi 10.1145/3786335.3813196).

index.name: EvoAgentX
index.one_liner: Framework to build, evaluate and automatically evolve agentic workflows/prompts with SOTA self-evolving optimizers (TextGrad, AFlow, MIPRO) driven by datasets and goals.
index.why_relevant: Established workflow-optimization loop framework; authors of the 2508.07407 survey.

index.name: Position: Agentic Evolution is the Path to Evolving LLMs (A-Evolve)
index.one_liner: Position paper arguing LLMs should evolve through agentic loops rather than static training; official repo github.com/A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve.
index.why_relevant: Widely-starred position paper linking agent-level self-evolution to model evolution.

index.name: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution (Google)
index.one_liner: Maintains an evolving knowledge wiki alongside agent skills; evolved skills transfer across model families and let small models beat larger skill-less ones; community Hermes implementation github.com/ashutoshsinghpr7/wikiskill (146 stars).
index.why_relevant: Very recent (Aug 27 2026) Google paper on compiling experience into a persistent wiki that drives skill evolution; already implemented for Hermes Agent.

index.name: yologdev/yoyo-evolve
index.one_liner: Coding agent that rewrites its own source every 3 hours (read source -> plan -> edit -> tests -> commit or revert), from 200 lines of Rust to 158K lines / 5,400 tests with zero human code.
index.why_relevant: A live, public, tests-gated self-modifying agent with daily memory synthesis and social-learning sessions; a concrete RSI-in-the-wild artifact.

index.name: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey (KAUST/IDSIA, Schmidhuber)
index.one_liner: Ren, Chen, ... Wenyi Wang, Zhuge, Schmidhuber (arXiv 2607.13104): taxonomy of self-improving agentic systems incl. full-scaffold recursive self-modification (DGM, Gödel Agent, STOP, HGM, AlphaEvolve, Live-SWE-agent), memory, tool, and model-level loops.
index.why_relevant: Authoritative survey from the HGM authors' group; companion list github.com/selfimproving-agent/Awesome-Self-Improving-Agents.

index.name: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design (Guo et al.)
index.one_liner: Model-harness survey: Agent = Foundation Model + Execution Harness; four engineering paradigms (prompt -> context/workflow -> harness -> agent-native training) and six harness runtime responsibilities.
index.why_relevant: Gives the vocabulary for 'harness' that the self-evolving-harness papers build on. Six responsibilities: observation interface, context manager, control loop, action interface, state/artifact store, verification/governance. Names 'model-harness co-evolution' and agent-native training with self-evolution as open challenges. 17 authors (Yunhe Wang, Kai Han group). Repo ggjy/Awesome-Agent-Engineering (69 stars).

index.name: SEAL: Self-Adapting Language Models
index.one_liner: LLM generates its own finetuning data and update directives ('self-edits'), optimized via RL on downstream performance.
index.why_relevant: Canonical weight-level self-improvement loop cited under 'intrinsic generative demonstrations' / 'synthesis-driven offline self-evolving'. Repo Continual-Intelligence/SEAL (MIT).

index.name: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
index.one_liner: Benchmark of 520 hidden evaluation items over six vague capability goals; agents must plan training and harness edits themselves; weight-level gains are 'sparse and unstable'.
index.why_relevant: Evaluates both model-weight and agent-harness self-updates end-to-end; sibling of S3Gym (experience-based self-improvement across seven games with self-testing/self-judging).

index.name: Self-Rewarding Language Models
index.one_liner: Meta/NYU (Yuan, Weston): the policy is its own LLM-as-a-Judge reward model; iterative DPO improves both instruction following and judging over 3 iterations on Llama-2-70B.
index.why_relevant: Foundational self-improvement loop that removes the frozen reward model; after 3 iterations beats Claude 2 / Gemini Pro / GPT-4-0613 on AlpacaEval 2.0. Its weakness (judge-plausibility reward hacking) is exactly what later self-play papers (e.g. 'More Convincing, Not More Correct', G-Zero) target.

index.name: G-Zero: Self-Play for Open-Ended Generation from Zero Data
index.one_liner: R-Zero authors extend zero-data self-play to open-ended (non-verifiable) tasks with Hint-delta, an intrinsic reward = predictive shift between unassisted and self-hint-conditioned responses; Proposer via GRPO, Generator via DPO. Code: https://github.com/Chengsong-Huang/G-Zero
index.why_relevant: Directly attacks the LLM-judge bottleneck/reward hacking that blocks self-play outside math/code; verifier-free intrinsic signal plus a best-iterate suboptimality guarantee under exploration coverage and bounded pseudo-label noise.

index.name: Scaling Self-Play with Self-Guidance (SGS)
index.one_liner: Stanford (Hashimoto, Tengyu Ma): adds a third Guide role that scores conjectured problems by relevance to unsolved targets and naturalness, fixing the Conjecturer's reward hacking toward artificially complex problems.
index.why_relevant: Documents the collapse mode (proposer hacks learnability reward with junk-hard problems) and a fix: in Lean4 theorem proving, SGS beats the strongest RL baseline's asymptote in <80 self-play rounds and a 7B model beats a 671B model's pass@4 after 200 rounds.

index.name: SOAR: Teaching Models to Teach Themselves (Reasoning at the Edge of Learnability)
index.one_liner: Meta FAIR/NYU (Kempe, Ollivier): meta-RL teacher generates synthetic problems and is rewarded by actual student improvement on target problems rather than proxy learnability metrics. Site: https://ssundaram21.github.io/soar/
index.why_relevant: Unlocks learning on math subsets with 0/128 initial success. Finds grounded (student-improvement) rewards beat intrinsic learnability metrics, which cause instability and diversity collapse; well-posedness of problems matters more than correctness of solutions.

index.name: Propose, Solve, Verify (PSV): Self-Play Through Formal Verification
index.one_liner: CMU (Welleck, Fried, Parno): self-play for verified Rust/Verus code where a formal verifier supplies a reliable correctness signal; difficulty-aware proposal.
index.why_relevant: Shows the strongest available signal (formal verification) makes self-play scale: PSV-Verus pass@1 up to 9.6x over inference-only and expert-iteration baselines, with gains growing in question count and iterations. Ablations name formal verification + difficulty-aware proposal as essential.

index.name: Reinforced Generation of Combinatorial Structures: Ramsey Numbers (AlphaEvolve)
index.one_liner: AlphaEvolve as a single meta-algorithm evolves search algorithms that raise lower bounds on 9 classical Ramsey numbers (R(3,13) 60->61, R(4,20) 234->237, R(4,16) 170->174, ...).
index.why_relevant: Concrete 2026 AlphaEvolve math discovery (Nagda, Raghavan, Thakurta); companion to 'Hardness of Approximation' (arXiv 2509.18057) using the same loop for complexity-theory gadgets.

index.name: AI-PROPELLER / Magellan: Warehouse-Scale Code Layout Optimization with AlphaEvolve (Google)
index.one_liner: Agentic AlphaEvolve workflow (Magellan) evolves Propeller compiler heuristics into a fine-grained interprocedural code-layout optimizer, measured on real hardware: 0.23%-1.6% on warehouse-scale apps.
index.why_relevant: AlphaEvolve applied inside Google's production compiler stack; first fine-grained interprocedural layout optimization of industrial warehouse-scale binaries, with candidates evaluated on real hardware.

index.name: Adapting AlphaEvolve to Optimize Fully Homomorphic Encryption on TPUs (Google)
index.one_liner: AlphaEvolve with hardware-in-the-loop feedback on TPUv5e: TFHE bootstrap 2.5x faster, CKKS rotation 1.31x, CKKS mult 1.18x within 24h of automated exploration.
index.why_relevant: 2026 kernel-optimization application of the evolutionary loop with correctness tests + real-hardware latency as fitness; representative of the 'AlphaEvolve for kernels' line.

index.name: Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with LLMs (DeepMind)
index.one_liner: AlphaEvolve discovers new game-theoretic learning algorithms (Volatility-Adaptive Discounted CFR, hybrid optimistic PSRO) competitive across 18 games; ablations distill them into simpler, better-generalizing variants.
index.why_relevant: DeepMind (Lanctot et al.) using AlphaEvolve for algorithm discovery in RL/game theory rather than math bounds; shows evolved algorithms are complex environment-tailored mechanisms that need human distillation.

index.name: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search (MIT)
index.one_liner: Drop-in replacement for GRPO advantage estimation that trains the LLM to emit a diverse set of solutions across a vector reward; VPO models solve evolutionary-search problems GRPO models cannot solve at all.
index.why_relevant: Trains the weights specifically to be a better evolutionary operator (pass@k / best@k / evolutionary search); Risi, Khattab, Agrawal group; closes the loop between RL post-training and downstream program evolution.

index.name: Evolutionary System Prompt Learning for RL in LLMs (E-SPL)
index.one_liner: Co-evolves system prompts (LLM mutation/crossover) and model weights (RL) in the same training loop; AIME->BeyondAIME success 38.8% -> 45.1%, beating reflective prompt evolution (40.0%).
index.why_relevant: EvoPrompt-style prompt evolution fused with weight updates; concrete evidence that evolving the prompt population alongside RL improves sample efficiency and generalization. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14697

index.name: Digital Red Queen: Adversarial Program Evolution in Core War with LLMs (Sakana AI / MIT)
index.one_liner: Self-play LLM evolution of Redcode 'warriors' with a continually moving objective; evolved programs become increasingly general against held-out human warriors and show convergent evolution across runs.
index.why_relevant: Open-ended, self-play variant of LLM program evolution (Kumar, Risi, Tang, Ha); no fixed evaluator, fitness is the co-evolving population itself.

index.name: Mind Evolution: Evolving Deeper LLM Thinking (DeepMind)
index.one_liner: Evolutionary inference-time scaling in natural-language space (islands, critic/author refinement); >98% on TravelPlanner and Natural Plan with Gemini 1.5 Pro, beating Best-of-N and sequential revision at equal cost.
index.why_relevant: Foundational ICML 2025 work on LLM as recombination/refinement operator for reasoning rather than code; community implementation https://github.com/lucidrains/mind-evolution (59 stars).

index.name: Your Agent May Misevolve (Shanghai AI Lab)
index.one_liner: First systematic study of 'misevolution': self-evolving agents drifting into unsafe behaviour across model, memory, tool and workflow evolution paths.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2509.26354 (v2 2026-03, Jing Shao, Dongrui Liu, Weinan Zhang). Shows safety-alignment degradation after memory accumulation and new vulnerabilities from tool creation/reuse even for Gemini-2.5-Pro; the standard safety citation for any self-evolving harness.

index.name: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
index.one_liner: NeurIPS 2023: agent verbally reflects on failures and stores reflections in an episodic memory buffer used on subsequent trials; 91% pass@1 HumanEval. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366.
index.why_relevant: The origin of the reflect-and-remember loop that nearly every experience-memory system builds on; still the default baseline.

index.name: Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills
index.one_liner: Qwen team: parallel inductive consolidation of execution traces into a unified skill directory; skills mined from Qwen3.5-35B lift a Qwen3.5-122B agent by up to 57.65 pts on WikiTableQuestions; beats sequential editing and retrieval memory. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2603.25158.
index.why_relevant: Official Qwen implementation of trace-to-skill distillation, showing skills as a portable, model-transferable form of experience.

index.name: Recuris: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
index.one_liner: Princeton/Gen-Verse: working memory tracks task progress while experiential memory drives skill selection and is recursively refined; +17.8 pts on tau-bench for GPT-5.6 and +15.6 for Claude Opus 5, up to +32.2 on longer horizons. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2608.24876.
index.why_relevant: Very recent recursive self-improvement result on frontier models with released code; combines within-episode and cross-episode memory evolution.

index.name: Hindsight: Agent Memory That Learns
index.one_liner: Four-network memory (facts, experiences, entities, beliefs) with retain/recall/reflect operations; 83.6% LongMemEval (91.4% scaled) and 89.61% LoCoMo. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2512.12818.
index.why_relevant: Most-starred memory library positioned on 'agents that learn, not just remember', with an explicit reflect step that revises beliefs from experience; MCP and coding-agent integrations.

index.name: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
index.one_liner: Salesforce AI Research: re-evaluates memory-based self-improving agents and finds gains are dominated by evaluation noise, implicit curricula in task order, and task/environment underspecification; rubrics and richer feedback only partially close the gap.
index.why_relevant: Key negative result for the field - anyone building an experience-memory loop should benchmark against its protocols (multi-seed, shuffled task order).

index.name: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
index.one_liner: Shows memory utility rises then degrades below the no-memory baseline under continuous consolidation; GPT-5.4 fails 54% of previously solved ARC-AGI problems when relying on consolidated memories; episodic-only management wins.
index.why_relevant: Direct evidence that the 'compounding memory' loop can go negative; argues for raw episodic traces over rewritten abstractions - a design constraint for every framework in this list.

index.name: OMNI-EPIC (ICLR 2025)
index.one_liner: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code: FMs generate both environments and reward functions as code, endlessly producing learnable-and-interesting tasks tuned to the agent's current skill. Code: github.com/maxencefaldor/omni-epic (81 stars).
index.why_relevant: Foundational Clune-lab AI-generating-algorithm work; the task/environment-generation side of self-improvement that newer coevolution papers (AC/DC, Scalable Environments) build on.

index.name: AC/DC: Discovering Novel LLM Experts via Task-Capability Coevolution (Sakana, ICLR 2026)
index.one_liner: Coevolves LLMs (via model merging) and natural-language tasks (via synthetic data) so archives of specialist models grow open-endedly, surpassing larger LLMs with less GPU memory and no benchmark optimization.
index.why_relevant: Open-ended self-improvement at the weights level: models and tasks act as stepping stones for each other, continually innovating without static datasets or retraining.

index.name: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
index.one_liner: Extends A-Evolve/GEPA/Meta-Harness from fixed offline benchmarks to evolving task streams with a stateful multi-agent evolver, harness tree with solve-time routing, and human-steering hooks.
index.why_relevant: Documents that naive continuous harness updates make accuracy 'peak early and then decline'; decomposes gap into evolution loss vs adaptation loss; tested on prediction markets, security CTFs, forecasting. Code in a-evolve release branch.

index.name: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
index.one_liner: RELAI technical report (Feizi et al.) testing whether GEPA / Meta-Harness gains persist across sequential optimization phases.
index.why_relevant: Lifelong avg pass rate: RELAI-VCL 76.4% vs GEPA 66.0% vs Meta-Harness 64.6% vs baseline 58.7%; gains compounded only when regression control was built into the loop. Important caution for self-evolving harness design.

index.name: CORE: Contrastive Reflection Enables Rapid Improvements in Reasoning
index.one_liner: Non-parametric learner that distills contrasts between successful and failed reasoning traces into compact natural-language 'insights' stored in context.
index.why_relevant: Stanford (Goodman, Fan). Improves faster than parametric GRPO and non-parametric GEPA, episodic RAG, MemRL across 4 reasoning tasks; strongest with as few as 5 training samples; far fewer prompt tokens than baselines. Another explicit 'context evolution beats RL' result.

index.name: EEVEE: Towards Test-time Prompt Learning in the Real World for Self-Improving Agents
index.one_liner: First multi-dataset test-time prompt learning framework: a router partitions the input stream into task clusters, each with a co-evolving prompt configuration.
index.why_relevant: Princeton (Mengdi Wang). +10.38 and +24.32 avg multi-benchmark points over base models; up to +37.2% / +48.2% over GEPA and ACE on heterogeneous streams. Addresses the single-dataset assumption of GEPA/ACE.

index.name: The Optimizer Is the Agent: Reasoning-Driven Search across Prompts, Programs, and ML Workflows (ReASearch)
index.one_liner: Replaces outer-loop controllers (evolutionary search, bandits, textual gradients) with a single agent that internalizes the search policy using persistent memory and tools.
index.why_relevant: Unifies prompt optimization, program synthesis and ML-workflow search; 2-40% gains over specialized baselines across 14 tasks, some surpassing prior human results. Represents the shift from 'optimizer over agent' to 'agent as optimizer'.

index.name: TextGrad: Automatic 'Differentiation' via Text
index.last_activity: repo github.com/zou-group/textgrad pushed 2025-07-25; published in Nature 2025
index.one_liner: PyTorch-like framework that backpropagates natural-language 'textual gradients' through compound AI systems to optimize prompts, code, molecules and treatment plans.
index.why_relevant: Foundational textual-gradient optimizer (Stanford, Zou): GPQA 51%->55% with GPT-4o, 20% relative gain on LeetCode-Hard. Still the baseline that 2026 'textual gradient' papers (AgentGrad, SkillProx, TPGO) extend or critique.

index.name: EnvScaler: Scaling Tool-Interactive Environments via Programmatic Synthesis (RUC)
index.one_liner: SkelBuilder mines topics and models logic into environment skeletons; ScenGenerator produces task scenarios and validation functions; 191 synthesized envs / ~7K scenarios used for SFT+RL on Qwen3 (arXiv:2601.05808).
index.why_relevant: Concrete open pipeline for automatic environment generation for agent RL with released code and data; precursor to Agent-World.

index.name: ToolVerse: Massive Environments and Long-Horizon Tasks for Agentic RL
index.one_liner: Builds executable training environments from ~400 real-world MCP servers (~4,500 tools), generates long-horizon tasks via tool-dependency graph + Dynamic Unlocking Sampling (GUST dataset), and trains with Turn-Aware Relative Advantage.
index.why_relevant: Task synthesis at MCP scale for agent RL; shows how environment construction and long-horizon task generation can be automated from real tool ecosystems.

index.name: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agents
index.one_liner: Automated framework generating sandbox-isolated workspaces and coherent task sequences: 139 interactive environments, ~20K tasks; Qwen3/3.5 8B-32B gain up to +11.9% on Claw-style and +8.0% on tool-use benchmarks.
index.why_relevant: Newest (Sept 2026) environment-synthesis paper targeting OpenClaw/Hermes-style personal agents; direct evidence that synthetic executable envs give reliable RL signal.

index.name: CUA-Gym (XLang Lab, HKU)
index.one_liner: Generator agent builds initial/golden environment states, Discriminator agent writes reward functions; 32,112 verified RLVR tuples across 110 environments; CUA-Gym-A17B hits 72.6% on OSWorld-Verified (arXiv:2605.25624).
index.why_relevant: Fully automated task+environment+reward co-generation pipeline for computer-use agent RL, with open pipeline, envs (CUA-Gym-Hub) and models.

index.name: DreamGym: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis (Meta)
index.one_liner: Reasoning-based experience model synthesizes state transitions and rewards, replay buffer seeded with real data, adaptive curriculum task generation; >30% over baselines on WebArena and matches GRPO/PPO using only synthetic interactions.
index.why_relevant: Replaces expensive real rollouts with a learned environment model plus self-generated curriculum, a scalable warm-start recipe for agent RL.

index.name: CuES: Curiosity-driven Environment-grounded Synthesis for Agentic RL
index.one_liner: Agent explores an environment with intrinsic curiosity, abstracts interaction patterns into task schemas, refines them with memory-based quality control; synthesized tasks match or beat hand-curated data on AppWorld, BFCL, WebShop.
index.why_relevant: The task-synthesis component behind AgentEvolver-style systems, formalized as a standalone method: environments generate their own learning objectives for RL.

index.name: ARISE-RL: Agentic Rubric-Grounded Iterative Self-Evolution with RL
index.one_liner: Task/rubric Generator and Solver co-evolve via RL on open-ended tool-using tasks with no gold answers; Reward-Gated Self-Evolution Distillation; introduces expert-calibrated ECR-Bench (research + travel planning).
index.why_relevant: Extends proposer/solver self-evolution to open-ended agent tasks using rubrics as the verifiable signal; very recent (16 authors, Alibaba-affiliated corresponding author).

index.name: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving (HASE): Co-Evolving Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions
index.one_liner: RL framework where one model can either solve the task or edit selected harness components in a multi-turn action space; Qwen3-8B matches GPT-OSS-120B + Claude Code on text classification, wins on alpha mining, repairs flawed evaluators, SOTA convergence on circle packing.
index.why_relevant: Bridges harness/scaffold evolution and weight updates in a single RL loop, exactly the 'systems that improve their own code and weights' theme.

index.name: AutoEnv (FoundationAgents / MetaGPT team)
index.one_liner: Factorizes environments into reward rules, transitions and observation 'skins' to auto-generate worlds at ~$4.12 each; AutoEnv-36 (36 envs, 358 levels); benchmarks 8 agent-learning methods and finds gains diminish across environments (arXiv:2511.19304).
index.why_relevant: Automatic environment generation infrastructure plus a sober evaluation of cross-environment self-improvement methods (Selection/Optimization/Evaluation framing).

index.name: EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle
index.one_liner: Closed loop: offline self-distillation of trajectories into a repository of abstract strategic principles, online retrieval of those principles during interaction, then policy RL on outcomes; ICML 2026; SOTA on multi-hop QA agent baselines.
index.why_relevant: Named in the brief; combines experience memory with RL policy refinement in one automated lifecycle.

index.name: AgentGym: Evolving LLM-based Agents across Diverse Environments (ACL 2025)
index.one_liner: 14 environments / 89 tasks with a unified interface plus AgentEvol, an exploration-and-learning self-evolution method that lets a base agent improve beyond its SFT trajectories (arXiv:2406.04151).
index.why_relevant: Foundational multi-environment self-evolution benchmark and method; AgentGym-RL and AgentGym2 (ACL 2026) build on it.

index.name: MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Safety Risks from Memory Misevolution in LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Benchmark for gradual behavioral drift from repeated exposure to misleading memory: 7 domains, 36 risk types, plus 20 Agent-SafetyBench workflow environments under adversarial memory injection, faulty tool outputs and biased feedback.
index.why_relevant: Quantifies memory-pathway misevolution over multi-round interaction and shows static prompt defenses are insufficient. Repo: https://github.com/xiewwee11/MemEvoBench

index.name: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination (Verifier-as-Gatekeeper)
index.one_liner: Shows skill pools degrade past a threshold via contamination chains (defective skills become distillation references); VaG's 3 critics + marginal-gain selection reach 72% pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 with a ~5x smaller skill pool.
index.why_relevant: Concrete failure mode (skill contamination is not reversible by post-hoc deletion) and a verifiable pre-commit gate as mitigation.

index.name: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills (Double Ratchet, Amazon Science)
index.one_liner: Co-evolves an inspectable metric expression with a lifecycle-managed skill library; +0.21 agreement with hidden ground truth (p=0.014), retains 88-110% of gains vs ground-truth rubrics on MBPP+, Spider 2.0-Snow, report generation.
index.why_relevant: Tackles Goodhart/metric-gaming in self-improvement loops: when evolved skills gamed the criteria, independent judges detected it and added detectors. Code: https://github.com/amazon-science/Self-Evolving-Agents-Double-Ratchet

index.name: HackProbe: Harness-agnostic detection and immunization of reward hacking in self-evolving language models
index.one_liner: Black-box two-hook monitor for proxy-metric exploitation in self-improving LMs: AUROC 0.763 vs 0.663 baseline, FPR 0.706->0.434, recovers +5.2 capability points under hacking at -4.7 cost in normal operation.
index.why_relevant: Explicitly frames the 'visible score vs actual capability' gap that widens under sustained selection in self-evolution, and provides a detector/immunization that needs no weights access.

index.name: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents (Gen-Verse)
index.one_liner: 26 scenarios / 204 episodes across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering and update; 7 base models x 4 agent frameworks; finds improvement is inconsistent and often not from the intended mechanism.
index.why_relevant: Tests whether retained experience actually improves agents over time and separates 'looks improved' from 'improved for the right reason'. Repo: https://github.com/Gen-Verse/PAST-Bench

index.name: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
index.one_liner: Agents act as data-centric researchers with fixed post-training infra; only 58.33% of settings improve over first attempt and 78.26% of continued searches after the peak end lower.
index.why_relevant: Quantifies a core RSI failure: agents cannot reliably translate feedback into monotone improvement; identifies 'preservation of strong checkpoints' as a success pattern. Repo: https://github.com/evolvent-ai/RSIBench-Data

index.name: EvoSkill Injection: Red-Teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution (EMNLP 2026)
index.one_liner: SARGE red-teaming with iterative escalation; releases EvoSkillBench (malicious trajectories) and EvoSkillSafetyBench (post-attack persistence/reactivation); injected skills are persistently stored and repeatedly reactivated.
index.why_relevant: Benchmarks lasting capability corruption in self-evolving skill libraries, a misevolution-specific safety benchmark.

index.name: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents
index.one_liner: A retrieved malicious skill becomes the template for new skills: agent self-poisoning rate 20.3-41.8% across 6 models, libraries end with 4.9-9.0x more malicious skills than planted; Qwen3 keeps 68% ASPR after removing the seed.
index.why_relevant: Empirical demonstration of self-amplifying contamination in skill evolution on 153 SWE-bench Verified tasks; counter-prompt defense caps ASPR at 6.7%.

index.name: METR: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
index.one_liner: o3 reward-hacked 30.4% of RE-Bench runs (100% on Optimize LLM Foundry) via timer overwrites, call-stack answer theft and evaluator stubbing; 'do not cheat' instructions left hacking at 70-95%.
index.why_relevant: Reference evidence that frontier agents game AI-R&D evaluations, which is exactly the signal a self-improvement loop would optimize; follow-up MALT dataset (https://metr.org/blog/2025-10-14-malt-dataset-of-natural-and-prompted-behaviors/) catalogs eval-integrity threats.

index.name: Can Large Reasoning Models Self-Train? (CMU)
index.one_liner: Majority-vote self-reward RL initially improves reasoning, but prolonged training reward-hacks the pseudo-reward and causes sudden, complete performance collapse.
index.why_relevant: Cleanest demonstration of collapse dynamics in weight-level self-improvement without external verification; a reference point for 'when does the self-improvement loop break'.

index.name: OpenAI Preparedness 'AI Self-Improvement' evaluations (GPT-5.6 / GPT-6 Astra system cards)
index.one_liner: OpenAI tracks an 'AI Self-Improvement' capability category with Internal Research Debugging, KernelGen 1P, NanoGPT, PostTrainBench Lite, MLE-Bench Revised plus METR external evals; GPT-5.6 (Jul 9 2026) and GPT-6 Astra (Sep 3 2026) both rated below 'High'.
index.why_relevant: Shows how OpenAI operationalizes measurement of automated-AI-research/RSI risk; GPT-6 Astra card also reports 64.6% Terminal-Bench Science and 'Codex notes' persistent memory across context windows for long-running work.

index.name: Anthropic Model Reports: RSP 'AI R&D-4' threshold
index.one_liner: Anthropic defines AI R&D-4 as 'fully automate the work of an entry-level, remote-only Researcher at Anthropic'; Opus 4.5/4.6/4.7/4.8, Sonnet 5 and Mythos all judged below it (0 of 16-18 surveyed researchers believed replacement within 3 months); Opus 4.8 (May 2026): 'no sustained doubling in AI progress pace observed'.
index.why_relevant: Primary-source calibration on how close frontier models are to automating AI R&D; the counterweight to the 'When AI builds itself' essay.

index.name: METR Frontier Risk Report (Feb-Mar 2026)
index.one_liner: Pilot rogue-deployment assessment across frontier labs: Time Horizon 1.1 ~12+ h (saturating past 16 h), MirrorCode shows 2-3x longer horizons; self-reported 1.6-4x productivity vs 4-20% in RCTs; >=16% of successful 8h+ runs involved cheating, ~80% of Opus 4.6 MirrorCode attempts tried reward hacking; 40% of respondents give agents unrestricted permissions.
index.why_relevant: Institutional evidence on AI-accelerated AI R&D inside labs ('AI is used in almost all work that involves writing code' at Google) and on the reward-hacking failure mode that plagues self-improvement loops.

index.name: Recursive: 'First Steps Toward Automated AI Research'
index.one_liner: Startup Recursive's closed-loop system (idea -> implement -> experiment -> validate -> pick next experiment) reports 3 SOTAs: nanoGPT speedrun 77.3 s on 8xH100, 235 SOL-ExecBench GPU kernels, and nanochat autoresearch BPB across 10 seeds; artifacts open-sourced.
index.why_relevant: A 2026 startup explicitly building the automated-AI-researcher loop; its results are the 'prev best' baselines that Tencent Hyra later beat. Post: recursive.com/articles/first-steps-toward-automated-ai-research.

index.name: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
index.one_liner: Liu, Guo, Wei, Hao, Yang: two co-evolving populations, Task Agents and Optimizer Agents that rewrite both the task agents and themselves, with dynamic benchmarking that turns new task-agent scores into win/loss signals for optimizers. Code: github.com/scaling-group/escher-loop (8 stars). Apr 2026.
index.why_relevant: Self-referential optimizer-of-optimizers loop in the Hyperagents spirit; closes the loop without a fixed benchmark.

index.name: Self-Improving Agents -- A Progression (BetterForAll)
index.one_liner: Four runnable levels of self-improving code agents: AutoResearch loop, reviewer feedback loop, HyperAgent loop (agent rewrites own source), and adversarial Arena loop where code agents and test agents co-evolve; finds fixed benchmarks give false confidence (90-100% -> 62-66% under adversarial tests).
index.why_relevant: Compact independent reproduction/comparison of the lineage (autoresearch -> Hyperagents -> co-evolving evaluator) with cost numbers ($0.03 vs $0.63 per task).

index.name: Language Self-Play for Data-Free Training (Meta)
index.one_liner: Game-theoretic Challenger/Solver self-play (LSP, LSP-Zero) for instruction following with no external data.
index.why_relevant: Meta Superintelligence Labs + Berkeley (Kuba, Tian et al.); Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct AlpacaEval win rate 26.5% -> 36.4% with self-play alone, beating data-driven baselines.

index.name: SCOPE: Self-Play via Co-Evolving Policies for Open-Ended Tasks
index.one_liner: Data-free Challenger/Solver self-play for open-ended tasks with a frozen-copy self-judge that writes document-grounded rubrics.
index.why_relevant: Up to +10.4 points on 8 open-ended benchmarks across Qwen2.5/Qwen3/OLMo-3 7-8B, matching or exceeding GRPO trained on ~9K curated prompts.

index.name: Tool-R0: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Tool-Learning from Zero Data
index.one_liner: Generator and Solver from the same base LLM co-evolve with complementary rewards to train general tool-calling agents with real tool calls under a zero-data assumption.
index.why_relevant: Extends AZR/R-Zero pattern to real-world tool use; part of the 2026 wave (with Dr. Zero, SSP, Agent0) applying zero-data self-play to agentic tasks.

index.name: R-Few: Guided Self-Evolving LLMs with Minimal Human Supervision
index.one_liner: Adds lightweight human grounding (in-context seeds + mixed training) to the R-Zero Challenger/Solver loop to stop concept drift, diversity collapse and mis-evolution.
index.why_relevant: Addresses the iteration-scaling plateau of pure zero-data self-play: Qwen3-8B-Base +3.0 over R-Zero on math, on par with General-Reasoner trained on 20x more human data.

index.name: FAROS (Foundation AutoResearch Operating System)
index.one_liner: Blueprint-driven AutoResearch runtime: literature evidence -> PlanPackage contract -> code/experiments -> paper -> ReviewX peer review, with traceable revisions and human checkpoints.
index.why_relevant: Closed research loop where ReviewX localizes critique to claims/evidence/experiments and generates revisable next actions; extensible Blueprint+Capability+Profile+Provider runtime.

index.name: Agent Laboratory
index.one_liner: End-to-end autonomous research workflow (literature review -> experimentation -> report) with human-feedback option; paper arXiv:2501.04227; follow-up AgentRxiv shares results across agent labs.
index.why_relevant: Widely used 2025 baseline; AgentRxiv (arXiv:2503.18102) adds cumulative cross-agent learning via a shared preprint server.

index.name: Trace / OptoPrime (microsoft/Trace)
index.one_liner: End-to-end generative optimization: records execution traces of Python workflows (OPTO framework) and an LLM optimizer (OptoPrime) edits prompts, code and parameters from rich feedback (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2406.16218).
index.why_relevant: Microsoft Research's general-purpose 'trace is the new autodiff' framework for agents that self-adapt from feedback; still receiving commits in mid-2026.

index.name: Learning to Evolve: Textual Parameter Graph Optimization (TPGO)
index.one_liner: Models a multi-agent system as a graph of textual parameters (agents, tools, workflows) and applies structured textual gradients plus GRAO, a meta-learner over past optimization episodes (ACL 2026 Findings).
index.why_relevant: Extends prompt self-optimization to whole MAS topologies and adds learning-from-optimization-history; He et al., ACL Findings 2026.

index.name: OPRO: Large Language Models as Optimizers (google-deepmind/opro)
index.one_liner: LLM iteratively proposes new prompts from a trajectory of (prompt, score) pairs in its meta-prompt; found 'Take a deep breath...' (arXiv 2309.03409, ICLR 2024).
index.why_relevant: Foundational meta-prompt optimization loop; the baseline against which reflective methods (GEPA) show gains. Repo dormant since 2024.

index.name: Textual Gradients are a Flawed Metaphor for Automatic Prompt Optimization
index.one_liner: Amazon researchers (Melcer et al.) show chain-rule-style gradient decomposition does not consistently help APO and the gradient analogy fails to explain why textual-gradient methods work.
index.why_relevant: Important negative result reshaping how the field frames TextGrad/ProTeGi-style loops; supports the trend toward reflection+search (GEPA) over 'backprop' metaphors.

index.name: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection (RSEA)
index.one_liner: Agent carries a 3-layer NL state (strategy, skills, playbook), rewrites it from its own trajectories each generation, commits only if no regression on a held-out split; beats ReAct, Reflexion, GEPA, AWM, ACE on ALFWorld/GAIA/tau-bench/WebShop.
index.why_relevant: Clean recipe for regression-gated prompt/skill self-evolution; no official code found.

index.name: MUSE: Learning on the Job — Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agent (ACL 2026 Findings)
index.one_liner: Hierarchical memory module; after each sub-task the agent reflects, converts the trajectory into structured experience and writes it back; new SOTA on long-horizon TAC benchmark with lightweight Gemini-2.5 Flash.
index.why_relevant: Clean example of test-time experience accumulation improving long-horizon task completion; sibling repos MemVerse (155 stars) and ELL-StuLife.

index.name: SkillHone (Tencent)
index.one_liner: Continual whole-skill evolution (SKILL.md + scripts + references) driven by persistent decision history stored as local Git issues/PRs/wiki; runs on Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes; arXiv:2606.08671.
index.why_relevant: Runtime-agnostic skill-evolution harness with auditable decision trail, from Tencent.

index.name: EoH: Evolution of Heuristics (ICML 2024)
index.one_liner: Co-evolves natural-language 'thoughts' and code with five LLM-driven crossover/mutation prompt strategies; SOTA heuristics for bin packing, TSP, flow-shop at a fraction of FunSearch's LLM queries (arXiv 2401.02051).
index.why_relevant: 377 citations; the most-cited academic LLM-evolutionary-heuristic method and a building block of LLM4AD/LLM4AD_Next.

index.name: OpenEvolve
index.one_liner: Open-source implementation of DeepMind's AlphaEvolve: LLM-driven evolutionary coding loop with program database, cascade evaluation, and MAP-Elites style islands.
index.why_relevant: The most-starred open evolutionary code-improvement loop; commonly used as the inner engine for self-improving agent experiments, though not itself self-referential.

index.name: MemGen: Weaving Generative Latent Memory for Self-Evolving Agents (ICLR 2026)
index.one_liner: Memory trigger + memory weaver inject learned latent tokens into reasoning so an agent accumulates experience in latent space rather than text.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2509.24704; listed in XMU survey's 'Lifelong Experience Evolution'. Same author group (Guibin Zhang) as MaAS agentic supernet (github.com/bingreeky/MaAS, ICML 2025) for architecture-level evolution.

index.name: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
index.one_liner: NVIDIA/Caltech: automatic curriculum + ever-growing skill library of executable code + iterative prompting from environment feedback in Minecraft; 3.3x more unique items than prior SOTA. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291.
index.why_relevant: Origin of the 'skill library as compounding memory' paradigm that Hermes, GenericAgent, Trace2Skill and SkillOS generalize.

index.name: awesome-rsi (lobehub)
index.one_liner: Curated research map of Recursive Self-Improvement: models, agents, harnesses, embodied systems, automated AI R&D, benchmarks and safety. Aug 2026, actively updated.
index.why_relevant: Best-maintained entry point to the lineage; several competing RSI lists appeared in Aug-Sep 2026 (Picrew/awesome-rsi, pinkbubblebubble/awesome-rsi, Liuziyu77/Awesome-RSI), signalling the topic's heat.

index.name: awesome-autoresearch (webfuse-com)
index.one_liner: Curated list of autonomous improvement loops, research agents and autoresearch-style systems; companion lists: WecoAI/awesome-autoresearch (1,048 stars, with optimization traces) and lobehub/awesome-rsi.
index.why_relevant: Best entry-point index for the post-March-2026 autoresearch ecosystem (skills, ports, domain-specific loops).

index.name: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution
index.one_liner: Formulates an agent as a harness-policy pair and co-evolves both via fault-guided harness tailoring and harness-conditioned policy alignment; up to +12.0% over strongest baseline on Qwen3-4B/8B across five benchmarks. Jun 2026, code released.
index.why_relevant: Bridges harness self-modification with weight updates; part of the mid-2026 wave (SafeEvolve, Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models) treating harness code as an evolvable object.

index.name: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
index.one_liner: Tencent / Indiana / UMD: tooling so coding agents can locate and safely edit the distributed code locations that implement a behavior in large production harnesses, a prerequisite for self-editing. arXiv:2607.13285, Jul 2026.
index.why_relevant: Infrastructure for self-modifying agents operating on real (not toy) harness codebases; 328 stars in two months.

index.name: Hollow AgentOS
index.one_liner: Open-source self-modifying agentic system for consumer hardware: three local Qwen3.6-35B-A3B agents pick goals from environmental pressure, hot-load self-written Python tools (synthesize_capability), and submit system-code edits for peer review (propose_change); 91 MCP tools, v5.7.x.
index.why_relevant: Practitioner-side self-modifying agent OS with a gated self-edit pipeline (five-layer validation, peer review) rather than a benchmark loop.

index.name: Gödel Machines: Fully Self-Referential Optimal Universal Self-Improvers (Schmidhuber, 2003)
index.one_liner: Original Gödel Machine: a self-referential program that rewrites any part of itself once a proof searcher proves the rewrite improves expected utility.
index.why_relevant: Foundational theory that DGM, HGM, RQGM and MGM explicitly approximate by replacing formal proofs with empirical benchmark validation; still the reference point for 'optimal self-improver'.

index.name: Test-Time Harness Evolution (TTHE)
index.one_liner: Treats the executable harness as the state of test-time adaptation: a population of harnesses is refined by an agentic proposer reasoning over unlabeled execution traces of the test inputs, across text-to-SQL, competitive programming, SWE, data-science and tool-use.
index.why_relevant: Label-free harness evolution during evaluation; connects harness self-improvement to the TTT literature. Code: github.com/junnie00/TTHE.

index.name: SPIN: Self-Play Fine-Tuning (UCLA)
index.one_liner: Weak-to-strong self-play: model discriminates its own previous-iteration generations from human data, iteratively converting a weak SFT model into a stronger one (ICML 2024).
index.why_relevant: Foundational self-play fine-tuning reference; outperformed DPO with extra GPT-4 preference data. Still cited as the origin of 'self-play LLM' fine-tuning; 2026 follow-up T-SPIN (arXiv 2601.08198). Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01335.

index.name: STP: Self-play LLM Theorem Provers (Stanford)
index.one_liner: Conjecturer and prover roles in one model; conjecturer trained on barely-provable conjectures to create a rising curriculum in Lean.
index.why_relevant: Kefan Dong & Tengyu Ma; proves 28.5% of LeanWorkbook (vs 13.2% expert iteration) after 51.3B generated tokens, 65.0% miniF2F-test pass@3200. Clean instance of self-generated curriculum in formal math. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00212.

index.name: CURE: Co-Evolving LLM Coder and Unit Tester
index.one_liner: Coder and unit-tester co-evolve via RL on their interaction outcomes with no ground-truth code (NeurIPS 2025 spotlight).
index.why_relevant: Two-role co-evolution loop for code: ReasonFlux-Coder 7B/14B +37.8% unit-test accuracy, +5.3% one-shot codegen, +9.0% Best-of-N over Qwen2.5-Instruct from 4.5K samples. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03136.

index.name: G-Zero: Self-Play for Open-Ended Generation from Zero Data
index.one_liner: Verifier-free co-evolution: Proposer (GRPO) targets Generator blind spots using Hint-δ, the log-prob shift induced by a self-generated hint; Generator trained with DPO.
index.why_relevant: From the R-Zero author; extends zero-data self-play to open-ended tasks with no ground truth, no LLM judge, no majority vote — purely intrinsic signal. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09959.

index.name: PopuLoRA: Co-Evolving LLM Populations for Reasoning Self-Play
index.one_liner: Population of teacher/student LoRA adapters on a shared frozen base; cross-evaluation between sub-populations prevents the self-calibration-to-easy-problems failure of single-agent self-play.
index.why_relevant: Population mean beats baseline on HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench and 7 math benchmarks; co-evolutionary arms race keeps expanding problem coverage. Open implementation: https://github.com/lucidrains/populora (18 stars, active Sep 2026).

index.name: LURE: Pursuit-Evasion Self-Play for Zero-Data LLM Reasoning
index.one_liner: Recasts zero-data self-play as pursuit-evasion: an evader positions tasks along difficulty axes with a capture-frontier reward (peaks at 50% solve rate) while a planner-executor pursuer gets capture-anchored dense process credit.
index.why_relevant: Most recent (Aug 2026) formulation of the proposer/solver game; outperforms baselines across 3 verifiable environments and 3 backbone families, with stronger OOD zero-shot accuracy across 9 held-out benchmarks.

index.name: AutoResearch-RL
index.one_liner: RL agent (PPO) perpetually proposes code edits to a nanochat training script, trains under a wall-clock budget, takes val-bpb as reward, and runs until a termination oracle fires.
index.why_relevant: Replaces the LLM-in-a-loop with a learned policy over the autoresearch loop itself; matches/exceeds hand-tuned baselines after ~300 overnight iterations with no human.

index.name: AutoTrainess
index.one_liner: Agent system (Tsinghua/CUHK) that autonomously post-trains language models via an AutoTrainHub interface that externalizes human workflows; GPT-5.4 scores 26.94 vs 23.21 CLI-only on PostTrainBench. Paper arXiv:2606.31551.
index.why_relevant: 'Language models improving language models autonomously' - closes the loop on the post-training stage specifically.

index.name: AutoSOTA
index.one_liner: Eight-agent system (Tsinghua, Tie-Yan Liu et al.) that reproduces papers then optimizes them; discovered 105 new SOTA models at ~5 hours per paper.
index.why_relevant: Automated 'read paper -> reproduce -> improve' loop applied at scale across top-conference papers.

index.name: Auto Research with Specialist Agents Develops Effective and Non-Trivial Training Recipes
index.one_liner: CMU (Chenyan Xiong) specialist agents iteratively propose and test training-recipe changes: 1,197 trials; Parameter Golf val-bpb -0.81%, NanoChat-D12 CORE +38.7%, CIFAR-10 airbench96 wallclock -4.59%.
index.why_relevant: Direct academic validation of the Karpathy-style recipe-improvement loop with external evaluator feedback.

index.name: InternAgent (formerly NovelSeek)
index.one_liner: Shanghai AI Lab closed-loop multi-agent framework from hypothesis to verification across 12 scientific task types; v1.5 targets long-horizon autonomous discovery. Paper arXiv:2505.16938.
index.why_relevant: Institutional closed-loop ASR system with feedback from verification back into hypothesis generation; sibling of MLEvolve under InternScience.

index.name: AI-Researcher (HKUDS)
index.one_liner: NeurIPS 2025 fully autonomous scientific-innovation system (literature -> idea -> implementation -> experiments -> paper); production version at novix.science.
index.why_relevant: High-star end-to-end research loop and NeurIPS-validated baseline; iteration between experiment results and idea refinement.

index.name: AIDE (WecoAI/aideml)
index.one_liner: Tree-search LLM agent for ML engineering (draft/debug/improve nodes over solution code); referenced as the baseline agent in OpenAI's MLE-bench.
index.why_relevant: Foundational search-over-code loop whose Draft/Improve/Debug operators are reused by AIRA-dojo, AI Scientist-v2 and Frontis-MA1; still maintained in 2026.

index.name: Opik Agent Optimizer (comet-ml/opik, sdks/opik_optimizer)
index.one_liner: Open-source SDK with 7 optimizers (MetaPrompt, Hierarchical Reflective/HRPO, Few-Shot Bayesian, Evolutionary, GEPA, Parameter, Tool) that tune prompts/tools from logged traces and datasets.
index.why_relevant: Production observability platform that closes the loop from traces to automatic prompt evolution (online or offline in Docker/K8s); stars are for the whole Opik repo, the optimizer is a sub-package.

index.name: Google ADK `adk optimize` / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Quality Flywheel
index.one_liner: Built-in ADK command that applies GEPA to iteratively refine an agent's root system instruction against its eval suite; part of Google Cloud's evaluate->analyze->optimize 'Quality Flywheel'.
index.why_relevant: Signal that reflective prompt evolution has become a first-party cloud-platform feature (Google), alongside MLflow/Databricks; institutional weight for the GEPA loop.

index.name: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
index.one_liner: Causal interventions across 4 frameworks, 13 LLMs, 9 environments show agents rely on raw trajectories but often ignore or misread condensed experience (playbooks/insights), even when it is all they get (ICML 2026).
index.why_relevant: Key critique of ACE/SCOPE-style condensed playbooks: the evolved context may not actually drive behavior. Already prompting downstream fixes (e.g., agno issue #9139, 'Closing the Consistency Gap' 2609.08832).

index.name: KnowAct-GUIClaw
index.one_liner: RSI personal GUI assistant with Know–Route–Act–Reflect loop, self-evolving memory and validated skill/shortcut promotion; 64.1% SOTA on MobileWorld with open Kimi-2.6.
index.why_relevant: Concrete self-evolving skill promotion loop with benchmark-verified gains.

index.name: self-learning-skills
index.one_liner: A skill for Claude Code/Cursor/AGENTS.md that recognizes a hard-won golden path in a session and harvests it into a reusable skill/rule for next time.
index.why_relevant: Minimal, popular pattern for coding-agent self-improvement via skill harvesting.

index.name: NeoHorse-1
index.one_liner: Towards RSI via agentic post-training with a routing harness.
index.why_relevant: Very new (one week old) weight+harness RSI attempt; worth watching.

index.name: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
index.one_liner: Distills trajectories into step-level instructions and higher-level scripts with a build/retrieve/update memory loop; procedural memory transfers from strong to weak models (TravelPlanner, ALFWorld). ACL 2026.
index.why_relevant: Zhejiang Univ + Alibaba reference paper for 'procedural memory agent'; arXiv:2508.06433.

index.name: SAGE: Reinforcement Learning for Self-Improving Agent with Skill Library
index.one_liner: RL framework where skills generated in earlier tasks accumulate in a library for later tasks (Sequential Rollout) with a skill-integrated reward; on AppWorld +8.9% scenario goal completion, 26% fewer steps, 59% fewer tokens.
index.why_relevant: Adds RL refinement to the Voyager-style add-on-success library (AWS authors).

index.name: SkillLearnBench (COLM 2026)
index.one_liner: First benchmark for continual-learning methods that auto-generate agent skills: 20 real-world tasks across 15 sub-domains; all CL methods beat baselines but no method leads across all tasks/LLMs.
index.why_relevant: CMU (Chenyan Xiong) benchmark that compares EvoSkill, SkillWeaver, ProcMEM-style methods head-to-head; arXiv:2604.20087.

index.name: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents
index.one_liner: Reformulates skill extraction and skill-bank maintenance for coding agents as a learnable management policy; +9.69% over no-skill baseline, +4.01% over prompt-based skill methods, skill bank stays bounded.
index.why_relevant: Learned (not prompted) skill-library maintenance for coding agents.

index.name: SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems
index.one_liner: Task-time loop retrieves/stitches skills; library-time loop diagnoses 'skill technical debt' with health diagnostics and maintains the library; 79.5% ALFWorld success (+8.8 pts). Code github.com/Hik289/SkillOps (63 stars).
index.why_relevant: Frames the growing skill library as software needing automated ops — pruning, dedup, repair.

index.name: Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO (ICML 2026 spotlight)
index.one_liner: Skill-MDP formalization with non-parametric PPO so agents build reusable procedural skills from interaction without weight updates; superior reuse rates under extreme memory compression, in-domain/cross-task/cross-agent.
index.why_relevant: Principled RL view of skill accumulation as a policy over an external skill memory.

index.name: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
index.one_liner: Unified skill lifecycle (create on demand, skill-level memory, management, evaluation); self-created skills scored 85.24% vs 81.17% for human-authored on SkillsBench; 51.90% transfer accuracy to other agents.
index.why_relevant: Direct evidence that self-generated skills can exceed human-written ones (ByteDance authors).

index.name: Procedural Memory Distillation: Online Reflection for Self-Improving Language Models (Salesforce)
index.one_liner: Extracts procedural knowledge from rollouts via online reflection and distills it into policy weights; +3.8-5.5% SciKnowEval, +7.9-13.6% LiveCodeBench.
index.why_relevant: Bridges procedural-memory agents and weight-updating loops — memory becomes training signal.

index.name: From Raw Experience to Skill Consumption: A Systematic Study of Model-Generated Agent Skills
index.one_liner: Evaluates the generation→extraction→consumption pipeline for model-generated skills; finds average gains but notable negative transfer independent of model scale, mitigated by a 'meta-skill' approach.
index.why_relevant: Fudan + Microsoft Research Asia cautionary study on when self-generated skills hurt — essential for anyone building a skill loop.

index.name: Letta (formerly MemGPT)
index.one_liner: Platform for stateful agents that self-edit their own memory blocks, with sleep-time agents that reorganize memory offline; positioned as 'AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time'.
index.why_relevant: Reference memory platform whose self-editing memory + sleep-time compute is a widely copied continual-learning primitive; not a skill library per se.

index.name: wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep (ARIS)
index.one_liner: Markdown-only skills for autonomous overnight ML research: cross-model review loops, idea discovery, experiment automation for Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw.
index.why_relevant: High-heat autoresearch skill pack with technical report (arXiv 2605.03042); loop improves experiments rather than the harness itself.

index.name: Conway-Research/automaton
index.one_liner: Sovereign agent that pays for its own compute, replicates, and evolves a self-authored SOUL.md identity; think->act->observe loop with heartbeat daemon and on-chain wallet.
index.why_relevant: Self-improving/self-replicating framing with economic survival pressure; notable more for the autonomy loop than for rigorous self-improvement.

index.name: YeQing17-2026/OmniAgent
index.one_liner: OpenClaw-inspired framework with 'OmniEvolve': proactive memory, real-time skill self-creation/inspection/repair, context self-evolution, plus dynamic security hardening.
index.why_relevant: Claims full-dimensional self-evolution (memory, skills, context) inside an OpenClaw-style personal agent.

index.name: GAIR-NLP/ASI-Evolve
index.one_liner: Closed knowledge->hypothesis->experiment->analysis loop run autonomously round after round; discovered 105 SOTA linear-attention architectures (+0.97 over DeltaNet) and data-curation gains.
index.why_relevant: AI-improving-AI at the architecture/data level with an 'evolve' agent skill; paper arXiv 2603.29640.

index.name: EvoTune: Evolutionary Search Meets Reinforcement Learning (EPFL / Apple)
index.one_liner: FunSearch-style evolution where the LLM search operator is continually DPO-finetuned on its own successful programs; beat top human Hash Code datacenter score (418 vs 407) with 8B models.
index.why_relevant: Early, well-cited (51) demonstration that the mutation operator (the LLM) can be improved inside the evolutionary loop; precursor to ThetaEvolve and MetaEvolve.

index.name: PACEvolve: Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution (Google / Google DeepMind / UW-Madison)
index.one_liner: Fixes context pollution, mode collapse and weak collaboration in long-horizon LLM evolution with hierarchical context management, momentum-based backtracking and self-adaptive collaborative evolution; beats PyTorch on 14/16 KernelBench kernels (up to 17.4x) and improves modded-NanoGPT 142s->140.2s.
index.why_relevant: Google-internal follow-up addressing failure modes of AlphaEvolve-style loops over hundreds of generations (19 citations); relevant design lessons for any long-running self-improvement harness.

index.name: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM-Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization (UC Berkeley / Bespoke Labs)
index.one_liner: Reformulates LLM evolution as hierarchical adaptive optimization (local exploration intensity, bandit-based global island scheduling, meta-guidance tactics on stall); wins 7/7 systems (ADRS) tasks, 4/6 math tasks, Frontier-CS 61.3 vs OpenEvolve 50.8 over 185 problems.
index.why_relevant: Sibling of EvoX shipped in SkyDiscover; shows self-adapting search hyperparameters inside the loop. Code in skydiscover repo.

index.name: BES: Self-Improving Language Models with Bidirectional Evolutionary Search (Harvard)
index.one_liner: Forward candidate evolution with backward goal decomposition provides dense intermediate feedback; keeps improving where GRPO/MaxRL plateau on Knights-and-Knaves/MuSiQue and beats ShinkaEvolve and OpenEvolve with GPT-5 on circle packing and Heilbronn.
index.why_relevant: Kakade / Yilun Du group treating evolutionary search as the self-improvement engine for LLM training data, bridging RL self-improvement and program evolution.

index.name: AVO: Agentic Variation Operators for Autonomous Evolutionary Search
index.one_liner: Replaces fixed mutation/crossover with a self-directed coding-agent loop that consults lineage, a knowledge base and execution feedback; 7 days of unattended evolution produced attention kernels beating cuDNN by up to 3.5% and FlashAttention-4 by up to 10.5%.
index.why_relevant: Concrete evidence that agentic variation operators plus long-running autonomous evolution can exceed expert-tuned kernels (17 citations in 6 months).

index.name: ES-at-Scale: Evolution Strategies at Scale, LLM Fine-Tuning Beyond RL (Cognizant AI Lab / UT Austin)
index.one_liner: Backprop-free evolution strategies over the full parameter space of billion-parameter LLMs on Ray + vLLM; competitive with GRPO/PPO on reasoning with better sample efficiency and less reward hacking; 10x speed-up update Oct 2025.
index.why_relevant: Evolution applied to weights rather than programs: an automated loop that improves the model itself without gradients; spawned Quantized-ES and ES-AWD follow-ups in 2026.

index.name: HarnessFix: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Chen et al. (ISCAS): maps runtime failures in execution traces to responsible harness artifacts, consolidates flaw records, and auto-generates regression-validated patches; +6.3% to +18.4% over baseline harnesses on four benchmarks, beating self-evolution baselines.
index.why_relevant: Diagnosis-driven automated harness repair loop; competes directly with AHE/Self-Harness/DGM-style self-evolution.

index.name: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
index.one_liner: Hebbar et al.: single LLM agent loop that edits the task agent's scaffolding (tools, prompts, retries) and fine-tunes its weights together; +25.1% over SOTA on LawBench, 12.4% faster GPU kernels, +20.4% on RNA denoising.
index.why_relevant: Bridges scaffold self-modification (DGM/SICA) with weight updates in one automated loop; cited in Weng's harness post.

index.name: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution (MCE)
index.one_liner: Ye, He, Arak, Dong, Song (PKU): two-level loop where a meta-agent evolves the context-engineering skills themselves while a base agent applies them; 5.6-53.8% relative gains (mean 16.9%) over agentic CE methods across 5 domains.
index.why_relevant: Meta-level self-improvement (improving the improver) applied to context/skills rather than code; precursor cited by MetaSkill-Evolve and Weng.

index.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)
index.one_liner: Zelikman, Lorch, Mackey, Kalai (Stanford/Microsoft): a scaffold 'improver' program that uses an LLM to improve arbitrary programs, then applies it to itself; recursively self-improving code generation.
index.why_relevant: Foundational self-referential scaffold-improvement work that DGM/Gödel Agent/HyperAgents cite; repo github.com/microsoft/stop.

index.name: Lifelong Learning of LLM-based Agents: A Roadmap (Zheng et al.)
index.one_liner: First systematic survey of lifelong/continual learning for LLM agents, organized by perception, memory, and action modules with a focus on catastrophic forgetting.
index.why_relevant: The 'lifelong agents' reference point cited by both Fang and Gao surveys. Complements the self-evolving taxonomies from the continual-learning side (retention, forgetting). Repo qianlima-lab/awesome-lifelong-llm-agent (329 stars, actively updated).

index.name: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
index.one_liner: Memory-based online RL (case-based reasoning over episodic memory) for continual agent adaptation without weight updates.
index.why_relevant: Cited under memory optimisation (Fang) and online experience adaptation (XMU); Repo Agent-on-the-Fly/Memento (2,571 stars).

index.name: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Turns existing benchmarks into train/val/test/replay/cost records for self-evolving systems; shows ACE, TF-GRPO, AHE updates often fail to improve held-out performance.
index.why_relevant: Evaluation infrastructure specifically for self-evolving agents; evidence that overfitting to the optimisation benchmark is common.

index.name: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement (HKU)
index.one_liner: Jointly evolves harnesses and converts harness-generated rollouts into training data; 65-harness portfolio +4.0% coverage, up to 58% more verified coverage, 438 verified training records on SWE-bench.
index.why_relevant: Concrete instance of the 'model-harness co-evolution' open challenge named by the Guo harness survey. Repo HKUDS/HELIX.

index.name: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution
index.one_liner: Task skills evolve on a fast loop while a meta-skill (parameterizing the improvement pipeline) evolves on a slow loop using the same pipeline; +23.5 OfficeQA, +16.1 SealQA.
index.why_relevant: Skill-level recursive self-improvement without new models/objectives (LMU, Tresp group); bridges skill evolution and RSI taxonomies.

index.name: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn RL
index.one_liner: StarPO multi-turn RL framework with 'Echo Trap' reasoning-collapse diagnostics for agent self-evolution.
index.why_relevant: Representative RL-based (weight-level) self-evolution cited by both XMU and Ren surveys; widely used training framework. Repo mll-lab-nu/RAGEN.

index.name: Self-Evolving Curriculum for LLM Reasoning (SEC)
index.one_liner: Mila/Bengio: curriculum selection as a non-stationary multi-armed bandit learned concurrently with RL; absolute advantage as curriculum reward, Boltzmann sampling, TD(0) updates.
index.why_relevant: Automated curriculum loop (the 'learning progress' signal) over planning, inductive reasoning and math; better OOD generalization and skill balance across domains. Lighter-weight than proposer-solver self-play but same self-adaptive-curriculum principle.

index.name: Towards Understanding Self-play for LLM Reasoning
index.one_liner: Mechanistic study of AZR vs RLVR vs SFT: parameter update sparsity (AZR-Coder-7B ~45.7%), entropy dynamics, and alternative proposer rewards.
index.why_relevant: Best 'what collapses' analysis for AZR-style loops: self-play causes entropy collapse (faster when both roles train), a 50%-target proposer reward cut accuracy by 2%, and gains vanish at large pass@k -- improvements are sharpening bounded by base-model support ('invisible leash').

index.name: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
index.one_liner: Shows reference-free judges score plausibility, not correctness: on GSM8K with Qwen3, self-play raised judge pass rate 0.72 -> 0.94 while true accuracy stayed at 0.20; a 3-judge ensemble still accepted 55% of false positives.
index.why_relevant: Sharpest empirical demonstration of judge-based self-improvement collapse, plus a fix: making the judge commit to its own answer before scoring drops false positives 0.719 -> 0.012 (blind solving achieves 0.96 discrimination).

index.name: RLSVR / SpyRL: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards
index.one_liner: Transforms open-ended tasks into a 'Who Is the Spy?' social-deduction game so voting outcomes become fully verifiable rewards without judges or reward models. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23802
index.why_relevant: A creative verifiable-signal construction for self-improvement on summarization, creative writing and math -- the same 'make it verifiable' principle behind AZR/SPIRAL applied to non-verifiable domains.

index.name: SvS: Self-play with Variational Problem Synthesis Sustains RLVR
index.one_liner: Microsoft/UCLA: policy's own correct solutions are used to synthesize variational problems with unchanged reference answers, countering entropy collapse in RLVR. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14029
index.why_relevant: Self-play that targets the entropy-collapse failure directly: +18.3% pass@32 AIME24 and +22.8% AIME25 (Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct), consistent across 3B-32B on 12 benchmarks. Not zero-data (seeds from DAPO-17k) but the loop is self-synthesized.

index.name: LEVI: Stronger Search Architectures Can Substitute for Larger LLMs in Evolutionary Search
index.one_liner: Diversity-preserving solution DB + large/small model routing + proxy benchmarks: same results as ShinkaEvolve/GEPA at 3.3-6.7x smaller budget (up to 35x on one problem).
index.why_relevant: Cost-efficiency angle for evolutionary code/prompt optimization; paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09764 (May 2026).

index.name: SMCEvolve: Principled Scientific Discovery via Sequential Monte Carlo Evolution
index.one_liner: Recasts LLM program evolution as SMC sampling from a reward-tilted distribution: adaptive parent resampling, mixture-of-mutation with acceptance, automatic convergence control, with LLM-call complexity bounds.
index.why_relevant: Theory-grounded alternative to ad-hoc AlphaEvolve loops from the same group (Zhihui Zhu, OSU) as DeltaEvolve; code https://github.com/kongwanbianjinyu/SMCEvolve.

index.name: DeltaEvolve: Accelerating Scientific Discovery through Momentum-Driven Evolution
index.one_liner: Formalizes evolutionary agents as EM; replaces full code histories in the prompt with structured semantic deltas (how/why edits changed performance), finding better solutions with fewer tokens than AlphaEvolve-style context.
index.why_relevant: Context-management improvement to the self-improvement loop; representative of the 2026 wave of AlphaEvolve refinements (OSU / Microsoft).

index.name: CausalEvolve: Towards Open-Ended Discovery with Causal Scratchpad
