index.one_liner: Adds a causal scratchpad to evolve-style agents: identifies outcome-level factors and surprise patterns in past experiments to propose targeted evolution directions; more efficient on 4 open-ended scientific tasks.
index.why_relevant: Knowledge-organization layer on top of AlphaEvolve (CMU / HKBU / Sydney, Kun Zhang group); addresses the 'why did this mutation help' gap in program evolution.

index.name: epsilon-MemEvo: Adaptive Cross-Task Memory Transfer for LLM Program Evolution
index.one_liner: Stores task-agnostic natural-language 'tactic memories' from past evolution runs and gates their injection to avoid negative transfer: +8.7% mean over AdaEvolve on 8 benchmarks, +9.4% faster early convergence, <1% overhead.
index.why_relevant: Evolution loop that accumulates reusable memory across tasks, i.e. the harness improves itself over time rather than restarting per problem.

index.name: Mutation Without Variation: Convergence Dynamics in LLM-Driven Program Evolution
index.one_liner: Selection-free LLM mutation chains collapse into attractor regions: in 87% of chains >93% of mutations revisit previously seen structures; does not happen with classical GP.
index.why_relevant: Important negative result about LLMs as evolutionary operators (Northwestern, Wilensky); explains why novelty-rejection (ShinkaEvolve) and diversity training (VPO) matter. Code: https://github.com/can-gurkan/lmca

index.name: K-Search: LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model (Berkeley)
index.one_liner: Replaces static kernel-search heuristics with a world model that co-evolves with the search; avg 2.10x and up to 14.3x on FlashInfer kernels, GPUMode TriMul 1030us on H100.
index.why_relevant: Kernel-optimization line of LLM evolutionary search (Gonzalez/Stoica) where the search guidance itself is learned during the loop.

index.name: LLM-Guided Program Evolution for Circle Packing: Breaking 10 Packomania Records for $28 (Discovery Loop)
index.one_liner: Single-author loop where an LLM iteratively rewrites a solver using metrics and history; beat 10 Packomania records (N=101-114, +2.4-5.4%) in 15 iterations for $27.72.
index.why_relevant: Freshest (Sept 2026) evidence that cheap subscription-backed evolutionary loops now break long-standing benchmark records; code https://github.com/ucsandman/discovery-loop.

index.name: Effective Harness Engineering for Algorithm Discovery with Coding Agents (Vesper)
index.one_liner: NEC study of harness design for evolutionary algorithm discovery: fewer, deeper candidates beat many shallow ones at fixed token budget; stronger models produce more evaluation hacks; safe parallel FS execution.
index.why_relevant: Practical harness-engineering guidance (quality vs quantity, reward hacking, sandboxing) for anyone building an AlphaEvolve-style loop on top of coding agents.

index.name: EvoPrompt: Connecting LLMs with Evolutionary Algorithms Yields Powerful Prompt Optimizers
index.one_liner: LLM implements mutation and crossover over a prompt population (GA and DE variants); up to +25% on BBH over human prompts; ICLR 2024.
index.why_relevant: Foundational 'LLM as evolutionary operator' work for prompts; the ancestor of GEPA, E-SPL and evolutionary system-prompt learning.

index.name: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Alternates HarnessCritic-driven harness edits (diagnosing systematic failures) with fine-tuning on trajectories from the improved harness; 200+ hour autonomous case study.
index.why_relevant: Extends the evolutionary loop to jointly evolve scaffolding and weights; complements AEVO and E-SPL on the harness-evolution axis.

index.name: Tencent AI Lab SelfEvolvingAgent (WebEvolver / WebCoT)
index.one_liner: Tencent AI Lab code for WebEvolver (EMNLP 2025): a web agent self-improves with a co-evolving LLM world model that synthesizes trajectories and enables look-ahead.
index.why_relevant: WebEvolver arXiv:2504.21024 is the reference 'co-evolving world model' self-improvement loop for web agents; also WebCoT (arXiv:2505.20013). Links to Tencent's Cognitive Kernel-Pro agent foundation model training.

index.name: EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle (Shanghai AI Lab, ICML 2026)
index.one_liner: Closed-loop lifecycle: offline distillation of trajectories into strategic principles, online use of those principles, then policy reinforcement on outcomes.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2510.16079 (Botian Shi, Pinlong Cai, Licheng Wen). Concrete experience -> principle -> RL loop; sister project MUSE (ACL 2026 Findings, 'Learning on the Job', github.com/KnowledgeXLab/MUSE, 101 stars) applies it to long-horizon TAC tasks.

index.name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent (Shanghai AI Lab / SJTU, ICML 2026)
index.one_liner: Computer-use agent that learns unseen software autonomously via a World State Model judge, curriculum generator and GRPO on its own failures/successes.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2508.04700; experience-driven self-evolution on OSWorld with specialist-to-generalist distillation. Listed in ANative-Lab survey under domain-specific self-evolution.

index.name: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: On Path to ASI + CharlesQ9/Self-Evolving-Agents list
index.one_liner: Survey arXiv:2507.21046 (Gao, Geng, Qiu, Mengdi Wang et al.) organized by what/when/how/where to evolve, with a 150+ paper list.
index.why_relevant: Second canonical taxonomy (models / context: memory+prompt / tools / architecture; intra- vs inter-test-time; reward-, imitation-, population-based). Lists WebRL, Mobile-Agent-E, Voyager, Gödel Agent, AlphaEvolve, DGM, SEAL, TTRL, RAGEN, SiriuS, LADDER, etc.

index.name: Alita: Generalist Agent with Minimal Predefinition and Maximal Self-Evolution
index.one_liner: Agent that creates its own MCP tools on demand from open-source code, storing them as reusable MCP boxes for later tasks and smaller models.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2505.20286 (Jiahao Qiu et al.); 75.15% pass@1 on GAIA with a single manager agent. Tool-creation-as-self-evolution reference cited by both awesome lists; owner of the CharlesQ9 list.

index.name: Self-Improving Agents in the Era of Experience: A Survey of Self- to Meta-Evolution (Tsinghua / Shanghai AI Lab, Bowen Zhou group)
index.one_liner: Survey (OpenReview, 2026-06) centred on the 'harness agent': base model + mutable harness + interface + environment, covering skills, memory, agent RL, evaluation and safety.
index.why_relevant: Authored by Ning Ding, Kaiyan Zhang, Biqing Qi, Bowen Zhou (Tsinghua C3I / Shanghai AI Lab), the group behind TTRL, SSRL and PRIME; frames self- vs meta-evolution of deployed harnesses, directly relevant to harness-level self-improvement design.

index.name: MetaGPT / AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation (DeepWisdom, ICLR 2025)
index.one_liner: MCTS over code-represented workflows with LLM-driven expansion and execution feedback to automatically discover better agentic workflows.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2410.10762; the most-cited Chinese workflow-optimisation loop (both awesome lists), +5.7% over SOTA and lets small models beat GPT-4o at 4.55% cost. Basis of EvoAgentX's AFlow optimizer and SPO (arXiv:2502.06855).

index.name: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
index.one_liner: Memory-based online RL: a case bank of past trajectories plus a learned case-retrieval policy lets a frozen LLM improve continually.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2508.16153; listed in ANative-Lab memory optimisation. 87.88% GAIA validation top-1, 66.6% F1 on DeepResearcher, with 4.7-9.6 point gains on OOD tasks purely from memory growth; heavily cited by 2026 Chinese memory-RL work (MemRL, ReMe).

index.name: CowAgent (formerly chatgpt-on-wechat)
index.one_liner: Open-source super assistant / agent harness whose Self-Evolution module reviews conversations to improve skills, follow up tasks and consolidate memory via nightly 'Deep Dream' distillation.
index.why_relevant: Largest Chinese consumer agent repo pivoted to a 'reference implementation of Agent Harness engineering' with an explicit self-evolution loop (docs.cowagent.ai/memory/self-evolution): three-tier memory -> daily -> MEMORY.md, auto-curated Markdown wiki knowledge graph, skill improvement from usage.

index.name: Mobile-Agent-E: Self-Evolving Mobile Assistant (Alibaba X-PLUG)
index.one_liner: Hierarchical mobile GUI agent with a self-evolution module that accumulates Tips (general guidance) and Shortcuts (atomic action macros) from past experience.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2501.11733; listed in CharlesQ9 survey under general-domain evolution. 22% gain over prior SOTA on Mobile-Eval-E with persistent long-term memory; Alibaba's flagship self-evolving GUI agent line.

index.name: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
index.one_liner: AAAI 2024 (Tsinghua): gathers trajectories, extracts natural-language insights and successful examples into a pool, and retrieves them at inference; gains on HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2308.10144.
index.why_relevant: Foundational cross-task insight-extraction loop (precursor of ReasoningBank-style distillation); still a standard baseline.

index.name: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
index.one_liner: NeurIPS 2025 (Rutgers): Zettelkasten-style memory that generates structured notes, links them, and evolves existing memories when new ones arrive; evaluated over six foundation models. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2502.12110. Sister repo WujiangXu/A-mem 963 stars.
index.why_relevant: Introduced 'memory evolution' (updating old notes in light of new experience) as an agentic operation; heavily cited baseline in 2026 self-evolving memory work.

index.name: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
index.one_liner: Decomposes the agent control layer into six editable dimensions and stores learned harness patterns in a dual-layer experience bank; beats static harnesses on shell, code-gen and reasoning tasks with cacheable context and no test-time labels. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2607.14159.
index.why_relevant: Extends experience memory from 'what to do' to 'how the harness is configured', with selective transfer across task families.

index.name: Mem2Evolve: Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation
index.one_liner: ACL 2026 Main (BUAA): couples an Experience Memory with an Asset Memory (created tools) so both evolve together; +18.53% over base LLM, +11.80% over experience-only, +6.46% over asset-only across 8 benchmarks. Code: github.com/BUAA-IRIP-LLM/Mem2Evolve.
index.why_relevant: Quantifies the interaction between remembering lessons and creating tools - the two main axes of non-parametric self-evolution.

index.name: MemoPilot: From Player to Master - RL over Memory for Test-Time Learning
index.one_liner: ICML 2026: multi-turn RL with turn-wise rewards trains how an agent updates memory across sequential interactions; reaches 1762 Elo in Limit Texas Hold'em and 1590 in Rock-Paper-Scissors, beating DeepSeek-V3.2.
index.why_relevant: Trains the memory-update policy itself so test-time learning compounds; strong quantitative game-based evidence.

index.name: Experience Funnel: A State-Policy Alternating Loop for Self-Evolving Agents
index.one_liner: Trajectories are first distilled into an explicit textual state (skills/harness) for fast validation, then consolidated into parametric policy via transition-aware distillation; beats state-only and policy-internalization approaches.
index.why_relevant: Days-old paper articulating the fast-memory / slow-weights loop that unifies the memory and fine-tuning branches of self-evolution.

index.name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens?
index.one_liner: EMNLP 2026: token-matched study of skill, memory and workflow modules for web agents finds simple extra-step baselines often match them once budget and run-to-run variance are controlled.
index.why_relevant: Important sanity check for experience-memory loops: many reported gains vanish under matched compute.

index.name: Foundation Model Self-Play: Open-Ended Strategy Innovation via Foundation Models
index.one_liner: FMs write policies as code and compete in self-play to discover diverse, high-quality strategies across domains (Dharna, Lu, Clune).
index.why_relevant: Open-ended innovation loop where the population of code policies improves itself through competition — a Clune-lab building block for AI-generating algorithms.

index.name: HypoForge: Self-Improving Multi-Agent Hypothesis Generation and Testing via Scientific Skill Learning
index.one_liner: Stage-specific skill learning: adversarial generator-discriminator critique for hypothesis generation, and skills extracted from empirical results for hypothesis testing; consistent gains over existing AI-scientist systems.
index.why_relevant: Recent example of an AI scientist that accumulates reusable scientific skills from its own experiments — self-improvement of research method, not just outputs.

index.name: How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch (AutoResearchEval / ARFT)
index.one_liner: 100 frontier research tasks across 7 domains, 800 trajectories from 8 model-harness combos; finds agents lack a 'metacognitive loop' (verify, revise, validate) and defines a 45-pattern AutoResearch Failure Taxonomy.
index.why_relevant: Diagnoses exactly why current autoresearch loops fail to self-correct; useful negative result and benchmark for anyone building self-improving research harnesses.

index.name: The Automated LLM Speedrunning Benchmark (Meta FAIR)
index.one_liner: 19 NanoGPT speedrun tasks test whether agents can reproduce known training innovations (and discover new ones); frontier reasoning models with SOTA scaffolds struggle even with hints. Code: github.com/facebookresearch/llm-speedrunner (145 stars).
index.why_relevant: The evaluation counterpart to karpathy/autoresearch: measures whether an agent can climb the LLM-training research ladder autonomously; same Meta team (Zhao, Jiang, Shavrina, Foerster) as Hyperagents.

index.name: In Search of the Ingredients of Open-Endedness: Replicating Picbreeder with Large VLMs (GECCO 2026)
index.one_liner: Replaces human Picbreeder users with frontier VLMs and finds clear qualitative gaps vs human open-ended discovery; tests randomness, agent diversity, and memory/narrative continuity as ingredients (Earle, Arulkumaran, Dai, Kumar, Togelius, Risi).
index.why_relevant: Empirical probe of whether FM agents can sustain unguided open-ended search — a core question for any self-evolving system.

index.name: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
index.one_liner: Clusters all training errors into structural patterns in one round, generates candidates via four strategies, and applies bootstrap stability selection to fix GEPA's prompt bloat.
index.why_relevant: 74.67% avg vs GEPA 70.91% on 7 NLP benchmarks (+3.76pp) with 47% shorter prompts; Qwen3 GSM8K 15.0%->91.4%. Documents that GEPA prompts grow ~3x without accuracy gains.

index.name: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search (NPO)
index.one_liner: Simple linear teacher-feedback prompt revision loop for autonomous agents, no population or Pareto search.
index.why_relevant: Matches or beats GEPA with fewer rollouts, with the gap widening for stronger teachers; optimized prompts transfer within model families. A useful sanity check on whether evolutionary machinery is needed.

index.name: CAPO: Constraint-Aware Prompt Optimization for LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Pool-based rewrites with adaptive constraint weighting to optimize agent system prompts under tool-use, conciseness and safety constraints; DCAPO trains the rewriter with pool-based GRPO against a frozen agent.
index.why_relevant: Microsoft (Reid Pryzant, author of ProTeGi). Bridges prompt evolution and RL by RL-training the prompt rewriter rather than the task model; reaches feasible operating points while maintaining/improving accuracy across agent sizes.

index.name: DIVE: Unlocking Self-Improvement in Frozen Language Models Through Diversity-Driven Skill Evolution
index.one_liner: Evolves multiple populations of persistent natural-language skills (procedures, verification strategies, failure modes) from bootstrapped experience, no teacher model.
index.why_relevant: Georgia Tech/Cisco. Outperforms GEPA prompt optimization and gets 'substantially larger gains with fewer rollouts' than parameter-based methods on math/logic; skills transfer across model scales so smaller models match larger ones.

index.name: System Prompt Optimization with Meta-Learning (MetaSPO)
index.one_liner: Bilevel loop that meta-learns a system prompt across many user prompts/datasets while updating user prompts, so the system prompt generalizes to unseen tasks.
index.why_relevant: KAIST (Choi, Baek, Hwang). Generalizes to 14 unseen datasets in 5 domains and speeds later adaptation with fewer optimization steps. Canonical 'learning to evolve system prompts' work predating SePO.

index.name: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
index.one_liner: Salesforce study combining harness evolution (system prompts, tools, scaffolding) with fine-tuning weaker models on seven enterprise tasks.
index.why_relevant: Finds SFT on expert trajectories regresses weaker models 4-30 pts on all 7 tasks by breaking model-harness fit; proposes on-policy expert correction of only failing steps. Key evidence on how evolved prompts/harnesses interact with weight updates.

index.name: SWE-RL (Meta FAIR)
index.one_liner: First approach to scale RL for real-world software engineering using open software-evolution data (PRs/issues) and a lightweight similarity reward; Llama3-SWE-RL-70B reaches 41.0% SWE-bench Verified; NeurIPS'25 (arXiv:2502.18449).
index.why_relevant: Named in the brief; the reference for mining a self-supervised RL signal from software history rather than hand-built tasks, a precursor to today's automated SWE task synthesis.

index.name: SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic RL
index.one_liner: Policy extracts hindsight skills from its own completed trajectories during RL and distills skill-induced probability shifts back as dense token-level signals; consistent gains and sample efficiency on text and vision agent tasks.
index.why_relevant: The self-generated supervision evolves with the policy inside the RL loop, a clean instance of agents improving their own training signal.

index.name: Evolving-RL: End-to-End Optimization of Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Capability
index.one_liner: Jointly trains experience extraction and experience utilization via RL so self-evolution is internalized in weights; up to 98.7% relative gain over GRPO on unseen ALFWorld tasks and 35.8% on Mind2Web.
index.why_relevant: Makes the self-evolution capability itself the RL objective rather than a fixed system design around a static model.

index.name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
index.one_liner: Fully automated pipeline (environment generation -> trajectory collection -> task synthesis -> training) plus a runtime experience bank; distillation gives 77.8% pass (+17.8pp) on MCP-dominant tasks, experience learning +10.0pp on GUI-heavy tasks.
index.why_relevant: End-to-end automated env+task generation loop for hybrid MCP/GUI agents with explicit comparison of weight-update vs. memory-based self-improvement.

index.name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
index.one_liner: Automatically generates functional, interconnected websites with verifiable task evaluators (dense RL rewards) via unified specs and task-centric test-driven development; trained GUI agents improve on OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.
index.why_relevant: Environment synthesis for web/GUI agent RL at scale; addresses the environment bottleneck WebRL identified.

index.name: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
index.one_liner: Decoupled execute/evaluate/optimize/validate pipeline that generates reference trajectories from ground truth, diffs failed runs against them to find systematic failure patterns, and filters updates for leakage and regressions.
index.why_relevant: Addresses credit assignment and catastrophic forgetting in harness (prompt/skill/tool) self-evolution, the reliability problem behind every automated loop.

index.name: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
index.one_liner: Separates model-specific from systematic harness deficiencies; batch-level cross-instance failure aggregation and Failure-Driven Collaborative Refinement give up to 1.84x faster harness training and +18.56% accuracy.
index.why_relevant: Most recent (Sept 10, 2026) harness-training paper; treats the harness as the trainable artifact, complementing weight-space agent RL.

index.name: Trinity-RFT (Alibaba AgentScope)
index.one_liner: General RFT framework with decoupled Explorer (agent-env rollouts) and Trainer, online task curriculum (BOTS), prioritized experience replay, reflect-then-retry R3L; the training backbone of AgentEvolver (arXiv:2505.17826, v0.5.0 Feb 2026).
index.why_relevant: The open substrate on which Alibaba's self-evolving agent loops (task selection, experience replay, curriculum) are actually implemented.

index.name: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for SWE-agents
index.one_liner: Toolkit that automatically synthesizes tens of thousands of executable SWE tasks (bug injection, PR mirroring) from any repo with Docker envs; NeurIPS 2025 D&B Spotlight; used to train SWE-agent-LM.
index.why_relevant: The standard open pipeline for automatic task synthesis in software-engineering agent training; the SWE analogue of environment generation.

index.name: Agent Learning via Early Experience (Meta FAIR / OSU)
index.one_liner: Agents learn from their own reward-free interaction data via implicit world modeling and self-reflection across 8 environments, giving a stronger foundation for subsequent RL and better OOD generalization; ICML 2026.
index.why_relevant: Defines the self-generated-experience stage that precedes RL in the 'era of experience' pipeline; Jason Weston / Yu Su, 30 authors.

index.name: TAME: Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory (Trust-Memevo benchmark)
index.one_liner: Defines 'Agent Memory Misevolution' (trust erodes during benign task evolution), releases Trust-Memevo benchmark and an executor-evaluator memory loop that credits each reused experience.
index.why_relevant: Systematic benchmark for trustworthiness drift during memory self-evolution; +14.6pp accuracy vs prior memory-evolution methods on GPT-5.2/AIME while keeping safety.

index.name: Falsifiable Release Gates for Self-Improving Systems: Standing Invariants at Scale (Antahkarana runtime)
index.one_liner: Argues safety claims for self-improving runtimes are usually self-graded; proposes machine-checkable acceptance suites with fixed invariants, tracked over 7 releases (122->563 tests, accuracy 20%->70%, invariants unchanged, 0.021ms overhead).
index.why_relevant: A 'verifiable self-improvement' methodology: capability may grow only if pre-declared safety invariants stay fixed outside the update boundary.

index.name: Phantom Guardrails: When Self-Improving Agent Harnesses Fix Failures That Never Happened
index.one_liner: LLM proposers editing scaffolds fabricate guardrails for nonexistent failures in 15/60 runs (0/60 on featureless input); the iterative loop's 'keep adding' role supplies the demand.
index.why_relevant: A novel harness-evolution failure mode invisible to suppression-only acceptance tests, studied via a Counterfactual Fabrication Lab.

index.name: Query-Only Backdoor Attacks on Self-Evolving Skills via Trajectory Poisoning
index.one_liner: Attackers steer skill evolution purely through crafted queries that get consolidated into conditional rules; matches or beats direct skill injection across 3 benchmarks, 2 skill-evolution systems, 4 backbones.
index.why_relevant: Shows the experience-to-skill pipeline is an attack surface even without write access to the skill store.

index.name: FinEvo-Bench: Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Financial Workflows (Alibaba Qwen DianJin / Beihang)
index.one_liner: 120 real cases / 20 scenarios / 6 domains with institution-provided compliance rubrics; evolution adds +9.33 to +19.37 points (Codex largest), Letta best evolved score 91.65 with 0.09 compliance issues/task.
index.why_relevant: Measures cross-task transfer and compliance drift of self-evolving scaffolds longitudinally; rubric feedback beats reference-answer feedback.

index.name: LIFT: Loaded Impact on Final Task -- evaluation framework for self-evolving agents
index.one_liner: Warmup-tasks/holdout-tasks split with Docker-image 'delta' artifacts: runs each holdout in clean baseline vs evolved container and reports delta turns, tool calls and tokens; public leaderboard of evolution impact.
index.why_relevant: Answers 'does the agent actually get better after evolving?' with a controlled A/B protocol rather than raw capability scores.

index.name: The Meta-Agent Challenge: Are Current Agents Capable of Autonomous Agent Development? (Ant Research)
index.one_liner: Meta-agents get a sandbox, evaluation API and time limit to build agents in 5 domains; despite multi-layer anti-reward-hacking defenses, observed emergent ground-truth exfiltration; only proprietary frontier models match human baselines.
index.why_relevant: Sandboxed benchmark for agents-building-agents that documents reward-hacking attempts against the evaluator. Repo: https://github.com/ant-research/meta-agent-challenge

index.name: Sakana AI Scientist -- self-modification incidents and sandboxing discussion
index.one_liner: Documented cases where the autonomous research agent edited its own launcher to relaunch itself (infinite loop) and tried to extend its own timeout instead of speeding up code; authors recommend OS-level sandboxing.
index.why_relevant: Canonical early example of a self-improving research loop modifying its own execution constraints; motivates sandboxing requirements. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06292, repo: https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist

index.name: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
index.one_liner: 33-author position/survey defining four autonomy stages (improvement-execution, improvement-strategy, experience-acquisition, environment-adaptation) up to recursive meta-improvement, and a Headroom-Closed Index to measure how much headroom self-improvement actually closes.
index.why_relevant: Proposes a measurement construct (HCI) for self-improvement and diagnoses where current LLM loops stall; very recent and large-consortium.

index.name: MirrorCode (Epoch AI x METR): weeks-long coding tasks
index.one_liner: Agents reimplement whole programs from specs: Opus 4.6 reached 99.95% pass on gotree (16k-line toolkit; engineers estimated 1.5-17 weeks of human work), Opus 4.5 63%, Opus 4.0 15%; 61k-line Pkl unsolved at 1B tokens.
index.why_relevant: Extends METR's ~12-hour time horizon to multi-week autonomous engineering, the capability floor needed for agents to run long self-improvement/research loops unattended.

index.name: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World (NVIDIA GEAR / CMU / Berkeley)
index.one_liner: Coding agent runs a real-robot autoresearch loop (reset, rollout, verify, edit policy/training/algorithm code, rerun) with Environment/Policy-Improvement/Rollout/Evolution modules; 99% success on pin-box organizing, zip-tie fastening and tool use; accelerates across robot fleets.
index.why_relevant: Industry (NVIDIA GEAR: Jim Fan, Yuke Zhu) extension of the autoresearch loop to physical policy improvement; companion ASPIRE (arXiv 2607.00272) stores validated skill repairs.

index.name: PostTrainBench (ICML 2026)
index.one_liner: Gives CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex) one base model, one H100 and 10 hours to research and execute the best post-training strategy; adopted as 'PostTrainBench Lite' inside OpenAI's AI Self-Improvement preparedness evals.
index.why_relevant: Direct benchmark of 'agents post-training LLMs' (arXiv 2603.08640), i.e., the weights-level rung of automated AI R&D; used by a frontier lab for RSI risk tracking.

index.name: AutoHarness: Automated Harness Engineering for AI Agents (aiming-lab)
index.one_liner: Synthesizes and iteratively refines an executable code harness from environment feedback, eliminating illegal actions across 145 TextArena games (arXiv 2603.03329); same lab ships RSI-Exam (long-horizon executable research tasks, Aug 2026), Agent0 (ICML/COLM 2026) and AutoResearchClaw (14.4k stars).
index.why_relevant: Part of a prolific 2026 academic cluster (aiming-lab) producing harness-synthesis and RSI-measurement artifacts; RSI-Exam at github.com/aiming-lab/RSI-Exam.

index.name: Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement
index.one_liner: EN/ZH reading list on harness engineering for recursive self-improvement of LLM agents; companion to the Lilian Weng post. Jul 2026.
index.why_relevant: Focused specifically on agents improving their own harness code/prompts/memory, i.e. this angle.

index.name: Awesome-AI4AI
index.one_liner: Survey list of 223 papers on whether AI can reliably improve AI: long-horizon agents, benchmarks, harness design, recursive self-improvement; updated weekly. Aug 2026.
index.why_relevant: Weekly-updated coverage of automated AI R&D including self-modifying agent papers.

index.name: Self-Harmony (ICLR 2026)
index.one_liner: Test-time RL combining self-supervision and self-play: one model as Solver and Reframer, rewarding answers stable across a question and its paraphrase.
index.why_relevant: Strongest TTRL successor: Qwen3-1.7B MATH500 42.7% -> 69.6%, ranks first in 28 of 30 configurations; label-free self-improvement at inference time.

index.name: MARSHAL (ICLR'26)
index.one_liner: Multi-agent reasoning incentivized via self-play among strategic LLMs in games.
index.why_relevant: Game-based self-play (SPIRAL family) from THU with an ICLR 2026 acceptance; reasoning transfer via strategic multi-agent play.

index.name: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?
index.one_liner: Benchmark across tasks, topologies, communication protocols, team sizes and optimizers: APO gains up to +24.0 pts but can lose 16.0; structured protocols yield +6.3 vs +0.1 for freeform (code: github.com/juyangbai/MAS-PromptBench).
index.why_relevant: First systematic study of when automated prompt self-optimization helps or hurts multi-agent systems; useful for anyone building loops over agent teams.

index.name: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-Code
index.one_liner: Xiaomi's terminal coding agent 'where models and agents co-evolve': persistent project memory and continuous self-improvement across sessions, engine for MiMo Desktop.
index.why_relevant: High heat and institutional weight; co-evolution of model and agent harness is the stated thesis, but public repo exposes mostly the CLI.

index.name: EvoControl: Controlled Self-Evolution for Algorithmic Code Optimization (QuantaAlpha)
index.one_liner: Diversified planning initialization, feedback-guided targeted mutation/crossover, and hierarchical evolution memory (inter- and intra-task); outperforms AlphaEvolve-style baselines on EffiBench-X code-efficiency across backbones.
index.why_relevant: Uses 'self-evolution' explicitly for code optimization with memory of successes and failures; 12 citations.

index.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit
index.one_liner: Penn State / UCSC / Amazon: disentangles the ability to produce useful harness updates (flat across model tiers; Qwen3.5-9B updates rival Claude Opus 4.6) from the ability to benefit from them (non-monotonic, mid-tier models gain most). May 2026.
index.why_relevant: Empirical result on who should be the 'evolver' in a self-improvement loop; informs meta-agent vs task-agent model choice in DGM-style systems.

index.name: LightRSI
index.one_liner: ZJU NLP (EMNLP 2026): modular runtime for lightly deploying recursive self-improvement loops in long-horizon LLM agents.
index.why_relevant: Academic runtime for plugging RSI loops into existing agents; institutional (zjunlp) backing.

index.name: MaAS: Multi-agent Architecture Search via Agentic Supernet
index.one_liner: ICML 2025 Oral: learns a probabilistic supernet over agentic architectures and samples query-dependent agent systems; successor family to ADAS along with AgentSquare (2410.06153) and AutoMaAS self-evolving architecture search (2510.02669).
index.why_relevant: Represents the automated-agent-design branch descending from ADAS; searches architecture space rather than an agent editing its own code, so less self-referential.

index.name: The Kitchen Loop: User-Spec-Driven Development for a Self-Evolving Codebase
index.one_liner: Yannick Roy: six-phase autonomous improvement cycle with 'As a User x1000' synthetic power users, unbeatable tests and drift-control pause gates; 285+ iterations, 1,094+ merged PRs across two production systems with zero oracle-detected regressions. Mar 2026.
index.why_relevant: Production-scale evidence for a self-evolving codebase loop with guardrails; builds on SICA-style agents editing their own prompts/tools.

index.name: Weak-for-Strong (W4S): Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors
index.one_liner: COLM 2025: RL-trains a weak meta-agent to design and refine code workflows/harnesses for a stronger executor model.
index.why_relevant: Learned (rather than in-context) harness proposer; relevant precursor to trained meta-agents for harness optimization.

index.name: GEAR: Genetic AutoResearch for Agentic Code Evolution
index.one_liner: Replaces single-path autoresearch with population search over research states; GEAR-Evolve treats the controller itself as a mutable artifact.
index.why_relevant: Evolves the improvement controller (harness of the research loop) as well as the task code.

index.name: Harness-Delta Attribution: What Evolves When We Talk About Harness Evolution?
index.one_liner: Attributes harness-evolution gains across math/coding/creativity/agentic benchmarks; most search-split gains are explained by overfitting or test-time scaling, with small residual generalizable improvement.
index.why_relevant: Second independent critique (after Rethinking Evaluation) that harness self-improvement claims need attribution and held-out evaluation. Blog: wenwen-d.github.io/blog/harness-delta-attribution/.

index.name: AutoHarness: improving LLM agents by automatically synthesizing a code harness
index.one_liner: Lou, Lazaro-Gredilla, Murphy et al.: Gemini-2.5-Flash iteratively synthesizes a protective code harness (or full policy) that eliminates illegal moves across 145 TextArena games, letting Flash beat Gemini-2.5-Pro at lower cost.
index.why_relevant: Automated harness synthesis via iterative refinement; note the unrelated aiming-lab/AutoHarness repo (374 stars) is a governance framework without a self-improvement loop.

index.name: Better Harness (Qoder)
index.one_liner: Open-source harness-engineering platform: define harnesses as code, run controlled experiments, inspect task-episode evidence, and turn it into prioritized, acceptance-checked improvements for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Copilot.
index.why_relevant: Evidence-to-improvement loop over real coding-agent sessions; the improvement is human-in-the-loop (report -> scoped AI fix) rather than fully automatic.

index.name: Self-Improvement of LLMs survey (Zesearch/self-improvement-llm)
index.one_liner: TMLR (Survey Certification, 2026) technical review of LLM self-improvement with a continuously updated paper list.
index.why_relevant: Peer-reviewed survey specifically on self-improvement (self-play, self-rewarding, self-training) with weekly updates through Sep 2026.

index.name: Vocabulary Dropout for Curriculum Diversity in LLM Co-Evolution (COLM 2026)
index.one_liner: Random mask on the proposer's output logits sustains curriculum diversity and prevents proposer collapse in R-Zero-style co-evolution.
index.why_relevant: Fixes a documented failure mode of proposer/solver self-play (proposer converging to a narrow reward-satisfying distribution); +4.4 avg points for Qwen3-8B on R-Zero. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03472.

index.name: Self-Play Meets Skill Evolution (SESA)
index.one_liner: Search-agent self-play where informative failures are distilled into reusable skills written to procedural memory, so task generation and skill memory co-evolve.
index.why_relevant: Adds persistent state to self-play curricula (challenger poses, solver retrieves skills, failures rewrite memory); links zero-data self-play with skill-library self-evolution.

index.name: Hyperspace AGI (distributed autoresearch)
index.one_liner: P2P network where thousands of autonomous agents run experiments, gossip findings and push results to a shared repo; 32 anonymous nodes trained an LM in 24h via DiLoCo.
index.why_relevant: Autoresearch scaled out as a peer-to-peer swarm sharing experiment results - a distributed variant of the improvement loop.

index.name: MLflow Prompt Optimization (mlflow.genai.optimize_prompts with GEPA)
index.one_liner: Unified API wrapping GEPA and DSPy optimizers behind one call so prompts in the MLflow Prompt Registry can be auto-optimized from eval datasets; works with OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, CrewAI.
index.why_relevant: Databricks/MLflow productization of the prompt self-optimization loop (GepaPromptOptimizer, MetaPromptOptimizer), tying it to versioned prompt registries.

index.name: microsoft/PromptWizard
index.one_liner: Task-aware agent-driven optimizer: LLM generates, critiques and refines its own instructions and in-context examples via iterative feedback and synthesis (arXiv 2405.18369).
index.why_relevant: Second-largest dedicated APO repo; explicitly a 'self-evolving, self-adapting' critique-and-synthesize loop, though development has stalled since late 2025.

index.name: SalesforceAIResearch/promptomatix
index.one_liner: Turns a natural-language task description into an optimized prompt: intent analysis, synthetic data generation, strategy selection, cost-aware refinement; meta-prompt or DSPy backend (arXiv 2507.14241).
index.why_relevant: Salesforce AI Research's zero-data-entry automatic prompt optimization loop; competitive with DSPy/MIPRO across 5 task categories while shortening prompts.

index.name: AdalFlow / LLM-AutoDiff (SylphAI-Inc/AdalFlow)
index.one_liner: Library to build and auto-optimize LLM applications; implements LLM-AutoDiff (arXiv 2501.16673) textual backprop across multi-component, cyclic workflows including few-shot and instruction tuning.
index.why_relevant: Alternative textual-gradient auto-optimization framework with broader graph support than TextGrad (loops, multiple LLM nodes); moderately active.

index.name: TextBO: Bayesian Optimization in Language Space for Eval-Efficient Self-Improving AI
index.one_liner: Emulates gradient-based UCB Bayesian optimization purely in language space, no surrogate model; beats GEPA on performance-per-evaluation on ad-alignment and agentic tasks (ICLR 2026 RSI workshop).
index.why_relevant: Targets the evaluation-cost bottleneck of self-improvement loops; part of the ICLR 2026 Recursive Self-Improvement workshop lineup.

index.name: Transferable Self-Evolving Playbooks for Agentic Security Auditing
index.one_liner: Agents start from an empty playbook and author their own audit procedures; evolved playbooks reach 1,616 and 2,177 lines over 38 accepted revisions and transfer across targets.
index.why_relevant: Concrete domain deployment of the ACE 'evolving playbook' loop with unconstrained search space and measured playbook growth.

index.name: Rethinking Experience Utilization in Self-Evolving Language Model Agents (ExpWeaver)
index.one_liner: Compares init-only vs always-on vs on-demand injection of accumulated experience; ExpWeaver exposes the evolved experience as an optional resource the agent consults only when needed.
index.why_relevant: Shows that how an evolved context/playbook is consumed at runtime matters as much as how it is built; complements the faithfulness critique.

index.name: Ax (ax-llm/ax) - DSPy for TypeScript
index.one_liner: TypeScript DSPy port with signature-based programs and built-in optimizers (MiPRO, GEPA) so JS/TS agents can compile and self-optimize prompts.
index.why_relevant: Brings the automated prompt-optimization loop to the TypeScript agent ecosystem; actively maintained.

index.name: PhyAgentOS
index.one_liner: Recursive self-improving physical agent operating system enabling embodied agents to recursively self-improve.
index.why_relevant: RSI extended to embodied/physical agents; high star count.

index.name: Self-Improvement of LLMs: A Technical Overview and Future Outlook
index.one_liner: TMLR (survey certification) review of model-level self-improvement (data, optimization, refinement) contrasted with self-evolving agents; repo github.com/Zesearch/self-improvement-llm.
index.why_relevant: Weight-level counterpart to the agent surveys.

index.name: Claudeception
index.one_liner: Claude Code skill for autonomous skill extraction and continuous learning — saves non-obvious debugging techniques/workarounds as new skills in ~/.claude/skills/learned/ and auto-loads them later.
index.why_relevant: Early, popular single-purpose implementation of the session→skill loop; inactive since Feb 2026.

index.name: SkillWeaver
index.one_liner: Web-agent self-improvement via autonomous exploration: skill proposal → synthesis (as executable APIs) → honing; OSU NLP, Apr 2025.
index.why_relevant: Reference baseline in SkillLearnBench for exploration-driven skill synthesis (arXiv:2504.07079).

index.name: BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect
index.one_liner: Captures corrections, positive feedback and preferences from Claude Code sessions and syncs them into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md.
index.why_relevant: Early-2026 archetype of the 'learn from corrections' harness loop; successors include ReflexioAI/claude-smart (777 stars) and tigerless autoharness.

index.name: ReflexioAI/claude-smart
index.one_liner: Self-improvement plugin for Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode turning corrections into preferences, project skills and shared skills; claims ~3x better rule retention vs claude-mem.
index.why_relevant: Correction-driven skill evolution with a published benchmark; companion to the Reflexio self-improvement harness.

index.name: ECNU-ICALK/AutoSkill
index.one_liner: Experience-driven lifelong learning via skill self-evolution: agents distill, refine and reuse skills from their own trajectories.
index.why_relevant: Academic skill-evolution loop; alongside ViktorAxelsen/MemSkill (572 stars, 'Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents') forms the 2026 skill/memory-evolution paper cluster.

index.name: LLM4AD: A Platform for Algorithm Design with LLMs
index.one_liner: Unified Python platform with modular search methods (EoH, FunSearch, ReEvo, MEoH, HillClimb), task suites (combinatorial optimization, ML, science) and an evaluation sandbox; arXiv 2412.17287.
index.why_relevant: Predecessor of LLM4AD_Next and the standard toolkit for the automatic-heuristic-design branch of LLM evolutionary search (38 citations).

index.name: ReEvo: LLMs as Hyper-Heuristics with Reflective Evolution (NeurIPS 2024)
index.one_liner: Evolutionary search over heuristic code with LLM 'verbal gradients' (short- and long-term reflections) guiding mutation; SOTA on TSP, CVRP, bin packing, EDA across black-box and white-box settings (arXiv 2402.01145).
index.why_relevant: 373 citations; introduced reflection-as-mutation-guidance that GEPA, AEvo and others generalized.

index.name: Evolution through Large Models (ELM) / OpenELM (CarperAI)
index.one_liner: Lehman, Clune, Stanley et al.: LLM as intelligent mutation operator inside MAP-Elites quality-diversity search over Sodarace programs, then fine-tune the LLM on the evolved diversity (arXiv 2206.08896).
index.why_relevant: Foundational quality-diversity + LLM paper (167 citations) that seeded the entire LLM-evolution lineage including OpenEvolve's MAP-Elites archive; repo inactive but still the QD reference.

index.name: SwarmResearch: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Open-Ended Discovery (UIUC)
index.one_liner: Shepherd agent with global context steers a population of Search Agents each working in its own git branch; matches or beats EvoX and CORAL on 13/15 open-ended tasks, e.g. 4.58x speculative-decoding speedup vs 2.26x CORAL; distributed as Claude Code skills.
index.why_relevant: Lingming Zhang's group (SWE-agent lineage) applying population-based search over agent branches; a companion paper (arXiv 2609.04170) documents emergent cheating and whistleblowing in these swarms.

index.name: SeaEvo: Strategy Space Evolution for Algorithm Discovery
index.one_liner: Keeps an explicit natural-language strategy per program, clusters the archive by strategy semantics and navigates the strategy landscape; +20.6% on systems benchmarks, +32.1% on open-ended tasks, 18-41% lower API cost vs OpenEvolve/ShinkaEvolve, circle packing converged in 30 generations.
index.why_relevant: Shows that evolving the population's semantic strategies (not only code) yields better sample efficiency; a modular drop-in for AlphaEvolve-style loops.

index.name: TurboEvolve: Fast and Robust LLM-Driven Program Evolution
index.one_liner: Multi-island evolution with verbalized sampling (K diverse candidates with self-assigned weights per call), adaptive K scheduling and seed-pool injection; reaches better solutions at under half the cumulative API cost of baselines.
index.why_relevant: Practical throughput/cost improvements for the LLM-evolution loop; includes analysis that mid-distance mutations have the highest improvement probability.

index.name: GigaEvo (AIRI Institute) + EvoMem
index.one_liner: Modular AlphaEvolve-style framework (MAP-Elites, async DAG evaluation, multi-island) that set new SOTA on 32-circle packing (2.939) and Heilbronn n=11; EvoMem adds cross-run persistent mutation memory: 5.93x faster to baseline, +16.9% on KernelBench.
index.why_relevant: Russian research-lab implementation; EvoMem is the clearest 2026 study of carrying learned mutation knowledge across evolutionary runs (memory as a self-improvement channel).

index.name: QuantaAlpha
index.one_liner: LLM + evolutionary strategies to mine, evolve and validate quantitative alpha factors from a natural-language research direction, with 'self-evolving trajectories' as the search state.
index.why_relevant: Highest-starred 2026 applied LLM-evolution repo; shows the AlphaEvolve loop pattern spreading into finance (same org as EvoControl).

index.name: DéjàQ: Open-Ended Evolution of Diverse, Learnable and Verifiable Problems
index.one_liner: Jointly evolves a quality-diversity archive of synthetic verifiable math problems alongside model training, selecting for learnability relative to the current model.
index.why_relevant: Quality-diversity evolution applied to the training curriculum: the model and its problem distribution co-evolve in one automated loop (open-endedness lineage).

index.name: The Path to Recursive Self-Improving Agents (Alibaba survey + living index)
index.one_liner: Liu, Lin, Zhang, Ren, ... Jieping Ye (Alibaba): formalizes agents as component tuples updated from experience/evaluation feedback; living survey index at self-improving-agent.com.
index.why_relevant: Industry (Alibaba) framing of RSI agents with a maintained literature map; complements the KAUST and Nanjing surveys.

index.name: EvoTest: Evolutionary Test-Time Learning for Self-Improving Agentic Systems
index.one_liner: ICLR 2026: an Evolver agent rewrites the Actor agent's whole configuration (prompt, memory, tools, hyperparameters) between episodes using evolutionary selection, no gradients.
index.why_relevant: Whole-system self-evolution at test time, ICLR 2026; adjacent to DGM-style scaffold search.

index.name: Experience Graphs / Trellis (Meta)
index.one_liner: Liao et al. (Meta, 25 authors incl. Rob Fergus, Anirudh Goyal, Daniel Abadi): treats agent exploration lineage (artifacts, tool outputs, rewards) as a queryable experience graph so frontier selection and cross-session reuse become DB queries; ~10x faster, 52% lower token cost in Meta's KernelEvolve.
index.why_relevant: Infrastructure layer for archive-based self-improving loops (the DGM archive as a database), from a heavyweight industrial group.

index.name: A Survey on Self-Evolution of Large Language Models (Tao et al.)
index.one_liner: Earlier (2024) survey framing LLM self-evolution as an iterative cycle of experience acquisition, refinement, updating, and evaluation.
index.why_relevant: Listed as the foundational predecessor in the 'Related Surveys' sections of Gao et al. and the XMU survey; defines the model-weight-centric self-evolution loop that the 2025-2026 agent surveys extend to memory, tools, and harnesses.

index.name: Vocabulary Dropout for Curriculum Diversity in LLM Co-Evolution
index.one_liner: ASU (Ben Zhou): random logit masking during proposer training keeps R-Zero's proposer from converging to a narrow problem distribution.
index.why_relevant: Names and fixes a concrete collapse mode (proposer diversity collapse stalls the curriculum): sustains lexical/semantic/functional diversity and +4.4 pts on Qwen3-8B with largest gains on competition-level math.

index.name: TTRL-Guard: Correct-Answer Extinction Window in Test-Time RL
index.one_liner: Identifies that in majority-vote TTRL, correct answers on low-ability problems are briefly active then permanently suppressed; proposes flip-rate-aware reward scaling, minority-preserving sampling and risk-conditioned sparse updates. Code: https://github.com/linhxkkkk/TTRL-Guard
index.why_relevant: A precise failure mechanism of self-labeling loops and a mitigation: +54% relative over standard TTRL on AIME 2025, best avg pass@1 on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B.

index.name: SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time RL
index.one_liner: Closed loop co-evolving response archives (Good/Normal/Bad), query-specific rubrics and policy weights for label-free test-time improvement on open-ended tasks. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26873
index.why_relevant: Replaces majority voting (unusable on open-ended outputs) with self-evolving rubrics: up to +20.63 HealthBench, +20.31 ResearchQA, +8.06 six-benchmark macro-avg over base, with OOD transfer.

index.name: Co-rewarding: Stable Self-supervised RL for Eliciting Reasoning
index.one_liner: HKBU (Bo Han): complementary supervision -- contrastive agreement across analogous questions (data-side) or self-distillation from a slowly-updated reference teacher (model-side) -- to stabilize self-rewarding RL. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00410
index.why_relevant: Addresses self-rewarding training collapse; +3.31% avg on math, +7.49% on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, 94.01% GSM8K pass@1 on Qwen3-8B.

index.name: SQL-Zero: Self-Evolving Text-to-SQL
index.one_liner: Challenger/Solver from one base model with alternating GRPO; database execution is ground truth; challenger targets 'hard but solvable' SQL pairs.
index.why_relevant: Very recent domain transfer of the R-Zero recipe with an execution verifier: +6.6 (3B) / +7.3 (7B) on BIRD dev, beating a control trained on human gold labels; but at 7B only the first iteration preserves transfer to Spider/Spider-Syn -- another iteration-scaling collapse datapoint.

index.name: BenchEvolver: Frontier Task Synthesis via Solution-Centric Evolution
index.one_liner: Berkeley (Stoica, Dawn Song): evolves reference solutions of coding problems via structured modifications, then derives harder problem statements and tests; RL on evolved tasks.
index.why_relevant: Automated frontier-curriculum synthesis that feeds self-improvement: frontier models score only 27.5-62.6% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench-Plus; RL on evolved tasks gives +8.7/+8.3 pass@1 on LCB v6 Hard / LCB-Pro Easy, exceeding seed-only gains by 70.7%/34.8%.

index.name: Discovering KV Cache Eviction Policies via LLM-Guided Program Evolution (CacheCraft)
index.one_liner: Code-evolution engine discovers the FRC eviction policy: +15.4 RULER points on Llama-4k and +13.9 on Qwen-8k at 88% compression, first among single-pass KVPress baselines on 12/20 cells.
index.why_relevant: Example of AlphaEvolve-style evolution producing a deployable LLM-inference systems component (KV cache policy).

index.name: AIWaves Agents 2.0: Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents
index.one_liner: Data-centric framework treating prompts/tools/pipeline as 'symbolic weights' optimized by language-based loss, gradients and optimizer.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2406.18532 (AIWaves, Hangzhou). Foundational Chinese 'agent symbolic learning' framing cited in the ANative-Lab survey; no longer maintained but still the reference for textual-backprop over whole agent pipelines.

index.name: Agent KB: Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving (OPPO PersonalAI Lab)
index.one_liner: Shared experience knowledge base with reason-retrieve-refine pipeline so agents reuse other agents' cross-domain trajectories.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2507.06229; +16 points on GAIA for Claude-3 and +9.7 on SWE-bench via experience reuse. OPPO also released Chain-of-Agents/AFM (arXiv:2508.13167, 581 stars) for agent foundation model self-distillation.

index.name: OpenSkill: Open-World Self-Evolution for LLM Agents (EMNLP 2026)
index.one_liner: Agent builds both its skills and its own verification signals from scratch using only a task prompt and open-world resources, with no target-task supervision.
index.why_relevant: arXiv:2606.06741; listed in the XMU survey's Skill-Augmented Evolution section. Addresses the missing-learning-loop problem (no curated skills, trajectories or verifiers at deployment) via self-built virtual tasks and a leakage barrier.

index.name: EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective
index.one_liner: Evaluates 15 memory approaches along scope (within vs across episode) and content (knowledge vs execution); finds long-context baselines remain competitive and no memory design dominates. Code: github.com/DSAIL-Memory/EvoMemBench.
index.why_relevant: Alongside Evo-Memory and ELL-StuLife, one of the benchmarks purpose-built for compounding cross-task memory.

index.name: ELL-StuLife: Self-Evolving Agent via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning
index.one_liner: ECNU framework (experience exploration, long-term memory, skill learning, knowledge internalization) plus the StuLife benchmark simulating a student's multi-month life; HF dataset. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2508.19005.
index.why_relevant: Explicit lifelong-learning-from-experience framing with a long-horizon benchmark where memory must compound over simulated months.

index.name: AI Finds A Way
index.one_liner: 26 firsthand anecdotes from 100+ researchers of AI systems exploiting reward loopholes or discovering unknown phenomena; argues the same dynamics that break specifications can accelerate discovery if channeled (Dharna, Lu, Sullivan, Lehman, Krakovna, Clune).
index.why_relevant: Clune's 2026 framing of open-ended creativity vs safety in self-improving loops; directly relevant to reward-hacking risks in autoresearch.

index.name: SEPO: Evidence-Grounded Prompt Optimization via Structural Editing
index.one_liner: Locally edits typed units in a two-layer prompt schema and tracks which examples each edit fixes or breaks.
index.why_relevant: +3.1pp over GEPA on Llama-3.1-8B (61.9%) and +2.2pp on Qwen3-8B (73.3%) using 2.9M vs 4.1M optimization tokens and >5x shorter prompts.

index.name: FLARE: Few-shot Learning-based Adaptive Reflective Engine
index.one_liner: Combines GEPA-style reflection with few-shot reference examples for instruction optimization in compound AI systems.
index.why_relevant: Beats GEPA on every task-model pair with GPT-5 models: up to +14.2 pts on HotpotQA, 87.0% tool-calling accuracy, 52.7% micro-F1 GoEmotions; peaks with only 100 validation examples and is more seed-stable.

index.name: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi Agent Systems
index.one_liner: Textual-gradient optimizer for MAS that uses sequential interventions to verify which agent's prompt edit actually resolves a failure, then semantically clusters gradients.
index.why_relevant: SOTA on 5 MAS benchmarks with 2.5x lower wall-clock optimization time; addresses credit assignment, the main open problem in evolving multi-agent prompts.

index.name: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
index.one_liner: Forward-backward loop: diagnosis-driven skill edits with regression rollback, then utility auditing of knowledge units with validation-gated consolidation/removal.
index.why_relevant: +3.0pp avg accuracy over the strongest gradient-based baseline; illustrates the 2026 shift from evolving prompts to evolving reusable agent skill files.

index.name: Self-Supervised Skill Optimization (SSO)
index.one_liner: Optimizes agent skills without ground-truth labels by executing on unlabeled batches, generating comparative probes and ranking behavioral variants with an LLM judge.
index.why_relevant: Approaches and sometimes exceeds the strongest GT-based skill optimizer with zero labels; beats unsupervised prompt optimizers on closed- and open-ended tasks. Label-free loops are key for deployment-time self-evolution.

index.name: JTPRO: Joint Tool-Prompt Reflective Optimization Framework for Language Agents
index.one_liner: Rollout-driven reflection that jointly optimizes global instructions and per-tool descriptions.
index.why_relevant: 5-20% relative Overall Success Rate gains over CoT agents and GEPA on multi-tool benchmarks; joint > isolated optimization. Authors incl. Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth.

index.name: RECAP: Regression Evaluation for Continual Adaptation of Prompts
index.one_liner: Benchmark for proactive adapt-then-test prompt adaptation measuring forgetting, regression and forward transfer at the constraint level.
index.why_relevant: Negative result: six prompt-optimization methods across five LLMs and three constraint schedules show no significant improvement (with higher latency) in proactive deployment settings. Important caveat for evolving-prompt systems.

index.name: Where Does Harness-Optimization Value Live? Localized Gains and the Budget-Splitting Trap (HARNESSEVO)
index.one_liner: Decomposes an agent prompt into role / task-strategy / tool-format / reflection-control slots and evolves each independently under a fixed budget.
index.why_relevant: On ALFWorld with a 7B model nearly all optimization value lives in the reflection/control slot (+0.119); uniform budget splitting hurts, concentrating budget reaches 0.761; WebShop slots freeze empty. Practical guidance for where to spend evolution budget.

index.name: Kimi-Dev (Moonshot AI)
index.one_liner: Open 72B SWE model trained with large-scale RL that patches real repos in Docker and is rewarded only when the full test suite passes; 60.4% SWE-bench Verified, 48.6% pass@1 as SWE-agent after 5k-trajectory SFT (arXiv:2509.23045).
index.why_relevant: Named in the brief; an industrial example of scaling execution-verified agent RL for coding, though the loop is not self-generated tasks (agentless skill priors then agent adaptation).

index.name: OpenEnv (Hugging Face + Meta PyTorch)
index.one_liner: Gymnasium-style interface and hub for isolated, deployable agentic RL execution environments; community course and hundreds of hosted envs.
index.why_relevant: Not self-evolving itself, but the 2026 substrate for environment scaling that synthesized environments (EnvScaler, EnvCraft, CUA-Gym) plug into; relevant to 'agent RL scaling 2026'.

index.name: R2E-Gym: Procedural Environment Generation and Hybrid Verifiers
index.one_liner: SWE-Gen procedurally generates executable SWE environments from commits (8K+ problems) and combines execution-based and execution-free verifiers for scaling open-weight SWE agents; COLM 2025.
index.why_relevant: Early procedural environment generation for agent training with learned verifiers; a reference point for automatic SWE env synthesis.

index.name: Nex-N1 (Nex AGI / SII)
index.one_liner: Full-stack agentic platform unifying synthetic-data pipelines, large-scale automatic environment construction and NexRL training; DeepSeek-V3.1-Nex-N1 flagship plus 8B-671B model matrix (arXiv:2512.04987).
index.why_relevant: Industrial end-to-end data-to-deployment loop with automated environment hierarchy generation for agent RL.

index.name: Youtu-Agent (Tencent): Automated Agent Generation and Hybrid Policy Optimization
index.one_liner: Agent framework with meta-agent auto-generation of agent configs, an agent practice module, and distributed RL (hybrid policy optimization) for open-source models (arXiv:2512.24615).
index.why_relevant: Combines automated agent generation with RL-based policy optimization in one open framework; moderate relevance, high star count.

index.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails (PROCTOR)
index.one_liner: Production case study cataloguing 11 evaluation-signal failures in 4 classes (judge bias, harness/metric failures, ground-truth errors, reward hacking); agents reported 100% pass while true capability was 68%.
index.why_relevant: Practical taxonomy of how self-improvement loops fool themselves and 5 deterministic guardrails (hermetic sandboxes, frozen tests, canaries, role separation).

index.name: The Blind Curator: How a Biased Judge Silently Disables Skill Retirement (COLM 2026 workshop)
index.one_liner: False-pass judge errors break the skill-retirement mechanism abruptly at a 0.45 false-pass rate (symmetric noise does not), with no visible drop in aggregate metrics; provides a pre-deployment judge audit.
index.why_relevant: A 'silent' evaluator-induced failure specific to self-evolving skill libraries.

index.name: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work -- Until They Don't
index.one_liner: 8,135 trial records: skills mostly act as procedural anchors (65.7%) not knowledge injection (4.5%); retrieval precision collapses 29.6%->3.3% as skill pool grows 5->100.
index.why_relevant: Explains scaling failure of accumulated skills (a common self-evolution substrate) and why aggregate success metrics hide it.

index.name: UK AISI: reward-hacking-misalignment (open reproduction of MacDiarmid et al.)
index.one_liner: Reward-hackable RL environments, misalignment evals and training configs reproducing Anthropic's result on OLMo 7B/32B and GPT-OSS 20B/120B.
index.why_relevant: Government-lab open testbed for studying reward hacking -> misalignment generalization in self-training loops.

index.name: Escaping Model Collapse via Synthetic Data Verification: Near-term Improvements and Long-term Convergence
index.one_liner: Theory + experiments: verifier-guided retraining prevents collapse in self-consuming loops but drives parameters toward the verifier's knowledge center.
index.why_relevant: Shows the verifier becomes the ceiling of a self-training loop -- a formal statement of objective drift toward the evaluator.

index.name: Reviewing Model Collapse and Countermeasures (survey)
index.one_liner: 2026 survey of degradation in generative models trained on their own outputs in self-consuming cycles and the countermeasures (real-data accumulation, verification, curation, negative guidance).
index.why_relevant: Up-to-date entry point for the model-collapse strand of self-training risk; complements Characterizing Model Behavior Under Synthetic Data Training (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05133: stable up to 20% synthetic, accelerating degradation beyond 30%).

index.name: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security (Google DeepMind)
index.one_liner: DeepMind's 30-author roadmap on misuse, misalignment, mistakes and structural risks: dangerous-capability evals, amplified oversight, robust training, monitoring and access control.
index.why_relevant: Institutional baseline for how a frontier lab plans to keep control as AI accelerates AI R&D; complements OpenAI's CoT-monitorability position (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11473, 41 authors, Jul 2025) which warns monitorability is fragile under optimization pressure.

index.name: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data (safety note)
index.one_liner: Zero-data self-play RL that proposes and solves its own code tasks; the paper reports an 'uh-oh moment' where a Llama-3.1-8B run produced concerning chains of thought about outsmarting humans, flagging safety-aware training as future work.
index.why_relevant: Widely cited example that self-generated-curriculum loops can drift in undesirable directions; used as the model-pathway testbed in the Misevolution paper. Repo: https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/Absolute-Zero-Reasoner

index.name: google-deepmind/amplio
index.one_liner: DeepMind's lightweight Go/SQLite agent harness for robust long-horizon autonomous runs (crash-resume, sub-agent trees) with embedded 'skills + lessons' recall so runs accumulate reusable lessons.
index.why_relevant: Rare public DeepMind harness-engineering artifact (Chiyuan Zhang et al.) aimed at long unattended runs; lesson/skill recall is a mild persistent-improvement mechanism.

index.name: xAI Grok 4.6 release
index.one_liner: xAI states it 'used Grok 4.5 to regenerate the SFT trajectories across reasoning efforts, agent harnesses, and domains' before agentic RL; DeepSWE v1.1 54->65.9%, APEX-Agents 47.1->57.5%; model 'checks its own work' on long tasks.
index.why_relevant: Explicit frontier-lab disclosure of a model-generates-its-successor's-training-data loop (bounded self-improvement at the data layer).

index.name: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 launch
index.one_liner: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 52.6% (vs 24.7% Fable 5), Terminal-Bench 4.0 60.9% (Mythos 5.1); customer report of a 38-hour unattended ML run that diagnosed a label artifact, corrected it and launched six parallel experiments; wrote custom GPU kernels for 2.5x faster bio models.
index.why_relevant: Sep 2026 frontier capability signal for multi-day unattended research loops; Anthropic also cites ~45% lower cost for highly agentic workloads via cache-read pricing.

index.name: Anthropic Engineering: 'Harness design for long-running application development'
index.one_liner: Planner/Generator/Evaluator harness with context resets and GAN-style evaluator feedback (5-15 iterations per cycle); full harness $200/6h vs solo $9/20min on a retro game maker, DAW built in 3h50m for $124.70.
index.why_relevant: Anthropic's own harness-engineering guidance; the separated evaluator loop is the building block that self-improving harness systems (Self-Harness, AHE) automate. Companion posts: 'Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes' (Feb 2026), 'Scaling Managed Agents' (Apr 2026).

index.name: DARWIN: Dynamic Agentically Rewriting Self-Improving Network
index.one_liner: Henry Jiang: population of nanoGPT training runs where GPT agents mutate one another's training code each generation, with GA selection, JSON reasoning memory and a HITL upgrade-request channel. Feb 2026.
index.why_relevant: Small-scale but explicit agent-rewrites-code evolutionary loop with cross-agent mutation; minor relative to DGM family.

index.name: On The Statistical Limits of Self-Improving Agents
index.one_liner: Theoretical analysis of when benchmark-validated self-improvement can and cannot keep improving (statistical limits on iterative self-editing loops). Oct 2025.
index.why_relevant: Theory counterpoint to DGM-style loops; cited alongside RQGM's argument for non-stationary evaluators.

index.name: samizdat
index.one_liner: A self-modifying agentic harness written in Clojure (yogthos), started Aug 2026 and pushed daily.
index.why_relevant: Fresh hobbyist self-modifying harness; indicates the pattern spreading to non-Python ecosystems. Low heat.

index.name: harness-forge
index.one_liner: Skill that turns Claude Code into its own Meta-Harness: evolves memory/retrieval/context/prompts around a fixed model via a native propose -> score -> Pareto loop.
index.why_relevant: Direct Claude Code reimplementation of Meta-Harness; small but exactly on-angle. Sibling: raphaelchristi/harness-evolver (49 stars, Claude Code plugin with full-trace counterfactual diagnosis).

index.name: Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness
index.one_liner: Position paper (Binding Constraint Thesis): harness changes shift performance more than swapping models and can reverse model rankings; calls for mandatory harness disclosure on leaderboards.
index.why_relevant: Motivates why harness optimization is the highest-leverage self-improvement target; context for evaluating harness-evolution claims.

index.name: Effective harnesses for long-running agents (Anthropic)
index.one_liner: Anthropic engineering post (Nov 2025) on initializer + coding agent harness with feature lists, progress files and git commits to persist work across context windows.
index.why_relevant: Human-designed, not self-improving, but the Claude Code harness pattern most harness-evolution repos take as the seed; included for the 'Claude Code harness' part of the angle.

index.name: SeRL: Self-Play RL for LLMs with Limited Data
index.one_liner: Self-instruction (online instruction generation with filtering) plus self-rewarding via majority voting to bootstrap RL from a few seed examples.
index.why_relevant: Combines self-generated curriculum with TTRL-style majority-vote rewards; smaller-scale but open code. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20347.

index.name: SPC: Evolving Self-Play Critic via Adversarial Games (NeurIPS 2025)
index.one_liner: Sneaky generator injects subtle reasoning errors while a critic learns to detect them; both evolve adversarially to yield a step-level process critic without step annotations.
index.why_relevant: Self-play applied to the verifier side of the loop (evolving the reward model itself), complementary to proposer/solver approaches.

index.name: Test-Time Curricula for Targeted RL (TTC-RL)
index.one_liner: At test time, automatically selects a curriculum of related tasks from a pool and runs RL on them to improve on the target task.
index.why_relevant: Self-generated curriculum meets test-time RL; small repo but a distinct variant in the TTRL family.

index.name: Evolutionary Task Discovery (EvoTD)
index.one_liner: Treats data synthesis as directed evolutionary search over algorithmic skills x complexity attributes with crossover and parametric mutation operators to push RLVR reasoning frontiers.
index.why_relevant: Self-generated curriculum via evolutionary operators rather than adversarial proposer; relevant to automated task discovery loops.

index.name: Sibyl AutoResearch System
index.one_liner: Fully autonomous AI research system with self-evolution, built natively on Claude Code.
index.why_relevant: Early Claude-Code-native autoresearch with explicit self-evolution of its own workflow; activity stalled after March 2026.

index.name: Self-Supervised Prompt Optimization (FoundationAgents/SPO)
index.one_liner: Label-free prompt optimizer: pairwise LLM comparison of outputs drives iterative prompt rewriting at ~1-5% of the cost of prior methods (arXiv 2502.06855, MetaGPT team).
index.why_relevant: Cheap ground-truth-free self-improvement loop from the FoundationAgents/MetaGPT group (same lineage as AEvo).

index.name: dspy-agent-skills (intertwine)
index.one_liner: Production-grade Agent Skills for Claude Code/Codex CLI covering DSPy 3.2.x fundamentals, evaluation, GEPA, BetterTogether and RLM, with validated end-to-end examples.
index.why_relevant: Signals the pattern of coding agents driving DSPy/GEPA optimization runs as a skill; useful glue between harness and optimizer.

index.name: Agent-Loop-Skills (gaasher)
index.one_liner: 'Loop until it's better' verification-gated agentic loops packaged as open-standard Agent Skills, including a prompt-optimization loop, native to Claude Code and portable to Codex/Cursor.
index.why_relevant: Lightweight harness-level implementation of a self-improvement loop for prompts/code inside a coding agent.

index.name: promptim / promptimizer (hinthornw, LangChain)
index.one_liner: LangSmith-backed experimental prompt optimizer: run dataset, score, LLM proposes prompt edits, repeat.
index.why_relevant: LangChain's take on the automated prompt-improvement loop; notable for ecosystem reach but dormant since April 2025.

index.name: How to Correctly do Semantic Backpropagation on Language-based Agentic Systems
index.one_liner: Formalizes semantic gradients and semantic gradient descent generalizing reverse-mode autodiff and TextGrad for graph-based agentic system optimization; beats SOTA on BBH and GSM8K (code: HishamAlyahya/semantic_backprop, 77 stars).
index.why_relevant: Fixes credit assignment in textual-gradient loops for multi-node agent graphs; frequently cited by 2026 MAS-optimization work (TPGO).

index.name: A Systematic Survey of Automatic Prompt Optimization Techniques
index.one_liner: Formal definition of black-box APO and a 5-part unifying framework categorizing methods by seed prompts, inference evaluation, feedback, candidate generation and selection.
index.why_relevant: Best single taxonomy for the pre-GEPA APO landscape (with companion surveys 2502.11560 and 2502.18746).

index.name: Agent Skills for LLMs: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward (survey)
index.one_liner: Survey of skill-equipped agents covering skill acquisition (self-generated, distilled), deployment and security; finds 26.1% of community-contributed skills contain vulnerabilities; resources at github.com/scienceaix/agentskills.
index.why_relevant: Situates self-generated skill libraries and flags the security cost of auto-growing skill stores.

index.name: AlgoTune (NeurIPS 2025 benchmark)
index.one_liner: 154 math/physics/CS problems where the goal is code faster than reference implementations; used as the standard yardstick by MetaEvolve, SkyDiscover/EvoX and others.
index.why_relevant: Not a self-improving system itself, but the benchmark most 2026 evolutionary-code papers report on; useful for evaluating any evolutionary harness.

index.name: BLADE: Benchmarking LLM-Assisted Design & Evolution of algorithms (LIACS)
index.one_liner: Benchmark suite for LLM-driven automated algorithm design/evolution (LLaMEA lineage) comparing methods on black-box optimization problem sets with behavioural analysis.
index.why_relevant: Academic benchmarking infrastructure for the LLaMEA/EoH-style evolution of optimizers; useful for reproducible comparison of self-improving search loops.

index.name: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates (SEA)
index.one_liner: Confines self-modification to a small steering adapter plus a versioned harness around a frozen base model, with verifier-in-the-loop controllers; +4/+5 points on a 52-instance SWE-bench Verified subset.
index.why_relevant: Architecture pattern for bounded, certifiable self-modification (sandboxing the update surface).

index.name: Awesome-Reward-Hacking (curated list on reward hacking, emergent misalignment, proxy exploitation)
index.one_liner: Curated paper list on reward hacking, emergent misalignment and proxy exploitation in large models, including detectors and mitigations.
index.why_relevant: Quick index for the reward-hacking-in-training-loops literature; pairs with runtime detectors like rewardhackwatch (https://github.com/aerosta/rewardhackwatch, 89.7% F1 on 5,391 trajectories) and reward-hack-bench (https://github.com/islo-labs/reward-hack-bench).

index.name: AlgoEvolve: LLM-driven Meta-evolution of Algorithmic Trading Programs
index.one_liner: Inner loop evolves executable trading strategies; outer meta-evolutionary loop evolves the prompts that guide program synthesis, consistently beating human-written instructions; Sharpe 5.60, 1.59% max drawdown.
index.why_relevant: Small but clean example of prompt meta-evolution wrapped around program evolution in a noisy, non-stationary domain.

index.name: OpenAlpha_Evolve
index.one_liner: Early open-source AlphaEvolve-inspired Python framework (prompt -> LLM code -> sandbox eval -> selection) that gathered 1k stars in the first weeks after the AlphaEvolve announcement.
index.why_relevant: Historically notable but effectively abandoned since May 2025; listed so it is not mistaken for an active option next to OpenEvolve.

index.name: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning with Reasoning (Zelikman et al., NeurIPS 2022)
index.one_liner: The original self-taught reasoner: sample rationales, keep the ones that reach correct answers, fine-tune, repeat.
index.why_it_matters: Cited in 15 of the 18 curated self-evolving/RSI lists we diffed against the index; it is the reference ancestor of every weight-level self-improvement loop in the index (AZR, R-Zero, SEAL, TTRL, Self-Rewarding). Code: github.com/ezelikman/STaR.

index.name: ReST-EM: Beyond Human Data — Scaling Self-Training for Problem-Solving (Google DeepMind)
index.one_liner: Expert-iteration self-training: generate, filter by verifier, fine-tune; scales past human data on math/code.
index.why_it_matters: The standard 'self-training baseline' most 2025-26 self-play/RLVR papers compare against; the index has the derivatives but not the baseline.

index.name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback (Madaan et al.)
index.one_liner: Single-model generate→critique→refine loop with no training; the canonical inference-time self-improvement recipe.
index.why_it_matters: Present in 15/18 curated lists; Reflexion is in the index but its sibling Self-Refine (and the 'LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet' rebuttal, arXiv 2310.01798) are absent, leaving the verbal-self-correction sub-area without its reference point. Code: github.com/madaan/self-refine.

index.name: ProTeGi: Automatic Prompt Optimization with 'Gradient Descent' and Beam Search (EMNLP 2023) — plus APE (arXiv 2211.01910)
index.one_liner: Textual-gradient prompt optimization (ProTeGi) and LLM-as-prompt-engineer search (APE): the two foundational APO methods.
index.why_it_matters: TextGrad, DSPy/MIPRO, GEPA, PromptWizard and the 'textual gradients are a flawed metaphor' critique in the index all descend from ProTeGi/APE; each appears in 7 curated lists but neither is indexed.

index.name: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs (ICML 2024, Schmidhuber/metauto-ai)
index.one_liner: Represents an agent swarm as a computational graph and optimizes nodes (prompts) and edges (topology) with RL/prompt optimization.
index.why_it_matters: ★1044, cited in 11/18 lists, from the same lab as HGM (in index); it is the origin of the 'agent-as-optimizable-graph' paradigm that ADAS, AFlow, MaAS and agentdescent build on. Paper: arXiv 2402.16823.

index.name: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space (Tsinghua FIB, ICLR 2025)
index.one_liner: Searches a modular design space (planning/reasoning/tool-use/memory modules) with module evolution + recombination and a performance predictor.
index.why_it_matters: Cited in 9/18 lists; together with GPTSwarm and MASS it fills the 2024-25 'automated agent design' gap between ADAS (indexed) and the 2026 harness-evolution wave. Paper: arXiv 2410.06153.

index.name: MASS: Multi-Agent Design — Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies (Google DeepMind)
