deep_reads.name: Hyperagents (DGM-H: Darwin Gödel Machine with Hyperagents)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Meta FAIR — Jenny Zhang (lead), Bingchen Zhao, Wannan Yang, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, Minqi Jiang, Sam Devlin, Tatiana Shavrina
deep_reads.last_activity: Last push 2026-07-31; last substantive commits 2026-04-14 (README/logs updates). Only 9 commits total; 30 open issues, most unanswered by maintainers (last maintainer activity ~April 2026).
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv:2603.19461 (cs.AI), CC BY 4.0 paper; code CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No peer-reviewed venue listed as of 2026-09. 358 forks.
deep_reads.mechanism: The unit of evolution is a git repo ('hyperagent') containing task_agent.py (initial: one FM call with prompt 'You are an agent... respond in JSON'), meta_agent.py (initial prompt is literally one line: 'Modify any part of the codebase at `{repo_path}`.'), the tool layer (bash + str_replace editor, text-based tool protocol, 40 tool-call cap per session), and a README stating the system should 'edit and enhance its own mechanisms for generating agents'. Loop (generate_loop.py): (1) select_parent from archive.jsonl with 'score_child_prop': sigmoid(10*(score - mean of top-3)) times exp(-(n_children/8)^3), score = val split if it exists else train; (2) spin up a fresh Docker container, git-apply the parent's full lineage of model_patch.diff files, copy the entire outputs/ tree (all prior gens' evals, chat histories, patches) into /tmp; (3) run the PARENT'S OWN meta_agent.py (Claude Sonnet 4.5; Claude 3.5 Sonnet for Polyglot parity with DGM) for up to 6h; it edits anything; edits under domains/ (eval harness) are git-checked-out back to base commit, then git diff is saved as the child patch; (4) compile gate: `python -c 'from meta_agent import MetaAgent'` and `from task_agent import TaskAgent`; (5) staged eval: 10 train samples (1 BALROG episode, 3 robotics reps); if any domain scores 0 the child keeps score 0, else full train (+val) eval; (6) child is ALWAYS appended to the archive; if the meta agent process crashed, the parent is flagged valid_parent=False; (7) repeat 80-200 iterations. Because the meta agent code is part of the patched lineage, changes to how it improves itself (memory files, performance trackers, prompt templates) propagate to descendants. Optional flags let the agent also edit select_next_parent.py (E.5) or ensemble.py.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Fitness = benchmark score from a fixed, human-written harness per domain (domains/harness.py + report.py): Polyglot pass rate (o3-mini task FM), paper-review accept/reject accuracy vs. ICLR-style ground truth (GPT-4o task FM), Genesis quadruped RL fitness from agent-written reward functions, IMO-GradingBench grading accuracy (o4-mini). Anti-drift measures: (a) staged eval on 10 tasks with a zero-score kill for format failures; (b) train/val/test splits for judge-like domains, parent selection uses val, test used only for reporting the best-by-val agent; (c) meta-agent edits to domains/ are reverted so the scoring code cannot be rewritten; (d) archive never deletes nodes, so regressions are tolerated but down-weighted by the sigmoid-around-frontier selection; (e) 5 seeds, bootstrap CIs, Wilcoxon tests. Weaknesses: issue #39 shows test-set files with labels are copied into the meta agent's workspace (leakage); score is single-benchmark; no held-out generalization beyond within-domain test split; no human or LLM-judge in the loop.
deep_reads.key_results: Polyglot: 0.140 -> 0.340 train (CI 0.300-0.380), 0.084 -> 0.267 full benchmark (DGM: 0.140 -> 0.380, 0.142 -> 0.307, i.e., slightly worse than DGM but with no coding-specific engineering). Paper review test: 0.0 -> 0.710 (CI 0.590-0.750) vs AI-Scientist-v2 static 0.630, DGM-custom 0.590, DGM 0.0, DGM-H w/o self-improve 0.0, w/o archive 0.0. Robotics reward design test: 0.060 -> 0.372 (CI 0.355-0.436) vs default reward 0.348, DGM-custom 0.348, DGM 0.0, w/o self-improve 0.213, w/o archive 0.116. Transfer (imp@50 on unseen IMO grading with meta agent frozen): initial meta agent 0.0; DGM-custom transfer 0.0; transferred DGM-H hyperagent 0.630 (CI 0.540-0.630), p<0.05. Compounding: 200 iters on IMO grading from transfer agent 0.640 vs from scratch 0.610 (n.s.). From ProofAutoGrader + transfer meta agent: 0.700 vs 0.670 test; full IMO-GradingBench 0.561 -> 0.601. E.5 self-modified parent selection: random 0.428, modifiable 0.491, handcrafted score-child-prop 0.532 (n.s.); agents reinvented UCB, softmax-temperature and stagnation-triggered exploration. Cost: ~33M tokens self-modification + ~50M eval per 100-iteration run (~88.6M tokens).
deep_reads.limitations: Fixed task distribution (no curriculum). Parent selection and evaluation harness are frozen in main results; E.5 shows self-modified selection does not beat the handcrafted one. DGM-H vs DGM-custom differences are not statistically significant on paper review or robotics; only 5 seeds. Compounding claim (0.640 vs 0.610) is not significant. Coding result is slightly below DGM. Released initial meta agent ignores the eval_path and iterations_left it is handed (issue #30) and select_next_parent.py is uniform random with dead child_counts code (issue #29) — so the shipped 'self-referential' seed relies entirely on the FM spontaneously discovering /tmp eval logs via bash. Test-set leakage into the meta agent workspace reported (issue #39), unaddressed. Unanswered reproduction-gap report (issue #28, with GPT-5.2). Experiment logs hosted on Google Drive with broken LFS (issue #13). Docker containers run with network_mode=host and no memory/CPU limits in code despite paper's 'restricted internet' claim (the bash tool prompt merely says there is no internet). Text-based tool protocol capped at 40 tool calls; 6h meta-agent timeout. Very expensive (~89M tokens/run) and NC license.
deep_reads.key_insight: Put the improver inside the evolving artifact: if the meta-agent's code lives in the same git lineage as the task agent and every child inherits the parent's meta-agent, then meta-level infrastructure (persistent memory, performance trackers, eval-analysis scripts, prompt templates) becomes heritable and transfers across domains — a one-line 'modify any part of the codebase' prompt plus an archive is enough for these to emerge, whereas a frozen human-written improver (DGM/ADAS) yields imp@k of about 0 on new domains.
open_gaps: Evaluation harness and task distribution are frozen: the agent cannot generate new tasks, curricula, or held-out tests, so a framework could co-evolve tasks/evaluators with the agent.
Self-modified parent selection (E.5) underperforms the handcrafted rule; no method to validate/accept outer-loop changes (selection, evaluation) separately from task-level changes.
No regression gate or rollback: every compiling child enters the archive; a lower-scoring child is only down-weighted, and there is no diff-level attribution of which meta-level change helped.

Meta-level improvements are only inherited along a single lineage — there is no crossover/merging of memory, trackers, or tools discovered in sibling branches or in other runs (transfer is done by hand-picking one node with a descendant-growth score).

Meta agent is not given the evaluation results or remaining budget in the released code (unused eval_path/iterations_left, issue #30); a framework should expose structured archive/eval context and budget to the improver by default.
Test-set data and labels are visible to the meta agent (issue #39); needs strict separation of train/val/test artifacts from the self-modifying workspace.
Sandbox is weak in practice: Docker with network_mode=host, no resource limits in code, and the only defense against editing the scorer is a git checkout of domains/ after the fact.
Fitness is a single benchmark number per domain; no held-out cross-domain generalization test at the task-agent level, and the Polyglot result slightly trails the domain-specific DGM.
Cost (~89M tokens per 100-iteration run, 6h per meta step, Docker+GPU per child) makes it unusable for app developers; no lightweight or incremental mode.
Repo is effectively unmaintained since April 2026 (open bug reports, no maintainer replies, broken log archive), so it is a reference implementation rather than a reusable framework.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Per paper: sandboxed Docker execution with timeouts (6h meta agent, 5h eval), 'restricted internet' (in practice, the bash tool description tells the model it has no internet; containers actually run with network_mode=host), predefined tasks and metrics, human oversight, and appendix F on bias amplification and evaluation gaming (Goodhart). In code: meta-agent edits under domains/ are reverted before diffing (protects the evaluator), compile checks before eval, each child runs in a fresh container reset to root commit. README carries a warning about executing untrusted model-generated code. No behavioral-drift detection, no approval gates, no audit of self-modifications beyond saved chat histories and diffs.

deep_reads.name: Hermes Agent
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Nous Research (Teknium et al.), ~400 contributors
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; weekly releases, latest v2026.9.7)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: GitHub only, no paper. 244.4k stars, 50.6k forks, ~41.9k open issues, MIT. Positioned as the de-facto reference for skill-from-experience loops (OpenClaw migration path built in; SkillClaw/Evolver compare against it).
deep_reads.mechanism:
Two mutable stores: (a) skills = SKILL.md + references/templates/scripts under ~/.hermes/skills (procedural memory, agentskills.io format, loaded on demand via skill_view); (b) memory = MEMORY.md (2,200 chars) + USER.md (1,375 chars) injected as a frozen block at session start, plus FTS5 session_search over SQLite and optional Honcho dialectic user model.

Foreground loop: system prompt orders the agent to load any relevant skill, to patch a skill that was wrong before finishing, and to record non-trivial workflows via skill_manage (create/patch/edit/write_file/delete). Memory tool errors when over cap, forcing consolidation in-turn.

Background loop (the core): two counters, _turns_since_memory (user turns, reset on memory-tool use) and _iters_since_skill (tool iterations, reset on skill_manage use). When either reaches nudge_interval (default 10), turn_finalizer spawns a daemon-thread fork of AIAgent that replays the conversation snapshot with a byte-identical system prompt/tool list (prompt-cache parity; or a digest when routed to a cheaper aux model) plus a review prompt ("Be ACTIVE - most sessions produce at least one skill update"; prefer patching a loaded skill > umbrella > support file > new class-level skill; explicit do-not-capture list). Fork runs under a tool whitelist (memory, skill_manage, skill_view, skills_list, read_file), auto-denies approvals, and writes straight to disk. Guards: read-before-write (must skill_view in this review), provenance write-origin (fork may only touch curator-managed, agent-created skills; bundled/hub/pinned/user-owned refused), heuristic injection/exfil scanner, advisory linter, optional write_approval staging (off by default).

Curator: weekly after 2h idle; usage telemetry (use/view/patch counts) drives active->stale(30d)->archived(90d); optional LLM consolidation merges narrow skills into umbrellas; tar.gz snapshot + JSONL ledger with per-mutation rollback. /learn builds skills from sources; Collective Wisdom (Sept 2026) proposes sharing well-used skills org-wide with explicit consent.
deep_reads.eval_loop: There is no fitness signal. Acceptance of a self-modification is the reviewing LLM's own judgment against a prose "shape contract" in the prompt (class-level rules, no incident narration, no negative tool claims, no unresolved failures), plus heuristic scanners (prompt-injection/exfil/invisible-unicode patterns, NVIDIA SkillEvaluator tier-1 advisory scan on installs), plus an optional human approval gate (write_approval, default off). The only quantitative signal is usage telemetry (use_count/view_count/patch_count/last_used), and it drives staleness/archival, not quality. Drift/bloat is countered structurally rather than by evaluation: hard character caps on memory, curator consolidation, pinning, snapshots and an append-only ledger enabling rollback of any single mutation. Nothing measures whether a learned skill improves later task outcomes; no held-out tasks, no A/B, no regression tests of skills. Reward hacking is moot (no reward), but the prompt's "be ACTIVE" bias produces over-writing, which users report (#70128, #99661 nudge floods pending queue).
deep_reads.key_results: Claimed: skills created after complex tasks, patched during use, memory nudges, cross-session recall, deepening user model. Demonstrated: the machinery exists end-to-end and ships in weekly releases; the maintainers cite ~3-5x cheaper review when routed to an aux model with "identical memory capture, near-identical skill capture" (internal, unpublished). Counter-evidence: issue #95976 (2026-08-27, still open) reports production telemetry of 41 background-review forks with 0 skill updates landing (408 read-before-write refusals) because the read guard conflicts with skill_view dedup; two earlier variants of the same bug (#88053, #93872) were closed. #70128: default config lets the fork rewrite skills silently with no recoverable diff (ledger added later). No benchmark of the learning loop's effect on task success exists in the repo; evals/ are engineering regression probes.
deep_reads.limitations: No outcome-based acceptance for self-modifications; the flagship skill self-improvement path has been intermittently broken for weeks in production without the system noticing (#95976); each review fork costs ~30K tokens and is suppressed for cron; memory is capped at ~1,300 tokens total; single agent per profile (two processes sharing a home corrupt memory); background fork only edits agent-created skills so user-written skills never self-improve unless manually "adopted"; curator LLM consolidation is off by default and can make broad structural changes; 41.9k open issues indicate a sprawling, fast-moving codebase; trajectory export for model training is offline and external to the loop.
deep_reads.key_insight: Split "doing" from "learning" by forking the same warm-cache agent context into a tool-whitelisted background reviewer after every N turns, and make the learned artifact a provenance-tagged, versioned file whose lifecycle is governed by usage telemetry plus rollback rather than by any accuracy metric; consent (approval gates, pins, ledger) substitutes for fitness.
open_gaps: No outcome signal: skill/memory writes are never validated against task success. A framework could replay recent sessions with and without the proposed skill (or run a held-out task set) before committing the write.
No regression testing of learned skills: scripts/ and references/ are never executed or checked after patch/consolidation; curator umbrella merges can silently break paths and instructions.
Usage telemetry counts loads, not helpfulness. A user correction that follows a skill load is a free negative label that is not attributed back to the skill.
Loop-health monitoring is absent: result=skill/memory/none is logged per fork but nothing alerts when learning silently fails for weeks (issue #95976 shows 41 forks, 0 skill updates).

Write-rate calibration: the review prompt is biased toward acting ('be ACTIVE'); there is no adaptive threshold, cross-session dedupe, or cost/benefit gate, so the default is silent over-writing and nudge floods.
Only SKILL.md text and two small memory files evolve. Tool code, tool selection policy, workflow topology, system prompt, and nudge schedules are static config, never learned.
Memory is a flat ~1,300-token block with no tiering; consolidation is ad hoc by the agent when the cap errors. No hierarchical or decay-weighted memory.
Cross-agent transfer is file sharing with manual consent (org Skill Sync, Collective Wisdom), not merging of lessons or population-level selection across instances.
User-authored skills are excluded from autonomous improvement unless manually adopted, so most of a mature library never self-improves.
Trajectory generation feeds offline model training outside the repo; there is no on-device or closed-loop weight/policy update tied to the skill loop.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Background fork runs under a dispatch-side tool whitelist (memory, skill_manage, skill_view, skills_list, read_file) with auto-deny of command approvals; provenance write-origin so the autonomous fork can only edit curator-managed (agent-created) skills and is refused on bundled, hub, external, pinned, and user-owned skills; enforced read-before-write; heuristic scanner blocks prompt-injection, credential-exfil, SSH-backdoor patterns and invisible Unicode in memory and skills; project/hub skills quarantined on dangerous scan verdicts; optional write_approval staging for memory and skills with /pending, /diff, /approve, /reject; curator never auto-deletes (archive only), takes a tar.gz snapshot before every run, keeps an append-only JSONL ledger with sha256 blob store enabling per-mutation rollback that fails closed; pins block deletes; notifications of background writes; Collective Wisdom requires explicit native consent and treats all skill content as untrusted data.

deep_reads.name: ACE — Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, Boyuan Ma, Fenglu Hong, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Jay Rainton, Chen Wu, Mengmeng Ji, Hanchen Li, Urmish Thakker, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun — Stanford University, SambaNova Systems, UC Berkeley
deep_reads.last_activity: Official code repo ace-agent/ace last pushed 2026-08-24 (ComBEE batched-curator merge); ace-appworld pushed 2026-07-24; paper v3 2026-03-29
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv 2510.04618 (cs.LG/cs.AI/cs.CL); third-party paper-notes list it as ICLR 2026 (not directly verified — arxiv/openreview unreachable from this machine). Semantic Scholar API rate-limited; by all indications several hundred citations and it is the default citation for playbook/memory-style self-improvement without weight updates. Official repo 1,310 stars / 168 forks; >20 independent reimplementations on GitHub.
deep_reads.mechanism:
The evolving artifact is a text "playbook": a sectioned list of bullets, each formatted `[slug-00042] helpful=X harmful=Y :: content`. Three LLM roles (paper: all non-thinking DeepSeek-V3.1) run per training sample:
1) Generator answers the task with the full playbook in context and must cite the bullet IDs it relied on.
2) Correctness is checked (ground-truth match for FiNER/Formula; AppWorld unit-test/execution feedback; a no-GT variant uses only execution feedback). Reflector receives trajectory + feedback + the cited bullets, writes a diagnosis/lesson, and tags each cited bullet helpful/harmful/neutral; counters are incremented deterministically (non-LLM). On failure, reflection→regeneration repeats up to max_num_rounds (3 in code, 5 in paper).
3) Curator sees playbook + stats + reflection and emits JSON delta operations; a deterministic merge appends new bullets with fresh IDs (C_{t+1} = C_t ∪ δ_t). No full rewrite ever happens — this is the anti-collapse guarantee.
4) Optional grow-and-refine: BulletpointAnalyzer embeds bullets (all-mpnet-base-v2 + FAISS), groups pairs with cosine ≥0.9, and LLM-merges each group, summing counters. Off by default.
Offline mode: iterate over a train split for N epochs (paper: up to 5), evaluate on a val split every eval_steps and keep best_playbook by val accuracy; the result is used as a fixed system prompt. Online mode: same loop over the test stream (batch size 1), the playbook acts as test-time memory. A 2026 "ComBEE" batched mode runs generator+reflector in parallel per mini-batch, each proposing ADDs from the same snapshot, then an LLM reducer dedups proposals before one merge. Single-lineage, no population or archive.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = per-sample task correctness (exact/normalized match vs. ground truth on FiNER/XBRL-Formula; AppWorld TGC/SGC from the environment's unit tests, or raw execution feedback in the no-GT variant) plus an LLM-judge Reflector that attributes credit/blame to individual cited bullets (helpful/harmful counters). Anti-drift measures: (a) delta-only, deterministic merges so knowledge cannot be silently compressed (the failure they measured in Dynamic Cheatsheet: 18,282-token context → 122 tokens at step 61, accuracy 66.7→57.1, below the 63.7 no-adaptation baseline); (b) offline mode checkpoints best_playbook by held-out validation accuracy, so a degrading playbook is not shipped; (c) curator output is JSON-schema validated and skipped on failure. There is no reward-hacking guard beyond this: counters are recorded but never used to prune in released code, online mode has no rollback, and an issue reports val accuracy oscillating 93%→53% across epochs as the playbook bloats.
deep_reads.key_results: AppWorld (DeepSeek-V3.1 ReAct; TGC test-normal / TGC test-challenge / avg of TGC+SGC): ReAct base 63.7/41.5/42.4; +ICL 64.3/46.0/46.0; +MIPROv2 ~37.7 avg; +GEPA 64.9/46.0/46.4; +ACE offline 76.2/57.3/59.4 (+17.1 over base); +ACE offline no-GT 75.0/54.4/57.2; online: +Dynamic Cheatsheet 65.5/52.3/51.9 vs +ACE online 69.6/66.0/59.5. Leaderboard snapshot 2025-09-20: ReAct+ACE 59.4 vs IBM-CUGA (GPT-4.1) 60.3 average, ACE ahead on test-challenge. Finance (FiNER / Formula / avg): base 70.7/67.5/69.1; GEPA 73.5/71.5/72.5; ACE offline 78.3/85.5/81.9; ACE offline no-GT ~71.1/83.0/77.1; ACE online 76.7/76.5/76.6. Headline "+10.6% agents, +8.6% finance" are averages over baselines/settings. Cost: offline AppWorld −82.3% adaptation latency and −75.1% rollouts vs GEPA; online FiNER −91.5% latency and −83.6% token cost vs Dynamic Cheatsheet (86.9% average latency reduction). Ablations (AppWorld offline avg): w/o Reflector & multi-epoch ≈55.1, w/o multi-epoch ≈56.8, full 59.4; online without offline warmup 56.1 vs 59.5 with. v3 (Mar 2026) reportedly adds medical (DDXPlus), text-to-SQL (BIRD) and Gemini-model results (not verified first-hand). Independent user report (repo issue #26, Gemini 2.0 Flash, lending compliance): +8% test after 3 epochs.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: heavily dependent on Reflector quality and on reliable feedback; noisy feedback can distil wrong lessons; long-horizon tasks may need hierarchical organisation; no-GT variant is clearly weaker on knowledge-intensive finance (FiNER 71.1 vs 78.3). Observed/skeptical: (1) released code implements ADD only — UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE are TODO stubs and the curator prompt only offers ADD, so the paper's "pruning of harmful bullets" is not what the code does; playbooks grow unboundedly (>100K tokens within 300 FiNER samples, issue #11; released AppWorld playbooks are ~118–130KB) and the token_budget parameter is only shown to the LLM, never enforced. (2) All three roles use the same model; no study of cheaper reflector/curator. (3) Benchmarks are all verifiable, single-domain tasks with train/val/test splits — no cross-task or cross-domain transfer of a playbook is measured. (4) Online-mode results train on the test stream, so 'online' numbers include ordering effects that are not analysed. (5) Efficiency wins are relative to rewrite-heavy baselines (GEPA, Dynamic Cheatsheet), not to static retrieval. (6) The AppWorld 'with GT' trained playbook file in the release repo is empty (0 bytes), weakening the reproducibility story. (7) Helpful/harmful counters are collected but not acted on; the only regression control is offline best-checkpoint selection. 'Self-improving' is accurate for the context, but nothing else in the system (prompts of the three roles, merge logic, evaluator) evolves.
deep_reads.key_insight: Never let an LLM rewrite the whole memory: represent accumulated knowledge as append-only, individually addressable bullets with usage counters, have the model emit small deltas, and merge them deterministically — this structurally forbids context collapse and brevity bias while keeping the memory human-editable, and lets a small open model match GPT-4.1 production agents by accumulating detailed, domain-specific tactics instead of concise prompts.
open_gaps: No pruning/forgetting actually implemented: helpful/harmful counters are recorded but DELETE/MERGE/UPDATE are TODO stubs, so playbooks bloat past 100K tokens and validation accuracy oscillates across epochs — a framework needs counter-driven decay, budget enforcement and retrieval over the playbook

No rollback or A/B verification of individual deltas: a new bullet is merged without measuring whether it helps; only offline best-checkpoint-by-val-accuracy guards against regressions, and online mode has none

Fitness is a single in-distribution benchmark per playbook; no held-out generalisation or cross-task/cross-domain transfer of learned bullets is measured, and no mechanism exists to move playbooks between tasks or agents
Reflector credit assignment is an unverified LLM judgment on cited bullet IDs — no consistency checks, no multi-sample voting, no detection of wrong lessons or poisoned entries entering the playbook

Only the context evolves; the Generator/Reflector/Curator prompts, the bullet schema, the merge/dedup policy and the evaluator are fixed by hand (repo issue #37/#38 asks for per-dataset prompts) — a second-order loop that tunes these is absent
Single lineage, no population/archive: there is one playbook, no diversity, no branching or selection among alternative playbooks
Requires a labelled train/val split or a verifiable environment; no strategy for open-ended or subjective tasks where feedback is sparse or noisy
Sequential per-sample loop with three LLM calls plus reflection rounds per sample; parallel ComBEE mode only landed Aug 2026 and lacks reported numbers
Playbook is injected whole into context every call; no retrieval/selection of relevant bullets (roadmap item, unimplemented), so cost scales linearly with accumulated knowledge
deep_reads.safety_measures: Minimal. Bullets are human-readable with IDs, enabling manual inspection and "selective unlearning" (delete a bullet) — the paper's main safety argument. Curator output is JSON-validated and the step is skipped on malformed output. Offline mode retains the best playbook by validation accuracy rather than the final one. No automatic rollback, no sandboxing concerns (context-only, no code self-modification), no defence against incorrect or adversarial lessons being accumulated, and the harmful counter is never used to remove content.

deep_reads.name: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-11 (meta-harness repo push: experimental Harbor pilot with trusted evaluator + leakage denylist; artifact repo last push 2026-03-26)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yoonho Lee, Roshen Nair, Qizheng Zhang, Kangwook Lee (KRAFTON), Omar Khattab (MIT), Chelsea Finn — Stanford IRIS Lab
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint cs.AI (v1 2026-03-30); citation count not retrieved (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); ~18k alphaXiv views; cited by Lilian Weng's harness-engineering post and by AHE as concurrent work; 5 community reimplementations listed in README
deep_reads.mechanism: Outer loop (Algorithm 1 / meta_harness.py): seed population = hand-written baseline harnesses (zero/few-shot, ACE, MCE; Terminus-2, Terminus-KIRA), each evaluated on a search set; results written to a filesystem D. Each iteration: (1) a single coding-agent proposer (Claude Code, Opus 4.6, effort=max, tools Read/Glob/Grep/Bash/Write/Edit/Agent) is launched with a short domain SKILL.md and a task prompt pointing at evolution_summary.jsonl (one row per past candidate: hypothesis, avg_val, delta), frontier_val.json (best per dataset/task + overall best/Pareto), and per-candidate dirs holding source code, val.json scores and raw log.jsonl trajectories. It greps/cats whatever it wants (median 82 files/iter, 41% prior code, 40% traces), forms a falsifiable hypothesis, prototypes, then copy-then-edits a top harness into a new single-file Python class (MemorySystem or Terminus2 subclass) and writes pending_eval.json (k=3 candidates for text classification, k=1 for TB2). (2) The trusted outer script import-validates (TB2 also runs a 1-task smoke trial), benchmarks each candidate on the search set only, updates the frontier (strictly-greater replacement; no parent selection, no pruning, no crossover operator), appends summary rows, and loops for a fixed N (typically 20 iters / ~60 harnesses; TB2 10 iters, 89 tasks x 2 trials, ~$500 and 4-6 h per iteration). (3) After search, --test freezes the run and evaluates the Pareto frontier once on held-out test data. Regressions are tolerated (candidates are separate files; frontier keeps the best); the proposer itself reasons over failures (paper shows it diagnosing a prompt-edit confound after 2 regressions and pivoting to an additive env-bootstrap change after 6).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = task benchmark score on a search/validation set (accuracy for online text classification on USPTO/S2D/LawBench; pass@1 on 250 olympiad problems with GPT-OSS-20B; Harbor pass rate on TB2). Multi-objective via Pareto dominance over accuracy vs context tokens. Drift/overfitting controls: test sets held out until a one-shot finalize step (text-class: separate results dir, run frozen after test; math: 200 unseen IMO-level problems and 4 unseen base models; corpus decontaminated by exact-prefix + Jaccard 0.8); SKILL.md forbids dataset/task names and parameter-only variants and mandates prototyping; TB2 has NO held-out split (search and reported eval on the same 89 tasks) and overfitting is checked only by manual inspection and regex audits for task-string leakage. The July 2026 experimental Harbor pilot adds a trusted subprocess controller with per-task forbidden_references denylists and a universal denylist (/tests, verifier, /solution) plus a bounded eval budget. No statistical acceptance test; 2 trials/task during TB2 search, 5 trials for the final number.
deep_reads.key_results: Text classification (GPT-OSS-120B): best discovered harness 48.6% avg vs ACE 40.9 (+7.7) and MCE 40.0, using 11.4K ctx tokens vs 50.8K (ACE); OOD on 9 unseen datasets 73.1 vs ACE 70.2 (best on 6/9). Optimizer comparison (search set, median/best): GEPA 32.6/40.2, Best-of-N 34.0/44.2, OpenEvolve 39.1/43.3, TTT-Discover 34.1/45.6, Meta-Harness 50.0/56.7; matches OpenEvolve/TTT-Discover's final accuracy in 0.1x the evaluations. Ablation: scores-only 34.6/41.3, scores+LLM-summary 34.9/38.7, full traces 50.0/56.7 — raw execution traces are the key ingredient. Math RAG: discovered 4-route BM25 harness 38.8 avg over 5 models (4 unseen) vs 34.1 no-retrieval (+4.7), 37.5 BM25 (+1.3), 38.1 dense k=5. TB2: Opus 4.6 76.4% (5 trials; #2 behind ForgeCode 81.8, above Terminus-KIRA 74.7), Haiku 4.5 37.6% (#1, Goose 35.5); the discovered change is ~80 lines of environment bootstrapping, gaining on 7/89 tasks.
deep_reads.limitations: Only one proposer (Claude Code/Opus 4.6) studied; authors say the workflow only became practical with early-2026 coding agents. TB2 search and final eval use the same 89 tasks, so 76.4% is a discovery-problem number, not generalization; gains over KIRA are +1.7 pts on 7/89 tasks, within benchmark noise (search-run KIRA baseline was 64.4% vs 74.7% leaderboard, showing high concurrency/timeout sensitivity). Math gain over plain BM25 is 1.3 pts. Cost is high (~$500 and 4-6 h per TB2 iteration; proposer reads ~82 files/iter). The hand-written SKILL.md is admitted to be the strongest lever ('larger effect than iteration count or population size'), requiring per-domain engineering and 3-5-iteration debug runs. Release note: code 'not tested beyond verifying that it runs'; text-class test data ships in the repo (operational, not real isolation). Search is a serial single-agent loop with k<=3 candidates/iteration and no re-evaluation of noisy frontier entries.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Proposer is told (via skill text) it CANNOT edit existing agents, meta_harness.py or claude_wrapper.py and must not encode task/dataset names — enforced by convention plus regex audits, not by sandbox, in the reference examples. Candidates must pass interface validation (import + Terminus2 subclass check) and a 1-task smoke test before paid evaluation. Test sets are never shown to the proposer; finalize step freezes runs. Experimental Harbor pilot (July 2026) adds: candidate code never imported by the outer agent/controller, staged in a temp dir and run in a child Harbor job; forbidden-string leakage checks; frozen append-only evaluation history and eval budget; credentials passed only to the child. No rollback needed since each candidate is a separate file and the frontier keeps the best.
deep_reads.key_insight: Give the improving agent uncompressed, selectively-accessed experience (all prior candidates' code, scores AND raw execution traces on a filesystem it greps) instead of a hand-designed search loop with compressed feedback; the ablation shows raw traces, not scores or LLM summaries, are what make code-space harness search work, and a minimal outer loop with no parent-selection rule is sufficient once the proposer is a capable coding agent.
open_gaps: Fitness on TB2 = the same 89-task benchmark that is reported; no automatic held-out or cross-benchmark generalization gate before a candidate is accepted onto the frontier
No statistical acceptance test: frontier replacement is strict greater-than on a 2-trial noisy score; no re-evaluation of incumbent vs challenger, no confidence intervals or bootstrap
Reward-hacking defense is a string denylist (task names, /tests, verifier) plus manual inspection; no behavioral detection of eval exploitation (reading grading scripts, peeking at test outputs)

Experience is never distilled: the filesystem grows unboundedly and the proposer re-reads ~82 files every iteration; no learned memory/lessons store, no cross-run or cross-domain transfer beyond ad hoc references to earlier runs
The meta-level (SKILL.md and outer-loop script) is hand-written and frozen even though the authors say it is the strongest lever; the skill itself is not optimized
Single serial proposer producing 1-3 candidates per iteration; no parallel proposers, island/population diversity, or crossover operators, so search throughput is bounded by one Claude Code session
No cheap proxy or progressive evaluation: every candidate pays full search-set cost (~$500/iteration on TB2); the 'hard' subset is only a manual bring-up suggestion
Search space restricted to a single-file Python class with a fixed interface; cannot co-evolve tools, multi-file systems, model choice, or model weights (co-evolution named as future work)
Proposer is Claude Code only; wrappers for other agents must be adapted by hand, and generality across proposers is unstudied
Reference examples rely on convention ('CANNOT modify meta_harness.py') rather than enforced sandboxing of the proposer, which has Bash/Write access to the repo

deep_reads.name: The AI Scientist-v2 (Sakana AI)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Sakana AI (Yutaro Yamada, Robert Tjarko Lange, Cong Lu, Shengran Hu, Chris Lu, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, David Ha; with UBC/Oxford/Vector)
deep_reads.date: 2025-04-08 (repo created); paper arXiv:2504.08066 submitted 2025-04-10 (v1 only, never revised)
deep_reads.last_activity: Last push 2025-12-19 (license/README disclosure text only). Last functional code change Oct 2025 (ollama support merged then reverted). Effectively unmaintained: 78 open issues, with June-Aug 2026 bug reports (single failed worker aborts run #122, machine-wide SIGTERM cleanup #123, UnboundLocalError #125/#131, VLM whitelist rejection #133) unanswered.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (2504.08066). The generated paper was reviewed at the ICLR 2025 "I Can't Believe It's Not Better" workshop (scores 6/6/7, avg 6.33, withdrawn before publication). OpenAlex lists 30 citations (known undercount for arXiv; Semantic Scholar rate-limited during check). Forks: 983. Companion repo AI-Scientist-ICLR2025-Workshop-Experiment: 303 stars. Predecessor AI-Scientist v1: 14.5k stars.
deep_reads.mechanism: Not a self-modifying agent: what evolves is the experiment program (Python "node" code + plotting code) for ONE research idea, within ONE run. Loop (agent_manager.py + parallel_agent.py, AIDE-derived): an AgentManager walks 4 hard-coded main stages (1 initial_implementation, 2 baseline_tuning, 3 creative_research, 4 ablation_studies), each with LLM-generated sub-stages whose goals are synthesized from a metrics/issues summary of the journal (a dynamic mini-curriculum). Each stage runs a ParallelAgent best-first tree search: fill num_workers (4) slots per step by (a) drafting roots until num_drafts=3, (b) with debug_prob=0.5 picking a random buggy leaf with debug_depth<=3 to debug, else (c) expanding the current best good node (stages 1/3) or the frozen best previous-stage node with a unique hyperparam/ablation idea generated in the main process (stages 2/4). Workers get an LLM "memory_summary" of the journal so far. Each node's code executes in a multiprocessing subprocess with a 1h timeout; a feedback LLM (gpt-4o) parses stdout to set is_buggy and extract the metric; separate plotting code produces figures that a VLM critiques, and VLM-flagged problems set is_buggy_plots. good_nodes = neither flag set. Best node = LLM judge (gpt-4o, T=0.3) over good nodes given metric, training analysis and VLM feedback (fallback: max metric). Stage completion = LLM judging VLM feedback against stage goals, plus hard caps (21/12/12/18 nodes). On completion the best node is re-run with 3 seeds, an aggregation node combines plots, and a deep-copied best node seeds the next stage's journal. Then: Semantic Scholar citation gathering (20 rounds), LaTeX writeup, 3 reflection rounds using VLM figure/caption review and page-limit checks, and a final LLM+VLM review written to disk (not fed back).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Entirely LLM/VLM-judged; there is no ground-truth fitness. Signals: (1) feedback LLM parses execution output to decide is_buggy and extract a self-declared metric (the agent itself defines the metric name/direction); (2) VLM critique of generated plots marks nodes buggy for unclear labels/missing legends/misleading visuals; (3) LLM judge picks the best node across candidates using metric + analysis + VLM feedback, explicitly told not to rely solely on validation loss; (4) LLM judges sub-stage/stage completion against natural-language goals; (5) writeup: 3 VLM-driven reflection rounds on figures/captions + LaTeX compile/page-limit checks; (6) final AI reviewer (NeurIPS-style rubric) — output only saved, never used to iterate. Anti-drift/regression measures are structural rather than verified: buggy nodes can never be selected as best; the tree keeps all nodes within a stage (archive); the best previous-stage node is frozen as the root/anchor of stages 2 and 4 so tuning/ablation branch from a known-good program; multi-seed (3) replication of the stage winner; hard iteration caps and a 15h wall clock. Reward hacking is not guarded: the agent chooses its own metric, the same LLM family judges output, and the paper's accepted manuscript had ~57% train/test overlap that no check caught. External ground truth came only from humans: workshop reviewers (blind) and authors' choice of the best of several seed manuscripts.
deep_reads.key_results: Three fully AI-generated manuscripts submitted to the ICLR 2025 ICBINB workshop (43 submissions; reviewers told some might be AI). One scored 6, 6, 7 (avg 6.33, roughly top 45%), above the average acceptance threshold — the first AI-generated paper to pass peer review; the other two were rejected; all were withdrawn before publication. Accepted paper's finding was a negative result (compositional regularization does not help). Authors' own assessment: borderline workshop accept, not conference-level; found citation hallucinations, caption inaccuracies, ~57% train/test overlap, synthetic-data-only evaluation. Cost ~$15-20 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet experiments) + ~$5 writeup per run; several hours up to a 15h limit; ~57 nodes per run (21/12/12/12). No quantitative benchmark, no v1-vs-v2 comparison, no ablations of the tree search or VLM loop; README concedes v2 does not necessarily beat template-based v1 and has lower success rates. Humans selected which ideas to run and which of several seed manuscripts to submit.
deep_reads.limitations: Single-run, single-idea search with zero cross-run learning (no memory, skill, or prompt persistence; issue #119 RFC explicitly requests cross-run memory). All fitness signals are LLM/VLM self-judgment on an agent-defined metric — no held-out test, no reproducibility check, no citation verification (hallucinated citations acknowledged). Only ML-flavored ideas runnable as one Python file on a GPU with HuggingFace datasets (stage prompts hard-code "THREE HuggingFace datasets"). Final AI review is not used to revise. Success rate unquantified and admitted to be low; results were cherry-picked by humans (best of N seeds). No sandbox: LLM code runs via exec() in a multiprocessing subprocess on the host; end-of-run cleanup SIGTERMs unrelated python processes machine-wide (#123). Fragile engineering: single worker failure aborts run (#122), writeup retries delete earlier PDFs (#124), stage summaries only persisted at the end (#127). Requires Linux + CUDA + conda + LaTeX + multiple paid APIs; Bedrock-only Claude path; effectively unmaintained since Oct 2025. Paper never revised (arXiv v1 only); claimed generality "across ML domains" demonstrated on only 3 ideas from one workshop theme.
deep_reads.key_insight: Decompose open-ended research into a fixed progression of stages (prototype -> tune baseline -> explore -> ablate), run an AIDE-style best-first tree search over executable experiment programs inside each stage, freeze and carry forward only the LLM/VLM-judged best node as the root of the next stage, and make figure quality a first-class fitness signal via VLM critique that marks nodes buggy — turning a template-free coding agent into an end-to-end paper producer without any learned component.
open_gaps: No cross-run or cross-idea transfer: every run starts from scratch; no persisted skills, code snippets, failure patterns, or prompt refinements (a framework could bank successful node code/plot code/debug fixes as reusable skills)

Fitness is agent-defined metric + same-family LLM/VLM judgment with no held-out or external verification; nothing catches train/test leakage, seed cherry-picking, or metric gaming (add independent reproduction, data-leakage detectors, statistical tests before a node can be 'best')
Final AI reviewer output is write-only; reviewer scores never drive another experiment or writeup iteration (close the loop: review -> targeted new stage/sub-stage)

Stage structure and stage goals are hard-coded English strings tuned for HuggingFace ML experiments; the manager cannot add/remove/reorder stages or change search hyperparameters (debug_prob, num_drafts, caps) based on observed progress
Citations are gathered but never verified against Semantic Scholar metadata; hallucinated references reach the PDF
No sandbox: exec() in a host subprocess, plus machine-wide process kill on cleanup; an evolving-agent framework needs container-per-node isolation and resource accounting
Journal/tree is per-stage and discarded conceptually after the best node is copied; no archive across stages or runs for quality-diversity style reuse
Single seed per idea in-run; human picks the best of N manuscripts offline — no automated ensemble/selection over multiple runs
Requires Linux+CUDA+conda+LaTeX+Bedrock/OpenAI keys and ~$25/run; not usable by app developers without GPUs; unmaintained with open crash bugs since mid-2026

No quantitative evaluation harness (no success-rate reporting, no benchmark of research quality, no ablation of tree search vs. linear, VLM loop on/off), so improvements to the system cannot be measured
deep_reads.safety_measures: README warns LLM-written code executes with risks (dangerous packages, web access, spawned processes) and tells users to run inside Docker, but the code itself provides no isolation (exec in multiprocessing subprocess, 1h timeout only). Custom 'AI Scientist Source Code License' (Responsible AI License derivative) legally mandates prominent disclosure of AI generation in any resulting paper. Human gates: humans chose the 3 ideas and the best manuscript per idea; workshop organizers/reviewers were pre-informed that some submissions might be AI-generated; all accepted AI papers were withdrawn to avoid setting a precedent for AI-only work entering the scientific record. No guardrails on data leakage, citation verification, or metric gaming.

deep_reads.name: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Stanford IRIS Lab (Chelsea Finn) — Yoonho Lee, Roshen Nair, Qizheng Zhang, Kangwook Lee, Omar Khattab, Chelsea Finn
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-11 (last push: Harbor meta-harness pilot merged, TB2/text-class aligned with Harbor 0.18)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: COLM 2026 (per project page). Citation count: scout reports ~170; OpenAlex (lagging) shows 7; Semantic Scholar rate-limited — treat 170 as unverified. Companion artifact repo meta-harness-tbench2-artifact has 1205 stars. 148 forks; 5 listed community reimplementations (HarnessForge, SuperagenticAI/metaharness, Harvey legal-agent HF space, etc.).
deep_reads.mechanism: Outer loop (meta_harness.py, ~600 LOC per domain) is deliberately minimal. Each iteration: (1) spawn Claude Code (Opus 4.6, effort=max, tools Read/Glob/Grep/Agent/Write/Edit/Bash) with a SKILL.md 'proposer prior' and a task prompt pointing at run directories; (2) the proposer reads evolution_summary.jsonl (one row per past candidate: score, hypothesis, delta, components), frontier_val.json (best-per-dataset/task + Pareto list), all prior candidate source files in agents/, and raw execution traces (log.jsonl per dataset/candidate, Harbor trial dirs with full trajectories) using grep/cat — median 82 files, >20 prior candidates per step, ~10M tokens/iter; (3) it must write k new single-file candidates (k=3 memory systems for text classification, k=1 Terminus2 subclass for TB2), each a copy-then-edit of an existing candidate with one falsifiable hypothesis, and is told to prototype in /tmp against real trace examples and self-critique that the change is a mechanism not a parameter sweep; (4) writes pending_eval.json; (5) controller import-checks (and for TB2 smoke-tests 1 trial on 1 task), then benchmarks on the search set (3 datasets online-learning val split; or 89 TB2 tasks x 2 trials, ~$500/iter); (6) appends scores to the summary, updates frontier only if strictly greater. No parent selection, no pruning: every candidate persists on disk as an archive the proposer can inspect. Test set is evaluated once at explicit --test finalization (text-cls); TB2 searches and reports on the same benchmark. Nothing is fine-tuned; the base model (GPT-OSS-120B, Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5) is frozen.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = benchmark score on a search set: mean validation accuracy over 3 classification datasets (online learning, GPT-OSS-120B) or flat pass rate over 89 TB2 tasks x 2 trials (Opus 4.6). Frontier/"best" advances only on strict improvement, but nothing is rolled back — losers simply sit in the archive as diagnostic data. Drift/overfit controls are mostly prompt-level: SKILL.md forbids dataset/task names and task-specific hints; the paper argues code-space overfitting (hard-coded class maps, if-chains) is auditable by reading the code. Held-out test results live in a separate results/ dir 'never exposed during evolution' and are computed once via --test on a frozen run. OOD check: 73.1% on 9 unseen datasets vs ACE 70.2%; math harness transfers to 5 unseen models (+4.7 avg). Ablation (text-cls, median/best): scores-only 34.6/41.3, scores+LLM summary 34.9/38.7, full traces 50.0/56.7 — raw traces are the whole signal. Weaknesses: TB2 search set == final eval set (acknowledged 'discovery problem'); 2 trials per task makes ~1-pt deltas within noise yet frontier accepts any positive delta; no automated leakage detector in the paper code (the July 2026 experimental Harbor pilot adds forbidden-string checks per task, a trusted evaluator subprocess and an eval budget, but scored only on the same tasks used during optimization).
deep_reads.key_results: Text classification (GPT-OSS-120B frozen, 20 iters/40 candidates): 48.6% vs ACE 40.9% (+7.7) with 11.4K vs 50.8K context tokens; matches OpenEvolve/TTT-Discover final accuracy in 0.1x evaluations and beats them by >10 pts at end. Math (250-problem search, 40 iters/109 candidates): discovered 4-route BM25 retrieval harness gives +4.7 avg on 200 IMO-level problems across 5 held-out models (GPT-OSS-20B +3.0, GPT-5.4-nano +8.7, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite +6.3). Terminal-Bench 2: 76.4% Opus 4.6 (#2 among Opus agents, beats Terminus-KIRA 74.7%), 37.6% Haiku 4.5 (#1 among Haiku agents, +2.1 over Goose). The TB2 winner is KIRA + ~80 LOC 'environment snapshot' injected before turn 1; it improved 7/89 tasks, and 6 of the first 7 iterations regressed before the proposer diagnosed a confound and switched to additive-only edits. Proposer context ~10M tok/iter vs 0.002-0.026M for OPRO/TextGrad/AlphaEvolve/GEPA/TTT-Discover. Search runs finish in 'a few hours'; TB2 costs ~$500 per iteration.
deep_reads.limitations: Single proposer (Claude Code Opus 4.6) — the authors say generality across proposers is untested. Framework is two domain-specific scripts, not a library; math example not released; README states code 'has not been tested beyond verifying that it runs'. TB2 search and report on the same 89 tasks; 2-trial evaluation is noisy relative to the 1-2 pt gains claimed; the TB2 discovered artifact is a small prompt-time addition, not a structural harness change. Frontier accepts any positive delta with no significance test; no rollback, no regression suite, no lineage tracking beyond a 'base_system' string. Overfitting defense is prompt instructions plus manual code reading. Very expensive (~$500/iter TB2; hours per iter) and tied to Runloop/Modal + Harbor + Claude Code subscription auth. Citation figure (170) not independently verifiable; OpenAlex shows 7.
deep_reads.key_insight: Give the proposer agent the entire filesystem of prior candidates — source, scores, and raw execution traces — and let it grep/cat selectively (~10M tokens/iter) instead of scalar rewards or LLM summaries; ablations show summaries add nothing (34.9 vs 34.6 median) while raw traces lift median accuracy to 50.0, so 'search with selective access to diagnostic experience' is the actual mechanism, not code evolution per se.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prompt-level anti-overfitting rules (no dataset/task names, no task-specific hints), import validation, 1-task smoke test (TB2), held-out test in a separate directory evaluated once after freezing the run, proposer disallowed from editing existing agents/controller/wrapper. Experimental Harbor pilot (July 2026): per-task forbidden_references strings + universal denylist (/tests, verifier, /solution, task.toml), generated harness never imported by the long-lived controller (staged in a temp dir, run in a child subprocess), frozen append-only EvaluationState with eval budget. No sandbox restrictions on the proposer itself (has Bash), no automated regression gate, no human-in-the-loop acceptance.
open_gaps: Fitness is a single search-set score accepted on any strictly positive delta with 2 trials/task — no statistical significance test, no repeated-trial confirmation, no held-out regression gate before a candidate becomes 'frontier'

No cross-domain or cross-task transfer of discovered harness components: each run starts from a hand-written baseline and the archive is per-run/per-domain; nothing is distilled into reusable skills or a library of mechanisms

No lineage/credit assignment: candidates record only a free-text 'base_system' and 'components' tags, so the proposer cannot query which mechanisms historically helped across runs (the paper's 'component analysis' is manual)

Overfitting/reward-hacking defense is prompt text plus manual code reading; no automated leakage detector in the released paper loop (the experimental pilot's forbidden-string check is only a string grep, easily circumvented)
Search set == final eval set on Terminal-Bench 2; no protocol for benchmarks without a natural held-out split
Proposer is a one-shot Claude Code session per iteration with no persistent memory of its own reasoning; insights (e.g. the iteration-3 confound diagnosis) live only in ad-hoc report files

The controller/evaluator/proposer prompt (SKILL.md) is fixed — the harness of the meta-loop itself is not evolved, and no meta-level signal detects when the proposer is stuck in parameter tweaking beyond a written rule
Cost is ~$500/iteration and hours of wall-clock with Runloop/Modal sandboxes; no cheap proxy evaluation, active task subsampling, or early stopping of clearly failing candidates

Only a single proposer (Claude Code Opus 4.6) is supported; swapping proposers requires rewriting claude_wrapper.py and the framework has no abstraction for multi-proposer or population-parallel search
No co-evolution of harness with model weights or with the task curriculum; search set is fixed and never adapted toward the failure modes that the traces reveal

deep_reads.name: OpenViking
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Volcengine (ByteDance / Beijing Volcano Engine Technology); VikingMem paper by Jiajie Fu, Junwen Chen, Mengzhao Wang et al. (Zhejiang Univ. + ByteDance); 257+ GitHub contributors
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed today; v0.4.19 released 2026-09-08; ~30 commits in the last 48h)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: VikingMem (arXiv:2605.29640, VLDB 2026); Directory-Aware Query and Maintenance in Vector DBs / TrieHI (arXiv:2606.16903, ICDE); VikingRAG (arXiv:2609.11390, submitted). 2,808 forks, 700 open issues, Trendshift-listed; commercial SaaS on Volcano Engine.
deep_reads.mechanism: Two loops over a filesystem-shaped context DB (viking://). ONLINE: session.commit() archives messages synchronously, then asynchronously runs SessionCompressorV3 -> ExtractLoop, a <=3-iteration ReAct orchestrator where the LLM may `read`/`find` existing memory files and then emits operations (JSON or restricted-Python SEARCH/REPLACE protocol). Candidates pass a vector pre-filter + LLM dedup decision (candidate: skip/create/none; per existing item: merge/delete) and are written by MemoryUpdater with a per-commit memory_diff.json (before/after audit) and re-embedded. If the server-wide agent_evolution switch is on (default false) and extraction yields >=1 `case` (task signature + JSON rubric), it extracts `trajectories` (add-only operation contracts tagged with outcome and the experience URIs the agent read) and upserts `experiences` (Situation/Approach/Reflect imperative rules with a `supersedes` field) and optionally an executable session skill. At recall, experiences are vector-searched under memories/experiences, gated by a deterministic task-likeness score, injected inside an <openviking-context> block and stripped before capture to avoid self-pollution. OFFLINE (openviking/session/train): the experiences directory is a versioned PolicySet. Per epoch: content-hash snapshot -> RolloutExecutor (remote env HTTP service, e.g. tau2 driving VikingBot's AgentLoop) -> TrajectoryRolloutAnalyzer (rubric evaluation from env reward, passed = reward>=1.0, feedback text injected into trajectory extraction) -> ExperienceGradientEstimator (ExtractLoop proposes before/after MemoryFile patches = PatchSemanticGradient with confidence and derived_from links) -> PatchMergePolicyOptimizer (one LLM pass merges/splits/deletes across all gradients) -> MemoryFilePolicyUpdater under a tree lock with reload, base-content guard and version+1. Held-out test split is evaluated with 8 trials against a cached baseline; the delta is only reported.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Online loop: no external fitness signal at all — extraction, dedup/merge and supersede decisions are single-LLM judgments (ExtractLoop with read/find tools, <=3 ReAct rounds); drift is limited only by schema prompts (abstraction mandate, atomic scope, 8-bullet cap), a base-content guard on writes, and a memory_diff.json audit trail (manual rollback). Offline loop: environment reward from a benchmark service (tau2: passed = reward>=1.0, score = reward) becomes a RubricEvaluation that is injected as feedback text into trajectory extraction and stored as trajectory outcome; auto-extracted cases carry LLM-written rubrics. Held-out evaluation is real (train split committed, test split scored, 8 trials averaged, cached baseline, per-epoch eval), but accuracy delta never gates or reverts a policy update — the pipeline is analyze->estimate->plan->apply with no acceptance test. When no env reward exists, fallback evaluation is 'passed iff a trajectory was extracted' (trivially true). Lineage tags (which experiences were read + trajectory outcome) feed a Studio 'outcome distribution' view but no automatic pruning. The sibling LLM harness mitigates reward hacking only by skipping failed train sessions and hiding reward from the extractor.
deep_reads.key_results: Claimed (blog/README, Doubao 2.0 Pro + Doubao embedding): LoCoMo accuracy OpenClaw 24.20%->82.08%, Hermes 33.38%->82.86%, Claude Code 57.21%->80.32% vs native memory, with input tokens -34.3% to -91.0% and latency -58% to -66%. Agent experience memory on tau2-bench: retail 70.94%->77.81% (+6.87pp), airline 54.38%->66.25% (+11.87pp) with train split committed to memory and test split held out (8 trials averaged). ClawWork net income +69.34%, token use -22.8%. HotpotQA top-20 91.00%. Reproduction scripts in ./benchmark. No confidence intervals, no ablations (experiences vs trajectories), no multi-epoch curves published; memory_organization benchmark exists internally with structural graders.
deep_reads.limitations: Agent Evolution (cases/trajectories/experiences) is OFF by default (server.agent_evolution.enabled=false); the 'self-evolving' loop only has a real fitness signal inside the benchmark harness that requires a custom rollout/reward HTTP service. Policy updates are greedy in-place LLM patches with no acceptance gate, no rollback on regression, no population/archive. PolicyStatus lifecycle (draft/staging/production/deprecated) is a data field with no automated transitions. Experience quality depends entirely on Doubao-tuned extraction prompts (32k output-token floor). Heavy infra: Python server + Rust CLI + C++ index + vector DB; AGPL-3.0 core. Benchmarks self-reported without CIs.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the agent's experience directory as a versioned, file-based Policy Set and optimize it with 'semantic gradients': rollouts -> outcome-tagged trajectories (with env reward injected as feedback) -> proposed before/after file patches -> one LLM merge/split/delete pass -> locked, version-guarded apply with an audit diff — so learned behavior stays browsable, diffable and lineage-tracked rather than hidden in a vector store or weights.
open_gaps: Held-out eval delta is only reported, never used as an acceptance gate: no automatic rollback or rejection of a policy update that lowers test accuracy (memory_diff.json is audit-only, restore is manual)

Outside benchmark harnesses there is no fitness signal: fallback RubricEvaluation is 'passed iff a trajectory was extracted', so real-world experience extraction is pure LLM self-judgment with no grounding in task success

Per-experience lineage stats (success/failure counts of trajectories that read it) are surfaced only in the Studio UI; not used to deprecate, prune, down-rank at retrieval, or re-train experiences; PolicyStatus draft->staging->production->deprecated has no automated promotion/demotion

Only memory/experience text evolves; the host harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw agent loop, tool set, system prompts) is untouched, and extracted session skills are not execution-tested before being served (a skill_test_generation prompt exists but no verification gate)

Offline training needs a bespoke HTTP rollout/environment service with ground-truth reward (tau2); no generic way for app developers to declare verifiable cases/rubrics, and auto-extracted case rubrics are LLM-written and never validated
Single greedy lineage: no population or archive of alternative policy snapshots, no A/B serving of policy versions, no exploration beyond one merge pass per epoch

Merge/dedup/supersede decisions are one LLM call (<=3 ReAct rounds) with no check that the merged experience still satisfies the cases/trajectories it was derived from (no regression suite over past cases)
Agent Evolution is a server-wide switch defaulting to off; experiences are per user_id with no cross-user/cross-agent curation or transfer of learned experiences
Published results lack confidence intervals and ablations (experiences vs trajectories vs both, epochs curve), so the size of the learning effect vs retrieval effect is unclear
deep_reads.safety_measures: Server-wide agent_evolution switch (default off) and session-level memory_policy allow-list; memory_diff.json before/after audit per commit; base-content guard + version bump on policy writes under a path tree lock (300s) with reload to avoid clobbering concurrent training; MemoryIsolationHandler routes writes to self/peer spaces and drops unsafe peer ids; abstraction mandate strips IDs/names/secrets from trajectories and cases; injected <openviking-context> blocks are stripped before capture to prevent self-pollution; experiences injected as 'task guidance, not user facts'; privacy extraction templates and encryption/ACL layers.

deep_reads.name: HyperAgents (DGM-Hyperagents / DGM-H)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Jenny Zhang (UBC/Vector, Meta intern), Bingchen Zhao (Edinburgh), Wannan Yang (NYU), Jakob Foerster (FAIR at Meta), Jeff Clune (UBC/Vector/CIFAR), Minqi Jiang (Meta), Sam Devlin (Meta Superintelligence Labs), Tatiana Shavrina (FAIR at Meta)
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2026-07-31 (dependabot); last substantive commit 2026-04-14 ("update outputs_os"). Community PRs (#36/#37, June 2026) closed by authors of the PRs for lack of maintainer engagement; issues #28/#29/#30/#39 (May-Aug 2026) unanswered.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (Meta's publication page lists Publisher: arXiv). The scout's "ICLR 2026" claim is NOT supported: paper first posted 2026-03-19, after ICLR 2026 decisions, and not found on OpenReview. HF Papers: 51 upvotes. Semantic Scholar rate-limited; known citing work includes 'Self-Improving Agent Factories for Paper Review: When Constrained Beats Open-Ended' (Sira, KDD 2026 Workshop SciSoc oral) which benchmarks against a HyperAgents-style adaptation, and COLM 2026 rebuttals. Repo 2,722 stars / 358 forks (created 2026-03-19).
deep_reads.mechanism: A hyperagent is one Python repo containing task_agent.py (initially a single FM call that returns JSON) and meta_agent.py (initially a one-line prompt "Modify any part of the codebase at {repo_path}" driving an FM — Claude Sonnet 4.5 by default, Claude 3.5 Sonnet for Polyglot parity — with bash + str_replace editor tools). DGM-H outer loop (generate_loop.py), one child per iteration, 80-200 iterations: (1) fixed parent selection over the whole archive: score = mean of per-domain val (or train) scores, sigmoid(10*(score - mean of top-3)) times a child-count penalty (paper: 1/(1+n); code: exp(-(n/8)^3)); (2) spin up a fresh Docker container, apply the parent's cumulative lineage of git diffs, copy previous generations' eval outputs into the container, then run the PARENT's own meta_agent.py (6h timeout) — so whatever self-modification machinery the parent evolved (memory files, trackers, planning) is what generates the child; (3) domains/ (the evaluator) is git-reset to base so the agent cannot edit it; the remaining diff becomes model_patch.diff; (4) compile gate: `from meta_agent import MetaAgent` and `from task_agent import TaskAgent` must import within 5 min; (5) staged eval on a small subset (10 tasks, or 3 RL reps) must score >0 in every domain, else the child is scored zero; then full train/val eval; (6) child is appended to the archive with scores (never pruned); parent flagged invalid if its meta agent crashed. Multi-domain runs average scores and expose all evals to the meta agent. Best-by-val agent is evaluated once on the held-out test set. Preliminary E.5 experiments additionally let the agent edit select_next_parent.py (--edit_select_parent), but main results keep selection/eval fixed.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = fixed benchmark scores on train/val splits: Polyglot pass@1 via unit tests (10+50 train tasks, 165 test); paper-review accuracy vs. real ICLR/NeurIPS accept/reject labels (100/100/100 train/val/test); Genesis Go2 walking RL policy fitness (3 then 6 repetitions; test = zero-shot torso-height task); IMO-GradingBench grade accuracy (100/100/100). Val split drives parent selection in AI-judge domains to reduce overfitting; test used only for final reporting. Drift/hacking controls: archive keeps all compiled children (no replacement), staged gating zeroes non-functional children, compile import-check, domains/ reset so the evaluator cannot be rewritten, sandbox + timeouts. Meta-level ability is measured separately with imp@50: freeze the meta agent, run 50 iterations on an unseen domain, report best-agent gain. Weaknesses: acceptance is purely score-based with no verification or rollback of individual self-modifications; GitHub issue #39 shows the meta agent's workspace contained test samples with labels (leak not excluded by ignore_function_domains), and the released meta agent ignores eval_path/iterations_left (issue #30), so feedback is only what the agent discovers via bash.
deep_reads.key_results: 5 seeds, medians with 95% bootstrap CIs. Polyglot (80 iters): train 0.140→0.340 (CI 0.300–0.380), full benchmark 0.084→0.267 (CI 0.231–0.280) vs original DGM 0.140→0.380 / 0.142→0.307. Paper review test (100 iters, joint run with robotics): 0.0→0.710 (CI 0.590–0.750) vs AI-Scientist-v2 reviewer 0.630, DGM-custom 0.590 (n.s. vs DGM-H), DGM 0.0, DGM-H w/o self-improve (ADAS-like) 0.0, w/o archive 0.0 (all p<0.05). Robotics reward design test: 0.060→0.372 (CI 0.355–0.436) vs default reward 0.348, DGM-custom 0.348 (n.s.), w/o self-improve 0.213, w/o archive 0.116, DGM 0.0. Meta-transfer on held-out IMO grading (imp@50, frozen meta agent): initial meta 0.0; DGM-custom transfer agents 0.0; DGM-H transfer hyperagents 0.630 (CI 0.540–0.630, p<0.05). Compounding (200 iters IMO): from transfer 0.640 vs from scratch 0.610 (n.s.); ProofAutoGrader + transfer meta 0.700 vs 0.670; on full IMO-GradingBench 0.561→0.601 accuracy, MAE 0.178→0.175. Evolved meta-level artifacts: PerformanceTracker class, persistent JSON memory of insights/hypotheses/plans, budget-aware planning.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: fixed task distribution (no curriculum co-evolution); parent selection and evaluation protocol are fixed outer-loop components (only preliminary E.5 on editable selection). Observed: DGM-H vs hand-customized DGM-custom is not statistically significant in either domain; compounding gain (0.640 vs 0.610) is n.s.; only 5 seeds with wide CIs (e.g. DGM paper-review CI 0.0–0.510); paper-review test is 100 binary items and its labels (ICLR 2024/25, NeurIPS 2023/24) are public and likely in the FM's pretraining, so contamination is plausible; issue #39 reports test data with labels reachable by the meta agent, undermining the 'held-out' claim; issue #28 reports an unanswered reproduction gap; released meta agent contradicts the paper (eval path / remaining budget never injected into the prompt; child penalty formula differs). Cost appendix not retrievable here, but 6h meta-agent timeouts x 100-200 iters x 5 seeds x RL training implies a large budget; one sequential child per iteration; 16 GB logs only via Google Drive (LFS broken, #13); CC BY-NC-SA license; repo effectively unmaintained since April 2026.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Docker sandbox per generation with git reset/clean afterwards; 6h meta-agent and 5-min compile timeouts; bash tool declares no internet (though the container is built with host networking + proxy in docker_utils.py); evaluator directory domains/ is reset to the base commit after every self-modification so the agent cannot alter scoring; fixed, human-defined tasks/metrics and human oversight; README warning that model-generated code is executed untrusted. Section 6 and Appendix F discuss oversight strain, Goodhart/reward gaming, and transparency; no runtime policy enforcement, admission manifests, or rollback exist (community issue #17/#35 propose them).
deep_reads.key_insight: Put the improvement procedure inside the same editable artifact as the task solver and have each child be generated by its parent's own meta code, so selection pressure on task score also selects for better self-modification machinery (memory, trackers, planning) that transfers to unseen domains; measure that meta-ability separately with imp@k under a frozen meta agent.
open_gaps: Outer loop (parent selection, staged gating, evaluation protocol) stays handcrafted and immutable; only a preliminary flag lets agents edit select_next_parent.py
No task/curriculum co-evolution: fitness is a fixed train/val benchmark, so improvement stalls when the benchmark saturates
No verification, regression test, or rollback for individual self-modifications beyond an import check and a benchmark score; no machine-readable admission record of why a child was accepted
Held-out data is not isolated from the self-modifier: test samples and labels were copied into the meta agent's workspace (issue #39)
Meta agent receives no structured feedback in the released code (eval_path, iterations_left unused); a framework could inject per-task failure traces, diffs-vs-score history, and budget explicitly
Children stack cumulative diffs along a single lineage; no crossover/merging of archive members, no ensembling in main results, no quality-diversity descriptors beyond a scalar averaged score
One sequential child per iteration with a 6h meta step and no cost-aware fitness; no parallel population or early-stopping economics
Meta-level transfer shown on one held-out domain with 5 seeds and n.s. compounding; no multi-domain imp@k battery or scaling study
Paper-review fitness relies on public accept/reject labels likely in FM pretraining; no contamination-resistant or hard-to-verify-task evaluator design
No interpretability/provenance tooling attributing task gains to specific meta-level edits
Not usable by app developers: requires Docker, GPUs for Genesis RL, multiple provider API keys, CC BY-NC-SA license, and repo is unmaintained since April 2026

deep_reads.name: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Chengsong Huang, Wenhao Yu, Xiaoyang Wang, Hongming Zhang, Zongxia Li, Ruosen Li, Jiaxin Huang, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu — Tencent AI Seattle Lab, Washington University in St. Louis, UMD College Park, UT Dallas
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last pushed 2026-02-04 (README typo fix); last substantive code change 2025-12-10; paper v4 2026-02-13
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted 2026-01-23); NeurIPS 2025 MATH-AI workshop; HF Daily Papers #2 (2025-08-08). Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); heavily cited by follow-ups Agent0, R-Few, VisPlay, Dr. Zero, Multi-Agent Evolve, Language Self-Play.
deep_reads.mechanism: One base LLM (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base, OctoThinker) is copied into two separately-trained weight sets: Challenger Q and Solver S. Each iteration (scripts/main.sh) has three phases. (1) Challenger GRPO, 5 steps: a single fixed prompt ("write one new competition-math problem, <question>…</question> + \boxed{answer}") is sampled n=4–5 times per group. Reward per question: the frozen current Solver (served via vLLM Flask servers) samples m=10 answers; p = fraction agreeing with the majority answer; r = min(p, 1−p) in code (paper: 1−2|p−0.5|, peak at p=0.5) minus a repetition penalty = share of the GRPO batch falling in the same BLEU agglomerative cluster (distance threshold 0.5); unparsable output gets −1. The Challenger's own \boxed answer is never used. (2) Data construction: trained Challenger samples 8×1000 = 8,000 questions at T=1.0; the Solver answers each 9–10 times; majority vote becomes the pseudo-label; keep only questions whose agreement lies in [0.3, 0.8] (paper δ=0.25, i.e. 3–7 of 10 agree); drop proofs/'text' answers; push to HF Hub as a dataset. (3) Solver GRPO, 15 steps (lr 1e-6, low-var KL coef 0.01, rollout n=5, rollout batch 512, 4096-token responses), binary reward = mathruler match to pseudo-label plus format check. Next iteration warm-starts both roles from their previous checkpoints; no reset, no population/archive, no rollback. Script loops 5 iterations; paper reports 3. Both weights AND the curriculum evolve, and because pseudo-labels come from the evolving Solver, the reward source co-evolves too.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Inside the loop there is NO external fitness signal: the Challenger is scored by Solver self-consistency (agreement with majority vote), and the Solver is scored by agreement with its own majority-vote pseudo-labels. Drift controls are only (a) the 0.3–0.8 agreement band, which drops questions that are trivially consistent or incoherent, (b) a BLEU-cluster repetition penalty within a GRPO batch (added after the authors observed near-duplicate question hacking, issue #8), (c) KL to the reference policy, and (d) fixed step counts (5/15) with no validation-gated checkpoint selection. Outer evaluation is post-hoc on external benchmarks after each Solver iteration: 7 math sets (MATH-500, GSM8K, AMC, Minerva, Olympiad, AIME24/25) scored rule-based then re-checked by GPT-4o (one-directional: only flips wrong to right), plus MMLU-Pro, SuperGPQA, BBEH. The paper's own GPT-4o oracle analysis shows the drift the loop cannot see: pseudo-label accuracy falls 79.0% (iter1) to 63.0% (iter3) as questions get harder, and performance collapses after 1 iteration for 0.6B and after 3 for 4B. Reproducers report (issue #20) 30–40% pseudo-label accuracy with the described protocol, and (issues #19/#31) the GPT-recheck script had swapped argument order; author concedes evaluation "had some issues" but says trends hold.
deep_reads.key_results: Qwen3-4B-Base: MATH avg 42.58 -> 49.07 (+6.49), overall avg 27.10 -> 34.92 (peak iter 2); Qwen3-8B-Base: MATH 49.18 -> 54.69 (+5.51), overall 34.49 -> 38.73, general-domain +5.13; OctoThinker-3B/8B also improve (+2.68 / +6.41 MATH). Zero-shot 'Base Challenger' (no RL) already gives ~half the gain (4B overall 30.83), RL-trained Challenger adds the rest. Ablations: removing Challenger RL training gives the largest drop; removing repetition penalty or difficulty filtering also hurts (exact numbers not retrievable here). R-Zero then SFT on human data beats SFT alone by +2.35 (4B). Single model playing both roles collapses earlier with lower pseudo-label accuracy. Gains saturate/decline by iteration 3; larger models tolerate more iterations.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: pseudo-label accuracy degrades with difficulty (79%->63%); model collapse after 1–3 iterations; restricted to domains with single verifiable final answers (math); open-ended tasks unaddressed. Observed from code/issues: hyperparameters in paper and scripts disagree (batch 128 vs 16, steps 5/15 vs 6/20, m=10 vs 9); GPT-4o recheck bug and one-directional correction inflate absolute numbers (base Qwen3-4B MATH 58 rule-based vs 68 reported, Minerva ~20 vs 38); pseudo-label accuracy not reproducible (30–40% vs 79%); requires 8 GPUs, two full model copies, vLLM servers and HF Hub round-trips; pipeline is fragile (pkill python, math_verify infinite loops, hard-coded paths); tested only at 3B–8B; each iteration discards prior questions (no replay).
deep_reads.key_insight: Use the solver's own self-consistency as a single unified signal for three jobs at once: as the generator's reward (target p~0.5 = the solver's capability frontier), as the label (majority vote), and as the data filter (keep only the 0.3–0.8 band). This removes the need for any external verifier or seed data, but the same coupling is the failure mode: as the curriculum hardens, self-consistency stops tracking correctness and the loop drifts within ~3 iterations unless an external anchor is added.
open_gaps: No external correctness anchor: pseudo-labels are pure majority vote, accuracy drops 79%->63% in 3 iterations; a framework could add cheap verifiers (code execution, tool calls, cross-model agreement, or a few human examples as R-Few does) or weight training samples by label confidence

No stopping, checkpoint-selection, or rollback rule: fixed 5/15 GRPO steps and fixed iteration count, collapse is only detected post-hoc on external benchmarks; needs a held-out or synthetic validation gate that can reject an iteration and revert

Single lineage, no archive or population: each iteration overwrites both roles, previous 8k-question sets are discarded (no replay/curriculum memory); a quality-diversity archive of tasks and checkpoints would counter diversity collapse and length inflation documented by R-Few
Repetition penalty is only intra-batch BLEU clustering; no cross-iteration novelty measure, so the Challenger can re-converge on the same problem families over time

Domain locked to single-answer competition math via a hard-coded generator prompt; no mechanism for open-ended, multi-step, or tool-using tasks (Agent0/Dr. Zero extend this with tools and search) and no cross-domain task mixing
Requires full-parameter RL of two model copies on 8 GPUs plus vLLM reward servers; no LoRA/API/prompt-level variant, so app developers cannot use the loop with closed models
Challenger's own \boxed answer is generated then discarded; no self-verification of the generator's solution, wasted signal that could be used to detect ambiguous questions

Evaluation reproducibility is weak (swapped-argument GPT recheck, one-directional correction, paper/script hyperparameter mismatches); a new framework should report rule-based and judge-based scores separately and pin the exact loop config
Single shared-parameter model for both roles collapses earlier and the paper offers no fix; role separation via LoRA adapters or role tokens is untested
Generalization is measured only after the fact on math and three general benchmarks; the loop has no internal signal about transfer, so it cannot steer toward skills that generalize
deep_reads.safety_measures: Minimal and all internal to training: KL regularization to reference policy; BLEU-cluster repetition penalty against duplicate-question reward hacking; 0.3–0.8 agreement band filter; proof/'text'-answer exclusion; 10s grader timeouts. No sandboxing concerns (no code execution), no human-in-the-loop, no rollback, no drift detection during the run. Ethical/safety discussion absent from paper; model collapse is treated as a scientific finding, not an operational safeguard.
