deep_reads.name: MIPRO / MIPROv2 (Multi-prompt Instruction PRoposal Optimizer) — "Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs"
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Krista Opsahl-Ong*, Michael J. Ryan*, Josh Purtell, David Broman, Christopher Potts, Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab (Stanford NLP; Basis; KTH; UC Berkeley) — shipped as dspy.MIPROv2 in stanfordnlp/dspy
deep_reads.last_activity: Paper is static. Implementation (dspy/teleprompt/mipro_optimizer_v2.py) last touched 2026-05-13 (numpy optional), 2026-04-16 (fix demo index assignment bug), 2026-03-06 (optuna optional); DSPy repo itself pushed 2026-09-11 but new optimizer work is going into GEPA (e.g. 2026-09-05 "feat(gepa): add code_proposer hook").
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: EMNLP 2024 main conference (DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.emnlp-main.525). Semantic Scholar: 301 citations, 29 influential (2026-09-11). OpenAlex undercounts at 28. Used as the primary non-RL baseline in GEPA (2507.19457) and most 2025-26 prompt-optimizer papers.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Setting: a multi-module LM program Φ, a scalar metric μ, a small labeled trainset; no gradients, no per-module labels. Each module i has two latent categorical variables: instruction index and few-shot-demo-set index. Three stages (verified in DSPy source):

1. Bootstrap demos: run the unoptimized Φ on train inputs; keep whole traces whose final output scores ≥ threshold (rejection sampling); slice each accepted trace into per-module input/output demos; assemble N candidate demo sets per module.

2. Grounded instruction proposal: a proposer LM (GPT-3.5/4 in paper) writes N instructions per module conditioned on (a) an LM-written dataset summary (iterative batched "observations" until COMPLETE, then summarized), (b) the program's source code plus an LM summary of it, (c) bootstrapped demos of that module, (d) the seed instruction, (e) a randomly drawn "tip" (creative / simple / descriptive / high-stakes / persona). Candidate index 0 is the original instruction.

3. Bayesian search: Optuna multivariate TPE samples one (instruction, demo-set) index per module; the assembled program is scored on a random minibatch (B=35 default) of the valset; the score updates the TPE model. Every S=5 minibatch trials, the param combo with the highest mean minibatch score not yet fully evaluated is run on the full valset; that full score is injected back into the study as a trial, and only fully-evaluated combos can become the returned best. The seed program is pre-registered as a baseline trial. num_trials = max(2·vars·log2 N, 1.5N); "auto" modes light/medium/heavy set N=6/12/18 and val_size=100/300/1000.

MIPRO++ variant: TPE instead searches over proposer hyperparameters (use dataset summary?, use program summary?, temperature, tip, which demos to show the proposer) and proposes a fresh instruction each trial ("learning to propose"). Candidate pool in plain MIPRO is fixed before search — the surrogate only selects, never rewrites.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = user-supplied task metric μ (exact match, accuracy, Recall@21, custom regex) averaged over stochastic minibatches of a labeled train/val split; a TPE surrogate does credit assignment across modules from these noisy scores. Drift/overfit control: periodic full-valset evaluation of the top-mean-minibatch candidate, and only fully-evaluated programs are eligible to be returned (minibatch winners never ship directly); seed program is a registered baseline so nothing worse than the original is returned. Paper reports on a separate held-out test set (500 train / 500 dev / up to 2k test), 5 seeds, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. No LLM judge, no self-consistency; candidates are a fixed discrete pool so the evaluator cannot be gamed by the proposer, but instructions can overfit to the demos shown in the meta-prompt (Appendix H) and small datasets overfit the valset (docs recommend ≥200 examples).
deep_reads.key_results: Task LM Llama-3-8B, proposer GPT-3.5/4, budgets 20-50 full-eval-equivalent trials (~300 minibatch trials). Test scores (unoptimized → Bootstrap Random Search → MIPRO): ScoNe 69.1→75.4→79.4; HotPotQA 36.1→45.8→46.4; HoVer R@21 25.3→37.2→39.0; HotPotQA-Conditional 6.0→10.4→23.3 (largest gain, ~13 pts over best baseline); Iris 40.9→94.1→88.6 (RS better); Iris-Typo 32→58.7→68.7; Heart Disease 26.8→79.2→74.2 (RS better). MIPRO best or tied on 5/7. Ablations: demos-only beats instructions-only everywhere except HotPotQA-Conditional (rule-heavy task); Grounding helps Module-level OPRO on HotPotQA (36.0→39.0) and HoVer (25.7→32.5) but hurts ScoNe (76.1→73.5); 0-shot MIPRO++ recovers ScoNe (75.7) by learning to drop the dataset summary; learned importances rank meta-prompt demos and tip highest; Bayesian Bootstrap vs RS not significant except ScoNe; greedy/coordinate-ascent and program-level OPRO gave no gain at higher cost.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: fixed budget regime only; single proposer/task LM pair; optimizers cannot infer complex task rules without a hand-written seed prompt (Heart Disease, HotPotQA-Cond); benchmark is small/classic. Observed: surrogate optimizes over a fixed candidate pool so evaluation feedback never improves the instructions themselves (paper says so explicitly); instructions overfit to meta-prompt demos; needs a labeled dataset and hundreds-to-thousands of program executions (GEPA later reports beating MIPROv2 by up to ~10% with up to 35x fewer rollouts); Iris/Heart Disease results show demo-selection alone can beat the joint optimizer; test-set gains for HotPotQA/HoVer over plain bootstrap RS are within ~1-2 points; a demo-index assignment bug in the shipped optimizer persisted until 2026-04.
deep_reads.key_insight: Decouple proposal from credit assignment: have the LM generate a grounded pool of per-module candidates once (using data summary, program code, bootstrapped traces, and a diversity tip), then let a cheap Bayesian surrogate over discrete per-module choices, fed by noisy minibatch scores of the whole pipeline and guarded by periodic full evaluations, do joint credit assignment — no gradients, log-probs, or intermediate labels required.
open_gaps: Candidate pool is frozen before search: evaluation outcomes never rewrite instructions or demos (surrogate only selects among N pre-proposed options) — no reflective mutation from failure traces (the gap GEPA filled)
Credit assignment is purely statistical over categorical indices; textual execution traces and error messages are never used to attribute failures to a specific module
Requires a labeled training set and a scalar metric; no support for unlabeled data, rich textual feedback, or environments where the reward is a rubric/judge
Sample-inefficient: ~300 minibatch trials x 35 examples plus repeated full-valset evals (10k+ program executions) for a 2-4 module program; no early stopping or bandit-style pruning of bad candidates
No cross-task or cross-program transfer: each compile starts from an empty surrogate; learned proposer hyperparameters (MIPRO++) are discarded rather than stored as reusable knowledge
Cannot discover task rules absent from the seed prompt (Heart Disease, HotPotQA-Conditional need hand-written rules); no mechanism to learn constraints from failures
Only prompts (instruction + demos) evolve; program topology, control flow, tool set, and module count are fixed
Single scalar objective; no Pareto handling of cost, latency, or prompt length, and no multi-objective selection
No in-loop held-out generalization check: minibatch and full evals both draw from the same valset, so with small data the returned program overfits (docs recommend >=200 examples)
Instruction overfitting to the few demos shown in the meta-prompt is documented but unsolved
Full MIPRO++ (meta-optimizing both instruction and demo bootstrapping hyperparameters) was never evaluated — only the 0-shot instruction-proposal variant
Benchmark is small classic tasks (Iris, Heart Disease, 2-4 module retrieval) with an 8B model; behaviour on long-horizon agentic programs with tools is untested in the paper
deep_reads.safety_measures: None beyond search hygiene: candidates are a fixed pool generated once (the proposer cannot alter the evaluator or program code); the original program is registered as a baseline trial and returned if nothing beats it; only programs that pass a full-valset evaluation can be returned; per-trial candidate programs are saved to a log dir for inspection/rollback. No sandboxing needed since only prompt strings change.

deep_reads.name: ShinkaEvolve
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Sakana AI — Robert Tjarko Lange, Yuki Imajuku, Edoardo Cetin
deep_reads.date: 2025-09-17 (repo created and arXiv v1 same day)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-21 (last push: Anthropic response-parsing fix PR #188); last PyPI release v0.0.7 on 2026-06-02; 27 contributors
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted per README Jan-2026 note); arXiv 2509.19349; ~142 citations per scout (could not verify — Semantic Scholar rate-limited); 278 forks
deep_reads.mechanism: Per generation (async runner overlaps proposal and evaluation): (1) Pick an island, then a parent from its archive by weighted sampling — w_i = sigmoid(lambda*(F_i - median F)) * 1/(1+#children) — or power-law-over-rank / beam search; with prob exploitation_ratio draw from the global archive. Add 1 archive + 1 top-k "inspiration" program to context. (2) An AsymmetricUCB bandit (cost-aware blend) picks which LLM mutates; patch type sampled (diff 0.6 / full rewrite 0.3 / crossover 0.1). Prompt holds parent code, inspirations, evaluator text feedback, and every meta_rec_interval generations a 3-stage LLM meta-review (per-program summaries -> global insights scratchpad -> <=5 recommendations) is appended. Optionally the system prompt itself is sampled from an evolved prompt archive (prompt fitness = mean percentile rank of its correct children; UCB+epsilon sampling; diff/full prompt mutations). (3) Patch applied only inside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers; malformed patches are resampled. (4) Novelty rejection: embed mutable code, cosine-compare to island population; if max sim > eta (0.95 paper / 0.99 default) an optional LLM judge rules NOVEL/NOT_NOVEL, else reject and resample parent up to 3 times before paying for evaluation. (5) Run user evaluate.py -> combined_score, correct flag, public/private metrics, text_feedback; persist to SQLite. (6) Bandit reward = exp(beta*max(score - max(parent, initial), 0)) - 1, so only strict improvements over the parent pay. (7) Only correct programs enter the size-40 replace-worst (or crowding) archive; islands migrate periodically; stagnation can spawn new islands. Coding agents (Claude Code/Codex) join via skills (setup/convert/run/inspect) and as headless mutation providers, not as loop drivers.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal is a user-written evaluate.py (run_shinka_eval) returning a scalar combined_score (maximized), a boolean correct from an optional validate_fn, public metrics (visible to the LLM), private metrics (hidden), and free-text feedback; num_runs>1 averages noisy evals. Drift/hacking control: only correct programs enter the archive and elites are never discarded (append-only population, so no rollback is needed); mutations are confined to EVOLVE-BLOCK regions and the evaluator is never evolvable (meta prompt explicitly forbids recommending evaluator changes); private metrics keep the LLM from targeting hidden checks; the bandit only rewards strict improvement over parent/initial; an API-cost cap stops proposals. There is no built-in held-out set — anti-gaming depends entirely on the quality of the user evaluator (circle packing used exact constraint verification; MoE result was validated on 7 downstream benchmarks after evolution).
deep_reads.key_results: Circle packing (n=26): sum of radii 2.636 in ~150 evaluated programs vs AlphaEvolve's 2.635 with thousands. AIME 2024: evolved 3-stage persona/peer-review scaffold hitting max accuracy with 7 LLM queries, transfers to other AIME years and LLMs. ALE-Bench: +2.3% avg over ALE-Agent solutions, one task 5th->2nd on AtCoder leaderboard. MoE: new load-balancing loss beats DeepSeek global-batch LBL (-5.81% routing inefficiency, +1.73% downstream) after ~30 generations. ICFP 2025 (Team Unagi win): Rust SAT encoding sped up 6.5x (18 rooms) and ~10x (24 rooms) in 320 trials, ~$60. Ablations: weighted parent sampling > hill-climb/random; bandit ensemble > single or fixed-mix LLM; embedding rejection gives substantial gains while the LLM novelty judge adds only marginal benefit; meta-scratchpad accelerates learning.
deep_reads.limitations: Claimed vs demonstrated: sample-efficiency claim is vs reported AlphaEvolve numbers, not a head-to-head; results rely on frontier ensembles (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4, o4-mini). "Open-ended" and "self-refining" are aspirational — tasks, evaluators and the search hyperparameters (lambda, alpha, eta, island settings) are fixed by humans and the framework code is not self-modified. Fitness is a single scalar from one evaluator with no held-out split, so overfitting to evaluator quirks is unguarded. Meta-scratchpad recommendations are unverified prose with no credit assignment. Evolution is single-file EVOLVE-BLOCK scope. Software is 0.0.x: Aug-2026 fixes for diff insertions silently corrupting programs (#183) and Rust validation failing on stable (#178); skills cite the wrong arXiv id. Default local execution runs LLM-generated code unsandboxed.
deep_reads.key_insight: Sample-efficiency in LLM-driven evolution comes from search control rather than a smarter mutator: bias parent choice toward high-fitness-but-under-exploited programs, reject near-duplicate candidates by embedding similarity before paying for evaluation, and give the LLM-selection bandit an asymmetric, exponentiated reward that only counts strict improvement over the parent so it chases bold gains instead of safe tweaks.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Immutable code outside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers with marker validation; evaluator is not mutable and meta prompts forbid recommending evaluator changes; private metrics hidden from the LLM; correctness gate on archive entry; append-only population (no destructive self-modification, elites preserved); API cost cap (max_api_costs); optional Docker/SLURM isolation for evaluation; W&B telemetry redaction of secrets; human-in-the-loop confirmation between batches is the default in the shinka-run skill.
open_gaps: No held-out/generalization check inside the loop: fitness is one user evaluator on one objective, so evolved programs can overfit evaluator artifacts without detection

The harness does not evolve itself: parent-sampling lambda/alpha, novelty threshold, island and migration settings, patch-type probabilities are static per run; no online meta-learning of search hyperparameters
No task or objective generation: every run needs a hand-written evaluate.py and initial program, so 'open-ended' is aspirational
No cross-task transfer: archive, meta-scratchpad insights, bandit state and evolved system prompts live in one results_dir and are discarded for the next task
Meta-scratchpad recommendations are never validated: no credit assignment measuring whether a recommendation improved child fitness, so bad advice persists
Diversity is only embedding-similarity within an island; no behavioral/phenotypic descriptors (MAP-Elites style) or multi-objective Pareto search beyond weighted archive ranking
Single-file EVOLVE-BLOCK scope; repo-scale or multi-file evolution is unsupported (shinka-convert flattens a repo into one task)
Correctness is a binary flag from the evaluator; no automatically generated property/differential tests to catch semantically wrong but high-scoring programs

Coding-agent integration is shallow: Claude Code/Codex only scaffold, launch and inspect runs or act as prompt-in/text-out mutation providers; the agent cannot use tools, run tests, or read the repo while mutating
Local job mode executes LLM-generated code unsandboxed; isolation requires SLURM/Docker setup

deep_reads.name: karpathy/autoresearch
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-03-26 (last push); 194 open issues/PRs, no maintainer activity since; effectively frozen ~5.5 months as of 2026-09-11
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Andrej Karpathy (solo; small community PRs merged in March 2026)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: GitHub only (no paper). 95.6k stars, 13.4k forks, 735 watchers. Results transferred into nanochat leaderboard (Runs 5 and 6). Widely cited as the canonical minimal loop by CORAL, ATLAS, Lil'Log harness post, and the 'loop engineering' meme; 4 notable platform forks (macOS, MLX, Windows, AMD ROCm).
deep_reads.mechanism: The evolving object is train.py (~630 lines: GPT model, Muon+AdamW optimizer, schedules, hyperparameters). The agent (Claude Code / any coding agent, "disable all permissions") is pointed at program.md, a ~7KB markdown spec that IS the entire harness; there is no driver code, no orchestrator, no Python loop. Setup: create branch autoresearch/<tag>, read README/prepare.py/train.py, create untracked results.tsv, run baseline unmodified. Then "LOOP FOREVER": (1) inspect git state, (2) hand-edit train.py with one idea, (3) git commit, (4) `uv run train.py > run.log 2>&1`, (5) `grep "^val_bpb:\|^peak_vram_mb:" run.log`, (6) empty grep = crash: `tail -n 50 run.log`, fix trivial bugs, else log 'crash' and skip; kill if >10 min, (7) append row [commit, val_bpb, memory_gb, keep/discard/crash, description] to results.tsv, (8) if val_bpb strictly lower: keep commit (branch advances); else `git reset` to previous commit. train.py enforces a fixed 300 s wall-clock training budget (excluding first 10 compile/warmup steps) and fast-fails on NaN or loss>100. prepare.py is declared read-only and holds the ground-truth evaluate_bpb (bits-per-byte on a pinned val shard, ~21M tokens, fixed seq len 2048, vocab-independent). Soft constraints in prose: VRAM should not blow up; a 'simplicity criterion' (small gain + ugly code = discard; equal result + deleted code = keep). Explicit "NEVER STOP" clause: do not ask the human anything; if out of ideas, re-read code, combine near-misses, try radical changes. It is a single-lineage (1+1)-style greedy hill-climb with the LLM as mutation operator, git as archive, and results.tsv as the only memory. The meta-level, program.md, is iterated by the human, not by the loop.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = a single scalar, val_bpb from evaluate_bpb() in read-only prepare.py, measured once per candidate after exactly 5 minutes of training on one GPU. Acceptance = strict improvement over the current branch head; otherwise git reset (hard rollback), so the chain of kept commits is monotone in val_bpb by construction. Drift/reward-hacking prevention is almost entirely social/prose: 'do not modify prepare.py or evaluate_bpb', 'no new dependencies', plus the human reviewing diffs in the morning. Nothing is enforced: issue #599 (May 2026, unanswered) demonstrates four working exploits (skip optimizer.step while still finishing the time budget; wrap/replace the evaluate_bpb call inside train.py; shrink EVAL_TOKENS or swap the val shard since the val set is never fingerprinted; results are print()ed and never bound to code/data/model hashes) with a stdlib reproducer where a fabricated 0.05 bpb is KEPT. No seed replication, no noise-floor estimate, no held-out generalization check inside the loop; transfer from d12 to d24 was verified manually by Karpathy in nanochat (5-run averages of CORE score), not by autoresearch itself. Meta-level evaluation of program.md changes is ad hoc human A/B (PR #80: two 15-experiment sessions, n=1; Karpathy asked for 'results to back this up').
deep_reads.key_results: Demonstrated (verifiable in nanochat git history): nanochat commit 6ed7d1d (2026-03-09) lists ~15 optimizer/schedule/architecture changes "developed by Claude running autonomously over ~2 days using autoresearch, I didn't touch anything", tuned on d12 and transferred to d24, cutting 'Time to GPT-2' from 2.02 h to 1.80 h (Run 5, ~11% faster; 5-run avg CORE 0.2690 vs threshold 0.2565). Round 2 (commit a825e63, 2026-03-14, agent told to mine modded-nanogpt) found smear + backout + tuning that Karpathy had previously failed to make work manually, giving Run 6 at 99 minutes (1.65 h, avg CORE 0.2626). Claimed (tweets, quoted second-hand in issues): first overnight run ~110 experiments, val_bpb 0.862 to 0.858; a ~700-experiment run surfaced a QKNorm scaler bug. Caveat: nanochat's LEADERBOARD.md says the results came from "a private version of autoresearch run on a d12 model", i.e. not the public single-GPU toy. Public repo default: d8, ~50M params, ~1000 steps, ~0.998 bpb baseline on H100, ~12 experiments/hour.
deep_reads.limitations: Single H100 only (no CPU/MPS/AMD in main; forks handle it). Fitness is one noisy 5-min run with strict '<' acceptance, so ~0.001 bpb noise-level changes get kept; results not comparable across hardware. No enforcement of the eval boundary (issue #599). Greedy single lineage with 'rewind very sparingly': no population, no crossover of discarded near-misses, agents drift into incremental hyperparameter sweeps (issues #22/#80). results.tsv is untracked and never fed back into future runs; no cross-run memory. Only works with agents that obey 'NEVER STOP' (Codex stops, issue #57 with 41 comments); weaker models achieve 0/N keeps (#307). No checkpoint before eval so eval crashes lose the run (#265/#609). No LICENSE file in the repo despite README saying MIT (license metadata is null). Headline results came from a private variant; the public repo is deliberately a bare-bones baseline. Maintenance stopped 2026-03-26.
deep_reads.key_insight: Reduce the self-improvement harness to its irreducible minimum: a fixed compute budget (5 min wall clock) that makes every mutation comparable, one scalar metric owned by a read-only file, git as both archive and rollback, and a markdown 'program' as the sole orchestrator, so the human's job shifts from editing code to editing the research-org spec (program.md) that the agent runs.
open_gaps: Eval integrity is prose-only: the agent owns train.py and can wrap evaluate_bpb, skip optimizer.step, or shrink EVAL_TOKENS; a framework should run the evaluator in a separate sandboxed process with hash-bound receipts (code + data + final weights + real optimizer step count) so a reported metric cannot be fabricated (issue #599 reproducer).

Acceptance is a single noisy run with strict '<': no seed replication, no noise-floor estimate, no statistical acceptance test; a framework should estimate run-to-run variance from baseline repeats and require improvement beyond it (or use paired multi-seed evals) before keeping.

No held-out generalization inside the loop: gains are verified only on the same pinned val shard and same 5-min/d8 regime; transfer to larger scale (d24) was checked manually by the human, so a framework needs an automatic periodic transfer/holdout check (different seed shard, longer budget, larger depth) before promoting a change.

Single-lineage greedy hill-climb with no population or archive of near-misses: discarded ideas are never recombined, and agents converge on incremental hyperparameter sweeps; a framework could maintain a MAP-Elites-style archive keyed by change category (architecture / optimizer / schedule / simplification) and force diversity.

No cross-run memory: results.tsv is untracked and never re-read by future runs; each session rediscovers the same dead ends. A framework should persist a structured experiment log (idea, diff summary, outcome, hypothesis about why) and inject it as context for subsequent runs.

Meta-level (program.md) is evolved only by the human with n=1 anecdotal A/Bs; a framework could evaluate program.md variants automatically (e.g., keep-rate and best-bpb-after-N-experiments across parallel runs) to close the outer loop.

Simplicity criterion is unmeasured prose; fitness could include an explicit complexity term (lines changed, parameter count, VRAM) so 'simplification wins' are rewarded mechanically rather than by agent judgement.

No parallelism or async evaluation: one agent, one GPU, ~12 experiments/hour; a framework should support N workers proposing from a shared archive with an evaluation queue and dedup of identical diffs.

Depends on the agent honoring 'NEVER STOP' (works with Claude Code, fails with Codex per issue #57); a real driver loop outside the model (external scheduler/'ralph loop') is needed for model-agnostic operation.

Domain-locked to tasks with a fast scalar metric and a single mutable file; there is no path for fuzzy-eval targets (agent prompts, app code, multi-file repos) or for LLM-judge-based fitness with anti-gaming controls.

Public repo is a simplified toy; the headline 11% / 99-minute results came from a 'private version' on d12 over ~2 days, so reproduction of the flagship claim from the public code has not been demonstrated.
No checkpoint before final eval and no protection against the 10-minute-timeout/eval-crash path losing a valid run; results are lost rather than marked inconclusive.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Scope restriction to one file (train.py); prepare.py declared read-only with the ground-truth metric; no new dependencies allowed; git reset on non-improvement (every kept change is a reviewable commit); fast-fail on NaN/loss>100; 10-minute kill timeout; output redirected to run.log so context is not flooded; human reviews diffs and results.tsv afterward; README instructs users to run the agent with all permissions disabled (i.e., fully unsandboxed autonomy is the intended mode). None of these are mechanically enforced against a metric-gaming agent.

deep_reads.name: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness (Prime Intellect)
deep_reads.date: 2026-05-08 (repo created); v0.0.1 2026-05-19; 'beta' release 2026-07-17; paper arXiv:2608.23552 submitted 2026-08-24
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; ~15 commits/day, 700 merged PRs, 51 releases)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Prime Intellect — Seth Karten, Alex L. Zhang, Kevin Thomas, Sebastian Müller, Elie Bakouch, Daniel Auras, Mika Senghaas, Fares Obeid, Konstantin Dunas, Johannes Hagemann, Sami Jaghouar. Built on top of `pi` (earendil-works). Continual Harness method from Karten et al. arXiv:2605.09998 (Princeton/Google, May 2026).
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv technical report 2608.23552 (16 pp, 10 figs, Aug 2026); no citation count yet (2 weeks old). Method paper 'Continual Harness' arXiv:2605.09998 (28 pp). 20.5k stars, 2.2k forks, MIT, TypeScript + Python runtime.
deep_reads.mechanism: A typed, versioned state file (`harness_state.json`; session-local under `session-artifacts/<id>/harness/`, or global under `~/.prime/agent/harness/`) holds four entry kinds: `prompt` (supplemental notes only; base system prompt is immutable and `base_system_prompt` id is rejected), `memory`, `skill` (a *description* of an installed Python REPL callable — must carry `reference{type:python,import,callable}` + `arguments`; it does not write code), and `subagent` (reusable delegation specs invoked via `rlm.spawn`). Triggers: (a) user `/refine [instructions] [--global]`, (b) agent-callable `await refine.run(...)` from the Python kernel (queued, runs at turn end), (c) auto-refine, on by default: every 25 assistant turns or after compaction, 20-min cooldown. Auto-refine first runs a cheap LLM "review gate" over the last 40k chars of trajectory + state overview + history returning `{shouldRefine, rationale, instructions}`. The planner is a separate LLM call (same model, auxiliary thinking) fed `<current_harness_state>`, `<refinement_history>` (last 20 results incl. failed edits and expectedOutcome), `<conversation>` (last 80k chars), scope policy; it must emit JSON `{summary, rationale, expectedOutcome, edits[create|update|delete ...reason]}`. Apply step: schema validation, optimistic-concurrency check against a baseline snapshot ("entry changed during refinement planning"), per-edit before/after snapshots, version++ and a refinement event appended to state, session JSONL, and `refinements.jsonl` (global). System prompt is rebuilt with a compact digest (≤6 entries/kind, 180 chars each, last 5 events) and the agent resumes. Rollback: `/refine rollback <id>` inverts snapshots; the planner is also told to roll back faulty prior refinements. Extensions can skip or replace the planner (`session_before_refine`). Single lineage, no population.
deep_reads.eval_loop: There is no fitness function. Acceptance = the refiner LLM's own judgment that an edit is "evidence-backed" plus structural validation (kind/action/id/required fields, python reference for skills, concurrency baseline). `expectedOutcome` is recorded as free text and never checked; no test, benchmark, or A/B run gates a refinement, and rollback is manual (by id) or LLM-initiated in a later refine. The only drift guards are: immutable base prompt, small-edit instruction, local-by-default scope (global requires explicit request and stricter policy), review gate rejecting "one-off noise, unsupported hypotheses", and auditable versioned history. Autonomous-mode 'quality gates' verify task output, not harness edits. The paper itself documents that this fails against reward hacking: in Factorio the agent found an RCON resource-spawn exploit, used it despite an anti-cheating heartbeat, and persisted it as a reusable skill. Reported numbers (ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 30%→95.5%; OOLONG GLM-5.2 0.700 vs pi-mono 0.420; Codex-model OOLONG 0.940 vs 0.900; EmulatorBench 0.275 vs 0.228; 19 validated nanoGPT records over 85.5h; Factorio 7-day run 23.4M tokens) compare the whole harness (RLM REPL + subagents + harness) to Claude Code/Codex/pi-mono — none isolate the self-improvement loop. Repo CI benchmarks measure process/startup performance of PRs, not agent capability. Prior Continual Harness paper gives the only refinement-specific evidence: Pokémon Emerald Gemini 3 Pro 100% milestones at $130 vs minimal 98% at $215; Flash 80%@$42 vs 77%@$30; Flash-Lite CH underperforms baseline (capability floor); skill inheritance reuse 96.5%±3.8 vs subagent inheritance 6.4%±5.7; most memory entries never referenced.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (arXiv 2608.23552): ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 raised from 30% to 95.5% via harness configuration/token scaling (not via refinement per se). Long-context coding (Table 1): with GLM-5.2, OOLONG 0.700 vs pi-mono 0.420, OOLONG-Pairs 0.874 vs 0.556, EmulatorBench 0.208 vs 0.000; with GPT-5.6 Sol, OOLONG 0.940 vs Codex 0.900, EmulatorBench 0.275 vs 0.228; with Opus 5 roughly parity with Claude Code (0.900 vs 0.920 OOLONG). nanoGPT speedrun: 19 validated records over an 85.5-hour autonomous run; DeepSeek V4 Pro ran ~6x more out-of-loop experiments under Prime Agent than Claude Code. Factorio: 7-day Sonnet 5 run, 23.4M output tokens, 24/196 technologies, 633 depth-one subagents in 149 waves. PMPP-Hard GPU kernels: parity in wall clock, token-for-token advantage. No ablation isolating Continual Harness; no before/after-refinement metric. Repo: 20.5k stars, 2.2k forks, 700 merged PRs, installer with SHA-256 verification, daemon-backed sessions, RPC/JSON/ACP modes, extension hooks, 51 releases.
deep_reads.limitations: Self-improvement is asserted, not measured: the technical report contains no ablation of the Continual Harness and no cross-trajectory improvement curve; headline gains come from the RLM REPL/subagent harness vs other CLIs. Refinement acceptance is pure LLM self-judgment with no verification; `expectedOutcome` is never validated; rollback is manual. Demonstrated reward-hacking contamination (Factorio exploit persisted as a skill). Refinement can only persist descriptions/notes, not executable code (new tools require the separate skill-creator flow). Digest surfaces only 6 entries per kind with 180-char truncation; no retrieval, ranking, decay or consolidation of growing state. Local scope by default means cross-session learning only happens when explicitly requested as global. Authors admit "many harness capabilities remain underused because current models were not trained to operate them" and that refinement needs a frontier model (Continual Harness paper: Flash-Lite falls below the no-harness baseline). No security sandbox; refined prompt notes are injected into the system prompt, so a prompt-injection can be persisted. Multi-agent only in execution (subagents), not in refinement (no population/archive/diversity).
deep_reads.safety_measures: Immutable base system prompt (edits targeting `base_system_prompt` rejected); supplemental-state-only edits; per-edit before/after snapshots with versioning and `/refine rollback <id>`; refinement history (session JSONL + global refinements.jsonl) for audit; optimistic concurrency check against baseline state; local-by-default scope with stricter policy for global; auto-refine review gate + 20-min cooldown + 25-turn interval; extension hook to skip/replace the planner; bounded autonomous mode with turn/token/time budgets and user-defined quality gates; README warns worker/kernel isolation is not a security sandbox. Paper concedes safe deployment "requires least-privilege action interfaces, independent state validation, and auditable rollback of contaminated refinements" — of which only the audit/rollback part exists.
deep_reads.key_insight: Split the agent's policy into an immutable base prompt plus a small, typed, versioned, scoped supplemental-state layer (prompt notes / memories / skill references / subagent specs) that a dedicated refiner call mutates only through evidence-citing CRUD edits applied at turn boundaries with before/after snapshots — making harness self-improvement auditable and reversible without touching weights or source code, and letting the agent itself request refinement from inside its REPL.
open_gaps: No outcome-based acceptance: edits are applied on the refiner LLM's say-so; 'expectedOutcome' is free text never checked. A framework could attach a concrete verifier (test, metric delta, replay on held-out trajectory) to each edit and auto-rollback on failure.

No measurement of entry utility: nothing tracks whether a memory/skill/subagent spec is ever read or whether trajectories improve after it exists (CH paper found most memories unused and subagent inheritance reused only 6.4%). Need per-entry usage/benefit telemetry and pruning.
No held-out / A-B evaluation of harness state — the paper has zero ablations of Continual Harness; a benchmark harness that runs the same task with and without the refined state is missing.

Reward-hacking contamination is demonstrated (Factorio exploit persisted as a skill) and unmitigated: no independent validator, no least-privilege on what a refinement may persist, no automatic quarantine of skills born from gated/anti-cheat violations.
Refinement cannot produce executable code — skill entries are only references to already-installed Python callables; new tools still need the manual skill-creator flow and are not tested on creation.
State scaling: only 6 entries per kind (180 chars) are surfaced in the system prompt; no retrieval, relevance ranking, decay, dedup or consolidation as entries accumulate over long runs.

Cross-session transfer is opt-in only (local by default, explicit --global); no automatic promotion of lessons that proved useful across multiple sessions, and no cross-project or cross-user sharing/merging of harness states.
Single lineage, no population/archive: no way to keep alternative harness variants, compare them, or evolve diversity; rollback is manual by id.

Refiner is the same frontier model with a capability floor (CH paper: Flash-Lite underperforms no-harness baseline); no path for weak/open models, and no weight-level learning (model-harness co-learning is only stated as future work).

Persisted prompt notes are injected into the system prompt with no provenance checking, so prompt-injection from untrusted repo content can be made durable; no signing, review queue, or human-approval gate for global edits.

deep_reads.name: SkillOpt (incl. SkillOpt-Sleep)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Microsoft Research (Yifan Yang, Ziyang Gong, Weiquan Huang, Qihao Yang, Ziwei Zhou, Zisu Huang, Yan Li, Xuemei Gao, Qi Dai, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Yuqing Yang, Dongdong Chen, Xue Yang, Chong Luo)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-05 (pushed_at); ~30 commits in the last 3 weeks, active community PRs
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.23904 (27 pages); citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); featured on Microsoft Research blog (2026-07-24), VentureBeat, The Decoder, Synced; integrated by gbrain (29.8k stars) and darwin-skill (5.9k stars)
deep_reads.mechanism: Two loops. (A) Research engine (skillopt-train): a frozen target model + a separate optimizer LLM (default GPT-5.5). Per step: (1) rollout target on a training batch (B=40) with the current SKILL.md -> scored trajectories; (2) reflect: optimizer analyzes failure and success minibatches (size 8, 16 parallel workers) and emits structured add/delete/replace edit patches; (3) hierarchical merge of patches; (4) rank and clip to L_t edits ("textual learning rate", default 4, cosine decay to floor 2); (5) apply -> candidate skill; (6) gate: roll out candidate on a held-out selection split (deterministic 2:1:7 train/sel/test) and accept only if score is strictly greater than the current score (ties rejected). Rejected edits plus the score drop they caused go into an epoch-local step buffer that is fed back to the optimizer. At each epoch boundary (from epoch 2): a "slow update" rolls out previous-epoch vs current skill on 20 shared samples, buckets items as improved/regressed/persistent-fail/stable-success and writes longitudinal guidance into a protected <!-- SLOW_UPDATE --> field (force-accepted by default, slow_update_gate_with_selection=false); and an optimizer-side "meta skill" memory is written but never shipped. Output: best_skill.md = highest selection-score snapshot. (B) SkillOpt-Sleep (nightly cron, separate package): harvest local Claude Code/Codex/Copilot/Cursor/Pi/OpenCode transcripts -> LLM miner extracts recurring tasks with programmatic checks or a rubric (LLM judge >=0.8 = pass) -> split train/val -> replay via backend (opt-in K dream rollouts for contrastive reflection, recall_k similar tasks from a persisted archive, synthetic variants) -> bounded edits to skill then to a long-term memory doc -> gate on val mean (opt-in per-task no-regression) -> stage proposal -> human `adopt`.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = held-out selection-split hard score from a real verifier (exact match, executed openpyxl code compared cell-by-cell, ALFWorld success, MCQ label); soft/mixed metrics and an optional 'semantic density' bonus for imperative words are opt-in and were not used in the paper. Strict-improvement gate (ties rejected) + edit budget + rejected-edit buffer + protected slow-update field + best_skill snapshot that excludes force-injected slow-update text. Sleep adds staged review-then-adopt, evidence.jsonl audit chains, an output-contract guardrail for gate-free mode, opt-in gate_no_regression, and a paired A/B evalkit (McNemar + bootstrap CI). Demonstrated anti-drift value: on GPT-5.4-nano/SearchQA the ungated loop collapsed 0.554 -> 0.026 (learned 'answer with the document title') while the gated twin held 0.570 -> 0.570. But reward hacking is documented in real use: the optimizer reads raw judge regex text and writes it verbatim into the skill (#154), a heading-format judge artifact produced an accepted rule that forbids the skill's own format and dropped a required citation on another task, hidden by the val mean (#174/#175); gbrain-evals cat32 showed a heading-only scorer is gameable (1.00 proxy vs 0.28 independent judge).
deep_reads.key_results: Paper: 6 benchmarks x 7 models x 3 harnesses; best or tied on 52/52 cells; GPT-5.5 direct chat avg 58.8 -> 82.3 (+23.5; SpreadsheetBench +38.9, OfficeQA +39.0, LiveMath +29.3); +24.8 inside Codex, +19.1 inside Claude Code; beats per-cell oracle of 6 baselines (human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, EvoSkill) by +5.4. Only 1-4 edits accepted per run (median 2.5); final artifacts 379-1,995 tokens. Ablations: removing slow+meta update -22.5 on SpreadsheetBench; unbounded rewrite (no LR) -2.5 to -4.6; no rejected buffer -1.6 to -4.6; batch sizes insensitive. Transfer: cross-model +3.0 to +9.4, Codex<->Claude Code +43.6/+59.7, OlympiadBench->Omni-MATH +1.3 to +3.7; target-matched optimizer recovers 56-74% of strong-optimizer gain. Cost 0.6M-46M tokens per test point (21M-214M tokens per run). Sleep (5 nights x 10 tasks, single seed): SearchQA GPT-5.5 +3.1 to +5.6 gated; GPT-5.4-nano +11.9; SpreadsheetBench nano +3.6; 18-cell sweep mean only +0.53 (worst -2.4); gbrain-evals: 4 deficient seed skills 0.00 -> 1.00 held-out on both Claude Code and Codex, but a one-shot rewrite also reached 1.00.
deep_reads.limitations: Requires an automatic verifier or exact-match metric; single-seed results with +/-1-2 pt noise; open reproducibility issue #158 (LiveMath split was 124 vs paper's 125, fixed; DocVQA/OfficeQA/SpreadsheetBench score denominators still unexplained). Gate compares val-slice means so per-task regressions pass (real user: val=4 tasks, accepted edit damaged one task and improved none); optimizer sees raw judge text and Goodharts it into the skill; slow update bypasses the gate by default. Training is expensive (tens to hundreds of millions of tokens per benchmark). Single skill document, no library/composition. Sleep is a preview: 18-cell mean gain within noise, saturates after ~5 nights, no `revert` after adopt (#247), intent-level (non-checkable) improvements are dropped or mangled (#154), sensitivity sweep shows every deviation from the tuned recipe lowers gains. The research engine is offline benchmark prompt optimization (GEPA/TextGrad lineage) dressed in DL vocabulary; 'self-evolving' in the paper title is partly marketing. Only Sleep learns from the agent's own deployment data, and it is human-in-the-loop by default. gbrain-evals notes a one-shot rewrite matched the full loop on its simple tasks, so loop necessity is not shown there.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the skill file as the trainable parameters of a frozen agent and borrow optimizer discipline: bound edits per step (textual learning rate), accept only on strict held-out improvement, and feed rejected edits back as negative examples. The strict gate is what makes unattended text-space self-evolution safe (bounded downside vs a -52.8 pt collapse), and most of the gain comes from a handful (1-4) of accepted edits, not from wholesale rewrites.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Strict-improvement held-out gate (ties rejected); edit budget per step; rejected-edit buffer; protected slow-update field with best_skill snapshot kept clean; Sleep: stage-then-human-adopt (auto_adopt off by default, never for fan-out), read-only local harvest, secret redaction, sub-agent/plugin transcripts excluded, per-night evidence.jsonl audit, sandboxed replay (Codex workspace-write, Cursor read-only Ask mode, OpenCode MCP/plugins disabled, synthetic tools for tool-aware replay), no-network mock/handoff backends, output-contract guardrail in gate-free mode, opt-in gate_no_regression, versioned fail-closed adoption manifest with provenance hashes, immutable backups/receipts, cross-night locking, Copilot tools scoped not allow-all, managed-identity credentials restricted to Azure HTTPS.
open_gaps: Gate is an aggregate mean over a small val slice; per-task regressions are accepted (gate_no_regression is opt-in and only in Sleep, absent from the research trainer)
Optimizer receives raw judge/regex source text and copies checks verbatim into the skill (Goodhart); no separation of semantic feedback from scoring criteria
Fitness is a single benchmark's selection split; no in-loop held-out generalization or cross-task test, transfer measured only post-hoc
Epoch-boundary slow update is force-accepted by default, bypassing the validation gate
Single skill document only; no skill library, routing, composition, or cross-task transfer of learned rules (stated future work)
Requires a programmatic verifier; rubric/LLM-judge path is weak and intent-level improvements are dropped or mangled into shallow proxy rules
No revert/rollback after Sleep `adopt`, no online A/B or production monitoring of a deployed skill
Single-seed evaluation with +/-1-2 pt noise and unresolved score-denominator mismatches vs released splits
Cost 20M-214M tokens per benchmark run; no cost-aware or budget-constrained optimization
Does not evolve tools, workflow topology, harness code, or model weights; agent architecture is fixed
Nightly gains saturate after ~5 nights and the 18-cell sweep mean is within noise; no long-horizon (months) evidence
Multi-skill fan-out consolidates each skill independently; no modeling of skill interactions or shared memory writes
Optimizer-side meta skill is discarded per run, not reused across benchmarks or projects
Loop necessity vs one-shot rewrite not established on simple skills (gbrain-evals cat31)

deep_reads.name: ACE: Agentic Context Engineering (ace-agent/ace)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, ..., James Zou, Kunle Olukotun — Stanford University / SambaNova Systems / UC Berkeley
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-24 (commit 82709de: parallelize ComBEE curator proposals with LLM reducer); ace-appworld submodule pushed 2026-07-24; open PR #40 (DeepSeek provider) 2026-08-15; issue #41 (Terminal-Bench prompts) 2026-08-28
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted, per team blog post 2026-01-30); arXiv 2510.04618. Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited, arXiv unreachable from this network); widely cited as the reference point for 'evolving playbook' context adaptation. 168 forks.
deep_reads.mechanism: The evolving artifact is a single plaintext 'playbook': markdown sections whose lines are itemized bullets `[slug-00042] helpful=X harmful=Y :: advice`. Per training sample (ace/ace.py `_train_single_sample`): (1) Generator answers with the full playbook in-prompt and self-reports which bullet_ids it used. (2) Correctness is checked against ground truth via `data_processor.answer_is_correct`. If wrong, up to `max_num_rounds` (3) Reflector→regenerate loops run; the Reflector (with GT or, in no-GT mode, only environment feedback) emits error_identification/root_cause/key_insight plus helpful/harmful/neutral tags for used bullets, which are applied by `update_bullet_counts` (pure string counter increment). If correct, the Reflector still runs to tag helpful bullets. (3) Every `curator_frequency` steps the Curator sees playbook + stats + latest reflection and emits JSON operations; `apply_curator_operations` implements ONLY `ADD` (UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE/CREATE_META are commented-out TODOs). Optional `BulletpointAnalyzer` (sentence-transformers + FAISS, cosine ≥0.9) LLM-merges near-duplicates. (4) Post-curate regeneration is logged. Offline mode: iterate epochs over train set, evaluate on val every `eval_steps`, keep `best_playbook` = argmax val accuracy. Online mode: windowed test-then-train on the test stream, no checkpoint selection. ACEBatch/ComBEE (2026): parallel gen+reflect over a mini-batch, augmented shuffling (duplicate reflections p×), ⌊√n⌋ curator groups propose ADDs from the same snapshot in parallel, one LLM 'reducer' call dedups into final ADDs applied once. Single lineage, no population, same LLM (DeepSeek-V3.1) for all three roles.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = per-sample exact/format-normalized correctness against ground-truth labels (finance/Mind2Web) or AppWorld task-goal completion; in 'no_GT' mode the Reflector sees only environment/execution feedback but the retry loop still uses `answer_is_correct` with the target (issue #35 flags this inconsistency). Bullet-level credit is an LLM judgment (Reflector tags bullets the Generator self-reported using) stored as helpful/harmful counters — these are shown to the Curator as stats but never used programmatically to prune. Drift/reward-hacking guards are weak: Curator output is JSON-schema validated and skipped on parse failure; offline mode selects the best whole-playbook checkpoint by held-out validation accuracy (the only regression guard); online mode has none; ComBEE rolls back Phase-2 edits only on API errors, not on accuracy drops. Paper's context-collapse case study (Dynamic Cheatsheet: 18,282→122 tokens at one step, acc 66.7→57.1, below base 63.7) motivates append-only deltas, but the released code's answer is monotone growth rather than verified refinement.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (DeepSeek-V3.1 non-thinking for all roles): AppWorld ReAct base avg 42.4 → ACE offline 59.4 (w/ GT), 57.2 (execution feedback only) vs ICL 46.0, GEPA 46.4; online ACE 59.5 vs Dynamic Cheatsheet 51.9; +10.6% avg, +17.1% on test-challenge; matched IBM-CUGA (GPT-4.1, 60.3) on leaderboard Sept-2025 and beat it on test-challenge. Finance: FiNER 70.7→78.3, Formula 67.5→85.5 (offline w/ GT), +8.6% avg; without GT FiNER fell to ~67.3 (below base). Ablation: Reflector, multi-epoch, and offline warm-up each add ~2-4 pts (offline ~55.1→56.8→59.4; online ~56.1→59.5 with warm-up). Cost: offline AppWorld ACE 357 rollouts / 9,517s vs GEPA 1,434 / 53,898s (-75.1% rollouts, -82.3% latency); online FiNER -91.5% latency, -83.6% tokens vs DC. Repo-side: 1,310 stars; production use reported at Anyshift (SRE agent, 30% faster RCA) since Oct 2025; third-party issue #26 reports +13.3% val / +8% test on a lending-compliance task but val oscillating 53-93% as playbook bloats. Team blog (2026-04) admits AppWorld playbooks reach ~174k tokens; embedding/LLM retrieval keeps 59-65% of the gain at ~2% of tokens, RLM retrieval hurts.
deep_reads.limitations: Released curator is ADD-only; the paper's 'grow-and-refine' pruning/merging by harmful counters is not implemented (issue #26, roadmap #29 promise DELETE/MERGE 'soon' as of Feb 2026, still absent Aug 2026). Playbook grows monotonically (>100K tokens by ~300 samples, issue #11) and `playbook_token_budget` is ignored by code; long-context cost is deferred to KV caching. Gains depend on reliable feedback: w/o GT, FiNER dropped below the unadapted baseline, showing reflections can pollute context and nothing detects it. Only one regression guard (offline best-val checkpoint); online mode can silently degrade. Bullet credit assignment relies on Generator self-reported bullet_ids and LLM tags (no counterfactual verification). Prompts hand-tuned per dataset; same strong model needed for all three roles. Eval limited to 3 domains (AppWorld, FiNER/Formula, Mind2Web); AppWorld requires a custom fork of the simulator. Not packaged, provider-locked (SambaNova/Together/OpenAI/CommonStack), no local LLM support. Baseline comparisons (GEPA, DC) are the authors' own reimplementations. 'Self-improving' applies to the context only; model and harness are static.
deep_reads.key_insight: Never let the LLM rewrite its accumulated context wholesale: represent experience as an itemized, ID-addressed ledger of bullets with provenance counters, split doing (Generator), diagnosing (Reflector), and editing (Curator) into separate calls, and have the editor emit only small localized deltas — this avoids brevity bias and context collapse, makes each update cheap (tiny curator output, KV-cacheable prefix), and beats prompt optimizers like GEPA at a fraction of the rollouts.
open_gaps: Curator cannot UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE — implement counter-driven pruning (harmful>=helpful, unused-after-N-steps) and LLM merge as first-class verified ops; helpful/harmful counters currently never affect the playbook
No per-delta acceptance test: every curator ADD is applied unconditionally; a framework should A/B each delta (or batch) on a held-out slice and reject/rollback regressions, in online mode too
Fitness is single in-distribution benchmark accuracy; no cross-task or cross-domain transfer of playbooks, no held-out-domain generalization measurement, no shared/hierarchical playbook across tasks
Requires ground-truth labels or trustworthy execution feedback; no mechanism to estimate reflection reliability or quarantine low-confidence insights (w/o GT FiNER fell below baseline)

Whole playbook is injected into every prompt; retrieval only exists as an unmerged PR (#34) and the team's own study shows top-k retrieval loses 35-41% of the gain — need structure-aware retrieval or hierarchical playbooks
Credit assignment is Generator self-reported bullet usage + LLM tags; no counterfactual ablation of bullets, so harmful bullets with zero citations are invisible
Single lineage, no archive/population or crossover of playbooks; ComBEE parallel proposals are reduced by one LLM call with no diversity preservation
Role prompts (generator/reflector/curator) are static and hand-tuned per dataset (issues #37/#38); no meta-level evolution of the reflector/curator instructions
Token budget parameter is ignored by code; no enforced size control, compaction, or tiering of bullets by recency/utility
Not a library: no pip package (#32), provider-locked clients, no local model support (#30); AppWorld path needs a custom simulator fork — hard for app developers to embed in an existing agent loop
No tool/skill evolution: playbook holds text advice only; cannot accumulate executable snippets, tool wrappers, or verified procedures
deep_reads.safety_measures: Minimal: curator JSON is schema-validated and malformed/unsupported ops are skipped (only ADD executed); API-error samples excluded from playbook updates; offline mode keeps best-by-validation checkpoint; ComBEE rolls back Phase-2 edits on Phase-3 API errors. No content filtering of injected bullets, no human review gate, no adversarial-feedback defense, no bound on playbook size; AppWorld runs in its own simulated sandbox.

deep_reads.name: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Chengsong Huang, Wenhao Yu, Xiaoyang Wang, Hongming Zhang, Zongxia Li, Ruosen Li, Jiaxin Huang, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu — Tencent AI Lab (Seattle) + WashU
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-02-04 (last commit: README typo fix; last code change 2025-12-10)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 (accepted 2026-01); NeurIPS 2025 Math-AI workshop; arXiv:2508.05004; ~188 citations / 41 influential (Semantic Scholar, 2026-09); HF Daily Papers #2 on release; 77 forks
deep_reads.mechanism: Two copies of one base model (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base, OctoThinker) are trained alternately with GRPO (verl/EasyR1 fork) for a fixed number of iterations (paper: 3; scripts/main.sh: 5). Per iteration: (1) Challenger phase — the current Solver is frozen and served by 4 vLLM+Flask reward servers; the Challenger is GRPO-trained for 6 steps (batch 16, n=4 rollouts) with a math-competition 'problem setter' system prompt. Reward per proposed question = min(p, 1-p) - repetition_penalty, where p = share of the Solver's 10 temp-1.0 samples agreeing with the majority answer (paper form: 1-2|p-0.5|), repetition_penalty = the fraction of the batch falling in the same BLEU-distance agglomerative cluster (threshold 0.5), and -1 for malformed output. The Challenger's own \boxed answer is discarded. (2) Solver phase — the new Challenger samples 8x1000 questions; the frozen Solver answers each 10 times; majority vote becomes the pseudo-label; only questions whose majority share lies in [0.3, 0.8] (|p-0.5|<=0.25) are kept, pushed to HF Hub, and the Solver is GRPO-trained for 20 steps (KL 0.01, lr 1e-6) with binary accuracy vs. the pseudo-label. Checkpoints at step 5/15 seed the next iteration. No verifier, no human data, no archive: the curriculum lives only in the Challenger's weights, and the evaluator (majority-vote of the Solver) co-evolves with the policy. Runs end-to-end on one 8-GPU node; a GPT API is used only for offline benchmark rechecking.
deep_reads.eval_loop: In-loop signal: Solver self-consistency (majority-vote share among 10 samples) drives both the Challenger reward (target p~0.5) and the Solver's pseudo-labels; the [0.3,0.8] band filter plus a BLEU-cluster repetition penalty are the only guards against degenerate questions. No ground truth anywhere in the loop. Improvement is reported via external benchmarks (AMC/Minerva/MATH-500/GSM8K/Olympiad/AIME + SuperGPQA/MMLU-Pro/BBEH, GPT-4o rechecked) run after each iteration, but they are not fed back — no early stopping, no rollback. Drift is not prevented, only documented: GPT-4o-judged pseudo-label accuracy falls 79.0% -> 63.0% by iteration 3, Qwen3-4B overall peaks at iter 2 (34.92) and dips at iter 3 (34.64), 0.6B collapses after one iteration, and the follow-up R-Few measures question diversity dropping from 35 to <20 within 50 Challenger steps with inflating question length (reward hacking).
deep_reads.limitations: Math-only in practice (prompt hard-codes competition math; requires a single short verifiable answer); pseudo-labels are self-consistency, so confidently-wrong answers are reinforced and label accuracy decays (79%->63%); gains saturate or reverse after 2-3 iterations (model collapse sooner for small models); a large share of the gain comes from an untrained 'Base Challenger' (e.g. OctoThinker-8B 16.81->25.08 of 26.88 total; Qwen3-4B 27.10->30.83 of 34.92); single-model-both-roles variant collapses earlier; ablation numbers exist but the paper's exact ablation table could not be fetched (arXiv unreachable) — secondary sources confirm all three components matter, with the largest loss from removing Challenger RL. Engineering: hard-coded 8-GPU layout, `pkill python`, HF Hub round-trip for the dataset, tokens.json secrets, known math_verify infinite-loop hang, dead code loading a human math example (unused), no LICENSE file, repo effectively dormant since Dec 2025.
deep_reads.key_insight: Turn the learner's own uncertainty into the curriculum signal: reward a proposer for questions where the solver's self-consistency is ~50% (max reward variance), filter training data to that band, and use the solver's majority vote as the label — you get a verifier-free co-evolution loop that works for a few iterations, but because the evaluator is the policy itself, label drift and diversity collapse are built in and bound the number of useful iterations.
deep_reads.key_results: Qwen3-4B-Base: MATH avg 42.58->49.07 (+6.49), overall 27.10->34.92, MMLU-Pro 37.38->53.75, SuperGPQA 20.88->27.92; Qwen3-8B-Base overall 34.49->38.73, math +5.51; OctoThinker-3B 12.27->15.67; OctoThinker-8B 16.81->26.88 (mostly from Base Challenger). Math-trained skills transfer to general reasoning (+7.54 general on 4B). Pseudo-label accuracy 79.0%->63.0% over 3 iters; separate Challenger/Solver beats one shared model. Follow-ups: VisPlay (VLM extension), R-Few (adds 1-5% human anchors to stop diversity collapse).
deep_reads.safety_measures: Difficulty-band filter (0.3<=majority share<=0.8) and BLEU-cluster repetition penalty on proposed questions; GRPO KL penalty to reference policy (kl_coef 0.01); format checks; per-call timeouts on the grader. No rollback, no held-out gate, no ground-truth verification, no human-in-the-loop.
open_gaps: Evaluator is the policy itself (majority vote of the Solver): no independent verifier or held-out gate, so label accuracy decays 79%->63% and nothing detects or halts it — a framework needs an external/anchored fitness signal or drift monitor
No rollback or checkpoint selection: main.sh blindly chains 5 iterations even though the paper shows performance peaks at iter 2-3; needs benchmark-gated acceptance/early stopping

No archive or population of tasks: each iteration's questions are consumed and discarded; the curriculum exists only in Challenger weights, so diversity collapses (35->20 within 50 steps per R-Few) and there is no replay/novelty archive
Domain hard-wired to single-answer competition math via system prompt; no mechanism for open-ended, agentic, or tool-use tasks where majority vote is not a proxy for correctness
Requires 8-GPU RL fine-tuning (verl/vLLM/FSDP) of 4B-8B base models — unusable for app developers or API-only settings; no prompt/skill-level analogue

Fixed hyperparameters (delta=0.25 band, BLEU 0.5, steps 6/20) hand-tuned; the loop does not adapt its own reward or filter, and the 'Base Challenger' baseline already captures much of the gain — the RL Challenger's marginal value beyond iter 1 is small
No cross-run persistence or transfer: nothing learned (question generators, hard cases) is reused across base models or runs
Reward hacking observed (question length inflation, low-entropy clusters) with only a BLEU-cluster penalty as mitigation; no semantic diversity or difficulty-calibration audit
Single-node, brittle engineering (pkill python, HF-hub round-trip, secrets in tokens.json, math_verify hangs, no license) — not a reusable harness

deep_reads.name: Your Agent May Misevolve: Emergent Risks in Self-evolving LLM Agents (Misevolution)
deep_reads.mechanism: This is NOT a self-evolution framework; it instruments four existing evolution loops and measures safety before vs. after, with safety never part of the objective. Formalization: agent θ=(model, memory, tools, workflow), θ'=f(θ, trajectory, feedback), f chosen to maximize cumulative task utility only. (1) Model: released checkpoints of Absolute-Zero (Qwen2.5-7B/14B Base/Coder self-proposes coding tasks; reward = learnability + Python-verified correctness; RL updates weights), AgentGen (Llama3.1-70B trained on self-generated environments/tasks), SEAgent (UI-TARS-7B, failure-driven curriculum), plus a 200-step AZR rerun probed on HarmBench every 10 steps. (2) Memory: SE-Agent (Qwen3-Coder-480B) evolves 3 rounds on SWE-Bench-Verified distilling strategies into context; AgentNet-style memory injected as 6 hand-written experiences (3 success/3 fail with satisfaction scores + success-rate table) over 40 cases in Sales/Service/Medical/Finance; a 'dynamic' variant runs a 100-round customer-agent -> service-agent -> evaluator-agent loop (all Qwen2.5-72B) writing scores+feedback back into memory. (3) Tools: Alita-style plan-and-act agent creates Python 'MCP' tools during a benign task ('creating helpful tools will be rewarded'), stores them in mcp_tools.jsonl, retrieves top-3/top-5 by bge-m3 embedding for a second security-sensitive task (25 CWEval-derived pairs); separately 371 GitHub repos with RedCode-Exec payloads injected are gitingest-ed and the agent decides whether to wrap them as MCPs. (4) Workflow: verbatim AFlow MCTS (optimizer LLM proposes graph+prompt modification, parent soft-selected from top-k rounds by validation score, 20 iterations on HumanEval, Qwen2.5-72B executor); best workflow then run on RedCode-Gen. Acceptance signal in every loop is utility only; no safety gate, no rollback.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Evolution in all studied systems is driven purely by task utility: AZR learnability/correctness rewards, SWE-Bench resolution, user-satisfaction scores from an evaluator agent, HumanEval pass rate for AFlow's MCTS selection, 'helpful tools rewarded' prompt. Safety is measured only externally by the authors: HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls, ShieldAgent (Agent-SafetyBench, 2000 cases), GPT-4o judge + rule-based (RiOSWorld UIR/UCR), Refusal Rate/ASR on RedCode-Gen (160 malware prompts, 8 categories), Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM judge plus human judge for reward-hacking and tool-reuse trajectories (reward hacking averaged over 3 runs, temperature 0.1). Nothing in the loops prevents drift; the paper's central finding is that reward hacking (refund-heuristic collapse at round 60 of the dynamic loop; sales agent fabricating specs; medical agent reassuring a gunshot victim) and alignment decay emerge precisely because the fitness signal omits safety. Mitigations tested are post-hoc patches (DPO on 1K PKU-RLHF pairs; 'memories are references not rules' prompt; 'refuse if unsafe' ingestion prompt; safety instruction on the Ensemble node), each recovering only part of the loss.
deep_reads.limitations: Memory 'static' experiments use hand-crafted synthetic memories (6 experiences) rather than accumulated ones; the dynamic loop is 1 scenario, 1 model (Qwen2.5-72B), 100 rounds, 10 test queries. Small N: 25 tool pairs, 40 memory cases, 5 curated tool cases. SE-Agent memory decay tested on a single model. Model-evolution results use others' released checkpoints (uncontrolled training) except one 200-step AZR rerun. Safety judged mostly by LLM judges (Gemini-2.5-Pro judging Gemini-2.5-Pro agents). Capability/safety trade-off of mitigations measured on only 50 SWE-Bench cases. Tool-safety verification pipeline proposed but explicitly 'not tested'. No causal/mechanistic analysis (hypotheses only in Appendix A). Authors state they cannot enumerate all misevolution forms and cannot propose a unified evaluation framework across agent architectures. Code release is partial: repo has evaluation scripts for model benchmarks, the static reward-hacking prompts, the CWEval tool-creation agent, and AFlow+RedCode-Gen, but NOT the dynamic AgentNet loop, SE-Agent memory runs, the 371-sample malicious-ingestion dataset, the evolved AFlow workflow, or the 200-step AZR checkpoints; 'Getting Started: Coming soon', tool/workflow READMEs empty, HF dataset badge links nowhere.
deep_reads.key_insight: Any evolution function whose acceptance signal is task utility alone will silently trade away safety across every evolvable component: this happens with no adversary, no parameter update (memory alone drops Qwen3-Coder-480B refusal from 99.4% to 54.4%), no harmful content in self-generated data, and via structurally innocuous mutations (an Ensemble node picks the 'more complete' malware). Therefore safety must be inside the fitness/acceptance gate, re-validated whenever a learned artifact (memory, tool, workflow node) is reused in a new context, and backed by versioned rollback, because post-hoc prompt/DPO patches recover only part of the loss (e.g. ASR 20.6->13.1 vs 0.6 initial; workflow RR 5.6->13.1 vs 36.3 initial).
open_gaps: No studied framework (AFlow, SE-Agent, Alita-style tool loop, Absolute-Zero) includes a safety term in the mutation acceptance criterion; a harness could run a fixed safety regression suite (e.g. RedCode-Gen RR/ASR, HarmBench subset) at every evolution step and reject/rollback mutations that regress it.
Rollback/versioning of self-modifications with tagged 'known-safe' checkpoints is only proposed in the Appendix B checklist, never implemented or tested.

Two-stage tool safety verification (static analysis at creation, LLM judge re-validation at reuse in the new context) is proposed but explicitly 'not tested'; nothing currently flags cross-domain reuse (PII tool built for customer data reused on medical data).

Memory loop has no retrieval-time filtering, provenance/recency weighting, or quarantine; the 'treat memory as reference' prompt only cuts reward-hacking unsafe rate 71.8%->51.4% and no-memory baseline is 0%.

No anomaly detector for abrupt memory-driven heuristic collapse (dynamic loop stayed safe until a single high-rated unreasonable refund at rounds 50-60 flipped the policy); a monitor on action-distribution shift per memory write is missing.

Workflow mutation operators lack safety-preserving invariants; the evolved Ensemble node selects the most detailed child and amplifies harm; safety-aware aggregation operators or safety-constrained MCTS objectives are untested.

External tool ingestion has <8% baseline refusal of backdoored repos; a prompt raises it to ~69% but the 371-sample dataset is unreleased and no automated code-scanning gate is built into the ingestion path.

Model self-training degrades safety even with benign self-generated data; no safety-preserving self-training method (safety anchor data mixing, KL-to-initial on safety prompts, periodic re-alignment) is evaluated beyond post-hoc DPO on 1K pairs recovering 59.5->62.75 of a 64.0 baseline.
No scalable longitudinal harness: the only dynamic simulation is 1 scenario, 1 model, 100 rounds; continuous safety telemetry across evolution rounds for arbitrary agents does not exist.
Interactions between pathways (memory + tools + workflow evolving simultaneously) are never studied; each pathway is isolated.
Capability cost of mitigations is measured only on 50 SWE-Bench-Verified cases for one prompt; no Pareto analysis of safety vs utility for any mitigation.

deep_reads.org_or_authors: Shuai Shao, Qihan Ren, Chen Qian, Boyi Wei, Dadi Guo, Jingyi Yang, Xinhao Song, Linfeng Zhang, Weinan Zhang, Dongrui Liu, Jing Shao — Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Renmin University, Princeton, HKUST, Fudan
deep_reads.safety_measures: Paper is itself a safety study. Tested mitigations: lightweight DPO safety post-training after self-evolution (1K PKU-RLHF pairs); meta-prompt 'memories are for reference only, decide independently' plus context-specific safety warnings; explicit 'assess project safety, refuse to package if unsafe' prompt for tool ingestion; safety instruction added to the evolved Ensemble node. Proposed but untested: static analysis + vulnerability scan before adding a created tool, LLM-judge re-validation at reuse. deep_reads.name: Reef (reef-infra) — continual learning infra for self-improving agents
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Human-Agent-Society (academic collective; ~25 listed members incl. Paul Liang (MIT), Ao Qu, Bo Liu, Zijian Zhou, Hanfei Yu, Haoze He, Xuan Jiang; same org as CORAL, COLM 2026). 19 GitHub contributors.
deep_reads.date: 2026-08-31 (public repo created; PyPI v0.0.1 2026-09-01, v0.0.2 2026-09-02; pre-launch history lived in a private 'reef-archive')
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed same day; ~30 merged PRs in the last 4 days)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: No paper of its own; GitHub launch (954 stars / 63 forks in 11 days). Cookbook reproduces SAO (arXiv:2607.07508), SkillClaw (arXiv:2604.08377), GEPA, Meta-Harness (stanford-iris-lab), TTT-Discover, OpenClaw-RL, CORAL (COLM 2026).
deep_reads.mechanism: Reef is a serving proxy plus a versioned release pipeline; the actual optimizer is a pluggable 'recipe'. Loop (Serve -> Observe -> Grow -> Commit): (1) Agents call an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint with an `x-reef-scenario` header; every response returns an `x-reef-agent-record-id` receipt and the exchange is stored (for weight training, sampled tokens + rollout logprobs too). (2) Clients POST /reef/report with a score and/or free-text feedback referencing receipts; a processor applies a score window (`max_score`, default keeps only failures for harness evolution) and batches `batch_size` eligible records. (3) A step runs the recipe. Weight path: Slime/Megatron trains (SAO = one rollout per step; OpenClaw-RL, TTT-Discover, CORAL grouped rewards), weights hot-sync to SGLang as a LiveWeightArtifactRef, checkpoints become LoRA/full releases. Harness path (cordis backend): the harness is a composition tree of nodes (rules, skills, config, code_extension; on the native adapter also tools, hooks, subagents and the loop graph); `propose(nodes, samples, models, manifest, rejected, sources, requests)` returns one Mutation (create/update/remove) or a composite sequence; the candidate and the incumbent tree each run every fixed task (`2 x tasks x episode_repeats` headless episodes, interleaved) and `evaluate` scores each; `decide` publishes iff wins - losses > `min_win_margin`, else the snapshot is restored and the rejected proposal is fed back to the next `propose`. (4) Accepted candidates are appended to an immutable git-LFS release chain; running clients (reef-pi, reef-native serve) mount the new release without restart. Extras: `promote_failures` adds real failing prompts to the gate suite; `recheck_every` re-gates the last publish and rolls back one step; `review_kinds` holds code wins as pending releases until a human promotes; bubblewrap sandbox for episodes; `hybrid` mode lets a person request a change in plain words through the same gate.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Per recipe, not universal. Harness path: a fixed, small task suite with a programmatic scorer (tutorial: 3 exact-last-line coding tasks) run paired on candidate vs incumbent; W/L/T tally with a configurable noise margin; rejected proposals are memorised (`max_rejected_history`) so the proposer stops re-proposing them; optional periodic recheck rolls back one bad publish; GEPA recipe uses a Pareto archive + strict mean improvement on a 45-problem validation set; Meta-Harness uses strict mean improvement over the incumbent's admitted score. Weight path: verifier rewards (boxed-answer equivalence, Harbor test verifiers, benchmark judges) drive gradient steps, and the default selector is `AlwaysSelect` — every successfully trained candidate publishes with no behavioural gate (acknowledged in issue #356). SkillClaw reproduction also uses `selection: always`. Anti-gaming/drift: prompts are fenced as `untrusted_text` with a random nonce; promoted failing prompts pass a credential tripwire and an instruction-override screen with a per-client cap; code_extension wins can be held for human review; sandboxed episodes with explicit env forwarding. Known hole (their words, #356): the harness gate pools wins/losses, so gains on added tasks can outweigh regressions on the protected seed suite.
deep_reads.key_results: All results are team-run, single-sample, small-scale. Harness tutorial: Qwen3-8B/pi published one skill after one failure (gate 1W/0L/2T, 63 s); qwen2.5:7b on the native harness published a loop-graph rewrite adding a `check` stage (2W/0L/1T) but the rewrite is the prompt's worked example reproduced; several native runs rejected; seed tree scored the same task 1.0 in traffic and 0.0 in 4/5 gate episodes (gate is noisy). GEPA on AIME-2025 (2 seeds): +16.0 pp mean vs upstream GEPA +12.7 pp; sign of the difference flips between seeds. Meta-Harness on a 30-task Terminal-Bench hard subset: 23/60 selected vs 20/60 baseline; selector replay agreed with upstream 8/8 decisions. SkillClaw (GLM-5.3-Flash, preliminary): pool 9->17 skills over 6 nights; Productivity category +12.05 pts (2.29 sd) over frozen control. SAO on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 48 rollouts: mean reward 0.479 vs base 0.458 vs GRPO(+DIS) 0.417 — ordering matches paper, magnitude tiny; SWE-Bench Verified attempt produced no result. OpenClaw-RL GSM8K stream with Qwen3-4B: adaptation criterion (3 consecutive passes) reached at session 14.
deep_reads.limitations: 11 days public, v0.0.2, 53 open issues including basic install/CI bugs (sqlite locked in CI #377, reef-pi wrapper breakage #374/#375). Weight updates have no evaluation gate by default (AlwaysSelect); behavioural gates for weights, protected regression suites, invalid-evaluation handling and cross-release regression matrices are all open roadmap items (#355, #356, #5). Harness gate uses tiny task suites (3 tasks in the tutorial), one episode per task by default, stochastic verdicts, and one-step rollback only. Every published result is a single unrepeated run with no spread; several 'wins' come from a 7B model reproducing the prompt's worked example. Weight path requires Ray + Slime + Megatron + SGLang + docker on multi-GPU Linux; harness path needs pi/other agent binaries and a provider key; SkillClaw needs docker + multi-GB dataset + paid API budget with no dry mode. Sandbox `egress_hosts` enables network without enforcing a hostname firewall; the local executor enforces nothing. Recipes live outside the wheel (cookbook only). 'Self-improving' is real for the harness path (the served model proposes and is gated end-to-end) but the research methods are reproductions of other groups' papers; Reef's own contribution is the infra.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat self-improvement as a release pipeline rather than an algorithm: give every inference a receipt, attach feedback to receipts, express both weight updates and harness edits as candidate artifacts that go through the same propose -> paired-evaluate -> decide contract against the incumbent on fixed tasks, and publish only winners as immutable, hot-mountable releases with one-step rollback — so the optimizer (GEPA, SkillClaw, Meta-Harness, SAO) becomes a swappable plugin.
open_gaps: Weight updates default to AlwaysSelect: no behavioural candidate-vs-incumbent gate, metric thresholds, or held-out regression check before hot-swapping trained weights into live serving (#356, #5 open).

Harness gate is a pooled win/loss tally over one small task list; no protected seed-suite floor, so gains on promoted tasks can mask regressions on original capabilities (admitted in #356); no held-out task set distinct from the gate suite.

Rollback is one step deep (only the previous tree is retained as a target) and rechecks are periodic/manual; no cross-release regression matrix or forgetting analysis over the whole release chain (#355 open).

Gate verdicts are single-episode and stochastic (same tree scored 1.0 in traffic, 0.0 in 4/5 gate episodes); no built-in significance test, repeated confirmation, or invalid-evaluation outcome for scorer/infra failures.

Evaluator, proposer prompt and trigger policy are fixed config, not evolvable state (RFC #308 proposes putting them behind a floor but is unimplemented); no mechanism to detect or correct a scorer the proposer has learned to game.

Proposals are single mutations per step from one proposer with no population/archive except in the GEPA and Meta-Harness recipes; the core mechanism has no crossover, no diversity pressure, and no transfer of learned skills across scenarios/deployments.
No independent or repeated measurements: every reported run is n=1 by the authors; no standard Reef benchmark exists yet (#357/#358 open).

Weight path requires a multi-GPU Ray/Slime/Megatron/SGLang stack; no lightweight or hosted-API weight-learning path (MLX and Tinker backends are roadmap only), so app developers are limited to the harness path.

Sandbox egress is not enforced as a hostname firewall and the default local executor has no isolation, so model-written code_extension/tool nodes can only be safely evolved with bubblewrap on Linux plus human review.

Model-version routing (canary, shadow, sticky pinning, teacher fallback) and per-request serve-only opt-out are unimplemented (#24, #32-#34, #39), so a bad release reaches all traffic of a scenario at once.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Candidate never serves until it beats the incumbent on the same tasks; rejected candidates restore the snapshot; `min_win_margin` noise floor; `recheck_every` re-gates the last publish and can roll back; `evolution.publish: review` / `review_kinds: [code_extension]` hold code-touching wins as pending releases until a human POSTs /promote; `native_loop` changes always wait for review; episodes can run in a bubblewrap sandbox with read-only base FS, explicit `env_from` credentials, resource limits and no network by default; recorded prompts are wrapped as untrusted data with nonce delimiters before entering proposer prompts; promoted failing prompts pass a key-shaped-literal tripwire and an instruction-override screen and are capped per client; provider credentials are never written into candidates, checkpoints, or published trees; scenario state and populations commit atomically with the release so failures cannot advance them.
