deep_reads.name: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Wenyi Wang, Piotr Piękos, Li Nanbo, Firas Laakom, Yimeng Chen, Mateusz Ostaszewski, Mingchen Zhuge, Jürgen Schmidhuber — KAUST (Center of Excellence for Generative AI); code at metauto-ai/HGM
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2026-02-07 (README news only); last code fix 2025-11-25; last substantive addition 2025-11-06 (best_agent + SWE-bench Lite results link)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2026 Oral (OpenReview forum T0EiEuhOOL). Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); ~20 tweets / 2 HN posts per EmergentMind; 431 stars / 71 forks; at least two independent reimplementations (weill-labs/hgm, z3nkr1s9n6-ctrl/hgm-lab); listed in coding-agent self-evolution surveys.
deep_reads.mechanism: Archive = a tree of coding-agent versions, each a git patch chain over a DGM-derived base agent (coding_agent.py forward() loop, tools/, prompts/). Budget = N benchmark task-evaluations (800 for the 60-task runs, 8000 for full SWE-bench Verified). Asynchronous loop with 20 workers; each iteration: if n_evals^α ≥ |tree| (+pending expansions), α=0.6 (UCB-Air widening rule), EXPAND, else EVALUATE. EXPAND: for every node with ≥1 success, pool the Bernoulli pass/fail outcomes of the node plus all its descendants (its clade) into (s_C, f_C); Thompson-sample Beta(τ(1+s_C), τ(1+f_C)) with τ=B/b annealing (config default: no annealing) and take the argmax. In a Docker container, apply the parent's patches, choose_entry picks one failed task (or a meta-issue: empty patches / stochasticity / context-length overflow), a diagnose LLM reads the agent's code, run log, the SWE-bench private test patch and eval log, and emits a general improvement plan; the parent agent is then run on its own repo (--self_improve) to implement it. A non-empty model_patch.diff becomes a child node with zero evaluations (no test gate; empty/failed patches are dropped). EVALUATE: Thompson-sample over nodes' own Beta(1+s, 1+f), give the winner one random not-yet-run task, run the official SWE-bench/Polyglot harness in Docker, append 0/1; counts propagate to all ancestors' clade tallies. At budget exhaustion return the best-belief agent (highest posterior percentile of per-agent Beta). Meta-level code (hgm.py, diagnosis/self-improvement prompts, the CMP estimator) is excluded from the container via .dockerignore, so only the object-level coding agent evolves.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = binary resolved/unresolved from the official SWE-bench Verified (60-task DGM subset or full 500) or Polyglot harness, run in Docker with hidden tests; evaluation LLM is GPT-5-mini (SWE) / Qwen3-Coder-30B (Polyglot), expansion LLM GPT-5 / Qwen3-Coder-480B. Each outcome is a Bernoulli sample feeding Beta posteriors; clade-pooled posteriors (CMP estimate) drive which lineage to expand, per-agent posteriors drive which agent gets more evaluation, and the N^α ≥ |T| rule arbitrates expand-vs-evaluate. Drift/regression control is purely statistical: bad children accumulate failures and get deprioritized by Thompson sampling; there is no rollback, no unit-test gate on self-modifications, and no verification beyond downstream task sampling. Reward hacking is limited by the outer harness being outside the agent's editable repo and by Docker sandboxing, but the diagnosis step is shown the private SWE-bench test patch (train-subset leakage into the mutation operator). Generalization is checked once, post hoc, on SWE-bench Lite filtered to the 207 tasks not in Verified, and on a backbone swap to GPT-5.
deep_reads.key_results: SWE-Verified-60 (from 40.0% initial, 800 evals): HGM 56.7% vs DGM 53.3% vs SICA 50.0%; allocated CPU-hours 517 vs DGM 1231 (2.38x) vs SICA stuck in a context-length loop after 360 evals. Polyglot (from 20.3%): HGM 30.5% vs DGM 27.1% vs SICA 25.4%; 347 h vs 2385 h (6.86x) vs 572 h (1.65x). CMP-estimator vs empirical-CMP Pearson (weighted): HGM 0.778 / 0.626 vs DGM 0.285 / 0.383 vs SICA 0.444 / 0.274 (SWE / Polyglot). Full SWE-bench Verified with bash-only initial agent (53.2%) after 8000 evals: 61.4%, top GPT-5-mini system and top-10 among checked submissions. Transfer to SWE-bench Lite with GPT-5-mini: filtered (207 unseen) 40.1% vs ancestor 34.8% vs SWE-agent+GPT-5-mini 39.6%; standard 49.0% vs 44.0% vs 47.6%. Backbone swap to GPT-5: 57.0% (172/300, checked submission) vs SWE-agent+Claude 4 Sonnet 56.7%; filtered 47.8% vs 48.3%. Total spend for the three-method comparison ~$5000. Independent clean-room replication (weill-labs/hgm, May 2026): CMP beats greedy in a $0 simulator (+0.055 skill over 40 seeds); live it rescued a deliberately crippled agent (0.00→0.35 pass@1, p=0.016) but showed no net gain from a competent 0.26 base with 50 held-out instances (7–7 discordant pairs, p≈1.0).
deep_reads.limitations: Single run per method/benchmark, no seeds or confidence intervals; 56.7 vs 53.3 on 60 tasks is a 2-task difference. No ablation separating CMP from the other simultaneous changes vs DGM (async execution, single-task evaluation granularity, UCB-Air widening), so the paper cannot attribute the gain to the clade metric. The held-out advantage over the human-designed SWE-agent on unseen SWE-Lite tasks is ~0.5 pt (about one task). Empirical-CMP targets are computed on trees the policies themselves generated (policy-dependent confounding), with a hand-designed leakage correction. Theorem 1 (CMP oracle = Gödel Machine) is a Q-value identity under strong assumptions (repeatable trials, zero-cost proofs, unit-cost self-modifications, final-agent-only objective); no guarantees for the estimator, and the paper has no explicit limitations section. Async execution biases toward agents with few evaluations (acknowledged, unfixed). Cost is hundreds to thousands of CPU-hours plus ~$5k of LLM spend per comparison; requires Docker and the full SWE-bench harness. Config default cool_down=false diverges from the paper's τ=B/b schedule. Only the object-level agent is modified; the search policy and mutation prompts are fixed. API keys are injected into the sandbox running model-generated code.
deep_reads.key_insight: Score a candidate for further self-modification by the pooled downstream success of its entire lineage (clade) rather than its own benchmark score, and decouple 'spawn a child' from 'measure an existing node' so evaluation budget flows one task at a time to whichever node the posterior says is most promising — the parent's own fitness is a weak predictor of its descendants' fitness (Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch).
open_gaps: Only the object-level coding agent (coding_agent.py, tools/, prompts/) is mutated; the self-improvement machinery itself (search policy, CMP estimator, diagnose and self-improve prompts, choose_entry heuristics) is explicitly excluded from the sandbox via .dockerignore — no meta-level self-improvement despite the Gödel Machine framing

Fitness is binary pass/fail on a fixed subset of one public benchmark (60 or 500 SWE-bench tasks); no held-out validation inside the loop, no task heterogeneity/difficulty modeling, no curriculum or task generation

No verification or rollback of self-modifications: a child enters the archive on any non-empty diff with no unit-test/static/diff-review gate; regressions are only discovered by spending benchmark evaluations on them

The diagnosis LLM is shown the SWE-bench private test patch and hidden-test logs of the training subset, leaking test knowledge into the mutation operator; a framework should isolate the mutator from held-out test contents

No statistical rigor or replication protocol: single run per configuration, no seeds/CIs, no ablation isolating CMP from async execution, single-task evaluation granularity, and the UCB-Air widening rule; an independent replication found a null effect from a competent base at small scale

Each expansion sees only its parent's code plus one diagnosed failure; there is no cross-lineage transfer, crossover, or persistent memory of which self-modifications worked, so discoveries in one clade are never reused by another

Compute cost is prohibitive for practitioners: 347–2385 allocated CPU-hours per run, 8000 evaluations for the full-benchmark run, ~$5k for the comparison; no cheap proxy or simulator for the search loop is provided (a third-party clean-room repo added one)
Asynchronous execution creates a known bias toward under-evaluated agents (easy tasks finish first, inflating early means); acknowledged but not corrected

Safety is Docker sandboxing plus a README warning; API keys are passed into the container environment of the self-modifying agent, and there is no monitoring of what the agent does to its own repo (e.g., the mutated agent could edit its internal eval_utils)

Theorem 1's assumptions (repeatable trials, zero-cost proofs, unit-cost modifications, final-agent-only objective) do not hold for real deployments where evaluation is noisy, costly, and non-stationary; no guarantees for the CMP estimator's bias or sample complexity are given
deep_reads.safety_measures: Every self-modification and every task evaluation runs inside a Docker container built from the initial-agent image; 1-hour (5-hour in Sec. 4.3) timeouts on self-modification and evaluation; the outer harness and search code live outside the agent's editable repo; README warns that model-generated code may behave destructively and asks users to accept the risk. No formal proofs (the 'Gödel Machine' link is a theoretical identity, not enforced at runtime), no rollback, no diff review, no unit-test gate on children; API keys (OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS/OpenRouter) are injected as environment variables into the sandbox running self-modification.

deep_reads.name: GenericAgent (GA)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Jiaqing Liang (lsdefine), Jinyi Han, ... Yanghua Xiao — Advantage AI Agent Lab (A³ LAB), Shenzhen Aquaintelling Technology × Fudan University (18 authors)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed today: hub/p2p reconnect, llmcore context_win 38000)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv 2604.17091 (Apr 2026); Semantic Scholar 10 citations / 0 influential (Sep 2026); reproduction repo JinyiHan99/GA-Technical-Report 23 stars; 1652 forks, 165 open issues; featured by Jiqizhixin; commercial partner DintalClaw
deep_reads.mechanism: Nothing in the model or harness code changes; what evolves is a file-based memory tree the agent edits with its own file_read/file_patch/file_write tools. Layers: L0 memory_management_sop.md (meta-rules), L1 global_mem_insight.txt (≤30-line index + RULES, injected into the system prompt at every task start and re-injected every 10 turns), L2 global_mem.txt (verified env facts), L3 memory/*.md SOPs and *.py scripts (skills), L4 raw session logs (cron-compressed every 12h by reflect/scheduler.py). Loop per task (agent_loop.py, ~100 lines): LLM turn -> tool dispatch -> anchor prompt (last 30 one-line turn summaries + key_info from update_working_checkpoint) -> repeat up to 180 turns. Crystallization is a tool call, start_long_term_update: the agent self-triggers it (rejected before turn 10; PR #790 forces an evaluation at >=15 turns), which returns L0 + a prompt instructing: extract only facts/steps 'verified by successful tool execution', route via a decision tree (env fact -> L2 + L1 pointer; general pitfall -> one-line L1 RULE; hard task technique -> L3 SOP or script), patch-only minimal edits, skip if nothing new. Over repeated runs the paper documents a ratchet: exploration -> textual SOP (rounds 2-5) -> codified script the SOP tells future runs to call (rounds 6-9). Idle-time evolution: reflect mode fires autonomous_operation_sop every few minutes; agent picks a TODO (planned from history.txt + a subagent 1-10 review), experiments in temp/, writes a report with memory-update proposals for human approval. The paper's skill-tree curriculum (breadth/depth/utility/innovation weighted score with usage-count weight adaptation) is not in the public code.
deep_reads.eval_loop: No automated fitness signal. Acceptance of a new skill/fact is the LLM's own judgment at start_long_term_update, gated only by prompt rules: 'No Execution, No Memory' (must come from a successful tool result), no volatile state, patch-only edits, L1 hard cap of 30 lines, decision tree for layer placement. Drift control is heuristic: memory_cleanup_sop.md ROI rule for L1 lines, 'existence encoding' (index only says a skill exists), file_access_stats.json read counters (written but not consumed by code), L4 raw archive for traceability. Regression prevention is absent: no tests or replay of SOPs/scripts, no versioning/rollback of memory files, no held-out check. Autonomous exploration uses a subagent LLM-judge on the TODO plan (not on outcomes) and human review of reports before memory changes. Improvement evidence is offline benchmark measurement by the authors (tokens/calls per round), not a signal the system optimizes against. The usage-feedback weight adaptation in the paper is self-described as 'unverified' and is not shipped.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (author-run, small n): 9-round LangChain GitHub-research longitudinal: 222,203 -> 23,010 total tokens (-89.6%), 32 -> 5 LLM calls, 7m30s -> 1m38s, stabilizing at 23k±1k once SOP codified to github_pr_analyzer.py. 8-task cross-task web benchmark (Claude Opus 4.6): 2nd/3rd runs save 61.0-92.4% tokens (79.3% overall) vs first run; OpenClaw shows no convergence (B2: 1,370k -> 2,330k -> 2,130k). Lifelong AgentBench (n=20, Sonnet 4.6): GA 100% acc @ 241k tokens vs OpenClaw 70% @ 1.45M, Claude Code 75% @ 814k. SOP-Bench (n=20): GA 100% @ 2.08M vs OpenClaw 100% @ 2.64M, Claude Code 85% @ 1.25M. RealFin: GA 65% @ 114k vs Codex/GPT-5.4 60% @ 892k. Memory ablation (dangerous_goods, GPT-5.4): no-memory 13.87% TSR, full SOP (575 tok) 52.44%, condensed (165 tok) 66.48%. LoCoMo F1 multi-hop 43.33 vs Mem0 39.32, A-MEM 29.03. Prompt after installing 20 skills: 2,298 tokens vs Claude Code 22,821 / OpenClaw 43,321. WebCanvas 0.834 vs 0.722; BrowseComp-ZH 0.60 vs 0.20 (n=10). Repo: 14.2k stars in 8 months, self-bootstrapped commits claimed.
deep_reads.limitations: Skill quality control is entirely prompt-level; an LLM can still write wrong or overfit SOPs and there is no test, replay, or rollback (memory edits are irreversible file patches; L0 itself warns 'memory mistakes compound every turn'). Evidence of evolution is on tiny samples (20 tasks per benchmark, 12/10/22 web tasks), same-workflow repetition rather than held-out transfer, and baselines were not given equivalent memory. The 9-round trace shows a crystallized script for one specific site; generalization is only a hand-written 'transferability note'. Paper's own limitations: 30-round autonomous cap, weight adaptation unverified, self-improvement log manually curated, skill-tree merging/deprecation manual. Paper's skill-tree curriculum is absent from the shipped code. Pre-installed SOPs are Chinese and Windows-honed. Real-world issues: agent skipped memory settlement often enough that a forced gate was added (#789/#790); loops beyond 50k context (#417). 'Self-evolving' is accurate for skills/memory but not for the loop, tools, or model.
deep_reads.key_insight: Evolve the informational environment, not the model: keep a hard ~30k-token budget, put only the existence of skills in an always-on ≤30-line index (the LLM is the decoder that fetches details on demand), admit to long-term memory only what a successful tool execution verified, and let skills ratchet from trajectory -> text SOP -> executable script so repeat tasks collapse from 32 LLM calls to 5.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prompt-level 'constitution': ask before modifying own source code, never read key/secret files, three-failure escalation to ask_user, patch-only edits under memory/, L1 size cap. Autonomous mode confines writes to temp/, requires memory/SOP changes and installs to be proposed in reports for human approval, forbids reading keys or core code. code_run timeouts and stop signals; --no-user-tools removes ask_user/start_long_term_update for subagents. No sandbox: the agent has full OS, real logged-in browser, and ADB device control; irreversible-op guard is a prompt rule only.
open_gaps: No automated verification of distilled skills: SOPs/scripts are never re-executed or tested before being trusted; a framework could replay the crystallized script against the original task and only promote on pass
No versioning or rollback of memory edits (patch-only rule is the sole guard); memory dir is not git-tracked, no diff review, no revert on regression
No outcome-based feedback loop actually shipped: file_access_stats.json read counts and the paper's usage-count weight adaptation are unused; nothing demotes or deprecates SOPs that stop working
No stale-skill detection: when a target site/API changes, the wrong SOP is still recalled; needs freshness checks or failure attribution to the SOP that was followed
No held-out generalization test of learned skills: evolution measured only on repeats of the same workflow; needs cross-task transfer benchmarks with memory-equalized baselines
Acceptance signal is LLM self-judgment with no external evaluator, no human rating, no unit tests; cannot detect hallucinated 'verified' facts
Skill index (L1) curation is a manual SOP run (memory_cleanup_sop); no automatic ROI-based pruning or merging of redundant SOPs
Single-instance skill library: incubator copies memory to remote nodes but has no merge/conflict resolution or population-level selection across instances

Autonomous exploration curriculum is a prose value formula ('not covered by training data' x 'future benefit') with a subagent scoring the plan, not the result; no measurable objective drives task selection
Loop, tool set, and harness are fixed; architectural self-update is only conjectured in the paper's Discussion
Evaluation reproducibility: n=20 tasks per benchmark, author-run, backbone model names internal; independent replication absent

deep_reads.name: EvoScientist
deep_reads.date: 2026-01-26 (repo created); paper arXiv:2603.08127 submitted 2026-03-09; public debut 2026-03-13
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (pushed); v0.2.10 released 2026-09-05; ~weekly releases
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Huawei Xiaoyi DeepResearch Team + academic collaborators (Yougang Lyu, Xi Zhang, Xinhao Yi, Yuyue Zhao, Shuyu Guo, Wenxiang Hu, Jan Piotrowski, Jakub Kaliski, Jacopo Urbani, Zaiqiao Meng, Lun Zhou, Xiaohui Yan)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2603.08127 (technical report, v1 only). Self-reported: 6/6 papers accepted at ICAIS 2025 AI Scientist Track (Best Paper + AI Reviewer's Appraisal Award); #1 DeepResearch Bench / DeepResearch Bench II / AstaBench Code & Data Analysis at submission time; #2 ResearchClawBench. Citation count not retrievable (S2 rate-limited).
deep_reads.mechanism: Two layers exist. (A) PAPER SYSTEM (not the repo code): Researcher Agent retrieves top-k_I=2 ideation-memory items by mxbai-embed cosine similarity, runs propose-review-refine tree search (21 candidates, 3 workers), ranks by Elo tournament on novelty/feasibility/relevance/clarity, expands top-1 into a proposal. Engineer Agent retrieves top-k_E=1 experimentation-memory item and runs 4-stage code tree search (budgets 20/12/12/18 attempts, 4 workers), keeping best-performing code per stage. Evolution Manager Agent then writes memory via three prompts: IDE (feasible directions from top-ranked ideas -> MEM_I), IVE (failed proposals -- no executable code within budget, or worse-than-baseline per LLM read of the execution report -> unsuccessful directions in MEM_I), ESE (data-processing + model-training strategies from trajectories and best code -> MEM_E). Next task retrieves updated memories. (B) REPO (deepagents harness, 6 sub-agents): EvoMemoryLifecycleMiddleware fires after every orchestrator turn and subagent run, launching a background memory-worker (auxiliary model, no execute/write_file/delete) that reviews the sanitized trajectory and either edits profile markdown (SOUL.md, USER_PROFILE.md, RESEARCH_TASTE.md, PROJECT_PROFILE.md -- injected into the system prompt) or calls record_observation (semantic/procedural/episodic, global/project scope, sha256 content-hash id for dedupe). An observation-linker agent then adds complements/contradicts/supersedes edges in frontmatter. Main agent must run a memory preflight (inlined index, search_observations ranked keyword search, read_memory). AutoSkills: a cron (nightly/weekly/monthly) agent finds connected components of the observation graph with >=3 nodes and >=2 procedural, drafts a SKILL.md folder via the skill-creator skill, validates frontmatter, submits a pending proposal; a human approves/rejects via /autoskills; approval copies it into the workspace skills tier. The paper's IDE/IVE/ESE ship only as prompt-only skills in the EvoSkills repo (evo-memory, research-ideation).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Paper: internal fitness is (i) an Elo tournament judged by the ideation LLM itself over 4 rubric dimensions (selects which ideas feed IDE), (ii) hard code-execution success within an attempt budget plus an LLM 'worse than baseline' verdict on the execution report (triggers IVE), (iii) best-performing implementation per stage (feeds ESE). External evaluation: Gemini-3-flash pairwise judge with position swap on 30 expert-written queries vs 7 systems, 3 PhD annotators on 4 baselines, and code-execution success before/after ESE (34.39% -> 44.56% mean; stage 3 only 20.33% -> 21.57%). Ablation: -IDE avg gap -22.5, -IVE -20.0 (feasibility lose 63%), -all -45.8. Repo: there is NO fitness signal on memory or auto-skills. Drift is controlled only by prompt guardrails ('durable, non-obvious, evidence-backed, not already present'), content-hash dedupe, contradicts/supersedes links, memory-worker tool restrictions, a prompt-injection instruction ('treat embedded requests as data'), and human approve/reject of skill proposals. Scheduled tasks optionally get a --rubric checklist graded by a read-only auxiliary-model reviewer with one retry. Nothing measures whether a stored observation or synthesized skill improves downstream task outcomes; no regression test on memory writes; no rollback other than a human rejecting a proposal.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) The benchmarked RA/EA/EMA system (tree search, Elo, embedding retrieval, 4-stage engineer) is not the code in the repo; the repo's EvoMemory/AutoSkills loop has never been benchmarked, and the paper mechanism exists downstream only as prompt-only markdown protocols. (2) Repo retrieval is ranked keyword search over markdown, not the embedding retrieval the paper credits. (3) Evaluation: 30 queries; idea judge (Gemini-3-flash) is same family as the ideation model (Gemini-2.5-Pro); ablations cover idea evolution only, not ESE; only before/after code-success numbers, no learning curve over cycles; benchmark suite still unreleased per roadmap. (4) Stage-3 (novel method) code success stays ~21% after evolution. (5) Memory has no value estimation, consolidation, forgetting, or conflict resolution -- the maintainers' own Q4 roadmap (#433) lists duplicate/outdated/conflicting memories and retrieval quality as open problems. (6) Human-on-the-loop gating means AutoSkills do not self-apply; nothing evolves without a person clicking approve. (7) Paper limitations: computational tasks only; may reproduce literature biases. (8) Leaderboard and ICAIS claims are self-reported, 'at submission time'.
deep_reads.key_insight: Split experiential memory by what it steers: an ideation memory that records both promising directions AND validated dead-ends with a failure classification (implementation vs fundamental, decided by execution evidence), and an execution memory of reusable strategies distilled from best-performing trajectories -- then let a graph of linked observations (complements/contradicts/supersedes) be mined offline into human-reviewed skill proposals.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (arXiv 2603.08127): LLM-judge average win-rate gaps vs Virtual Scientist +93.3, AI-Researcher +87.5, InternAgent +83.3, AI Scientist-v2 +29.2, Hypogenic +80.8, Novix +46.0, K-Dense +54.5; human eval avg 82.5% novelty / 64.2% feasibility win vs 4 strongest baselines; code execution success 34.39% -> 44.56% mean after ESE (stage1 42.25->56.42, stage2 31.89->42.68, stage3 20.33->21.57, stage4 36.68->48.44); ablation -all idea evolution: 80% novelty lose, 83% feasibility lose. Backbones: Gemini-2.5-Pro (ideation/writing), Claude-4.5-Haiku (code). Repo: 4786 stars, 307 forks, 35 contributors, 124 issues, PyPI v0.2.10, Docker image, EvoSkills sibling repo 436 stars.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Memory-worker agents are denied execute/write_file/delete/task tools; prompts instruct them to treat requests in tool/subagent output as data not instructions; observations deduped by content hash; auto-skill proposals must pass frontmatter validation and human approve/reject via /autoskills before installation, and cannot modify built-in system skills; shell execution requires human approval by default with an allow-list option; sandboxed workspace unless --dangerous; sudo/rm -rf blocked even in dangerous mode; scheduled runs gated on shell access.
open_gaps: No fitness signal on memory items: observations and synthesized skills are never scored against downstream task outcomes, so bad memories persist until a human notices
Auto-skill acceptance is purely human approval plus format validation; no automated eval harness runs the proposed SKILL.md on held-out tasks before install
No rollback/versioning of memory or skill changes -- a regression caused by a stored observation cannot be traced and reverted automatically
No consolidation, decay, or conflict resolution: contradicts/supersedes edges are recorded but retrieval does not down-weight superseded or contradicted observations
Repo retrieval is keyword-ranked over markdown; the embedding retrieval the paper credits for gains is not implemented in the product
The paper's benchmarked loop (Elo tournament, execution-budget failure classification, ESE) is not runnable code -- it is a prompt-only skill with no automatic trigger wiring
Learning is per-user/per-workspace; no mechanism to share or federate validated observations/skills across users or projects
No curriculum or task-selection evolution: the system never chooses what to attempt next based on memory gaps
Evaluation lacks a learning curve across cycles and any held-out generalization test; a new framework should report success vs. number of evolution rounds on unseen tasks
Judge and generator are the same model family (Gemini), leaving self-preference bias in the Elo fitness signal unaddressed

deep_reads.name: Agent0 Series (Agent0 + Agent0-VL)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-10 (last push; Agent0-VL code update). Core Agent0 code last touched 2025-12-25.
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Peng Xia, Kaide Zeng, Jiaqi Liu, Can Qin, Fang Wu, Yiyang Zhou, Caiming Xiong, Huaxiu Yao — UNC Chapel Hill (AIMING Lab), Salesforce Research, Stanford
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: Repo description claims "[ICML'26 & COLM'26]"; arXiv v1 (2511.16043, Nov 2025) carries no venue comment and project page lists no acceptance. OpenAlex shows 0 citations (index incomplete); Semantic Scholar rate-limited. 150 forks, 13 open issues.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Two copies of the same base LLM (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base) alternate in a 2-stage loop, T=3 iterations, hand-driven via shell scripts and manual checkpoint selection.

Stage 1 (curriculum agent, GRPO, 5 steps, batch 128, 4 rollouts): it emits <question>…</question> + boxed answer. Reward = format gate x [ min(p̂, 1-p̂) (uncertainty; p̂ = executor majority-vote agreement over 10 tool-integrated samples, max 4 Python turns via SandboxFusion) + 0.05 x min(#tool calls, 4) (tool-use reward, counted in the proposer's text) - within-batch BLEU-agglomerative-cluster share (repetition penalty, distance threshold 0.5) ]. Executor is frozen.

Stage 2 (executor, ADPO in verl-tool): frozen curriculum generates ~8x1000 questions; executor samples 9 answers each (in evaluate.py, without tools); majority answer becomes the pseudo-label, its vote share p̂ the "score"; keep 0.3<=p̂<=0.8, drop proofs/text answers. Multi-turn RL (16 rollouts, max_turns=4, ~40-100 steps, KL 0.01) with reward I(answer == pseudo-label). ADPO = GRPO with (a) advantage x [0.5 + 0.5*(p̂-0.3)/0.5] (down-weight ambiguous tasks) and (b) eps_high = eps + 0.1*(0.8-p̂)/0.5 (looser upper clip on ambiguous tasks).

Next iteration re-trains the curriculum against the new executor. Reported ratchet: executor pass rate on curriculum sets 64->58.5->51%, avg tool calls 1.65->2.10->2.60.

Agent0-VL variant: one VLM plays Solver and Verifier; Verifier emits (score, conf, critique) per step; confidence-gated self-repair; GRPO on self-generated process reward; needs SFT cold-start data and an external question set (zero external reward, not zero data).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Inside the loop the only signal is self-consistency: the curriculum is rewarded for tasks where the executor's majority vote is ~50%, and the executor is rewarded for matching its own majority-vote pseudo-label. No ground truth or external verifier is used; tool execution grounds computation but never checks correctness. Anti-drift/anti-hacking measures: format gate (must emit question + boxed answer), band filter 0.3-0.8 (rejects trivial/unsolvable), BLEU-cluster repetition penalty (curriculum diversity), KL penalty 0.01, ADPO down-weighting of low-consistency samples, tool-reward cap at 4 calls. Improvement is only verified post-hoc on external held-out benchmarks (AIME/MATH/GSM8K/Olympiad, SuperGPQA/MMLU-Pro/BBEH); nothing in the loop gates or rolls back an iteration — the README says to "manually select the checkpoint". Reported numbers (Qwen3-8B): math avg 49.2->58.2 (55.1/56.5/58.2 per iteration), general 34.5->42.1; ablations: removing curriculum training 58.2->46.8, tool reward ->48.7, repetition penalty ->47.9, ADPO ->56.2, multi-turn ->55.9. Qwen3-4B math plateaus (51.9/52.2/52.5).
deep_reads.limitations: Paper has no limitations section. Demonstrated only on math-style tasks with a single numeric boxed answer (proofs/text answers explicitly discarded); "general reasoning" gains are transfer, not trained. Pseudo-labels from majority vote can be confidently wrong and are reinforced. 'Zero data' still needs a seed prompt dataset (hiyouga/math12k) to trigger generation (issue #21), and Agent0-VL needs SFT tool-usage data. Compute-heavy: 8xA100/H200; a user reports 5 curriculum steps took 24h+ (issue #37). Pipeline is not runnable end-to-end: two separate codebases/conda envs, manual handoff, executor config file missing (issue #26 open). Code/paper mismatches: data-curation scoring runs without tools; ablation table's full-model general avg (36.7) disagrees with main table (42.1); ADPO functional forms only in code. Gains shrink per iteration and 4B saturates after iter 1. Curriculum diversity question (issue #36) unanswered; open security issues (unauthenticated code-exec server, pickle loads). Venue acceptance claimed in repo description but not independently verified.
deep_reads.key_insight: Pairing a task-proposer whose reward is the solver's uncertainty (p̂ near 0.5) with a solver that has real tools, and paying the proposer for tool-dependent tasks, creates an automatic difficulty ratchet; the proposer's self-consistency score should then be reused as a trust signal that scales both advantage magnitude and the PPO clip range when training on pseudo-labels.
deep_reads.key_results: Qwen3-8B-Base: math avg 49.2->58.2 (+18%; beats R-Zero 54.7, Socratic-Zero 56.1, Absolute Zero 52.6), general avg 34.5->42.1. Qwen3-4B: math 42.6->52.5, general 27.1->37.6. Curriculum escalates: pass rate 64%->51%, tool calls/task 1.65->2.60 over 3 iterations. Ablation: curriculum training (-11.4 math), repetition penalty (-10.3), tool reward (-9.5) matter far more than ADPO (-2.0) or multi-turn (-2.3). Agent0-VL-7B: +8.2 avg over Qwen2.5-VL-7B across 3 iterations; also usable as a PRM (+3.6 to +4.7 Best-of-N).
deep_reads.safety_measures: Python execution goes through SandboxFusion (or a subprocess sandbox in Agent0-VL) with timeouts; KL penalty to base; format/band filters. No sandboxing of the self-improvement process itself, no rollback, no human review of generated curricula; open issues flag an unauthenticated 0.0.0.0 code-execution server and pickle deserialization in the data path.
open_gaps: Fitness is pure self-consistency majority vote with no external or tool-based correctness verification, so confidently-wrong majority answers are reinforced; a framework could add executable/verifier-checked ground truth or adversarial verification.
Restricted to single-numeric-answer math (proofs and text answers are dropped in evaluate.py); no mechanism for open-ended, agentic, or multi-step environment tasks (web, code repos, GUIs).
Only model weights evolve; prompts, tool set (a single Python sandbox), harness, and reward functions are fixed — no tool/skill creation or workflow evolution.

No regression gate or rollback between iterations: checkpoints are picked manually and there is no in-loop held-out evaluation; gains plateau (4B: 51.9->52.5) with no stopping criterion or collapse detection.
Requires multi-GPU RL fine-tuning (8xA100/H200, 24h+ per curriculum stage per user report), so unusable by application developers working with API models.
Loop is not automated end-to-end: two codebases (EasyR1-style verl + verl-tool), three conda envs, shell-script handoffs, and a missing executor config (issue #26) — no orchestrator.

No archive or population: each iteration keeps a single curriculum/executor lineage and discards prior curricula; diversity is enforced only by within-batch BLEU clustering with no cross-iteration dedup or memory of solved tasks.
No contamination/leakage audit of generated questions against benchmarks (issue #30) and no measurement of curriculum diversity over training (issue #36 unanswered).

Curriculum reward is a hand-tuned scalar mix (uncertainty + tool count + repetition penalty); the reward/evaluator itself never evolves and tool-call counting is gameable (trivially inserting code blocks).
'Zero data' still depends on a seed prompt dataset (math12k) and, for Agent0-VL, SFT cold-start data plus external question sets.

deep_reads.name: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Fudan University (Jiahang Lin, Shichun Liu, Chengjun Pan, Lizhi Lin, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Xuanjing Huang, Tao Gui, Yu-Gang Jiang) with Nex-AGI / Dawning Road (Hang Yan, Zhenhua Han); maintainer GitHub handle Curry09
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-03 (last push: crash-guard fix PR #11); open PRs #16-#19 from Aug-Sep 2026 unmerged; NexAU framework itself pushed 2026-09-10
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv only (cs.CL, cs.SE), no peer-reviewed venue; ranked #3 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 leaderboard as of 2026-05-15 (NexAU-AHE, GPT-5.5, 84.7%)
deep_reads.mechanism: Outer loop `evaluate -> analyze -> improve`, orchestrated by a 200KB `evolve.py`; base model frozen (GPT-5.4 high). (1) Evaluate: `harbor` runs the code agent (NexAU framework, seed = bash-only single shell tool + 10-line system prompt) with k=2 rollouts on all 89 Terminal-Bench 2 tasks in E2B sandboxes (64-96 concurrent), emitting per-task JSON traces + pass/fail. (2) Analyze: orchestrator computes task-level diff vs previous iteration (flipped / regressed / rollout_regressed) and runs `evaluate_changes()`: for each change in last iteration's `change_manifest.json` it intersects the declared `predicted_fixes` with observed flips and `risk_tasks` with observed regressions, yielding a verdict EFFECTIVE / PARTIALLY_EFFECTIVE / MIXED / INEFFECTIVE / HARMFUL plus `unattributed_regressions`. Agent Debugger (partially closed-source, GPT-5.4, 16 parallel `adb ask` jobs) distills >10M-token traces into `analysis/overview.md` + per-task `detail/*.md`. (3) Improve: Evolve Agent (NexAU meta-agent, GPT-5.4 xhigh, 500 turns, file/shell/web tools, context compaction, "ralph loop" middleware) reads evolution_history, analysis, attribution table and may only edit `workspace/`: systemprompt.md, code_agent.yaml, tool_descriptions/, tools/*.py, middleware/*.py, skills/, sub_agents/, LongTermMEMORY.md. Each logical change = one git commit + manifest entry (id, files, failure_pattern, predicted_fixes, risk_tasks, constraint_level, why_this_component); it runs `validate_agent.py` for schema/import checks. Rollback is prompted ("HARMFUL: must rollback") but executed by the LLM, not enforced by code — `perform_auto_rollback` only fires on manual resume. Optional Best-of-N (off by default): N=2 evolve agents with orthogonal strategy hints (structural vs guidance), both evaluated, higher pass_rate adopted. Stops at target_pass_rate 0.95 or max_iterations.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Fitness = pass@1 on the same 89 Terminal-Bench 2 tasks used for evolution (k=2 rollouts, ~3.2h/iteration); there is no train/held-out split (author confirms in issue #14 that the harness is evolved on the tasks it is scored on). Drift control is (a) falsifiable per-edit predictions checked against next-round task flips, (b) git-tracked file-level components so any edit is revertible, (c) prompt-level bans on task-specific logic / reverse-engineering tests / touching llm_config, (d) a best_ever.json snapshot surfaced to the agent. Reward hacking is only weakly guarded: the evolve agent can write to exp_dir including best_ever.json (issue #15), rollbacks are LLM-decided, and regression predictions are near random (11.8% precision vs 5.6% random) so 6/10 iterations did not improve. Generalization is argued post hoc via frozen-harness transfer to SWE-bench Verified (+0.4pp, -12% tokens) and to 4 other models (+2.3 to +10.1pp).
deep_reads.key_results: GPT-5.4 high on Terminal-Bench 2: 69.7% -> 77.0% pass@1 after 10 iterations (only 4 iterations improved: +0.6, +1.1, +2.8, +1.1); beats hand-written Codex-CLI 71.9%, ACE 68.9% (regresses below seed), Training-Free GRPO 72.3%. By difficulty: easy 100%, medium 88.2%, hard 53.3% (Codex hard 56.7% — no gain on hard). Component ablation (single component swapped into seed): memory-only 75.3%, tools-only 73.0%, middleware-only 71.9%, prompt-only 67.4% (below seed); gains non-additive. Attribution accuracy: fix precision 33.7% vs 6.5% random, fix recall 51.4%; regression precision 11.8% vs 5.6%. Frozen harness on SWE-bench Verified: 75.6% vs 75.2% seed with 461k vs 526k tokens (12% fewer); ACE/TF-GRPO regressed 9-11% there. Cross-model transfer without re-evolution: DeepSeek-v4-flash 51.7->61.8 (+10.1), Qwen-3.6-plus +6.3, Gemini-3.1-flash-lite +5.1, GPT-5.4 medium/xhigh +2.3. README/leaderboard claim NexAU-AHE 84.7% +/-2.1 with GPT-5.5 (not in paper; unclear whether re-evolved).
deep_reads.limitations: Evolves on the evaluation set itself with no held-out tasks; the released evolved harness is visibly benchmark-shaped ("mirror the evaluator", "verifier scripts are source of truth", references to "annealing spans" and cherry-pick recovery that match specific TB2 tasks). Seed is deliberately minimal (bash-only, ~10-line prompt) so a large share of the +7.3pp is recovering basic harness engineering; no gain on hard tasks. Curve is non-monotone and regression-blind; rollbacks are suggested to the LLM rather than enforced; the optimized agent can overwrite orchestrator state (best_ever.json, issue #15). Agent Debugger is only partially open-sourced; sandbox needs a 1-star fork NexAU-harbor and E2B (SaaS concurrency caps or self-hosted cluster); Python >=3.13; ~32h and heavy GPT-5.4 token spend for one campaign; k=2 rollouts is a noisy signal on 89 tasks. Single-lineage (no archive/population except optional Best-of-2). Baseline parity with ACE/TF-GRPO budgets not documented. Repo is mostly docs commits after May; community bug-fix PRs unmerged.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat every harness edit as a falsifiable experiment: force the optimizer to declare which tasks should flip and which are at risk, then mechanically score those predictions against the next round's per-task deltas and feed the verdicts back — this turns opaque LLM-driven "self-improvement" into an auditable, revertible, evidence-gated loop, and the ablation shows the durable gains live in tools, middleware and long-term memory, not in the system prompt (prompt-only edits regressed).
open_gaps: No train/held-out task split: fitness is pass@1 on the same 89 tasks being optimized, so overfitting to Terminal-Bench evaluator conventions is unmeasured (a new framework should evolve on a train slice and gate acceptance on a disjoint validation slice)
Rollback is advisory: attribution verdicts (HARMFUL/INEFFECTIVE) are shown to the LLM but no code reverts a change or blocks re-adoption; auto-revert to best-ever snapshot only runs on manual resume

Regression prediction is near random (11.8% precision vs 5.6% baseline) and unattributed regressions are just listed, so there is no causal isolation of which edit broke which task (e.g. per-edit A/B or leave-one-out evaluation)
Single lineage with greedy acceptance; no archive/population of harness variants, no Pareto front across task subsets, Best-of-N is n=2 and off by default
Optimizer process can write to orchestrator state (best_ever.json, exp_dir) — no integrity boundary between the evolved agent and its scorer
k=2 rollouts on 89 tasks gives noisy pass@1 (+/-1-2pp) yet single-iteration deltas of +0.6pp are treated as signal; no statistical acceptance test
Requires E2B sandboxes, a private-ish NexAU-harbor fork, and a partially closed Agent Debugger — not reproducible or usable by ordinary app developers; cost (~32h, GPT-5.4 xhigh) per campaign
Evolution only tested from a deliberately minimal bash-only seed with a frontier model; no evidence it improves a mature harness (Codex/OpenCode-like) or works with weaker evolve-agent models
No cross-task/cross-benchmark generalization during evolution — transfer is tested only post hoc on a frozen artifact; no mechanism to detect benchmark-specific leakage into prompts/memory
Evolved knowledge is unstructured (free-text LongTermMEMORY + prompt rules) with no dedup, decay, or conflict resolution across iterations
deep_reads.safety_measures: Edits confined to workspace/ (runs/, verifier, tracer, llm_config read-only); original seed prompt rules non-deletable; prompt bans on task-specific logic, hardcoded solutions and reverse-engineering tests; every change git-committed with a manifest for auditability; validate_agent.py schema/import check before eval; rollouts sandboxed in E2B; best-ever snapshot retained. Paper explicitly says it "does not provide a complete guardrail stack" and is a controlled research prototype; in practice rollback is LLM-discretionary and the evolve agent has write access to orchestrator state files.
sources_read: evolve.py (evaluate_changes, update_best_ever, perform_auto_rollback, select_variant_winner, main loop)

deep_reads.name: CORAL (Human-Agent-Society)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Human-Agent-Society / compounding-intelligence.ai — Ao Qu, Han Zheng, Zijian Zhou, Yihao Yan, ... Cathy Wu, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Jinhua Zhao, Paul Pu Liang (MIT, NUS, Stanford, Meta SI Lab)
deep_reads.date: Repo created 2026-03-16; public release 2026-03-18; paper arXiv:2604.01658 2026-04-03; COLM 2026 acceptance announced 2026-07-08
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-08 (last push); v0.7.21 released 2026-09-06; new issues 2026-09-09; ~weekly dev→main promotions since March
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: COLM 2026 (accepted); arXiv:2604.01658. Citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); 123 forks, 20 open issues
deep_reads.mechanism: The evolving object is a user-supplied codebase ("other"), not the harness. `coral start` clones the repo, creates one git worktree per agent (branch coral/<id>), symlinks a shared `.coral/public/` (attempts/, notes/, skills/, roles/, agents/) into each worktree as `.claude/` (or `.codex/` etc.), and spawns N external coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code default; Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Kiro, DeepSeek Harness, Pi). Each agent reads a generated CORAL.md and runs plan→edit→`coral eval -m "..."`→reflect. `coral eval` is the only git path: it commits, writes a pending Attempt JSON, and blocks until a separate grader daemon checks out the commit in a detached worktree and writes back score+status (improved/baseline/regressed vs that agent's personal best). All attempts form a parent_hash DAG; agents branch via `coral checkout <hash>` from any attempt (theirs or a teammate's). Knowledge evolves in the shared filesystem: agents must write a note or skill after every eval (create-notes skill with lint), and self-author an evidence-backed role file with a generation counter. A HeartbeatRunner injects prompts on eval-count triggers: reflect (every 1), consolidate (every 10 global: synthesize notes, audit team roles/lanes/postures, extract skills), lint_wiki (spawn librarian subagent), and pivot on a per-agent plateau streak (default 5 non-improving real evals, epsilon-tolerant, cooldown). Agents can rewrite their own heartbeat schedule (`coral heartbeat set`). Optional islands (v0.6) partition agents with island-local shared state; every K global evals the top-scoring agent per island migrates (uniform/round_robin/score/weakest weighting), carrying attempts+role but leaving notes/skills behind. An optional warm-start research-only phase precedes coding. Optional apex_judge grader evolves its own rubric on plateau.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = a user-written scalar grader (TaskGrader.evaluate → ScoreBundle, direction max/min), run by a long-lived daemon in a subprocess with SIGKILL timeout, inside `git worktree add --detach <commit>` under `.coral/private/grader_checkouts/` so concurrent agent edits cannot perturb grading; results written atomically. Hidden data (answer keys) lives in `.coral/private/` (denied to agents; Docker mode runs agents as unprivileged user), while the grader SOURCE is deliberately readable read-only so agents know exactly how they are scored (by design, invites specialization to the grader). Attempts are tagged budget_class real vs tune (`--tune` = cheaper sweep; excluded from leaderboard and plateau counter). Harbor benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, terminal-bench) use tiered eval (5→30→all instances gated on thresholds). Optional LLM rubric judges (static or self-evolving rubric) for open-ended artifacts, with feedback redaction levels. Drift/reward-hacking prevention is structural, not statistical: evaluator isolation, CLI-owned git, sandbox (srt FS/network enforcement or Docker), per-agent best-score comparison, plateau-triggered pivot, restart circuit breaker. There is no held-out set, no automatic rollback of regressions (agents are only told 'regressed' and must `coral checkout` themselves), and no validation of shared notes/skills before other agents consume them (open issues #67, #124).
deep_reads.limitations: Evidence is small-N and single-run: blog reports one run per config (no seeds, variance, or 1/2/4-agent scaling curve); heartbeat ablation is qualitative only ('agents share less without it'); only the notes/skills ablation has a number (-18.6% on kernel task). Erdős 'beats AlphaEvolve' margin is 0.38089 vs 0.38092, and the web-search variant discovered together.ai's published solution rather than deriving it. Baseline is OpenEvolve (open reimplementation), not AlphaEvolve itself; the paper summary also cites EvoX/ShinkaEvolve but exact table values were not retrievable. Cost/tokens not reported in the paper (blog: 'less than half the cost' on Erdős; hours of Opus 4.6 per run). Requires an authenticated external coding-agent CLI per agent (Claude Code/Codex subscriptions). Fitness must be a scalar per task; open-ended tasks depend on an LLM judge from the same model family as the worker. Shared memory has no validation layer, so hallucinated notes can become team doctrine (self-acknowledged in issues #67/#124); maintainers also report stalled attempts and tuning burning attempt budget (#72). Notes and skills do not persist across runs or tasks (each run reseeds from bundled templates). Human steering only at resume, not live. Docker-in-Docker unsupported for Harbor graders.
deep_reads.key_insight: Give a full coding agent the whole RETRIEVE→PROPOSE→EVALUATE→UPDATE loop instead of only PROPOSE (as AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve do), then make the harness's only jobs (a) an unhackable async grader and (b) periodic heartbeat interrupts (reflect/consolidate/pivot-on-plateau) that force agents to externalize knowledge into a shared filesystem — the blog's own finding is that without the interrupts, autonomous agents fixate and never write the notes/skills that make multi-agent gains (1363→1103 cycles) possible.
deep_reads.key_results: Kernel (Anthropic VLIW take-home, Opus 4.6, no web): seed 18,532 cycles; prior best-known 1,363; single CORAL agent 1,350 in 4.6h; 4 agents 1,103 in ~4.5h (24% better than single agent, 18-19% better than prior SOTA); OpenEvolve failed to beat 1,363. Erdős min-overlap C5: CORAL 0.38089 vs AlphaEvolve 0.38092 vs OpenEvolve 0.38111; reached 99% of AlphaEvolve score in 34 min vs 5.2h for OpenEvolve (claimed 10x faster, 7x fewer evals, 2.5x higher improved-attempt rate, <half the cost); with web search 0.380871→0.3808703. Stanford OpenVaccine (MLEBench split): 20.5% better MCRMSE than top human score, beating human in 2 evals. Paper adds: polyomino packing 89.4% coverage vs prior 87%; 36% of successful attempts descended from another agent's commit and cross-agent transfers had 17% improvement rate vs 9% average; disabling notes/skills regressed kernel result by 18.6%; 'best-known solution in 5-20 evals vs 100+ for traditional methods'.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Grader and hidden data in `.coral/private/` denied to agents (Docker: agents run as unprivileged user; host: opt-in `agents.isolate_user`); grader runs in separate venv + subprocess + detached worktree with SIGKILL timeout; CORAL owns git (agents never run git; `coral validate` rejects private data placed inside the visible grader package); workspace guard makes sibling worktrees read-only; optional `srt` sandbox provider with OS-level filesystem/network enforcement and allow-all proxy; optional LiteLLM gateway to intercept/log all model traffic; blocking tools (AskUserQuestion, plan mode) disabled for unmanned runs; manager health monitoring, exit classifier, restart-burst circuit breaker, auto-stop; run-level stop caps (max_real_attempts); constitution prompt asks for honesty/no deception (prompt-level only). No reported reward-hacking incidents; no automated detection of grader gaming beyond isolation.
open_gaps: No validation or quarantine gate on shared notes/skills before other agents consume them — hallucinated or overfit notes propagate as team doctrine (maintainers' own open issues #67, #124)
Fitness is a single visible scalar grader with readable source and no held-out evaluation; agents can specialize to the exact scoring code and nothing measures generalization
No automatic regression handling: a worse attempt is only labeled 'regressed'; no auto-revert, no best-of selection or final-artifact promotion policy — agent must manually `coral checkout`
No cross-run or cross-task transfer: notes/skills/roles live in results/<run>/.coral/ and every run reseeds from static bundled templates; nothing learned in run N is available in run N+1

Harness parameters are hand-set and static (heartbeat cadence every 1/10, plateau 5, migration every 16, prompts): the loop does not meta-optimize its own schedule, prompts, or team composition (issue #74 'gradient-style meta-evolve' open)
Population management ranks migrants by score window only; no novelty/diversity measure (MAP-Elites style), so the 'copycatting' convergence the blog documents is unmitigated
Evidence lacks seeds/variance and an agent-count scaling curve; heartbeat contribution is asserted qualitatively, not ablated numerically
Budget accounting is weak: stalled/infra-killed attempts consume the attempt budget and token cost is not tracked as a first-class metric (issue #72; gateway optional)
Open-ended tasks rely on an LLM judge (optionally self-evolving rubric) from the same model family as the worker with no calibration against judge gaming
Human steering is resume-only; no live human-in-the-loop injection into a running population

deep_reads.name: Everything Claude Code (ECC) — continuous-learning-v2.1 "instincts"
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Affaan Mustafa (affaan-m), single maintainer + community PRs; repo now canonical at github.com/affaan-m/ECC
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: GitHub OSS (MIT); 256k stars, 38k forks; npm ecc-universal; ECC Tools GitHub App. No paper, no benchmark.
deep_reads.mechanism: Four stages, all file-based under ~/.local/share/ecc-homunculus/projects/<git-remote-hash>/. (1) OBSERVE: plugin PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks (matcher .*, async, 10s timeout) run observe.sh, which appends one JSON line per tool call (tool, 5000-char-truncated input/output, session, project_id; regex secret-scrub) to observations.jsonl. Five guard layers stop it from observing subagents/its own observer (self-loop). No UserPromptSubmit hook, so user message text is never captured. (2) ANALYZE (off by default: observer.enabled=false): a per-project bash daemon (observer-loop.sh) wakes every 5 min or every 20 observations (SIGUSR1, 60s cooldown, session-guardian gating), tails the last 500 lines, and spawns `claude --model haiku --print --allowedTools Read,Write --max-turns 20-100` with a prompt: find patterns with 3+ occurrences (corrections, error resolutions, repeated tool sequences, tool preferences), write/update an instinct .md with YAML frontmatter (id, trigger, confidence by frequency bucket 3-5=0.5/6-10=0.7/11+=0.85, domain, scope project|global). Haiku must emit `{"status":"analysis_complete"}` as last line (verified via unlinked-inode fd); only then observations are archived, else retained for retry. 120s watchdog. (3) APPLY: SessionStart hook loads project+global instincts, keeps confidence>=0.7, dedupes by id, ranks by confidence + relevance boost (+0.25 project-scoped, +0.2 stack keyword match), injects top 6 as one-line "Active instincts" bullets into additionalContext. (4) EVOLVE/PROMOTE (manual CLI): greedy keyword-overlap clustering of triggers; clusters>=2 -> SKILL.md (concatenated action lines), workflow instincts>=0.7 -> command .md, clusters>=3 & avg>=0.75 -> agent .md, written to an evolved/ dir Claude Code does not auto-load. `promote`: same instinct id in >=2 projects with avg confidence>=0.8 -> copied to global. Pending instincts pruned after 30 days.
deep_reads.eval_loop: No objective fitness signal. "Confidence" is a frequency bucket assigned by the Haiku observer at write time; the documented dynamics (+0.05 per confirmation, -0.1 per contradiction, -0.02/week decay) are not implemented anywhere in instinct-cli.py or hooks. The only acceptance checks are format contracts: frontmatter present, completion record emitted, 3+ occurrences as judged by the LLM. Nothing records whether an injected instinct was followed, helped, or was overridden, so there is no closed feedback loop and no anti-drift mechanism beyond (a) project scoping to limit contamination, (b) the 0.7 injection floor and 6-item cap, (c) a prompt line telling the observer to treat observations as untrusted data, and (d) observer restricted to Read/Write tools. No A/B, benchmark, held-out test, or regression check on instinct quality exists; the repo's "eval framework" (PR #3040) is unrelated to this loop.
deep_reads.key_results: No quantitative results reported anywhere. Demonstrated: hooks reliably capture tool calls; SessionStart injection works (added 2026-04-05 after issue #1231 showed instincts were stored but never used); Haiku observer writes instinct files on macOS/Linux when enabled. Issue history shows the loop was effectively non-functional Jan-Apr 2026: --max-turns 3 produced 2,534 errors and zero instincts (#386), evolve --generate was a no-op stub (#217), ~/.claude writes blocked in --print mode (#1599, fixed by relocating data dir #1431), and no injection existed until #1231. Observer never survives on native Windows (#2489). Auto-generated instincts from the hosted GitHub App were reported as wrong-language, contradictory conventions (#2841). Repo-curated example instincts (8 items, e.g. "use conventional commits") illustrate typical output granularity.
deep_reads.limitations: Analysis stage disabled by default; fragile background daemon (dozens of observer bug issues, Windows unsupported). Observations lack user prompt text, so "user correction" detection is inference from tool patterns only. Confidence never updated after creation; no decay or contradiction handling despite docs. Promotion requires exact id string equality across projects whose ids are independently LLM-generated. Evolved skills/commands/agents land outside Claude Code discovery paths and are just concatenated action lines with no verification. Only 6 one-line instincts injected at session start, ranked by stack keywords not by task. Instinct files written by an LLM reading untrusted tool output are injected into future system context (prompt-injection surface). Single-user, manual export/import for sharing. Documentation overstates implemented behavior ("self-evolving" is partly marketing).
deep_reads.key_insight: Decouple learning from the working agent: deterministic harness hooks (100% capture) feed a cheap background LLM that distills sessions into atomic, confidence-scored, scope-tagged "instincts" stored as files, which a SessionStart hook re-injects above a confidence floor — a memory-write/memory-read loop that needs no model training and lives entirely in the harness.
open_gaps: No outcome-based fitness: confidence is LLM-estimated frequency, never tied to test pass/fail, task success, or user acceptance of an injected instinct
Confidence update rules (+0.05 confirm, -0.1 contradiction, weekly decay) are documented but unimplemented; nothing lowers or retires an instinct the user keeps overriding
No feedback capture on application: the system never logs whether an injected instinct was followed, helped, or was contradicted in the session it was injected into
User prompt text is not observed (no UserPromptSubmit hook), so explicit corrections — the highest-signal event — are invisible to the observer
Cross-project promotion needs exact id match across independently generated ids; no semantic/embedding dedup or merge of near-duplicate instincts
Evolved skills/commands/agents are written to a non-discovered directory and are unverified concatenations; no test that a generated skill executes or improves anything, no auto-install
No rollback, versioning, or A/B of instinct sets; no held-out evaluation to detect that a learned instinct degrades behavior
Retrieval is SessionStart-only, capped at 6 lines, ranked by stack keywords — no task-time or query-conditioned retrieval of relevant instincts
Prompt-injection path: untrusted tool outputs -> LLM-written instinct files -> injected into future system context, mitigated only by a prompt instruction
Analysis stage is off by default and depends on a fragile bash daemon (fails on Windows, many macOS/Linux edge cases); no yield/health metric on instincts produced per observation batch
Single-user learning with manual export/import; no team-level aggregation, conflict resolution, or provenance across users
deep_reads.safety_measures: Observer session self-loop guards (entrypoint, ECC_SKIP_OBSERVE, agent_id, path exclusions); observer limited to Read/Write tools, haiku, max-turns and 120s watchdog; regex secret scrubbing before persisting observations; data dir moved out of ~/.claude; completion record validated on an unlinked inode to prevent forged results; observations archived only after verified analysis; instincts must contain no code snippets (prompt rule); project scoping to prevent cross-project contamination; confidence >=0.7 floor and 6-item cap on injection; 30-day TTL prune of pending instincts; AgentShield scanner for hooks/prompts. No human-in-the-loop approval on auto-generated instincts before injection.
sources_read: GitHub issues #386, #217, #1231, #1599, #1431, #2489, #2841, #2746 and issue search for instinct/observer

deep_reads.name: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Mirac Suzgun, Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Dan Jurafsky, James Zou (Stanford)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-03-12 (single "dynamic cheatsheet v2.0" commit: unified multi-provider client, hybrid CumulativeRetrieval variant, README rewrite; before that untouched since Apr 2025)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv 2504.07952 (Apr 2025); published as EACL 2026 long paper (DOI 10.18653/v1/2026.eacl-long.333). Exact citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited; OpenAlex shows 4 on the EACL DOI, a clear undercount). Used as the primary baseline by ACE (Agentic Context Engineering), ReasoningBank, MemSkill lines.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Single black-box LM plays two roles per query, state is ONE string (the cheatsheet). Verified in dynamic_cheatsheet/language_model.py (advanced_generate):

DC-Cumulative: (1) Generator prompt = fixed solver instructions + [[CHEATSHEET]] + [[QUESTION]]. If the output contains a ```python block followed by "EXECUTE CODE!", the harness runs it via subprocess (python3 temp file, 3s timeout, no sandbox) and appends the stdout, looping until no more code. (2) Curator prompt = curator instructions + [[PREVIOUS_CHEATSHEET]] + [[QUESTION]] + [[MODEL_ANSWER]] (full generator transcript incl. execution output). The curator is told to "assess the correctness of the provided solution" itself, then REWRITE THE ENTIRE cheatsheet inside <cheatsheet> tags (cap ~2000-2500 words; <memory_item> blocks with description/example, Q-references, and an LLM-maintained "Count" field). extract_cheatsheet() replaces the old string; if no tags are found the old cheatsheet is silently kept. No labels, no reward, no verifier gate, no rollback, no archive: acceptance = whatever the curator emits.

DC-RetrievalSynthesis: precomputed input embeddings (per-dataset CSV) retrieve top-k=3 prior (input, generator-output) pairs by cosine similarity; curator synthesizes a per-query cheatsheet from those pairs + previous cheatsheet; generator then answers. v2.0 adds CumulativeRetrieval (cumulative sheet + retrieved raw pairs in the same prompt). Baselines: FullHistoryAppending (verbatim history) and Dynamic_Retrieval (retrieval without curation).

Runs once over a shuffled (seed 10) test set, single trajectory, single agent, max_num_rounds defaults to 1. run_benchmark.py computes accuracy only for printing/logging; it is never fed back into the cheatsheet.
deep_reads.eval_loop: There is no fitness signal in the loop. Memory updates are driven solely by the curator LM's own judgment of the generator transcript (plus incidental Python execution output the generator chose to run). Ground-truth accuracy is computed offline in run_benchmark.py purely for reporting. Nothing prevents drift or reward hacking except prompt wording ("only include solutions that have been tested and proven effective", "copy relevant old content or it is lost"). Empirically from the released logs: the cheatsheet does not grow (stays at 4-6 memory_items, 400-1300 words) because each step is a full rewrite; older entries are overwritten (final AIME sheet after 133 problems is dominated by Q131-Q133); the "Count" field is hallucinated (an entry citing 16 unrelated AIME questions); a stored angle-bisector "theorem" is mathematically garbled; curator emitted an unparseable/no-op sheet in 14/133 GPT-4o AIME steps. Regressions (e.g. DC-Cu lowering GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Physics from 75.6 to 70.4) are not detected or reverted.
deep_reads.key_results: Recomputed from released results/*.jsonl with the repo's own evaluators (BL = plain baseline; DC-0 = same solver prompt + code execution but empty memory; DC-Cu; DC-RS). Claude 3.5 Sonnet: AIME 2020-24 (n=133) BL 6.8 -> DC-0 30.1 -> DC-Cu 38.3 -> DC-RS 40.6; AIME 2025 (n=30) 6.7 -> 23.3 -> 36.7 / 30.0; AIME 2024 23.3 -> 36.7 -> 50.0 / 46.7; GPQA-Diamond (n=198) 59.6 -> 60.1 -> 60.6 / 68.7; MMLU-Pro Physics 74.0 -> 75.6 -> 77.6 / 82.0; MMLU-Pro Engineering 61.2 -> 57.2 -> 66.8 / 67.6; MathEquationBalancer 44.8 -> 56.4 -> 100 / 97.8. GPT-4o: AIME 2020-24 BL 9.8 -> DC-0 24.1 -> DC-Cu 18.0 (worse than empty) -> DC-RS 24.8 (no gain over empty); GPQA-D 57.1 -> 56.6 -> 57.6 / 57.1 (nil); MMLU-Pro Physics 75.6 -> 70.8 -> 70.4 / 75.2 (DC-Cu hurts); Engineering 53.2 -> 51.6 -> 44.0 (run incomplete, 141/250) / 50.8; MathEqBalancer 50 -> 88 -> 100 / 99.2, but uncurated Dynamic_Retrieval also hits 100. The headline "Game of 24 GPT-4o 10% -> 99%" is claimed in README/paper but NO Game of 24 logs are released. Key takeaway: a large share of the "doubling" on AIME comes from the DC-0 scaffold (structured prompt + Python execution), with memory adding ~8-13pp on Claude and ~0 on GPT-4o; biggest memory-specific win is on homogeneous tasks (equation balancing, Game of 24) where the sheet converges on "write Python to brute-force/verify".
deep_reads.limitations: Paper-stated: context-length bound on memory; effectiveness bounded by base model (smaller models gain less); benefits require high similarity across test-time examples; sensitive to prompt wording. Observed in code/logs: (1) no correctness signal to the curator, wrong strategies and garbled theorems are stored; (2) full-rewrite curation makes memory a bounded rolling summary, not an accumulating archive, with strong recency bias and hallucinated usage counters; (3) no versioning/rollback/A-B, regressions on GPT-4o go unnoticed; (4) order-dependent single pass over a shuffled test set, i.e. it learns on the test stream it is evaluated on, no held-out generalization or cross-task transfer test; (5) retrieval variant depends on offline precomputed OpenAI-embedding CSVs per dataset, not an online memory store; (6) Python execution is an unsandboxed subprocess (author TODO admits it); (7) curator call doubles API cost and the 1000+-word sheet is re-sent every query, no cost accounting; (8) only short single-turn QA benchmarks, no agentic/multi-step/coding tasks (issue #4 asking about SWE-bench is unanswered); (9) no tests, no packaging, one .ipynb for evaluation; results JSONLs for some runs are incomplete (141/250, 139/250).
deep_reads.key_insight: Splitting inference into a solver and a curator that rewrites a compact, structured natural-language memory after every episode is enough to get label-free test-time learning on a black-box model, but it only pays off when a cheap verifier (Python execution) is in the loop and the task stream is homogeneous; without an external acceptance signal, the memory converges to a handful of recency-biased, unverified entries rather than a growing library.
open_gaps: No acceptance gate on memory writes: curator judges correctness by itself; a framework could gate insertions on execution-verified outcomes, self-consistency, or later downstream success and evict entries whose use correlates with failures
Full-rewrite curation caps memory at ~5 items and silently discards older insights; needs incremental append/edit/dedup operations with stable IDs (delta updates rather than regeneration)
No versioning, rollback, or A/B evaluation of memory states, so regressions (e.g. GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Physics -5pp with DC-Cu) are never detected or reverted
Learns and is evaluated on the same shuffled test stream; no held-out split, no measurement of order sensitivity, no cross-task transfer (e.g. reuse an AIME cheatsheet on GPQA)
Single agent, single trajectory: no population/archive of alternative cheatsheets, no selection among candidates
Usage counters and Q-references are LLM-maintained text and hallucinate; provenance and hit-counts should be tracked by the harness, not the model
Retrieval variant needs offline precomputed per-dataset embedding CSVs; no online embedding/store, so it cannot be deployed on an open-ended query stream
Unsandboxed Python execution (subprocess, 3s timeout) with no resource/network isolation
Only single-turn QA tasks; not tested on multi-step agentic, tool-use, or coding benchmarks (SWE-bench request in issue #4 unanswered)
No token/cost accounting: curator doubles calls and a 1000+-word sheet is resent per query; no policy for when to skip curation
Gains vanish or reverse for weaker models (GPT-4o often at or below the empty-cheatsheet scaffold); no open-weight model results
Game of 24 headline (10% to 99%) is not reproducible from released artifacts since those logs are absent
deep_reads.safety_measures: None beyond prompt text. Code execution is an unsandboxed python3 subprocess with a 3-second timeout (author's TODO acknowledges it). extract_cheatsheet() falls back to the previous cheatsheet if the curator output lacks <cheatsheet> tags. Curator prompt asks the model to assess correctness and to preserve old content, but nothing enforces either.

deep_reads.name: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Huan-ang Gao, Jiayi Geng, Wenyue Hua, Mengkang Hu, Xinzhe Juan, Hongzhang Liu, Shilong Liu, Jiahao Qiu, ... Qingyun Wu, Heng Ji, Mengdi Wang (26 authors in v1, ~35 in v4; Princeton, Tsinghua, CMU, UIUC, Penn State, U. Sydney, and ~10 other institutions; corresponding: Mengdi Wang / Heng Ji)
deep_reads.date: v1 2025-07-28 (title 'On Path to Artificial Super Intelligence'); v4 2026-01-16 (retitled 'What, When, How, and Where to Evolve ...')
deep_reads.last_activity: Paper: v4 on 2026-01-16. Companion repo: last push 2025-10-15; community PRs/issues still being filed through 2026-06-14 but none merged since Oct 2025.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI), no peer-reviewed venue found. OpenAlex reports 3 citations (clearly an undercount for a preprint; Semantic Scholar was rate-limited so its count could not be verified). Companion repo CharlesQ9/Self-Evolving-Agents: 1,313 stars, 106 forks. Widely referenced as the canonical taxonomy for the term 'self-evolving agent' (scout note), though a competing 'Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents' (arXiv 2508.07407) appeared two weeks later.
deep_reads.mechanism:
This is a survey, not a system: it proposes no loop of its own and runs no experiments. Its contribution is a formal frame plus a four-axis taxonomy for other people's loops.

Formalization: agent-environment interaction is a POMDP; an agent is a tuple of (architecture, model(s), context [memory + prompts], toolset). 'Self-evolution' is an update operator that rewrites one or more tuple components from observed trajectories and feedback so as to maximize cumulative utility over a task stream.

Taxonomy axes:
- WHAT to evolve: (1) model weights via self-generated supervision / env feedback (STaR, SELF, Self-Challenging, RAGEN); (2) context: memory evolution (Mem0, MemoryOS, Agent Workflow Memory) and prompt optimization (APE, OPRO, ProTeGi, PromptAgent, TextGrad, DSPy); (3) tools: creation/mastery/selection (Voyager, Alita, ATLASS, ToolGen); (4) architecture: single-agent workflow search (AgentSquare, ADAS, AFlow, Godel Agent, AlphaEvolve) and multi-agent topology/orchestration (EvoFlow, MaAS, ScoreFlow, FlowReasoner, ReMA).
- WHEN: intra-test-time (adaptation during a task via ICL/reflection, TTT, TTRL, SEAL) vs inter-test-time (retrospective learning between tasks: STaR, SiriuS, WebRL curriculum, DigiRL).
- HOW: reward-based (scalar env reward, textual critique, self-confidence/consistency, rule-based rewards, self-play), imitation/demonstration (self-generated, cross-agent, hybrid), population-based/evolutionary (Darwin Godel Machine, GA over LLM populations, SPIN/SPC self-play, evolving orchestration).
- WHERE: general (web/GUI/mobile assistants) vs specialized (coding, healthcare, education, finance).

Evaluation frame: five goals (adaptivity, retention, generalization, efficiency, safety) and three paradigms (static, short-horizon adaptive, long-horizon lifelong assessment).
deep_reads.eval_loop: None of its own. The survey catalogs signals used by others (env rewards, unit tests/SWE-bench, textual critiques, self-consistency/confidence, self-play win rates, LLM/agent-as-judge e.g. Mind2Web 2) and benchmarks (AgentBench, GAIA, SWE-bench, OSWorld, WebArena, MLE-bench, MCP-Universe, LifelongAgentBench, Agent-SafetyBench). Its normative contribution is to argue that adaptivity should be measured alongside retention (forgetting), generalization under shift, cost/efficiency, and safety, and that longitudinal, persistent-state, cost-aware evaluation is needed because 'most benchmarks use episodic evaluation that resets agent states', so cumulative learning and catastrophic forgetting are invisible. On drift/reward hacking it only names the risks ('misevolution', deployment-time reward hacking, unsafe self-created tools) and prescribes guardrails (sandboxing, automated verification of self-generated tools, immutable audit trails, tested rollback, monitoring, red-teaming, human approval gates); no metric, protocol, or formula is specified.
deep_reads.key_results: No empirical results. Deliverables: (a) a POMDP/agent-tuple formalization of self-evolution; (b) the What/When/How/Where taxonomy; (c) a five-goal, three-paradigm evaluation framework; (d) domain review (coding, GUI, healthcare, education, finance); (e) future-direction list (personalization/cold-start, generalization vs specialization, safe and controllable evolution, multi-agent ecosystems). Companion repo catalogs ~183 entries (~157 unique arXiv papers) organized by the taxonomy. Retitled and expanded in v4 (Jan 2026) to add the 'Where' axis and grew to ~35 authors.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated by authors: evaluation is 'the most underserved area'; retention/forgetting rarely measured; safety mechanisms for self-modifying agents underdeveloped; co-evolutionary multi-agent dynamics and theory of safe adaptation not addressed in depth. Observed: no unified benchmark or reproduction; the formalization is a thin POMDP restatement with no operational definition distinguishing 'self-evolution' from ordinary test-time refinement (Reflexion/Self-Refine are filed as intra-test-time evolution even though nothing persists); the 'path to ASI' framing is rhetorical; the companion repo is a link list with no code and has been effectively unmaintained since Oct 2025 (5 community PRs open since Jan-Jun 2026). 'Self-evolving' here is a taxonomy label, not a demonstrated capability.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat self-evolution as an explicit update operator over a typed agent tuple (model, context, tools, architecture), classify every method by which component it rewrites, whether it fires inside a task or between tasks, and what signal drives it (reward / demonstration / population), and then evaluate not just adaptivity but retention, generalization, cost and safety over a persistent, non-resetting task stream.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Discussion only, no implementation: identifies misevolution (goal/alignment drift), deployment-time reward hacking of self-defined rewards, vulnerable/malicious self-generated tools, and memory privacy leakage; recommends sandboxing, automated security verification of self-created tools, immutable audit trails for every evolutionary change, tested rollback, continuous monitoring, automated red-teaming, and human approval gates for high-stakes changes. Cites TrustAgent, AgentDAM, Agent-SafetyBench, ST-WebAgentBench.
open_gaps: No executable reference implementation of the taxonomy: a framework could expose the agent tuple (model/context/tools/architecture) as typed, versioned mutable slots with a uniform evolve() interface
No benchmark or protocol for the 'retention' goal the survey calls most underserved: a persistent, non-resetting task stream that measures cumulative gain and forgetting across sessions
No cost-aware evaluation: the survey asks for efficiency metrics but gives none; a framework could log tokens/wall-clock per evolution step and report improvement-per-dollar
Guardrails (audit trail, rollback, tool verification, human approval gates) are prescribed but never operationalized; none of the cataloged systems ship an immutable change log with rollback
No treatment of when NOT to evolve: no trigger/gating policy that decides whether a task warrants a persistent update versus one-off in-context adaptation
Cross-component coupling is unexamined: nothing about co-evolving memory + tools + prompts jointly, or arbitration when updates to different slots conflict
No held-out generalization discipline: cataloged methods mostly optimize on the evaluation distribution; a framework could enforce train/holdout task splits for every accepted mutation
Reward-evaluator evolution (self-rewarding, self-play critics) is listed but the survey gives no defense against evaluator drift or Goodharting when the judge is itself mutable
Nearly all covered methods require either GPU fine-tuning or offline search; no lightweight, weight-free loop targeted at application developers running frontier APIs
Companion repo is a stale link list (no merges since Oct 2025); no living, machine-readable registry of self-evolving methods with reproducible results
