deep_reads.name: ReasoningBank (+ MaTTS: memory-aware test-time scaling)
deep_reads.mechanism: Closed loop per task in a stream, with frozen weights and a fixed agent scaffold. (1) Retrieve: embed the new task query (gemini-embedding-001, 3072-d; Qwen3-Embedding-8B optional), cosine-score against cached embeddings of PAST TASK QUERIES (not memory items), take the top-1 prior task (code: select_memory(n=1)) and paste its memory items (<=3) into the system prompt with an instruction to "explicitly discuss if you want to use each memory item". (2) Act: BrowserGym/WebArena agent or mini-swe-agent runs the task. (3) Self-judge: an LLM labels the trajectory success/fail with no ground truth -- WebArena uses a prompt over last-5 page captions + think/action history; SWE-Bench uses a one-line "Did the agent succeed? answer success/fail" prompt at temp 0. (4) Extract: the backbone LLM (temp 1.0) is given the trajectory + judge rationale and one of two system prompts (SUCCESSFUL_SI / FAILED_SI) to emit <=3 items of {Title, Description (when/when-not to use), Content (1-3 sentences)}; failures yield "recovery procedures / pitfalls". (5) Consolidate: items are appended to a JSONL file keyed by task_id; no dedup, pruning, merging, scoring, or decay. MaTTS: parallel = run k trajectories per task (separate ports), pick answer by LLM best-of-N (paper), then induce memory from ALL k trajectories with a "self-contrast" prompt (PARALLEL_SI, <=5 items) that compares successes vs failures; sequential = re-prompt the agent to re-examine its own trajectory, using the intermediate reflections as memory signal. The claim is bidirectional: better memory makes scaling productive, and more diverse rollouts give richer contrastive signal for memory.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Improvement signal is purely the LLM self-judge (success/fail label, no ground truth, no test execution even on SWE-Bench) feeding a one-shot memory-extraction prompt. There is NO fitness gate on the memory itself: every extracted item is appended regardless of whether it later helps, there is no held-out check, no A/B of memory vs no-memory, no rollback, no dedup/contradiction resolution, and no exclusion of the current task from retrieval (issues #17/#36: reruns can retrieve memory from the same task instance). Reported metric = task success rate + avg steps on WebArena/Mind2Web/SWE-Bench-Verified, graded by a vendored, modified WebArena harness (lenient 'MemEvol' llm_fuzzy_match prompt with Gemini-2.5-pro instead of GPT-4-turbo, patched shopping annotations), so absolute numbers are not leaderboard-comparable. Paper says judge noise is tolerated empirically; drift/reward-hacking is not addressed beyond that.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated by authors: retrieval and consolidation are 'intentionally minimal'; judge dependence introduces noise; future work on compositional memory and learned controllers. Observed: (a) reproducibility is contested -- three independent reports (issues #2, #6, #11) find no gain or degradation vs no-memory on WebArena-Shopping with Gemini-2.5-Flash (e.g. 42.2->42.8 with GT reward; 50.05 no-memory vs 45.99 ReasoningBank via AI Studio; ~36-37% vs paper's 49.7%); another user found ReasoningBank ~= AWM on Qwen3.5. Authors acknowledged codebase errors, pushed a cleanup in Apr 2026, and results were obtained with a modified WebArena grader not originally in the repo. (b) Released code is incomplete vs paper: no sequential-MaTTS pipeline, no LLM best-of-N selector, parallel induction prompt omits success/fail labels, induce_scaling.py still has inverted 'reward==0 -> success' and reads the same results dir for every sample. (c) Memory bank is a flat append-only JSONL per website; retrieval is top-1 prior task by query similarity; bank grows linearly with no forgetting. (d) Benchmarks are sequential single-pass over a test stream, so 'learning' and 'evaluation' are on the same tasks (online setting), and cross-site transfer is not tested (memory files are per-website). (e) Only Gemini/Claude via Vertex supported cleanly. Google disclaimer: 'demonstration purposes only... not intended for production'.
deep_reads.key_insight: Store distilled, reusable reasoning strategies (title/description/content) rather than raw trajectories or success-only workflows, and mine FAILED trajectories for explicit pitfalls/recovery rules; then treat extra test-time rollouts as a source of contrastive signal for memory synthesis (memory <-> TTS synergy) rather than only as answer-selection.
open_gaps: No fitness/acceptance test for a memory item: items are appended unconditionally; a framework should score items by downstream lift (e.g. counterfactual replay or held-out tasks) and evict/rollback harmful ones
No consolidation: no dedup, merging, contradiction resolution, versioning, or decay -- bank grows linearly; template_id is stored 'for deduplication' but never used
Retrieval is top-1 prior TASK by query-embedding similarity, not retrieval over memory items themselves; no reranking, no usage/success statistics, no negative-result tracking
Self-judge is a single unverified LLM call (SWE-Bench: one-line 'success/fail' prompt) -- no test execution, no calibration, no confidence gating; mislabeled trajectories poison memory silently

Current-task/self-retrieval contamination not guarded (issue #17/#36 open); evaluation protocol conflates online learning on the test stream with generalization -- no train/test split, no cross-website or cross-domain transfer of one bank
Memory is per-website/per-model text; no cross-task, cross-environment, or cross-agent sharing, and no mechanism to evolve tools/skills/code, only prompt-injected text

Sequential MaTTS and LLM best-of-N selector described in the paper are not in the released code; parallel-induction script has an inverted success label -- an implementable, tested reference loop is missing

Reported gains rely on a modified, lenient WebArena grader (Gemini-2.5-pro fuzzy match) and are not reproduced by three independent groups -- a new framework needs a standardized, GT-verified eval harness with ablations against no-memory at equal token budget

Absolute numbers depend on Vertex AI-hosted Gemini; no open-weight reproduction; token/cost overhead of memory extraction (extra LLM calls per task, k-fold under MaTTS) is only reported as +4.3% inference tokens
No safety layer: no filtering of memory content, no protection against adversarial/injected memory, no human review, no rollback

deep_reads.name: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Xunjian Yin, Xinyi Wang, Liangming Pan, Li Lin, Xiaojun Wan, William Yang Wang — Peking University, UC Santa Barbara, University of Arizona
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2025-09-17 ("fix typo and change api": swapped optimizer to o3-2025-04-16, solver to gpt-4.1-mini / gpt-4o-mini). Only 9 commits total; no substantive code evolution since Oct 2024.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ACL 2025 main (Long Papers). Semantic Scholar: 30 citations on the ACL record (+23 on the arXiv record, likely overlapping), 2 influential; OpenAlex: 5. Cited as the self-referential predecessor by Darwin Gödel Machine (Zhang et al. 2025) and HyperAgents.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Single Python process; the agent IS the running module `agent_module`. Fixed parts: goal prompt (goal_prompt.md), `action_call_llm` / `action_call_json_format_llm` (explicitly protected from modification), the task's `evaluate()` harness, and the OpenAI API. Everything else — including `solver` (the policy π), `Agent.evolve` and `Agent.execute_action` (the meta-learner I), and the tool list — lives in runtime memory and is mutable.

Loop (mutual recursion, not a for-loop): `evolve()` builds messages = [goal prompt, `action_environment_aware()` summary of globals/attributes, last 10 items of `optimize_history`], calls the optimizer LLM (GPT-4o in paper; o3 in current code) with `tool_choice="required"` over 7 tools: display_analysis (think-before-act), environment_aware, read_logic (inspect.getsource on any function/class), adjust_logic (exec new code and setattr onto module/class = monkey patching; stores `__source__` so it can re-read itself), run_code (python exec into globals / bash), call_json_format_llm, evaluate_on_task. `execute_action()` runs each tool call, catches all exceptions and returns the traceback as the tool result (error handling), then calls `agent.evolve()` again. Hard stop after 100 evolve calls; paper used 30 iterations x 6 independent cycles per task.

Fitness: `evaluate_on_task` runs solver on 50 random questions from a 128-question validation set (48 threads); if valid acc >= 0.94 threshold it also runs the 800-question test set and returns BOTH numbers as feedback (per-sample info is commented out). If test acc beats `last_test_acc`, `store_all_logic()` dumps all in-memory functions/classes to disk as a best-so-far snapshot. No automatic rollback: the goal prompt tells the LLM to "backtrack, restore the original state" itself.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = task accuracy (F1 for DROP) on a held-out validation subset (128 q; 32 for GPQA), sampled 50 at a time with a time-seeded shuffle, plus the 800-question test accuracy once valid acc crosses 0.94. The feedback string returned to the optimizer LLM is just "Valid Accuracy: X / Test Accuracy: Y" (the released code comments out per-sample diagnostics, though the goal prompt asks for case studies of low-score examples). Drift/regression control is weak and delegated to the LLM: there is no automatic accept/reject gate on a modification — a new solver stays live regardless of score; the only mechanical safeguard is that the best-scoring snapshot is written to disk. The paper reports 92% of 100 MGSM trials show temporary performance drops, 4% terminate unexpectedly (usually the agent broke its own `evolve`), and 14% end worse than the initial policy. Anti-reward-hacking is minimal: `adjust_logic` refuses edits to `action_call_llm`, bans `time.sleep`/`logging`, and the harness code (task_*.py) is a separate module the agent is not told to edit, but `run_code` gives it unrestricted exec and it could modify `task_mgsm.evaluate` or `last_test_acc`. Test accuracy leaking into the optimization feedback is a genuine evaluation flaw. A random-sampling control (30 GPT-4o resamples of the initial prompt) stays ~30% on MGSM vs. Gödel Agent's climb, showing the feedback matters.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 1 (solver = gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, optimizer = gpt-4o-2024-05-13, ADAS/Meta Agent Search protocol): Gödel-base DROP 80.9 F1 / MGSM 64.2 / MMLU 70.9 / GPQA 34.9 vs Meta Agent Search 79.4 / 53.4 / 69.6 / 34.6 vs CoT 64.2 / 28.0 / 65.4 / 29.2. Gödel-free (agent allowed to call GPT-4o inside the solver) 90.5 / 90.6 / 87.9 / 55.7 — this is mostly a model-upgrade effect the paper itself admits. Ablation on MGSM: w/o think-before-act 50.8 (-13.4), w/o error handling 49.4 (-14.8), w/o run_code 57.1 (-7.1), w/o call_LLM 60.4 (-3.8). Cost ~$15 for 30 iterations across all four datasets vs ~$300 for Meta Agent Search. Game of 24: after 6 failed LLM-prompt tweaks the agent rewrote the solver as brute-force arithmetic search -> 100%; but with ToT as the initial policy, no run exceeded ToT's own performance. Robustness: 100 MGSM trials -> 4% crash, 92% temporary dips, 14% end below initial policy. Repo's archived best solvers (matching Table 1 numbers) are all variants of CoT + self-consistency majority voting with n=5-20 samples (plus few-shot for MMLU); the archived `Agent.evolve` is byte-identical to the initial one, i.e. the meta-learner was never actually improved in the released best runs.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: can't compete with heavily engineered systems (e.g. OpenDevin) since it must build all task code itself; self-comprehension may degrade as the agent's own code grows (Yampolskiy); unsafe without sandboxing and constrained modification. Observed from code/paper: (1) demonstrated gains come almost entirely from policy-level edits — the discovered policies are textbook self-consistency/few-shot, and the meta-level (evolve/execute_action) was not improved in any released run, so 'recursive' self-improvement of the learner is claimed but not demonstrated; (2) no acceptance gate or rollback — bad edits stay live and the LLM must notice and revert; (3) test-set accuracy is fed back to the optimizer, contaminating the reported test numbers; (4) memory is the last 10 messages, so the agent forgets earlier experiments and repeats them; (5) mutual recursion evolve->execute_action->evolve grows the Python stack every step (capped at 100); (6) single-agent, single-lineage, no population/archive beyond a best-snapshot dump; (7) Gödel-free numbers are inflated by calling a stronger model; (8) baselines copied from the ADAS paper rather than re-run; (9) Game-of-24 'innovation' is brute-force search, and with a strong initial policy (ToT) the agent never beat it; (10) unrestricted exec of LLM-generated code in the host process with the API key on disk.
deep_reads.key_insight: Make the agent's own runtime memory the substrate of evolution: expose inspect/exec-based read and monkey-patch write of every live function (including the improver itself) as ordinary tool calls, so the boundary between 'policy' and 'meta-learner' disappears and a single LLM tool-loop can in principle rewrite either — and the two things that actually made this work empirically were not the self-reference but (a) forcing an explicit analysis step before each edit and (b) catching every exception and feeding the traceback back as a tool result instead of crashing.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Minimal and mostly prompt-level: `action_adjust_logic` raises on attempts to modify `Agent.action_call_llm`/`action_call_json_format_llm`, on `time.sleep` in solver, and on use of `logging`; all tool exceptions are caught and returned as text; hard cap of 100 evolve calls (sys.exit). Everything else is unrestricted: `action_run_code` does raw `exec` in module globals and `subprocess.run(shell=True)`, the agent can edit its own `evolve`, and the evaluation harness module is reachable. Paper's ethics statement recommends sandboxing and constrained-modification rules but neither is implemented. No rollback, no diff review, no human-in-the-loop.
open_gaps: No automatic accept/reject gate: a modified solver goes live regardless of its validation score; the only safeguard is a best-snapshot dump to disk, so a framework should add score-gated commit + automatic revert to the last accepted version.

Meta-level self-modification is possible but never demonstrated to help: the released best runs leave Agent.evolve untouched, and modifications to it were the main cause of crashes (4%). A framework needs a protected/versioned meta-loop with a separate acceptance test for improver edits.

Fitness = single-task accuracy on 50 sampled validation questions with test accuracy leaked into the feedback string; no held-out generalization, no cross-task transfer, no noise-aware comparison (50-sample acc has ~±7% CI).

Memory is the last 10 tool messages; there is no archive of tried modifications, their scores, or diffs, so the agent re-tries ideas and cannot do credit assignment across iterations (paper's own cost note says growing history is the main cost driver — a structured experiment log would fix both).
Single lineage, no population/branching: a bad edit stalls the run; nothing like DGM's archive or tree search over agent variants.

Discovered policies are all self-consistency + few-shot variants; with a strong initial policy (ToT) no run beat it, so the open-endedness claim is untested — a framework needs curricula or task sequencing (the authors list this as future work) to push past the LLM's known tricks.

No sandboxing: LLM-generated code is exec'd in the host process with shell access and the API key on disk; the evaluation harness and score variable (last_test_acc) are reachable and could be gamed. Needs process isolation plus an immutable evaluator.

Mutual recursion evolve->execute_action->evolve grows the Python stack each iteration and hard-exits at 100; the loop should be a resumable, checkpointable state machine so long runs, crash recovery and multi-day evolution are possible.
Optimizer and solver are both OpenAI-only with hard-coded model enums; no model-agnostic interface, no local models, no cost/budget accounting inside the loop.

Evaluation of the evolved agent happens on the same task it evolved on; no study of whether an evolved solver or evolved improver transfers to a new benchmark, and no comparison against simply running CoT-SC with n=20 on the base model (the trick the agent found).

deep_reads.name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM): Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
deep_reads.mechanism: Substrate is the Huxley-Gödel Machine archive tree, but each node is a multi-agent *workspace*: one shared codebase holding a meta-agent (edits the workspace), task agents (coder / paper writer / prover) and learned evaluators (code reviewer / paper reviewer / proof grader). Algorithm 1 loop over a budget of 12,288 binary validation outcomes: (1) UCB-Air gate: expand when N^0.6 >= |archive|; pick a parent by Thompson sampling on clade-metaproductivity (Beta posterior pooled over the subtree); the meta-agent self-modifies the workspace using ~3 training tasks as feedback; the child enters the archive if it runs. (2) Otherwise evaluate: Thompson-sample a node, choose the least-measured role, then its least-measured task; record a binary outcome tagged with (utility, evaluator slot, epoch). Utility = mean over tasks, then over roles. Evaluator-independent utilities (Polyglot unit tests, CRAVE code-review labels, APReS human accept/reject, IMO-GradingBench human grades) coexist with evaluator-dependent ones (the frozen incumbent judge's verdict on the task agent's artifact). (3) At power-of-two checkpoints (8,16,...,8192) each evaluator slot compares its incumbent with challenger evaluators discovered in the archive on a fixed held-out ground-truth anchor (e.g. 100 CRAVE items) via BB_eps = Beta^-1(0.05; 1+S, 1+F); a challenger with >=5 anchor outcomes wins only if strictly higher (ties keep incumbent). On replacement the slot's epoch increments, the new evaluator is frozen, and every record that depended on the old evaluator is erased (anchor/test records survive; cached artifacts are lazily re-scored), so the archive re-ranks under the stricter criterion. Adversarial objectives can be injected at boundaries: AI-written papers the old reviewer over-accepted become an adversarial pool the next reviewer must reject. Output: per-utility specialist (max BB_eps) and generalist (max mean BB_eps).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = binary success/failure per (node, role, task), aggregated by clade-metaproductivity for search and by an eps=0.05 Beta-posterior lower bound (best-belief) for selection. Two signal classes: evaluator-independent ground truth (Polyglot executable tests; CRAVE PR-acceptance labels; APReS human accept/reject; IMO-GradingBench human grades) and evaluator-dependent LLM-judge verdicts from the frozen incumbent reviewer/grader. Anti-drift / anti-reward-hacking controls: (a) the learned judge is frozen within an epoch so HGM's fixed-criterion guarantees hold per epoch; (b) judges are replaced only at exponentially spaced checkpoints and only when a challenger strictly beats the incumbent's conservative lower bound on a held-out ground-truth anchor the proposer never sees; (c) selective erasure deletes all evidence that depended on the displaced judge so stale scores cannot steer search; (d) strict train (10) / validation (49) / held-out test (166) isolation on Polyglot; (e) adversarial pools of over-accepted AI papers debias reviewers (baseline reviewer accepted AI papers at 1.42-1.91x the human rate; RQGM reviewers become equally stringent). Residual weaknesses: within an epoch the task agent can still overfit the frozen judge; the ceiling is the anchor's decision boundary; there is no cross-epoch convergence guarantee; evaluation in the writing domain is itself an LLM-judge panel.
deep_reads.limitations: Demonstrated gains on verifiable coding are small: Polyglot 71.7% (119/166) vs HGM-H 69.9% (116/166) with GPT-5.5 low; the real win is 1.35-1.72x fewer blended search tokens (efficiency, not capability), and seed count is unclear. All guarantees are epoch-local (no global convergence across evaluator changes) and horizons are short. Improvement is capped by the fixed human-labeled ground-truth anchor (APReS, CRAVE, IMO-GradingBench): evaluators cannot exceed the anchor's decision boundary and repeated promotion risks anchor overfitting. Writing-domain results (40.5% vs 21.8% acceptance) are judged by an LLM panel, not humans. In proof writing the co-evolved prover still loses at the strictest Pass@7 threshold (48.3% vs 55%) to the hand-built IMO25 pipeline (authors attribute this to budget). Binary outcomes only; uniform role/task weighting; SWE-bench excluded for runtime. Per an independent reimplementer, Appendix E notes the measured gains came mostly from prompt rewrites, not deep code self-modification. Expensive (12,288 evals, $25/expansion caps, frontier model). Official code NOT released: camlsys/godel-machines is a stub (LICENSE + requirements.txt, 0 stars) and the private 16-tool coder harness, full prompts, task splits and CRAVE anchor sample are unpublished; the independent OpenRQGM 12,288-outcome reconstruction saw 4 evaluator replacements but an earlier 128-outcome run saw none, so co-evolution may simply not fire at small budgets.
deep_reads.key_insight: Make the evaluator a versioned, replaceable slot rather than a fixed frame: freeze it within epochs so fixed-criterion search guarantees still hold, replace it only at sparse checkpoints when a challenger beats the incumbent's conservative Beta lower bound on a held-out ground-truth anchor, and on replacement erase only the evidence that depended on the old judge so the archive re-ranks under the stricter criterion (an emergent curriculum) while anchor-based evidence persists.
open_gaps: No official code: camlsys/godel-machines is an empty stub, so the private coder harness (16 tools), full role prompts, Polyglot split and CRAVE anchor sample are unavailable; nobody can reproduce the headline numbers

Requires a fixed human-labeled ground-truth anchor per domain (CRAVE, APReS, IMO grades); no mechanism to create, grow, rotate or audit anchors automatically, so the evaluator's ceiling is the anchor and anchor overfitting is unaddressed
Guarantees are only per-epoch; no regret/convergence bound across evaluator transitions and no detection of oscillation or regression after a swap
Within an epoch the task agent can still Goodhart the frozen LLM judge; no collusion detection, randomized holdout queries or judge ensembles
Binary 0/1 outcomes only; graded rubrics, partial credit and continuous rewards must be thresholded
Uniform averaging across roles and tasks; no learned weighting, no handling of negative transfer between co-evolving roles sharing one codebase
Checkpoint schedule (rho=2), eps=0.05 and alpha=0.6 are fixed hyperparameters with no published sensitivity ablations; no multiple-testing control across many sequential replacement decisions
Self-modification gains were mostly prompt rewrites (App. E); no analysis of which workspace edits (tools, code, prompts) transfer across domains
Compute-heavy: 12,288 frontier-model evaluations per run and SWE-bench excluded for runtime; no cheap-model or app-developer-scale recipe
Coding gain is +1.8pp on a single benchmark with unclear seed count; no held-out cross-benchmark generalization of the discovered coder/reviewer
Evaluator replacement can fail to fire at small budgets (OpenRQGM 128-outcome run: zero replacements), so small-scale users get plain HGM plus a reviewer overhead
Safety/containment for evolved evaluators (sandboxing, permission boundaries, rollback of a bad evaluator promotion) is not specified beyond Docker and $ caps

deep_reads.safety_measures: Frozen evaluators within epochs; replacement only at checkpoints and only when a challenger strictly beats the incumbent's eps=0.05 Beta lower bound on a held-out anchor (ties keep incumbent, min 5 anchor outcomes); selective erasure of evaluator-dependent evidence after replacement; anchors isolated from proposers; train/val/test isolation; adversarial pools to debias reviewers against AI-generated text; Valid(a') gate (child must run); Docker-sandboxed code execution; per-call cost caps ($25 expand / $8 train / $25 val). No formal containment, rollback of bad evaluator promotions, or collusion detection is specified.
deep_reads.key_results: Coding (Polyglot, GPT-5.5 low, 12,288 evals): RQGM 71.7% (119/166) vs HGM-H 69.9% (116/166) with 1.35-1.72x fewer blended search tokens; ~90% of workspace edits shared between coder and reviewer roles. Scientific writing (APReS anchor): co-evolved writer 40.5% vs 21.8% acceptance under a diverse agent-as-a-judge panel (1.78-1.86x); baseline reviewers over-accepted AI papers at 1.42-1.91x the human rate, adversarial objective yields reviewers equally stringent on AI and human work. Proofs (IMO-GradingBench): co-evolved grader +9% ground-truth accuracy at ~3x lower search cost than HGM-H; prover beats SOTA self-improvers and IMO25 pipeline on mean score and Pass@6 but trails at Pass@7 (48.3% vs 55%). Theory: epoch-local validity inherited from HGM; anchor-gated promotion; erasure overhead linear in budget with exponential checkpoints (Prop. 6). Fig. 3: evaluator replacement permanently re-ranks the archive (curriculum effect). Independent OpenRQGM reconstruction (single seed, different harness) reached 163/166 held-out with 4 evaluator replacements, but without matched HGM-H controls.

deep_reads.name: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Seth Karten*, Joel Zhang*, Tersoo Upaa Jr, Ruirong Feng, Wenzhe Li, Chengshuai Shi, Chi Jin (Princeton University; Zhang also ARISE Foundation), Kiran Vodrahalli (Google DeepMind)
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2026-05-13 (release commit, renamed from sethkarten/pokeagent-speedrun); open security issue #52 filed 2026-08-03 unanswered
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (no venue yet); HF Papers 20 upvotes, alphaXiv ~2.1k views; citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited). Repo stars are inherited from the earlier PokeAgent Challenge (NeurIPS 2025 competition) framework, created 2025-07-08, so not attributable purely to this paper.
deep_reads.mechanism: Harness state H=(p,G,K,M): strategic system prompt p, sub-agent registry G (looping/one-step delegates with own tool lists and max_turns), skill library K (text heuristics or inline-Python executed via run_skill in a pseudo-sandbox), memory store M. Inner loop: VLM agent observes frame + ASCII map, acts via press_buttons and meta-tools (process_skill, run_code, process_subagent, process_memory). Outer loop (HarnessEvolver, same model as agent, text-only): after 25-step warmup, every 25 steps for first 200 then every 100 (or on-demand via the agent calling the evolve_harness tool), it loads the last ~50 JSONL trajectory rows, extracts tool-call failures by regex on results, counts run_code-vs-run_skill antipattern, then runs four independent LLM passes each returning JSON: (1) full rewrite of p; (2) create/update/retire sub-agents; (3) add/update skills incl. full code replacement; (4) add/update memory with importance rebalancing. Edits are applied in place immediately (H_{t+1}=H_t ⊕ Δ) with no episode reset; a summary is injected into the agent's context. Bootstrap mode imports a prior run's memory/skills/subagents/evolved prompt re-pathed under bootstrapped/. Co-learning loop (not released): Gemma-4 student (E2B/E4B/26B-MoE/31B) after SFT warmup + offline GRPO runs K=256-step DAgger rollouts inside the live-refining harness; a process reward model scores sliding windows in [0,1] (progress, correctness, reasoning quality, format); low-reward windows are relabeled by Gemini-3.1-Pro teacher; soft SFT updates θ; emulator + harness state carry over between iterations.
deep_reads.eval_loop: For the harness loop there is no fitness signal, acceptance test, or rollback: every Refiner edit (including a wholesale prompt rewrite) is accepted unconditionally on the LLM's own reading of a 50-step trajectory window; 'effectiveness' ratings on skills are LLM self-assigned. The only mechanical signals are regex-detected tool-call errors and a run_code/run_skill ratio warning. Milestone count vs cumulative button presses / API dollars is the paper's evaluation metric but is not fed back into refinement. In the co-learning loop the signal is a PRM plus frontier-teacher relabeling (DAgger), which is the only place drift is countered; the paper itself documents drift in the harness loop (Red bootstrap-updating: sub-agent inheritance collapsed to 6.4% and milestones regressed). Per-entry mutation_history and evolution_log.jsonl exist for audit only. Released code also has a bug where store.add returns a str but the evolver reads .id, so newly created components are logged as failures and never announced to the agent, and Refiner-created skills omit the code field.
deep_reads.limitations: Capability floor: strictly Pareto-dominant only on Gemini 3 Pro (Emerald from-scratch 100% milestones at median $130 vs H_min 98% at $215, ~40% cheaper), high variance on Flash ($42/80% vs $30/77%), worse than the minimalist baseline on Flash-Lite (3-13% vs 20%). Evaluation only reaches gym 3 (Red 18 milestones, Emerald 31) on a single game family. Residual gap to hand-engineered expert harness concentrated in dialogue-heavy areas and multi-turn battle strategy. Most Refiner-created skills are never invoked (create-forget-focus-fix funnel). Bootstrap transfer is fragile (Emerald >96% inheritance, Red 6.4% with regression). No head-to-head comparison against reset-based optimizers like GEPA at matched budget. Co-learning loop is not saturated and has no convergence criterion; it needs a frontier teacher and GPU fine-tuning, and that pipeline is not in the released repo. Expensive ($130+/run). Skill exec 'sandbox' keeps __import__ and /mcp/* routes are unauthenticated (issue #52). GPP completions of Blue/Yellow/Crystal were human-in-the-loop, not by Continual Harness.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the whole harness (prompt, sub-agents, executable skills, memory) as a mutable CRUD-editable state that a Refiner rewrites mid-episode from a rolling trajectory window, so improvements compound within one long run and can be exported as a bootstrap artifact; but without a fitness gate this only works above a model-capability threshold.
open_gaps: No acceptance test or rollback for harness edits: prompt rewrites and skill/sub-agent CRUD are applied unconditionally with no A/B on milestone rate, cost, or held-out tasks
No regression guard against drift/forgetting: paper shows bootstrap-updating on Red discarded inherited sub-agents (6.4% reuse) and regressed; needs reuse priors or dedup/retention rules
Refiner is schedule-driven (every 25/100 steps) rather than triggered by measured stagnation or uncertainty; no adaptive or budget-aware update policy
Fitness/eval is a single game family (Pokemon Red/Emerald to gym 3); no cross-game or cross-domain transfer of learned skills/sub-agents
Weight update loop requires a frontier teacher, PRM, and GPU SFT and is not released; no API-only, app-developer-usable path to weight co-learning
Skill lifecycle is wasteful: most created skills are never used; no usage-based pruning, testing, or verification before a skill enters the working set
Skill code runs in a fake sandbox (retains __import__) with unauthenticated write routes; no isolation or review of self-written executable code
No reset-vs-reset-free comparison at matched budget, so the core claim that online adaptation beats GEPA-style episodic optimization is untested
Released Refiner has bugs (add() returns str but .id is read; created skills lack code), so evolution logs undercount and agent is never told about new components
Works only above a capability floor (fails on Flash-Lite); no mechanism to let weaker/cheaper models bootstrap via simpler refinement tiers
deep_reads.key_results: Emerald, Gemini 3 Pro: CH from scratch reaches 100% of 31 milestones at median $130 vs minimalist harness 98% at $215 (~40% cost cut); bootstrap variants cheaper still; CH strictly Pareto-dominant on Pro, high-variance on Flash, below baseline on Flash-Lite. Red (18 milestones): all CH variants cut button-press cost vs H_min and recover a majority of the gap to the hand-engineered expert harness; bootstrap-updating beats from-scratch at every milestone. Navigation skill path-cost deficit vs Dijkstra oracle falls from ~50% to single digits with hundreds of skill calls in 24h (zero for H_min). Sub-agent context cost ~10x lower than orchestrator, near-100% return success on nav/dialogue/menu. Co-learning: Gemma-4 26B/31B advance milestones across 30+ reset-free iterations from game start and from mid-game checkpoints (milestones 12/15/24); Gemma warmup-only and Qwen3.5 27B/35B controls make no progress. GPP (human-in-the-loop precursor) first AI to finish Blue, Yellow Legacy hard mode, and Crystal with no lost battle.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Minimal. Sub-agent tool lists are validated against an allowlist, max_turns capped at 50, char caps on sub-agent fields, built-in sub-agents cannot be deleted, evolution passes are isolated so one failure does not block others, prompt rewrite falls back to prior prompt on exception, and every store edit records mutation_history plus an evolution_log.jsonl. Skill/run_code execution uses a hand-built __builtins__ dict but leaves __import__ in it (escape trivial), and the game server exposes unauthenticated /mcp/process_skill and /mcp/process_subagent routes with wildcard CORS (open issue #52). No sandbox timeout, no human review, no rollback of harmful edits.

deep_reads.name: AgentEvolver
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Alibaba Tongyi Lab / ModelScope (Yunpeng Zhai, Shuchang Tao, Cheng Chen, Anni Zou, ..., Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou; 13 authors)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-04-01 (last push; last substantive master commit 2026-01-30 'online observer'; SeeUPO branch 2026-04-01). Issues still being filed through 2026-08 with no maintainer replies.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2511.10395 (cs.LG), Nov 2025; no venue. Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar 429). Follow-ups from same group: CuES (arXiv 2512.01311, curiosity-driven task synthesis) and SeeUPO (sequence-level agentic RL, Mar 2026 branch).
deep_reads.mechanism:
Outer loop is standard GRPO on veRL/Ray updating Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct weights (lr 1e-6, batch 32, n=8 rollouts/task, KL 0.001, max 30 env steps, 8xA100). Three LLM-driven modules feed it:

1) Self-questioning (Task Manager): a human-written Environment Profile JSON (entities/attributes/operations + task_preference difficulty knobs) seeds a random-walk exploration by an external LLM (Qwen-Plus, temp 1.0; breadth-first Nb steps then depth-first Nd) against the sandboxed env_service. Trajectories are summarized into TaskObjective = {query, ground_truth action_sequence}. Curation: lexical dedup (0.8), FeasibilityFilter re-executes the reference solution, UnifiedMixtureStrategy mixes synthetic with original tasks. Synthetic tasks are graded by an LLM judge (Qwen3-235B) that sees the reference solution (`llm-binary-gt-no_constraint`); original tasks use env reward.

2) Self-navigating (Experience Manager + ReMe service): before training, the initial policy does 4 rollouts/task; ReMe runs success/failure/comparative extraction -> LLM validation -> dedup -> vector store. At rollout, top-k (3) experiences are retrieved by cosine similarity and prepended for eta=0.5 of each group ('mixed'); experience text is regex-stripped before the gradient ('alldiscard') so the policy must internalize it; positive-advantage experience samples get a wider PPO upper clip (0.6 vs 0.28) via an exp_mask heterogeneous loss. Reference config sets updated_freq: 0, so the pool is static after cold-start (code supports periodic async re-summarization).

3) Self-attributing (ADCA-GRPO): Qwen-Max labels every step GOOD/BAD in one pass given the trajectory and outcome; mapped to +/-0.2, z-scored per group at trajectory level, fused with separately z-scored outcome reward at the terminal step (alpha=1.0), suffix-summed into step advantages and broadcast to tokens.

Single policy; no population, no archive, no acceptance gate — every RL step is applied.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = benchmark scores on held-out AppWorld (TGC, test-normal) and BFCL v3 multi-turn val splits, avg@8/best@8, run before training and periodically; validation rollouts use no experience injection (woexp) so it measures internalized capability. Training reward: env verifier for original tasks, reference-grounded LLM judge for synthetic tasks (judge sees ground truth, actor does not — but this isolation is not machine-checked, see issue #48). Drift/hacking guards: feasibility re-execution of reference solutions, dedup filters, experience stripping before gradient, separate normalization of process vs outcome signals, KL penalty. There is NO fitness-based acceptance or rollback of weight updates, no held-out-environment generalization test, and the judges/attributors are fixed frontier models that are never audited during training. Reproducibility is contested: issue #46 reports far lower step-0 and post-training BFCL/AppWorld numbers (TGC@8 <10%), unanswered.
deep_reads.key_results: Qwen2.5-7B: AppWorld avg@8 1.8 -> 32.4 (best@8 5.6 -> 51.2), BFCL v3 29.8 -> 57.9; avg 15.8 -> 45.2. Qwen2.5-14B: AppWorld 18.0 -> 48.7, BFCL 41.6 -> 66.5; avg 29.8 -> 57.6. The trained 7B (45.2) beats the untrained 14B base (29.8) — the 'small beats 14B' claim compares to an un-finetuned baseline, not a 14B trained with plain GRPO. Ablations: +Questioning alone gives most of the gain (7B avg 15.8 -> 36.1); +Navigating adds ~3.7, +Attributing adds ~5.2, all three 45.2. Docs claim ADCA-GRPO gives ~10% improvement and ~40% fewer training steps vs GRPO. Paper claims synthetic tasks match ground-truth data and reference-grounded judge beats naive LLM judging (numbers not extractable from HTML).
deep_reads.limitations: (1) Not truly 'self': exploration, task synthesis, reward judging, step attribution and experience summarization all call stronger external teacher models (Qwen-Plus/Qwen-Max/Qwen3-235B) — the evolving policy is distilling from fixed frontier models. (2) Requires manual Environment Profile per environment plus a sandboxed env_service. (3) Experience pool is static after cold start in the reference config (updated_freq: 0); no experience retirement or utility tracking; experience unused at test. (4) No acceptance test/rollback/best-checkpoint gating of weight updates. (5) Evaluated only on two tool-use benchmarks; mixture uses original benchmark tasks (use_original_tasks: true) so gains are not purely from synthetic data. (6) Heavy: 8xA100, Ray+veRL+vLLM+ReMe services; OOM reports (#30, #41). (7) Reproducibility contested (#46, #45), BFCL training script missing (#32), no HF checkpoint export (#29). (8) Master effectively unmaintained since ~Feb 2026; security issue (#50: env_service unauthenticated, code execution) open. (9) Modules are independent; no coupling of attribution/experience back into task generation (listed as 'upcoming').
deep_reads.key_insight: Turn the three bottlenecks of agentic RL (no tasks, blind exploration, sparse credit) into LLM-generated signals that are kept OUT of the gradient path: tasks come from environment exploration with executable reference solutions for grounded judging; retrieved experience is injected only at rollout and stripped before the policy update (with a looser off-policy clip) so it is distilled into weights instead of memorized; and per-step GOOD/BAD attribution is z-scored separately from the outcome reward so dense process credit cannot swamp the sparse success signal.
open_gaps: Evaluator/teacher does not evolve: judges (Qwen3-235B, Qwen-Max) and explorer (Qwen-Plus) are fixed external APIs; no self-consistency check of judge against env ground truth during training and no mechanism to detect judge exploitation
No acceptance gate or rollback: every RL step is applied regardless of validation; no best-checkpoint selection, no regression detection on held-out tasks

Experience pool is cold-start only (updated_freq: 0 in overall.yaml); no online curation, no per-experience utility scoring, no retirement of stale/harmful experiences, and experience is never used at inference time
Task curriculum is static: difficulty set by hand-tuned task_preference in the Environment Profile, not adapted to the policy's current pass rate (no targeting of 20-80% success band)
Environment Profile (entities/attributes/operations) must be hand-written per environment; no automatic schema induction from API specs or exploration
Ground-truth/reference-solution isolation from the actor is not machine-checked (issue #48 asks for a canary test) — a leak would let the policy learn the answer channel
Weights-only evolution requiring 8xA100 + Ray/veRL/vLLM/ReMe; nothing here is usable by an application developer who cannot fine-tune
Three modules run independently; attribution labels are not fed back to task generation or experience extraction, and no multi-agent co-evolution despite the separate Game Arena
No cross-environment transfer: experiences and synthetic tasks are per-workspace; generalization is only tested on the same benchmark's held-out split
Reproducibility unresolved: multiple users report much lower AppWorld/BFCL numbers than the paper (#46), BFCL training script absent (#32), and master has had no maintainer response since ~Mar 2026
deep_reads.safety_measures: Sandboxed env_service for exploration/rollouts (but unauthenticated, binds 0.0.0.0, /step executes code — open issue #50). FeasibilityFilter re-executes reference solutions to drop hallucinated tasks; lexical/semantic dedup. Reference solution is passed only to the judge path by design but without a regression test. KL penalty (0.001) and PPO clipping bound policy drift; experience stripping prevents memorizing injected text. No guard against judge-model reward hacking, no rollback of bad updates, no human-in-the-loop.

deep_reads.name: OpenEvolve
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Asankhaya Sharma (codelion) / algorithmicsuperintelligence org; ~53 contributors
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-18 (last push; v0.3.0-0.3.2 released Jul 2026; before that a gap Mar-Jul 2026)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: No paper; software citation only. Two HF blog posts by the author. Used as the RL environment/verifier in ThetaEvolve (arXiv 2511.23473, 177-star repo) and as the comparison baseline in most 2026 LLM-evolution papers per scout. PyPI ~17k downloads/month (Sep 2026). 1154 forks, 118 open issues.
deep_reads.mechanism: A single fixed harness evolves a user-supplied artifact (a source file in any language, or a prompt text file) against a user-written evaluator; nothing about the agent itself evolves. Loop per iteration (process_parallel.py:_run_iteration_worker): (1) controller round-robins islands, snapshots the DB, samples a parent from the current island (20% uniform island pick, 70% from the elite archive, 10% random) plus inspirations (island-best + top-k by fitness + programs from perturbed neighbouring MAP-Elites cells + random island members); (2) prompt sampler builds system+user prompt containing parent code, parent metrics, previous attempts with per-metric improved/regressed outcome vs their parents, top and diverse exemplars, parent's execution artifacts (stderr, timeouts, LLM feedback, up to 20KB), and optional stochastic template variations; (3) one LLM from a weighted ensemble emits SEARCH/REPLACE diffs (or a full rewrite); diffs are applied to the parent, rejected if no valid diff or code > max_code_length; (4) child is evaluated via the user's evaluate() with timeout (300s default), optional cascade stages gated by thresholds [0.5,0.75,0.9], optional LLM-judge metrics blended at weight 0.1; (5) child is inserted into the island's MAP-Elites grid keyed by (code-length bin, edit-distance-diversity bin, plus user feature metrics); it takes a cell only if fitness (combined_score, else mean of non-feature metrics) beats the incumbent; optional embedding+LLM novelty gate; population cap 1000 evicts non-cell-owners first; (6) every 50 island generations the top 10% migrate to ring neighbours (once per lineage, dedup by code). Checkpoints every 100 iterations; early stopping on patience or target score.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = user-written evaluator returning a metrics dict; fitness = metrics["combined_score"] if present else mean of numeric metrics excluding MAP-Elites feature dimensions (boolean metrics excluded since v0.3.2). Optional cascade evaluation (cheap stage1 -> stage2 -> stage3, each gated by a threshold) and optional LLM-as-judge quality scores mixed in at weight 0.1 (prompt-evolution example uses 70% task accuracy + 30% LLM feedback). Drift/regression control is purely archival elitism: a child never overwrites a parent, only displaces a MAP-Elites cell incumbent with lower fitness; global best_program_id is protected from eviction; islands + migration-once-per-lineage limit takeover by clones; optional cosine-similarity + LLM novelty rejection. There is no held-out/generalization split, no re-evaluation of noisy scores, no verification that the LLM stayed inside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers (open issue #106), and no sandbox: evaluated code runs in the worker process via run_in_executor with only a timeout (memory_limit_mb/cpu_limit are config fields never enforced). Reward hacking is therefore bounded only by how well the user wrote the evaluator; the LLM-judge component is directly gameable by the same LLM that writes the code.
deep_reads.key_results: Circle packing n=26: sum of radii 2.634 (99.97% of AlphaEvolve's 2.635; 'matches', not exceeds; ThetaEvolve later used OpenEvolve as env to reach 2.63598). Prompt evolution (examples/llm_prompt_optimization, Qwen3): IFEval 95.01->97.41, HotpotQA 77.93->88.62 (+10.7 pts), HoVer 43.83->42.90 (regressed); README's '+23%' figure does not match the example's own table. Function minimization: random search -> simulated annealing. MLX Metal GQA kernel: README advertises '2.8x faster' and the 2025 blog claimed +12.5% decode; but PR #377 (merged 2026-01-28) found evolved kernels were never actually applied in the benchmark subprocess and the head ratio was wrong; after the fix, 25 iterations produced a kernel 3.2% SLOWER than baseline (example README, 'Current Status'). TSP example claims SOTA-style results via the new changes-description mode (Jan 2026). Reproducibility: seed=42 default, full deterministic component seeding.
deep_reads.limitations: 1) Marketing exceeds evidence: top-level README still claims 2.8x kernel speedup that the example's own README now says is -3.2% after validity fixes; HotpotQA '+23%' vs measured +10.7 pts; HoVer regressed. 2) Nothing self-modifies: the harness, prompts (use_meta_prompting is a dead config flag; 'Self-Modifying Prompts' is still roadmap), evaluator and search hyperparameters are fixed per run; no learning carries across runs or tasks. 3) Single file, single EVOLVE-BLOCK region; multi-file/codebase evolution unsupported (issues #111, #149); LLM often ignores block markers (#106). 4) Fitness is a scalar; multi-objective handling is a weighted combined_score or naive mean (#110, #453, #458). 5) No sandbox or resource limits on evaluated code; no held-out evaluation, so overfitting to the evaluator's samples is undetected (prompt example evaluates on 10/40-sample subsets). 6) Noisy evaluators are not re-evaluated; a lucky score permanently occupies a cell. 7) Operational fragility: process-pool crashes (#246), retry cleanup bugs (#288); MAP-Elites eviction and island-sampling bugs only fixed Jul 2026 (#452, #454, #471) meaning many published baselines ran on buggy sampling. 8) Cost: $0.01-0.60 per iteration; 100s-1000s of iterations typical.
deep_reads.key_insight: Use the LLM purely as a mutation operator and put all the 'intelligence' of the loop into the archive and the prompt: an island-partitioned MAP-Elites grid (keyed by cheap structural features like code length and edit-distance diversity plus user metrics) accepts a child only if it beats its cell incumbent, and the mutation prompt is filled with structured feedback the search already has for free: parent metrics, per-attempt improved/regressed deltas, top and diverse exemplars, and raw execution artifacts (stderr, timeouts). Elitism-by-cell rather than trust in the model is what prevents collapse and regressions.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Per-evaluation asyncio timeout (300s default) with timeout artifacts; max_retries; max_code_length (10k chars) rejection; artifact_security_filter and 20KB artifact cap in prompts; parent programs are immutable (children are new DB entries, so 'rollback' is implicit); best program protected from eviction; per-model max_budget_usd for the Claude Code backend; checkpoints every 100 iterations for resume. No sandboxing of evaluated code, no enforced memory/CPU limits (config fields exist but are unused), no verification that edits stayed within EVOLVE-BLOCK, no held-out check.
open_gaps: No cross-run or cross-task transfer: every run starts from a blank archive; discovered strategies, failure patterns and good prompts are not persisted as reusable skills/memory

Harness does not evolve itself: system prompt, template variations, sampling ratios, feature dimensions, cascade thresholds and migration schedule are static per run (use_meta_prompting is an unused flag; 'self-modifying prompts' is roadmap only)

Fitness = the user's single evaluator on the same samples every time; no held-out split, no re-evaluation of noisy scores, no detection of overfitting or evaluator gaming (LLM-judge feedback is blended into fitness and can be gamed by the same model)
No sandbox or resource isolation for evaluated programs (memory_limit_mb/cpu_limit are parsed but never enforced); evolved code runs in the worker process
Single-file, single EVOLVE-BLOCK target; no multi-file/repository-scale evolution and no check that the LLM respected block markers (issue #106)
Scalar fitness only; no Pareto front / vector-valued combined_score (issues #110, #453, #458)
Mutation is one-shot: no agentic repair loop, tool use, or test execution inside the mutation step (issues #276, #339, #443 request 'repair sub-agent')
No credit assignment over which prompt ingredients (artifacts, inspirations, template variants) actually caused improvements; the trace exists (evolution_trace.py) but nothing consumes it
Evaluator must be hand-written per task; no automatic evaluator/test synthesis or curriculum of tasks
No mechanism to start from multiple seed programs or to crossover across islands beyond copy-migration (issues #55, #126)

deep_reads.name: OpenRSI / Frontis-MA1 / OpenMLE (Gym + ERL + Evo + Sandbox)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Frontis AI + Tsinghua University (Junlin Yang, Che Jiang, Yu Fu, ..., Ning Ding, Bowen Zhou, Kaiyan Zhang; 24 authors)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-08 (gym fixes for task packages; NatureBench eval-contract fix 2026-09-04; EEMA EMNLP announcement 2026-08-25)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv 2607.28568 (186 HF Papers upvotes); companion EEMA paper accepted EMNLP 2026 Main (code not yet released); RSI survey on OpenReview; NatureBench arXiv 2606.24530
deep_reads.mechanism: Two nested loops on a shared action space of four program operators (Draft, Improve, Debug, Crossover). INNER LOOP (OpenMLE-Evo, test-time, per task, 12h budget): a FunSearch/REvolve-style island population vendored from Meta's AIRA-Dojo. Default config: 1 island, max 500 nodes, 800 steps, 100 generations x 5 individuals, crossover_prob 0.5, debug chains up to depth 10. Each step picks an operator, then parents by utility U = 1.0*score + 0.4*delta_vs_parent + 0.25*novelty (novelty = 1/sqrt(1+count of same auto-detected method family, e.g. lightgbm/transformers). The model emits a full program; the sandbox runs it and scores submission.csv against a private answer. Each node gets an 'experience card' (operator, parents, score, delta, method family, error signature, token cost); cards aggregate into a 'strategy board' (family stats, repeated errors, underexplored families) which is injected into Improve (3 ancestors + 3 siblings), Crossover (2+2) and Debug (8 cards) prompts. Acceptance: a child joins the island only if fitness >= island mean; worst pruned above max size; the model's self-reported validation score is NOT trusted for selection (trust_model_validation_score=false). OUTER LOOP (OpenMLE-ERL): (1) SFT on 26,259 execution-verified traces, mostly GLM-4.7 teacher rollouts (parallel top-4 + evolutionary segments gated by 'Draft positive / Improve beats parent / Crossover beats stronger parent / endpoint reaches a medal'); (2) GSPO RL with 16 prompts x 16 samples, operators sampled 0.50/0.17/0.17/0.16 from a SQLite Program Database (top-10 per task, exploit/explore/cooling coefficients), reward = clip((s-s_min)/(s_max-s_min),0,1) from leaderboard bounds, plus GPT-judge hack_check, validation/test-gap penalty, and entropic-advantage post-processing. The trained model then drives the inner loop. Only ONE generation was run; MA1 did not retrain itself.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Fitness inside search = sandbox execution score on an agent-constructed validation split (fixed split instructions supplied per task); self-reported scores are diagnostics only. RL reward = leaderboard-normalized sandbox score with a GPT-based hack_check judge that rejects cheating/guessing code (categories valid/hack/hack_verify), a validation-vs-test gap penalty, and entropic advantage normalization per rollout group. Anti-leakage: SFT/RL task descriptions SHA256-deduplicated against all evaluation benchmarks. Outer benchmark: MLE-Bench Lite (22 tasks x 3 seeds, 12h on one RTX 4090 capped at 12GB VRAM; Valid Rate, Medal Average, Human Rank) plus held-out NatureBench Lite (10 tasks, hidden evaluator, 4h budget, Match/Surpass-SOTA). Drift is prevented by external, private-answer scoring only; there is no human-in-the-loop and no LLM judge for quality beyond hack detection.
deep_reads.key_results: MLE-Bench Lite Medal Average with OpenMLE-Evo fixed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 39.39% -> Frontis-MA1-35B 60.61% (+21.22pp); 30B: 34.85% -> 53.03%. With OpenMLE-Evo-Max (MLE-Bench-disjoint experience priors + async multi-GPU search): 71.21% (35B), 66.67% (30B); claimed to exceed GPT-5.5+Codex and approach GPT-5.6 Sol / Kimi K3. Harness effect for fixed models: GLM-5.2 59.09% (Claude Code) -> 62.12% (Evo) -> 66.67% (Evo-Max); MiniMax M3 54.55% (Codex) -> 65.15% (Evo-Max). Search efficiency vs original AIRA-Evo on 66 matched runs: -41.7% model tokens, -50.3% prompt tokens, +84.3% new-best updates per 1M tokens, Improve success 4.73% -> 9.36%. NatureBench Lite transfer: model swap 50% -> 70% Match-SOTA; framework swap 20% -> 50%. Case studies: 85-92% of validation gain came from later Improve/Crossover steps. Training: 8 H200, SFT 3 epochs bs128 lr3e-5 32k ctx; RL 221 policy updates, rollout reward 0.18 -> 0.40.
deep_reads.limitations: Not actually recursive: one generation only; SFT data is distilled from GLM-4.7 (a stronger external teacher) and Qwen, and the trained model never regenerates its own training data or retrains itself. The improver never modifies its own harness, operators, reward, or training pipeline (only task programs evolve). OpenMLE-Evo-Max 'experience priors' are not described or released, yet they account for +10.6pp of the headline. MLE-Bench Lite (22 easiest tasks) and a 10-task NatureBench subset only; 3 seeds. RL validated only as a 2-step smoke on 8xH200 (from a step-669 checkpoint), not a paper reproduction; multi-node profiles unvalidated. Requires a self-hosted distributed sandbox service (Postgres/Redis/NFS/worker containers), external task packages (4,343 of 5,758 tasks are rebuild recipes only), and pinned SLIME image. CC BY-NC 4.0 (no commercial use). EEMA code not yet released. Fitness relies on an agent-built validation split (overfitting/leakage risk mitigated only by instructions and a gap penalty). Single-island default (migration_prob=0) reduces the population diversity story.
deep_reads.key_insight: Align the training action space with the search action space: train the exact same four atomic program-evolution operators (Draft/Improve/Debug/Crossover) with execution-grounded rewards, so post-training directly improves the per-step productivity of a long-horizon evolutionary search rather than one-shot generation, and attribute gains with controlled model-swap vs harness-swap comparisons.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Isolated sandbox worker containers with private answers never exposed to the agent; GPT-judge hack_check that rejects guessing/cheating code in RL; validation/test-gap penalty; self-reported scores excluded from parent selection; benchmark deduplication of training tasks; public configs scanned for credentials; local-execution security boundary documented. No self-modification of harness, so no rollback machinery needed.
open_gaps: No closed loop: the post-trained model's own search trajectories are never selected back into SFT/RL to retrain the next generation (paper shows one generation, seeded by GLM-4.7 teacher data)
The improver only mutates task programs; it cannot mutate its own operators, prompts, parent-selection utility weights, or search hyperparameters, and there is no meta-level fitness for such changes
Experience is per-task and per-run: experience cards/strategy boards are discarded between tasks, and the cross-task 'experience priors' of Evo-Max are undocumented and unreleased
Fitness is a single scalar sandbox score on an agent-chosen validation split; no held-out early-stopping or multi-objective (cost, runtime) selection beyond token accounting
Requires a self-hosted distributed sandbox service plus 8xH200 for training; no lightweight path for application developers to run the improvement loop on API models
Reward hacking defense is a GPT judge and a gap penalty, with no verifiable check that generated validation splits are leakage-free
Only 22 MLE-Bench Lite + 10 NatureBench tasks; no evidence of transfer to non-tabular/ML-engineering domains or to agentic multi-file codebases
CC BY-NC license and EEMA code not released block reuse and extension of the meta-evolution component
Single-island default with migration disabled; no archive-level diversity maintenance (e.g., MAP-Elites) despite novelty term in parent selection
No automatic task/curriculum generation: OpenMLE-Gym tasks are statically curated, not evolved with the agent
