deep_reads.name: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Meta Superintelligence Labs + UIUC (Zhenrui Yue, Kartikeya Upasani, Xianjun Yang, Suyu Ge, Shaoliang Nie, Yuning Mao, Zhe Liu, Dong Wang)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-03-23 (last push: "fix rollout inconsistency"; last issue activity 2026-06-05)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2601.07055 (Jan 2026); citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); ~3.5k alphaxiv views; 65 forks
deep_reads.mechanism: Two agents initialized from the same base LLM (Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct) co-evolve over 3 manual iterations, each = proposer RL -> data synthesis -> solver RL -> checkpoint convert. Seed prompts (process_train.py) are random 256-token Wikipedia passages plus a sampled hop count n in {1,2,3,4} (ratio 4:3:2:1); the Search-R1 dataset is downloaded only for row count, questions are discarded. Proposer: multi-turn tool-using rollout that must issue exactly n-1 searches and emit <question>/<answer>. Reward (reward_function.py) = 0.5*format + difficulty. Format = mean of [1, fraction of turns starting with <think>, tool-call-count match to n, answer grounded as substring of doc+retrieved text and <=5 words], zeroed if question/answer empty or answer leaks into question. Difficulty: question is posed 5x to the CURRENT solver (served via sglang; base model in iter1, previous solver later); k = EM-correct count; score = (5-k)/4 if 0<k<5 else 0 (peaks at k=1, zero for trivial or unsolvable). HRPO = GRPO with rollout.n=1 per prompt and the advantage baseline (mean/std) computed over all batch samples sharing the same hop-count tag ("search_zero_n"), replacing per-prompt groups and cutting nested sampling from m*n to n. Data synthesis (main_generation.py): 5 proposer samples per seed prompt over 1/5 of seeds (~34k), keep argmax format score, proposer's own answer becomes ground truth (no solver filter, no dedup, no correctness verifier). Solver: standard GRPO (n=5), Search-R1-style EM reward, 50 steps, batch 256, lr 1e-6, no KL; iter k+1 solver resumes from iter k solver weights, proposer resumes from previous proposer. External benchmark validation every 25 steps is monitoring only.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Proposer fitness = format score (regex/substring checks) + difficulty score derived from 5 rollouts of the evolving solver, EM-checked against the proposer's own answer; solver fitness = EM against proposer-labeled answers via GRPO. Drift controls are weak: difficulty is zero for unsolvable (k=0) and trivial (k=5) questions, hop-ratio prior (40/30/20/10%) forces structural diversity, answer must be grounded in document/retrieved text and short, grad clip 0.1 (7B additionally needed KL 0.001). No held-out acceptance gate, no rollback between iterations; benchmarks (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle; 1200-sample subset during training) are logged for monitoring only, not used for selection. Labels are self-generated and never verified, so reward hacking via ambiguous/wrong-label questions is possible; authors themselves list reward hacking and bias amplification as unaddressed.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (3B): Dr. Zero beats supervised Search-R1 by up to 22.9% on NQ (0.397 vs 0.323 EM) and up to 14.1% on select benchmarks; multi-hop reaches ~90% of supervised; 7B approaches or surpasses supervised baselines on multi-hop. HRPO matches GRPO (0.326 vs 0.320 avg EM, 3B) at ~25-40% of GPU hours. Iteration 2 adds +4.93% (3B) / +1.64% (7B); marginal gains after 3 iterations; solver saturates in ~50 steps. Compute: 8xA100/H100, 2-3 days for 3 iterations. Independent reproduction (issues #5/#7, unresolved): 3B iter1 avg EM 32.0 but iter2 dropped to 28.4 (multi-hop degraded), 7B collapsed before step 50 even with authors' Appendix hyperparameters; authors could not release weights/data and first author lost access to the Meta cluster.
deep_reads.limitations: Closed-world setting: single Wikipedia corpus + e5 retriever shared with all eval benchmarks, so 'zero data' still means in-distribution corpus. Proposer's answers are unverified ground truth. Plateaus after 2-3 iterations; 7B training unstable (token-inconsistency collapse; a fix landed 2026-03 but reproduction remains open). Expensive difficulty signal (5 solver rollouts per proposed question). EM-only evaluation. Iterations are chained by hand-edited shell scripts with no orchestration. Non-commercial license, no checkpoints, no requirements.txt; external users could not reproduce reported numbers.
deep_reads.key_insight: Score proposed tasks by the current solver's pass rate and reward exactly the 'hard but solvable' band (k=1 of 5), and you get an automatic curriculum at the solver's frontier without any labeled data; and GRPO's baseline does not need multiple samples of the same prompt: grouping single samples by a structural attribute (hop count) gives a usable baseline at a fraction of the sampling cost.
deep_reads.safety_measures: None beyond training hygiene: format reward rejects answer-leaking or ungrounded questions, difficulty reward zeroes unsolvable questions, grad clip 0.1 and optional KL 0.001 for 7B; no verification of self-generated labels, no rollback or acceptance gate between iterations, no robustness testing to adversarial/poisoned documents (authors acknowledge); non-commercial license, weights withheld.
open_gaps: No correctness verifier for proposer-generated answers: the proposer's own <answer> becomes solver ground truth with no evidence-grounded check, so label noise compounds across iterations
No regression guard between iterations: iter k+1 blindly resumes from iter k weights; an independent run saw 3B avg EM fall from 32.0 (iter1) to 28.4 (iter2) with no mechanism to detect or roll back
Fitness is EM on 7 Wikipedia QA benchmarks only; no held-out generalization test to other corpora, live web search, other tools, or non-QA tasks
Difficulty estimation costs 5 full multi-turn solver rollouts per proposed question; no learned difficulty predictor or cached estimates
No dedup or coverage tracking of synthesized questions; diversity is enforced only by a hard-coded 4:3:2:1 hop-ratio prior and random seed documents
Curriculum structure itself is static (hop ratio, 50 steps, 3 iterations chosen by hand); nothing adapts the curriculum schedule based on solver progress
Requires 8xA100/H100 full-parameter RL for 2-3 days and hand-edited shell scripts per iteration; unusable by app developers and not orchestrated end-to-end
Training instability at 7B (collapse before step 50, token-ID inconsistency in multi-turn rollouts) remains unresolved and unreproduced externally; no checkpoints or requirements.txt released
Only model weights evolve; the search tool, retriever, prompts, and reward function are fixed and cannot be self-modified
No defense against proposer reward hacking (e.g., ambiguous questions that hit k=1 by chance) or bias amplification, which the authors explicitly list as future work

deep_reads.name: AutoResearchClaw
deep_reads.org_or_authors: AIMING Lab, UNC Chapel Hill (Huaxiu Yao's group; Jiaqi Liu, Shi Qiu et al., 35 authors); 49 GitHub contributors
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-19 (last push; v0.5.0 released 2026-05-20; PR-integration merges Aug 2026)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.20025 (May 2026), no venue listed; 1669 forks; ARC-Bench dataset on HuggingFace
deep_reads.mechanism: Two loops, neither touches weights or code. INNER (intra-run): a fixed 23-stage linear pipeline (topic -> literature -> hypothesis -> code -> sandbox -> analysis -> paper). Stage 12/13 run generated code in a sandbox; failures trigger targeted LLM repair, then up to 10 "iterative refine" rounds that keep the best version by a single scalar metric_key/direction (`_is_better`). Stage 15 has an LLM choose PROCEED / REFINE (back to 13) / PIVOT (back to 8) with artifact versioning. Optional multi-model debate (stages 8/14/18) and best-of-N tournament (8/9) add breadth. OUTER ("evolution"): only at pipeline END, `extract_lessons()` applies keyword rules to StageResults (failed/blocked stages, PIVOT/REFINE rationale, stderr warnings, NaN/Inf metrics) producing LessonEntry(stage, category, severity string, truncated error text) appended to `run_dir/evolution/lessons.jsonl`. `build_overlay()` ranks lessons by exp(-age*ln2/30d) x2 for stage match x1.5 for errors (90-day cutoff), takes top-5, and appends them as "## Lessons from Prior Runs" text to each stage's user prompt. Because the store lives in the per-run directory, this only recurs on --resume of the same run. True cross-run transfer requires the opt-in MetaClaw bridge (default off): `convert_lessons_to_skills()` asks an LLM once to write up to 3 `arc-*` SKILL.md files into ~/.metaclaw/skills/; later runs inject the first 5 alphabetically-sorted arc-* skills plus keyword-matched registry skills. Skill-effectiveness records are written per run but `compute_skill_stats` is never called; the A-Evolve module (LLM diagnosis + mutation gate + prompt patches) and ALHF InterventionLearner exist but are imported only by tests.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Inner loop signals: sandbox execution success, AST hard-validation (blocks identical ablations/hardcoded metrics), NaN/Inf fast-fail, improvement on one configured scalar metric, VerifiedRegistry that scrubs numbers not present in measurement records, 4-layer citation verification, LLM peer review (7-dim), and an optional PRM gate (3-vote LLM-as-judge returning +1/0/-1 at stages 5/9/15/20; -1 marks the stage FAILED and retries). Outer loop has NO fitness signal: lessons are accepted unconditionally, skills are accepted from a single LLM call with only a "do not duplicate these names" hint, and 30-day time decay is the sole forgetting mechanism; no held-out check that a lesson/skill helps, no rollback. Drift/reward-hacking guard is limited to the anti-fabrication verifier on numbers; the paper itself documents a silent semantic collapse (T10: all conditions output identical zeros that pass the numeric gate). Evidence for the evolution component is a 10-topic best-of-3 LLM-judged ablation (-0.48 quality, -1 completion without it) and a MetaClaw A/B with unspecified n using an author-defined composite score.
deep_reads.limitations: Cross-run learning is off by default and depends on the MetaClaw bridge; the base lesson store is per-run. Lesson extraction is regex/keyword classification of error strings, not root-cause diagnosis; the paper's "severity score s(l) in (0,1] with recommended mitigation" does not exist in code (severity is info/warning/error). Skill injection is capped at 5 alphabetically-first arc-* files, so accumulated skills starve newer ones; no pruning, scoring, or rollback of learned skills. Evaluation is entirely LLM-judged (GPT-5.3-codex is both backbone and judge), on CPU-only <10-min ML tasks; full-auto paper acceptance is 3/10 and mean quality 4.03/10 in the end-to-end test; HEP score 0.489; no human expert review of scientific merit; no cost-per-paper disclosure. Community issue #326 calls it a toy that fails on anything slightly complex. Pipeline topology, stage prompts, and agent code never change.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat every pipeline failure as a first-class artifact: extract it into a time-decayed natural-language lesson and re-inject it as a prompt overlay (or LLM-authored SKILL.md) so any LLM backbone avoids it next run without retraining - but the ablation shows this cross-run memory buys far less (-0.48 quality) than robust inner loops (debate -1.37, self-healing -40% completion), so long-horizon agents should invest in in-run repair/verification before cross-run evolution.
deep_reads.key_results: ARC-Bench experiment-stage (25 ML topics, LLM judge): AutoResearchClaw CoPilot 0.648, Full-Auto 0.596, AIDE-ML 0.511, AI Scientist v2 0.419 (+54.7% overall, +100.4% on result analysis). Domain tasks: biology 0.912, statistics 0.898, HEP 0.489 (baselines score 0 there). End-to-end HITL (10 topics): CoPilot quality 7.27 / 87.5% accept with 6 interventions vs Full-Auto 4.03 / 25% and Step-by-Step 5.19 / 50% with 23 interventions. Component ablation (10 topics, best-of-3): full 5.62 quality, 10/10 completion, 3/10 accept; w/o debate 4.25 (p=0.003); w/o self-healing 6/10 completion; w/o evolution 5.14, 9/10 completion. MetaClaw A/B (README, n unspecified): stage retry 10.5%->7.9%, refine cycles 2.0->1.2, composite robustness +18.3%. 8 showcase papers across 8 domains. 2699 tests claimed.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Docker/venv sandbox with allowed_imports, memory limits and network_policy (none/setup_only/pip_only/full); AST validation of generated code; immutable harness; NaN/Inf fast-fail; VerifiedRegistry anti-fabrication (unverified numbers sanitized); 4-layer citation verification removing hallucinated refs; 3 HITL gates (stages 5/9/20) with rollback and 7 intervention modes; cost budget guardrails with auto-pause; SHA256 artifact manifests and versioned undo. For self-modification specifically: none - learned lessons/skills are plain text written to ~/.metaclaw/skills without review, gating, or rollback, though they cannot execute code.
open_gaps: Lesson store is scoped to run_dir/evolution; no global store aggregating lessons across artifacts/rc-* runs, so out-of-the-box runs are stateless and cross-run learning requires enabling the MetaClaw bridge

No fitness/acceptance signal on evolved artifacts: lessons accepted unconditionally, skills accepted from one LLM call; skill_effectiveness.jsonl is written but compute_skill_stats() is never called, so harmful skills are never pruned or rolled back
Learned-skill injection takes the first 5 alphabetically sorted arc-* directories; once >5 skills exist newer ones are silently never used, and the library grows unboundedly with name-only dedup

Lesson extraction is keyword scoring over truncated error strings; no root-cause diagnosis, no mitigation field, no dedup of repeated identical lessons (the A-Evolve LLM-diagnosis + mutation-gate module exists but is unwired)
Only prompt-overlay text evolves; the 23-stage topology, stage prompts (prompt_patches.md is written but never read), tool set, and agent code are fixed
Human feedback is not learned from: hitl/learning.py InterventionLearner (ALHF) is never instantiated outside tests, so rejection/edit patterns never change future pause policies
Evolution benefit is not tested for transfer: ablation on 10 same-distribution ML topics with unspecified warm-start; no held-out topic/domain evaluation of whether a lesson from run N helps run N+1
Fitness is entirely LLM-as-judge with the same model family as the backbone; no human expert scoring of scientific validity, and full-auto acceptance is only 3/10
Inner refine loop optimizes a single scalar metric_key, enabling Goodhart failures (paper's T10 silent semantic collapse passes verification)
No token/cost accounting per paper and ~46K tokens of static prompt overhead; not usable for evolving arbitrary application agents outside the research-paper pipeline
sources_read: https://github.com/aiming-lab/AutoResearchClaw (README, metadata, commits, releases, issues via gh api)

deep_reads.name: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Hexo AI (Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, Alesia Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-26 (v0.6.0 on PyPI as `sia-agent`; last commits: OpenRouter provider, Windows venv fix)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint 2605.27276; featured on HuggingFace Daily Papers; citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited). 257 forks, 17 open issues.
deep_reads.mechanism: Three LLM roles in a strictly linear chain, `sia run --task X --max_gen N --focus {harness|weights}`. Gen 1: Meta-Agent (Claude Agent SDK / OpenHands / pydantic-ai) reads task.md, sample task descriptions, a reference_target_agent.py and a sample trajectory, and writes `gen_1/target_agent.py`. Each gen: orchestrator runs `python target_agent.py --dataset_dir --working_dir` in a per-run venv (optional Docker sandbox), which calls the target model and logs agent_execution.json; then runs the task's `evaluate.py --gen-dir` against `data/private/` to write results.json; then appends an LLM-written summary + metric deltas + code-size deltas to `context.md`. Feedback-Agent gets: current target_agent.py, task.md, SUCCESS/FAILED status, the full results.json dump, the first 3 trajectories truncated to 1000 chars each, and a pointer to context.md/prior improvement.md files (it can read the filesystem). It must write `gen_{n+1}/improvement.md` and `target_agent.py` (plus optional requirements.txt). Loop repeats until max_gen. In `--focus weights` mode the same loop instead mutates `train.py`: Meta-Agent is given an embedded "RL Integration Guide" and must implement tinker-cookbook Env/EnvGroupBuilder/RLDataset/RLDatasetBuilder (GRPO, LoRA, default Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on Thinking Machines' Tinker; code execution via Modal or SandboxFusion; majority-vote pseudo-reward suggested when labels are hidden). The Feedback-Agent then rewrites reward shaping/env design per generation; a COMPLETED file early-stops. So weights are updated by an LLM-authored RL pipeline that is itself evolved. In code, harness and weights are mutually exclusive per run; the paper's "W+H" interleaving is not implemented as an in-loop policy.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = whatever the task's `evaluate.py` writes to results.json (scored against data/private/), injected verbatim into the next feedback prompt; in weights mode the GRPO reward is defined by the agent-written EnvGroupBuilder. There is NO acceptance gate: gen n+1 is always derived from gen n even if n regressed; no rollback to best, no archive/population, no statistical test. "Best generation" is only computed post-hoc in context_manager.finalize() by max self-reported `accuracy`. Drift/Goodhart prevention is documentation-only (docs/evaluator_design.md checklist; paper names "coupled co-evolutionary Goodharting" as an open risk). Community issues show the loop is exploitable: #59 (evaluator computed accuracy over answered items, so abstaining raised the score to 75% reported vs 4.5% real); #60 (feedback agent sees ~0.3% of trajectory evidence, chosen by filename not outcome; observed 62.1→57.1→46.5% decline over 3 gens); #61 (HTTP 429s indistinguishable from wrong answers); #36 (results.json dump leaks held-out gold answers for longcot-chess into the feedback prompt).
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (single runs, no seeds/variance, generation counts unstated): LawBench charge classification (191 classes) prior SOTA 45.0% → SIA-H 50.0% → SIA-W+H 70.1% (the "56.6%" is relative gain over initial baseline). AlphaFold-3 TriMul Triton kernel on H100: 12,483µs → 1,017µs (91.9% reduction, 14.02x; 12.4% faster than prior 1,161µs). scRNA-seq denoising mse_norm: SIA-H 0.241 → SIA-W+H 0.289 (prior SOTA 0.240; "502%" over initial baseline). README claims #1 on MLE-Bench Hard (chart only, no numbers). No SIA-W-only ablation reported. LoRA checkpoints not released (issue #35 open). Repo ships 4 tasks (gpqa, lawbench, longcot-chess, spaceship-titanic — the last without a bundled evaluator), CI, golden-prompt tests, a live web dashboard.
deep_reads.limitations: Linear single-lineage loop with no selection, rollback, or archive; feedback evidence is 3 truncated trajectories picked by filename; fitness is one task's evaluator with no held-out generalization or transfer check despite the prompt saying "don't optimize for this task"; evaluator can be gamed (abstention inflates accuracy) and can leak gold answers into the feedback prompt; infra failures pollute the signal. Weights mode requires Tinker + Modal/SandboxFusion accounts (no local-GPU path), has zero test coverage, and harness/weights cannot run in the same loop. Paper results are single-run with no variance, no generation counts, no SIA-W ablation, no compute cost, no released weights. Default `--sandbox none` executes LLM-written code on the host.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the RL training pipeline (env, reward function, dataset builder) as just another source file the meta-loop can rewrite: by having the Feedback-Agent author `train.py` for a hosted fine-tuning API in the same rewrite-from-logs loop it uses for `target_agent.py`, weight updates become an artifact of harness evolution rather than a separate hand-built system — harness edits shape how the model searches/acts, weight edits build domain intuition prompts cannot instil.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Optional `--sandbox docker` (no network) for target-agent execution; default is host execution. data/private/ held-out split is a convention, not enforced (feedback agent has filesystem access). Evaluator-design checklist (anti-gaming advice) is documentation only. Network calls capped at 60s/2 retries by prompt instruction. No rollback, no diff review, no human-in-the-loop gate between generations. SECURITY.md documents the threat model.
open_gaps: No acceptance gate or rollback: gen n+1 is always built from gen n even when n regressed; add best-so-far parent selection, McNemar/paired significance test, or a population/archive (MAP-Elites style) before promoting

Fitness is a single task evaluator on one private split with no held-out or perturbed slice; no measurement of whether harness improvements transfer to other tasks (each run restarts from the reference agent)
Feedback evidence selection is positional (first 3 trajectories, 1000 chars each): no failure-driven sampling, no full failure transcripts, no clustering of error modes

Self-reported metrics are gameable (abstention raises accuracy; results.json can leak gold answers); need harness-owned coverage floors, gold-stripped eval summaries, and a fixed evaluator the agent cannot author
Infrastructure failures (429/timeouts/truncation) are conflated with reasoning failures in the score; no per-item failure taxonomy
Harness and weights are mutually exclusive per run (`--focus` XOR); no in-loop policy that decides when to spend budget on scaffold edits vs. RL, so the paper's W+H interleaving is manual
Weight updates require Tinker + Modal accounts; no local-GPU/LoRA path, no tests for weights mode, no released checkpoints, so app developers cannot reproduce W results

The evaluator, task set, and curriculum are frozen: the loop cannot generate new tasks, harden its own grader, or co-evolve verifiers against Goodharting (the paper names this risk but offers no mechanism)
No compute/cost accounting or budget-aware stopping in harness mode (fixed max_gen); no memory of failed approaches beyond an LLM-summarized context.md
Single-lineage, single-agent design: no parallel candidate generation, no crossover between runs, no reuse of improvements across tasks

deep_reads.name: SkillClaw: Let Skills Evolve Collectively with Agentic Evolver
deep_reads.org_or_authors: AMAP-ML (Alibaba Amap); Ziyu Ma, Shidong Yang, Yuxiang Ji, Xucong Wang, Yong Wang, Yiming Hu, Tongwen Huang, Xiangxiang Chu
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-17 (last push: batch of bug-fix merges). Open issue #89 (2026-09-09) asks if the project is abandoned; unanswered.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv:2604.08377 (cs.AI, cs.CL), preprint only; Hugging Face Daily Papers #2 (2026-04-10), 294 upvotes; 259 forks; citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited).
deep_reads.mechanism: Two components joined only by shared object storage (local FS / OSS / S3 / Nacos) under a group_id. (1) Client proxy: a local OpenAI/Anthropic/Responses-compatible API proxy that the agent (Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, ...) is repointed to. Per request it appends an `<available_skills>` XML catalog (name/description/location, capped ~30k chars) to the system prompt so the model lazily `read`s SKILL.md files; it records every turn (prompt, response, tool calls/results/errors), infers `read_skills`/`modified_skills` from tool calls, optionally scores each turn with a PRM (LLM judge voting +1/0/-1, majority of M samples, adapted from MetaClaw), and uploads session JSON to `{group}/sessions/`. (2) Evolve server polls (default 600s), drains queued sessions and runs a fixed 3-stage `workflow` engine: Summarize (programmatic lossless trajectory + LLM causal summary; optional LLM session judge backfills a 0-1 score weighted 0.55 completion/0.30 quality/0.05 efficiency/0.10 tool-use) -> Aggregate (sessions grouped by each skill they read/modified; no-skill bucket separate) -> Execute (one LLM call per skill group with current SKILL.md + up to 30 sessions of evidence chooses improve_skill / optimize_description / create_skill / skip under a heavily conservative editing prompt; no-skill bucket -> create_skill/skip). Same-name SHA conflicts are LLM-merged. Accepted output overwrites `{group}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, bumps a version registry (content SHA, <=20 history entries), stores a version bundle snapshot and manifest; clients poll/pull and hot-reload. Optional gates: LLM skill verifier (off by default, threshold 0.75) and `validated` publish mode where idle clients replay <=3 single-turn prompts with baseline vs candidate skill in the system prompt, PRM-score both, and accept if candidate_mean >= 0.75 and >= baseline. Alternative `agent` engine: an OpenClaw agent edits a skills/ workspace following EVOLVE_AGENTS.md (history/ ledger, self-validation instructions); every changed file is uploaded with no programmatic gate.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal is almost entirely LLM judgment, no ground truth: (a) per-turn PRM = LLM judge majority vote on helpfulness (+1/0/-1) of the response to the instruction; (b) session-level LLM judge (0-1 weighted score) that overrides PRM; (c) the evolver LLM itself decides skip vs edit from summaries + these scores. Acceptance by default is 'direct' publish with verifier OFF, so the evolver's own output is the fitness. Opt-in gates: an LLM verifier (grounded_in_evidence / preserves_existing_value / specificity / safe_to_publish, threshold 0.75) and client replay validation (3 single-turn text replays, no tool execution, candidate vs baseline PRM means, 1 approval / 1 rejection thresholds by default). Drift/reward-hacking mitigation is prompt-based: 'prefer skip', preserve API facts, distinguish skill vs agent vs environment failures, targeted edits not rewrites, LLM merge on conflicts, versioned snapshots (no automatic rollback or post-publish monitoring). The paper claims a sandbox A/B of candidate s' vs deployed s on task success and execution stability with 'monotonic capability growth', but no such benchmark harness exists in the repo (issue #49 confirms the WildClawBench numbers are not reproducible from the code).
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (numbers via alphaxiv overview; arXiv full text unreachable in this session): 8 concurrent users over 6 days on WildClawBench (6 domains) with Qwen3-Max as backbone. Search & Retrieval 22.73% -> 34.55% (+52.0% relative); Creative Synthesis 11.57% -> 21.80% (+88.4% rel); Safety & Alignment 24.00% -> 32.00% (+33.3% rel); Social Interaction +11.7% rel; a 'save report' task 28.3% -> 100.0%. Two domains and the overall average were not surfaced; no ablations, no comparison to other skill/memory-learning baselines, evolver model and initial skill seed not disclosed. Repo: 2.6k stars / 259 forks in 5 months, HF Daily Papers #2 (294 upvotes), integrations for Hermes/OpenClaw/QwenPaw/Codex/Claude Code, dashboard, Nacos lifecycle; a third-party review (issue #56) rated it 70/100 'research tool, not production'.
deep_reads.limitations: No execution-grounded fitness in the shipped loop (all judges are LLMs; replay validation is single-turn text without tools); verifier and validated-publish are off by default, so evolved skills go straight to the group store; no rollback command or post-publish regression detection despite version snapshots; same LLM family generates and judges; one converging skill per name for a whole group (heterogeneous environments get LLM-merged, no per-user forks); attribution is 'skill was read', not counterfactual benefit; evidence capped at 30 sessions/group and 8 for the verifier; session boundaries rely on proxy heuristics unless the agent sends headers; group-wide poisoning surface (any member's sessions steer shared skills; two path-traversal bugs #68/#69 already found); proxy rewrites agent config files on startup (#71); Windows has no installer; paper eval is 8 users x 6 days on one self-built benchmark with low absolute scores and is not reproducible from the repo (#49); maintenance appears stalled since 2026-08-17 (#89).
deep_reads.key_insight: Put the learning loop in a protocol-level proxy between the agent and the model so every real session from every user/agent/device is captured with zero user effort, group trajectories by the skill they actually touched to form natural cross-user control experiments, and let a deliberately conservative 'skill engineer' LLM choose improve / optimize-description / create / skip per group, syncing the result back to everyone through a shared versioned SKILL.md store.
open_gaps: No execution-grounded acceptance: build a sandboxed re-execution harness that replays tool-using sessions with candidate vs deployed skill and measures task success, instead of single-turn text replay scored by an LLM PRM

Regression gate is opt-in and LLM-only; default publish is direct with verifier off — need mandatory pre-publish gating plus post-publish monitoring of per-skill session scores with automatic rollback to the archived version bundle
Attribution is 'skill was read', not 'skill helped': add counterfactual A/B (withhold/inject skill on matched tasks) to estimate each skill's causal value before editing it
Single converging skill per name for the whole group: no per-user/per-environment forks, overrides, or conditional sections; heterogeneous ports/APIs/OS facts get LLM-merged into one document
Generator and judge are the same LLM family with no held-out task set — no defense against the evolver and verifier agreeing on plausible-but-wrong edits
Library-level consolidation missing: near-duplicate or stale skills are only avoided by showing the evolver a list of names; no embedding-based dedup, pruning, or usage-decay of unread skills
Flat catalog injection capped at 30k chars with no retrieval/ranking — will not scale as the shared library grows
Trust/provenance: any group member's sessions (including prompt-injected tool outputs) can steer shared skills; no per-contributor weighting, quarantine, or diff review before group-wide propagation
Evidence budget and cost are unmanaged: 30 sessions/group/cycle, 8 for the verifier, 100k-token summaries, no token accounting or cost-aware scheduling
Evaluation is not reproducible from the repo (no benchmark scripts, seeds, task split, or raw outputs) and lacks ablations (no-validation, single-user vs multi-user, evolver model choice)
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prompt-level conservatism (prefer skip, targeted edits, preserve endpoints/ports/payload facts, do not add generic advice, distinguish skill vs agent vs environment failures); opt-in LLM verifier gate (threshold 0.75) and opt-in 'validated' publish mode with client replay votes (required results/approvals/min mean score/max rejections thresholds); Nacos 'review'/'draft' publish modes for human review; version registry with content SHA, capped history and per-version bundle snapshots (manual restore only); LLM merge on same-name conflicts; agent engine confined to a workspace, instructed to self-validate and keep a history/ evidence ledger; path-safety rejection of unsafe bundle paths (#81); `doctor`/`restore` commands to undo agent-config rewrites; daily quota and idle-only execution for client validation. No human-in-the-loop by default and no automatic rollback.

deep_reads.name: pi-autoresearch
deep_reads.org_or_authors: davebcn87 (primary, 99 commits); tobi (Tobi Lütke, 51 commits); ~20 community contributors. Extension for badlogic's pi coding agent (pi-mono, 104k stars). Inspired by karpathy/autoresearch (95k stars).
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: Not a paper. 8,036 GitHub stars, 455 forks, 12 npm releases (latest 1.8.1), ~5.1k npm downloads/month (Aug 11-Sep 9 2026). Created 5 days after karpathy/autoresearch as its generalization to arbitrary metrics inside a coding-agent harness.
deep_reads.mechanism: Single pi agent, single git branch, greedy hill-climb over the TARGET CODEBASE (the "other" that evolves). Setup: the `autoresearch-create` skill makes the agent write `.auto/prompt.md` (objective, primary metric + direction, secondary monitors, files in scope, off-limits, "What's Been Tried") and `.auto/measure.sh` (emits `METRIC name=value` lines), creates a branch, calls `init_experiment`, runs and logs a baseline. Loop per iteration: agent edits code -> `run_experiment` runs measure.sh with timeout, parses METRIC lines, then runs optional `.auto/checks.sh` (tests/types/lint) -> `log_experiment(status=keep|discard|crash|checks_failed, metric, description, asi{hypothesis, rollback_reason, next_action_hint, revisits_run})`. On `keep`: `git add -A && git commit` with a JSON Result trailer. On anything else: `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd` excluding `.auto/`. Every run appends a line to `.auto/log.jsonl`. `before.sh`/`after.sh` hooks (bash, JSON on stdin, stdout delivered as a steer message, 30s/8KB caps) fire around each iteration. The tool result also appends a nudge to reconsider discards whose rollback assumption may now be invalid. Continuation is harness-driven: on `agent_end`, if an experiment ran this turn, after an 800ms settle window it sends "Run the next iteration now"; capped at 200 auto-resume turns, stopped after >20 consecutive discards/crashes or `maxIterations`. On context compaction, the LLM summary is replaced with a deterministic summary rebuilt from log.jsonl (last 50 runs + ASI), prompt.md and ideas.md, so memory = files. Context-memory (prompt.md, ideas.md, ASI) is agent-maintained. measure.sh is agent-editable mid-loop and persists across reverts. `autoresearch-finalize` regroups kept commits into independent review branches.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Fitness = one user-defined scalar parsed from `.auto/measure.sh` output (lower or higher is better), plus secondary metrics that are monitors only. The KEEP decision is made by the agent, not the tool: `log_experiment` trusts `params.status` and never checks that the metric actually beat the current best; the only hard gates are (a) `keep` is refused when `.auto/checks.sh` failed on that run and (b) the secondary-metric set must stay consistent. Anti-drift is soft: a MAD-based confidence score (|best_kept - baseline| / MAD of all runs in segment) shown after 3+ runs but explicitly advisory ("never auto-discards"); the string "Be careful not to overfit to the benchmarks and do not cheat on the benchmarks" in resume prompts; optional hooks (anti-thrash after 5 discards). No hidden holdout: the agent can read and edit measure.sh, and issue #81 requesting holdout evaluators was closed without implementation. No human in the loop during the run; a human reviews at finalize time.
deep_reads.key_results: No quantitative results are published in the repo; the README's screenshots and the website's 48s-build scenario are explicitly documented as illustrative in site/ASSETS.md. Demonstrated: runs end-to-end (65 passing tests, CI, npm provenance releases), real user sessions reported in issues (e.g. #64 reached a saturated feature_score=1 in a UI task), 5k+ monthly installs. Claimed domains: test runtime, bundle size, LLM training loss, build time, Lighthouse. Maintainer's own stance on adding a swarm mode (#77): "how would you prove the result is better than the simple version?" - no comparative evaluation exists for the simple version either.
deep_reads.limitations: Single agent, single lineage, greedy: no population, archive, or branching from non-best kept states (swarm PRD #77 closed not_planned). Keep/discard unenforced by the harness, so a misjudging agent can commit regressions. Evaluator is fully visible and mutable by the optimizer and survives reverts. Noise handled only advisorily; no repeats/A-B replay (#69 open). Saturated/binary objectives trap the loop into discard-only (#64 open). Single scalar objective, no Pareto handling. Tightly coupled to pi's extension API (activation, compaction hooks, setActiveTools); not a standalone SDK. Learnings do not transfer across projects or sessions beyond the per-project .auto/ folder. The agent itself (prompts, tools, strategy) does not evolve; only the target code and the agent's notes do. No published evidence of improvement over an unassisted agent.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Experiment tools hidden from the model outside /autoresearch mode (v1.5.0) so the agent cannot self-start a loop; auto-resume ceiling 200 turns and stop after >20 consecutive discards/crashes; optional maxIterations; git revert on every non-keep with .auto/ preserved; checks.sh backpressure blocks keep on failing tests; hook scripts have 30s timeout and 8KB stdout cap; shell-injection fix in commit messages (PR #13); "don't cheat on benchmarks" guardrail text; README warns extension runs with full user permissions and recommends a dedicated branch/worktree and sandbox; npm releases carry provenance attestations. No sandboxing of the target project's commands, no evaluator integrity check, no cost/token cap beyond iteration count.
deep_reads.key_insight: Split the loop into domain-agnostic harness infrastructure (run/measure/commit-or-revert/auto-resume/deterministic compaction) and a per-domain playbook the agent writes itself, and make the on-disk log + playbook the sole source of truth so the optimization loop survives context resets, restarts, and reverts - the agent's memory is files, not its context window.
open_gaps: Harness does not enforce the acceptance rule: log_experiment commits whenever the agent says 'keep' without comparing metric to current best; a framework should gate commits on metric improvement plus a noise-aware threshold.

Evaluator (measure.sh) is readable and editable by the optimizing agent and is preserved across reverts; no hidden holdout benchmark, no hash/integrity check on the evaluator, no train/holdout split (issue #81 closed unimplemented).

Single-lineage greedy hill climb: no archive/population of kept states, no parent selection, no branching from a non-best commit; swarm/orchestrator mode (#77) was declined for lack of proof it helps.
Noise handling is advisory only: no automatic repeated measurement, no A/B replay of marginal candidates, no statistical acceptance test (#69 open).
No completion semantics for bounded/binary objectives; loop keeps demanding iterations after the metric saturates (#64 open).
Single scalar objective; secondary metrics are monitors only, no multi-objective or Pareto-front acceptance.
No cross-session or cross-project transfer of learnings: ASI/prompt.md/ideas.md are per-project; nothing distills logs into reusable skills, prompts, or heuristics.
Only the target code evolves; the agent's own prompts, tools, and search strategy are static and hand-authored.
Tightly coupled to pi's extension API; not usable as a standalone optimization SDK from other harnesses (requested in #77 comments).
No published quantitative evidence (case studies, ablations) that the loop beats an unassisted agent or that features like confidence scoring and revisit-discards change outcomes.

deep_reads.name: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Jinyuan Fang, Yanwen Peng, Xi Zhang, Yingxu Wang, Xinhao Yi, Guibin Zhang, Yi Xu, Bin Wu, Siwei Liu, Zihao Li, Zhaochun Ren, Nikos Aletras, Xi Wang, Han Zhou, Zaiqiao Meng (University of Glasgow-led; EvoAgentX team; co-authors from Sheffield, Leiden, Cambridge, etc.)
deep_reads.last_activity: Companion awesome-list last push 2026-05-16 (still merging PRs adding 2026 papers, e.g. CORAL, ReasoningBank); EvoAgentX framework repo last push 2026-08-27
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (no peer-reviewed venue as of 2026-09). Citation count could not be verified (Semantic Scholar rate-limited; OpenAlex shows only 5, a known undercount for arXiv). Proxy impact: companion repo EvoAgentX/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents 2,477 stars / 190 forks; sibling framework EvoAgentX 3,317 stars (EMNLP'25 Demo paper).
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a survey, so the 'mechanism' is an abstraction, not a runnable loop. The paper's Figure 1 (verified from the repo asset) defines a 4-node cycle: (1) System Inputs I — task-level {T, D_train, D_test} or instance-level {x, y, C (context)}; (2) Agent System A — single-agent (prompt, tools, memory) or multi-agent (agents, communication, topology); (3) Environment — scenarios (coding, legal, research, medicine) that return Proxy Metrics: accuracy/F1/success rate or LLM-based evaluators; (4) Optimiser P = Search Space S (prompt template, tool selection, LLM parameters, architecture) x Optimisation Algorithm H (rule-based heuristics, gradient descent/text-gradients, Bayesian/MCTS/RL, learned policy). Edges: I -Setup-> A -Execution-> Env -Feedback-> P -Mutation-> A, plus a dashed P -Refine-> I edge (optimiser can alter the inputs/data). The taxonomy then classifies methods by which S they mutate: LLM behaviour (SFT/RL vs test-time feedback/search), prompts (edit/evolutionary/generative/text-gradient), memory, tools (training, inference-time selection, tool creation), and multi-agent (prompt-level, topology/workflow search e.g. AFlow/ADAS/GPTSwarm, unified, backbone fine-tuning). It frames a historical progression MOP -> MOA -> MAO -> MASE (Multi-Agent Self-Evolving) and proposes 'Three Laws': Endure (safety/stability during modification), Excel (preserve or improve performance), Evolve (autonomously optimise subject to the first two). The only concrete instantiation is the authors' EvoAgentX, which wraps TextGrad, MIPRO, AFlow and EvoPrompt as optimisers over a workflow graph: Original -> best optimiser: HotPotQA F1 63.6->71.0 (TextGrad), MBPP 69->79 (AFlow), MATH 66->76 (TextGrad), using 50 validation / 100 test samples.
deep_reads.eval_loop: In the abstraction, the Environment emits proxy metrics (accuracy, F1, success rate) computed on D_train/D_test at task level, or on a single (x, y) at instance level; where no ground truth exists, LLM-as-a-Judge / Agent-as-a-Judge provide the score. The survey's Evaluation section is a catalogue of static benchmarks (ToolBench, WebArena, SWE-bench, GAIA, OSWorld, AgentBench, MLGym) plus judge paradigms plus safety benchmarks (AgentHarm, RedCode, MACHIAVELLI, R-Judge, AGrail). Drift / reward-hacking prevention is addressed only normatively via the 'Endure' and 'Excel' laws and a call for 'evolution-aware audits' and continuous monitoring; the paper itself flags 'reward modeling scarcity destabilizes behavior' as an open problem. No held-out generalisation protocol, regression test, or rollback mechanism is specified. In EvoAgentX the signal is a fixed benchmark split (50 val / 100 test) with best-on-validation selection.
deep_reads.limitations: Survey-only: no experiments, no formal guarantees; the 4-node framework is descriptive and the 'Refine' (optimiser->inputs) and 'Mutation' edges are never formalised as operators. The Three Laws are Asimov-style aspirations with no enforcement mechanism (no versioning, rollback, canary evaluation, sandboxing, or human approval gates discussed). Evaluation section lists benchmarks for agents, not metrics for evolution itself (learning curves across rounds, forgetting, transfer). Taxonomy is prompt/topology-heavy and 2025-arXiv-heavy; agent-source-code self-modification (Darwin Godel Machine), Voyager-style skill libraries, and quality-diversity archives are thin or absent. 'Lifelong' in the title is not matched by coverage of continual deployment loops; the only instantiation (EvoAgentX) is offline, one-shot optimisation on tiny splits. Competes with and largely overlaps the earlier Gao et al. survey (arXiv 2507.21046, July 2025) which it cites but does not compare against. Full HTML/PDF could not be fetched directly (arXiv connection resets); details verified via abstract page, repo figure/README, and third-party summaries.
deep_reads.key_insight: Every self-evolving agent system reduces to one cycle — Inputs -> Agent System -> Environment (proxy metric) -> Optimiser -> mutate Agent System — where 'what evolves' is just the chosen Search Space S (prompt / tools / memory / weights / topology) and 'how' is the algorithm H (heuristic / text-gradient / MCTS / RL); a harness should therefore make S and H pluggable and keep the evaluator separate from both.
open_gaps: No formalisation of the Optimiser->Inputs 'Refine' edge: task/curriculum self-generation is drawn in the figure but never taxonomised or given an operator; a framework could make curriculum evolution a first-class, evaluated component

Evaluation of evolution itself is absent: no metrics for per-round improvement, regression rate, catastrophic forgetting, or held-out cross-task transfer of evolved prompts/workflows (fitness = single benchmark split)
'Endure' and 'Excel' laws have no enforcement mechanism: no versioned artifact store, rollback, canary/shadow evaluation, sandboxing of self-modifications, or human approval gate is described
Evaluator is treated as a fixed environment output; no coverage of evaluator co-evolution, judge robustness, or defenses against the agent gaming an LLM-as-judge signal
Single-loop abstraction ignores multiple loops at different timescales (instance-level test-time refinement vs task-level offline optimisation vs weight updates) and how they interact or conflict

Agent-source-code / harness self-modification (DGM-style), skill-library accumulation (Voyager-style), and quality-diversity archives/populations are missing or thin; search is framed as best-so-far only
No treatment of optimisation budget: token/compute cost per evolution round, stopping criteria, or cost-aware acceptance
Companion EvoAgentX instantiation is offline, one-shot (50 val / 100 test) with no continual/lifelong deployment loop despite 'lifelong' framing
No multi-tenant / production concerns: how evolved artifacts are promoted, A/B tested, or shared across users and tasks
deep_reads.safety_measures: Discussed normatively only: Three Laws (Endure = maintain safety/stability during modification; Excel = preserve performance; Evolve = autonomous optimisation subordinate to the first two); calls for continuous monitoring across the evolutionary lifecycle, 'evolution-aware audits and adaptive regulatory mechanisms', and notes that dynamic evolution undermines static legal/safety frameworks. Cites safety benchmarks (AgentHarm, RedCode, MobileSafetyBench, MACHIAVELLI, R-Judge, SafeLawBench) and lifelong guardrails/attacks (AGrail, AutoDAN-Turbo). No concrete technical mechanism (rollback, sandbox, constraint enforcement) is specified.
deep_reads.key_results: No experimental results (survey). Headline artifacts: unified 4-component feedback-loop framework (Inputs/Agent System/Environment/Optimiser with Search Space + Algorithm); Three Laws (Endure/Excel/Evolve); MOP->MOA->MAO->MASE progression; taxonomy across single-agent (LLM behaviour, prompt, memory, tool), multi-agent (prompt, topology, unified, backbone), domain-specific (biomedicine, programming, finance/law), evaluation (benchmarks, LLM/Agent-as-judge), safety. Companion EvoAgentX numbers (its own README): Original vs best optimiser HotPotQA F1 63.58->71.02 (TextGrad), MBPP pass@1 69->79 (AFlow), MATH 66->76 (TextGrad); also prompt-optimised Open Deep Research and OWL on GAIA validation.

deep_reads.name: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lil'Log)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-04 (single publication; no updates observed)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Lilian Weng (independent; ex-OpenAI, Thinking Machines Lab)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: Self-published on Lil'Log; ~31-min read; 39 references. Downstream: one reading list explicitly built around it (leezythu/Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement, created 2026-07-08, 85 stars). The large 'awesome-harness-engineering' lists (4k stars) predate the essay (March 2026) and do not cite it. Scout's 'DeepSeek endorsement' claim could not be verified (search budget exhausted).
deep_reads.mechanism: The essay is a survey/position piece; it does not run a loop itself. It defines a harness as 'the system surrounding a base model that orchestrates execution and decides how the model thinks and plans, calls tools and acts, perceives and manages context, stores artifacts, and evaluates results', and argues near-term RSI will start by optimizing this layer, not weights. It organizes the field on an 'optimization ladder' of what is mutated: instruction prompts -> structured context (ACE playbook bullets; MCE bi-level skill/context) -> workflow graphs (ADAS archive + meta-agent; AFlow MCTS over LLM-node graphs) -> harness code (Meta-Harness proposer coding agent keeping a Pareto frontier; DGM self-modifying agent with performance-weighted parent selection; Self-Harness; AHE) -> optimizer code (STOP improver improving itself via meta-utility; Promptbreeder's evolving mutation prompts). The canonical loop she distills: (1) run harness h_t on tasks, persist traces as files; (2) mine failures into verifier-grounded patterns mapped to a specific editable component (AHE's 7: system prompt, tool description, tool implementation, middleware, skill, sub-agent config, memory); (3) same or stronger model proposes bounded, diverse edits conditioned on editable surfaces, failure patterns, passing behaviors to preserve, and prior-edit summaries, each paired with a falsifiable predicted impact; (4) validate on held-in and held-out splits, accept only zero-regression candidates, log rejects; (5) merge to h_{t+1}, repeat. Joint harness+weight loops (SIA, Continual Harness) are noted as provisional.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal is always an external, verifier-grounded task score: Terminal-Bench-2 / SWE-bench Verified / Polyglot pass rates, AFlow/ADAS task accuracy, STOP's meta-utility (mean utility of the improver across a task distribution), MCE's train/val split (inner loop on train, outer on val). Anti-drift measures she highlights from cited work: Self-Harness accepts an edit only if there is no regression on both held-in and held-out splits; AHE makes the runs directory, tracer, verifier and LLM config read-only so gains are attributable to harness edits and the loop cannot disable the verifier, swap models or raise reasoning budgets; AHE also requires each edit to carry a falsifiable prediction checked next round, and tests transfer by freezing the evolved harness and running SWE-bench Verified; ShinkaEvolve rejects candidates too similar to the population via embedding cosine similarity; DGM/ADAS keep an archive and only re-admit candidates above a threshold. Her stated principle: the evaluator and permission control must sit outside the evolving loop, with held-out tests, trace audits and human review at decision points. Weak/fuzzy evaluators (research taste, novelty, long-term repo health) are named as the primary unsolved bottleneck.
deep_reads.key_results: No new experiments (synthesis only). Numbers she relays: DGM raised Claude 3.5 Sonnet from 20% to 50% on SWE-bench Verified and 14.2% to 30.7% on Polyglot; AHE beats OpenCode/Terminus-2/Codex on Terminal-Bench-2 except the Hard tier and transfers frozen to SWE-bench Verified; Meta-Harness improves on Terminus-KIRA/Terminus-2 initializations; STOP improves with GPT-4 but degrades with GPT-3.5/Mixtral; Lin et al. 2026 find harness-updating ability is flat from Qwen3.5-9B to Claude Opus 4.6 while harness-benefit is non-monotonic (mid-tier models gain most); Trehan & Chopra's 6 auto-research failure modes; benchmark appendix (PaperBench ~21% for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, CORE-Bench 21%, MLE-bench 16.9% bronze, RE-Bench humans win at 8-32h).
deep_reads.limitations: It is an essay, not a framework: no code, no unified interface, no new evidence; predictions ('harness improvements will be internalized into the model') are unfalsified. Almost all cited wins are on coding benchmarks with cheap exact verifiers; she concedes evolutionary methods 'struggle with domains where evaluation is slow, ambiguous, or mostly heuristic-based'. Recursive structure alone does not help weak models (STOP), and harness benefit is non-monotonic in model size, so results do not transfer across base models. SIA (joint weights+harness) is called 'provisional' due to confounded baselines. Reception claims in the scout note are overstated: the 'harness engineering' wave and its 4k-star lists predate the essay; only one 85-star list is derived from it.
deep_reads.key_insight: Because a harness is code, harness design becomes an executable search space that a coding agent can explore with the same tools human engineers use; the transferable recipe is: expose every editable component as a file, mine failures into component-attributed patterns, propose bounded edits paired with falsifiable predictions, and accept only on zero regression across held-in and held-out splits, with the evaluator and permission layer kept read-only outside the loop.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prescribed rather than implemented: evaluator and permission control outside the evolution loop; explicitly declared editable surfaces (AlphaEvolve EVOLVE-BLOCK markers, AHE harness-workspace-only edits with read-only verifier/runs/model config); held-out regression gates before merging; trace audits; human review 'at the right time and abstraction level'; she flags that letting a program edit its own OS-like layer breaks abstraction boundaries and that all reward-hacking risks remain.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of the full ladder: ACE, MCE, Meta-Harness, Self-Harness, AHE and DGM each use bespoke file layouts and loops; a framework could define one component schema (system prompt, tool description, tool impl, middleware, skill, sub-agent config, memory) with a common editable-surface manifest and a pluggable proposer/validator.

Evaluator is fixed by fiat: the essay says the verifier must sit outside the loop but offers no mechanism to harden or extend evaluators for fuzzy domains (research taste, maintainability); a framework could evolve evaluators on a separate, human-audited track with disagreement detection against held-out labels.

No standard generalization gate: only AHE tests frozen-harness transfer to a second benchmark; acceptance criteria could require cross-benchmark or cross-task held-out gains, not just no-regression on the same suite.

Harness edits are not model-conditioned despite non-monotonic harness-benefit: a framework could measure harness-updating and harness-benefit separately per base model and gate or re-target edits by that profile.
Rejected edits are logged (Self-Harness) but never used: no system feeds the negative-result archive back into proposal conditioning to avoid repeated dead ends.
Diversity control is limited to embedding cosine rejection (ShinkaEvolve) on solution code; there is no diversity metric or niching for harness prompts/workflows to prevent population collapse.

Fitness is single-run task pass rate; long-horizon costs (repo health, backward compatibility, token/latency cost of the harness itself) are not in the objective; a framework could add multi-objective fitness with cost and maintainability terms.

Human touchpoints are unspecified: no concrete interface for which edits require approval, how to summarize a proposed edit plus its predicted impact for review, or how to feed human verdicts back as training signal.
Sample efficiency: every candidate needs full benchmark rollouts; no staged evaluation, early stopping, or bandit allocation across candidates is proposed beyond ShinkaEvolve parent sampling.
Joint harness+weights decision (SIA Feedback-Agent) is unvalidated; no clean protocol for when a recurring failure should trigger a weight update versus a harness edit.
sources_read: GitHub search results for 'harness engineering' and 'awesome harness' repos (creation dates, stars, README grep for essay citations)

deep_reads.name: ASI-Arch (AlphaGo Moment for Model Architecture Discovery)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yixiu Liu, Yang Nan, Weixian Xu, Xiangkun Hu, Lyumanshan Ye, Zhen Qin, Pengfei Liu — GAIR / SII / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Taptap
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2025-12-03 (file upload only); last substantive code commit 2025-08-04; no paper revision since v1.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint only (not peer-reviewed). Semantic Scholar 2026-09-11: 21 citations, 0 influential. GitHub: 1,187 stars, 218 forks, 5 open issues.
deep_reads.mechanism:
The evolving artifact is a single PyTorch file (a DeltaNet-class linear-attention layer), not the agents. One experiment (pipeline.py) = sample -> evolve -> evaluate -> analyse -> update:

1. SAMPLE: candidate pool = top-50 archive entries by fitness. Parent drawn uniformly from ranks 1-10 (its code overwrites SOURCE_FILE); 4 references from ranks 11-50. Each entry's motivation/analysis/cognition are re-summarised by a low-temp LLM every cycle (never stored) to keep context non-static.
2. EVOLVE (Researcher, o3 + GPT-4.1): planner reads code, writes modified layer + motivation in one agent (to avoid design/implementation drift). Novelty gate: FAISS top-5 similar motivations -> LLM "repeated?" verdict; if repeated, re-plan with a dedup prompt. Sanity gate (o3 code checker): causal mask, sub-quadratic complexity, chunking, dynamic shapes; may rewrite; 10 retries.
3. EVALUATE (Engineer, GPT-4.1): trainer runs a bash script (20M params, 1B tokens, 2000 steps, FLAME + lm-eval with 500 samples/task). On failure a debugger agent patches the code from the error log, max 3 attempts. Paper also describes early-kill of runs 2-3x slower or with suspiciously low loss.
4. ANALYSE (Analyst, o3): gets results plus parent/grandparent/strongest siblings as a pseudo-ablation, writes a structured analysis; the identified shortcoming is the RAG query into a Cognition Base (~100 linear-attention papers, 1-3 distilled "cognitions" each); top-3 stored with the node.
5. UPDATE: node inserted into MongoDB with parent pointer (phylogenetic tree). Every 50 insertions (after a 200-experiment cold start with no updates) the pool is re-scored and truncated to 50. Fitness = sigmoid(Δloss vs DeltaNet, ±10% window) + sigmoid(Δbenchmark) + LLM-judge (1-10, DeltaNet=5, GatedDeltaNet=10; rubric weights performance 30%, innovation 25%, complexity/efficiency 45%). Loss >10% below baseline = leakage, discarded. Many workers share the DB in parallel.

Stage 2 (manual): 1,350 20M winners -> ~400 retrained at 340M/1B tokens -> 106 beat baselines -> 5 hand-picked trained on 15B tokens.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = composite fitness per architecture: sigmoid-capped final-train-loss delta and sigmoid-capped average-benchmark delta vs a fixed DeltaNet baseline (only ±10% window counts), plus an LLM-as-judge score on a rubric anchored to DeltaNet=5/GatedDeltaNet=10. Selection is elitist: only top-50 pool members are ever parents. Anti-hacking measures: sigmoid capping so no single metric dominates; discard runs whose loss is >10% below baseline as information leakage; LLM code checker for causal-mask/complexity bugs; embedding+LLM novelty check to stop repeated ideas; batched pool updates and a 200-run cold start to keep diversity. Weaknesses: single seed, 500 samples per benchmark at 20M scale (noise floor unreported); one-third of fitness is a subjective judge whose largest weight (45% complexity/efficiency) is inferred from code, never measured; no held-out tasks; failed experiments are not archived (survivorship bias). Only ~8% of 20M winners survived the 340M re-check, showing the explore-stage fitness is a weak proxy. Final selection of 5 architectures and the 40 component categories were curated by humans.
deep_reads.key_results: 1,773 autonomous experiments at 20M params/1B tokens (~10k GPU-h); 1,350 beat DeltaNet on loss+benchmark at 20M; ~400 retrained at 340M/1B tokens (~10k GPU-h) of which 106 beat both DeltaNet and Gated DeltaNet ("SOTA", Table 2: 7-task avg gains over GDN 42.10 range +0.27 to +2.48 pts; loss -0.007 to -0.077). Final 5 at 340M/15B tokens (Table 1, avg over 8 accuracy tasks): PathGateFusionNet 48.51, ContentSharpRouter 48.34, FusionGatedFIRNet 48.29, HierGateNet 48.24, AdaMultiPathGateNet 48.18 vs Mamba2 47.84, Gated DeltaNet 47.32, DeltaNet 46.54 (note their GDN reproduction underperforms Mamba2, unlike the GDN paper, hinting at under-tuned baselines; no seeds/variance reported). "Scaling law": cumulative SOTA count grows linearly with GPU-hours (Fig. 1), i.e., a constant hit-rate, not a Kaplan-style law. Pool fitness plateaus by design while raw loss/benchmark keep improving; parameter counts stay stable (no bloat). Provenance (LLM-classified): gallery ideas 44.8% experience/analysis, 48.6% cognition, 6.6% original vs 37.7/51.9/10.4 for non-gallery. Models: o3 (planner, checker, analyst), GPT-4.1 (planner mix, dedup, trainer, debugger).
deep_reads.limitations: Stated by authors: single initial architecture (DeltaNet) so all discoveries are DeltaNet variants; no ablation of pipeline components (cognition vs analysis vs judge); no custom kernels so efficiency/latency never measured despite being 45% of the judge rubric. Observed: gains are marginal (sub-1-point average at 15B tokens vs Mamba2) with single seed and no significance testing; benchmark evaluation uses 500 samples/task at 20M scale; the "ASI"/"AlphaGo moment"/"scaling law for discovery" framing far outruns the evidence; the released repo omits the training script (issue #10), config is placeholders, real-time anomaly termination is not in the code, and it hard-depends on Azure OpenAI o3/GPT-4.1, MongoDB, OpenSearch, FAISS, Docker plus ~20k GPU-hours; repo effectively dormant since Aug 2025 with install issues open; 21 citations/0 influential after 14 months. Agents themselves never change — "self-evolution" refers to the target artifact plus its archive, so this is AlphaEvolve-style evolutionary program search with an LLM judge, not a self-improving agent.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the archive's post-mortem analysis as a first-class evolvable memory: each child is analysed against its parent, grandparent and strongest siblings (a free pseudo-ablation), the identified shortcoming is used to retrieve distilled literature "cognitions", and both are stored on the node and fed to the next proposal — their provenance study claims the best designs lean more on this accumulated experience (44.8%) than the population average, i.e., evolving what the system knows about the search space matters as much as mutating the artifact. Secondary: sigmoid-capped deltas plus an LLM judge blunt single-metric reward hacking, and a cheap explore stage (20M) feeding an expensive verify stage (340M) is what made 1,773 trials affordable.
open_gaps: Fitness is single-seed, 500-sample-per-task at 20M params with no variance estimate or held-out task suite; only ~8% of 20M winners survived the 340M re-check, so the cheap proxy needs multi-seed/significance gating or a learned scale-transfer predictor before promotion.
The search procedure itself is frozen: planner prompts, judge rubric, dedup rules, and sampling policy never change in response to discovery yield — no meta-level self-improvement of the harness.

One-third of fitness is an uncalibrated LLM judge whose largest weight (45% complexity/efficiency) is inferred from code and never measured; no human-rating calibration or measured throughput/latency in the loop.
Failed or rejected experiments (evolution/eval failures) are not stored in the archive, so the memory has survivorship bias and the system cannot learn 'what not to try'.

Elitist top-50 scalar pool with no quality-diversity/niching (MAP-Elites style), so lineages collapsed onto gating/routing variants of one DeltaNet class; only 6.6% of gallery ideas judged 'original'.
Novelty check compares motivation text embeddings plus an LLM opinion, never code or behavioral equivalence; functionally identical architectures with different prose pass.
Hard-coded to a single DeltaNet class inside FLA/FLAME with a Delta-specific judge rubric; no abstraction for swapping the target artifact or task family (no cross-domain transfer).

Human intervention remains at key points: cold-start/threshold hyperparameters, choosing the 5 finalists for the 15B-token run, and curating 40 component categories — the 'fully autonomous' claim stops at stage 1.
No sandboxing or resource limits: agents rewrite a file and run a bash script via subprocess on shared GPUs; parallel workers share an unauthenticated MongoDB/REST API.
Not usable without ~20k GPU-hours, Azure OpenAI o3/GPT-4.1, MongoDB, OpenSearch, FAISS and Docker; training script and anomaly-monitoring code are not released, so end-to-end reproduction is blocked.
deep_reads.safety_measures: No dedicated safety section. Practical guards only: LLM code checker for causal-mask leakage and O(n^2) complexity; runs with loss >10% below baseline treated as information leakage and discarded; sigmoid capping of metric deltas to discourage single-metric hacking; bounded retries (10 for evolve/checker, 3 for debug); paper describes killing runs that are 2-3x slower or have abnormally low loss. No sandboxing (agents write code and execute a bash script via subprocess), no resource quotas, no authentication on the shared DB API, no rollback concept (the agent code never self-modifies).

deep_reads.name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Hangfan Zhang, Shao Zhang, Kangcong Li, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Yiqun Zhang, Lei Bai, Shuyue Hu (Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
deep_reads.last_activity: Paper v3 Aug 2026; code repo github.com/qzzqzzb/Self-Harness created 2026-07-01, single 'Init' commit, last push 2026-07-02
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.CL), no venue; citation count not retrievable (arxiv/S2 unreachable from this environment)
deep_reads.mechanism: Model weights and evaluator are frozen; only the harness h_t (a Python module built on LangChain Deep Agents, run under Harbor for Terminal-Bench) changes. Per round: (1) Weakness Mining: every failed train-split trace is normalized into steps/stages and an LLM (same model) labels each stage with terminal_cause / criticality / agent_mechanism; failures are clustered by exact signature tuple, ranked (root_cause first, then cluster size), and rendered into a markdown 'diagnosis brief' that also lists all passing cases as regression tests to preserve. (2) Harness Proposal: the same model is prompted K times (default route_count=4), one slot at a time with previously generated proposals shown, to emit exactly one JSON proposal that changes exactly one 'virtual hook' from a fixed menu: 6 prompt-instruction hooks (system/bootstrap/execution/verification/failure-recovery/multimodal), build_subagents or subagent_call_policy, build_skills/skill_bundle (writes SKILL.md files), build_tools, middleware_policy (conditional prompt injection on always/initial/tool_error/image_input), runtime_control_policy, permissions/interrupt_on. Edits are applied by AST-replacing that function's body in the baseline file; the proposer may 'decline' with evidence. (3) Validation: each candidate is materialized, evaluated on train (43 TB2 tasks) and heldout (21 tasks) with 2 repeats each; accept iff no split's mean pass rate drops and at least one improves. All accepted candidates from a round are function-level merged, the merge is re-evaluated under the same gate, and if accepted becomes the new active branch (linear lineage). Repeat.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal is benchmark pass rate (verifier-judged: Terminal-Bench-2.0 tests, SWE-bench Verified tests, AppWorld) on a train split plus a 'held-out' split, averaged over 2 repeats. Acceptance rule (acceptance/scripts/run_acceptance_gate.py): 'no split drops and at least one split improves' — a pure non-regression gate with no statistical test. Passing train cases are explicitly passed to the proposer as regression tests to protect. The proposer is told to use train-side evidence only, but the held-out split IS consulted by the gate, so it functions as a validation set (selection-contaminated), not a true test set; reward hacking is limited structurally because edits are constrained to one whitelisted hook per candidate and cannot touch the evaluator. Diagnosis is LLM-generated (same model), so failure attribution quality is unverified.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) 'Held-out' split is used inside the acceptance gate, so reported held-out gains are optimistically biased; no truly untouched test set is evident. (2) Tiny eval sets: 43 train / 21 held-out TB2 tasks x 2 repeats — one extra pass on held-out is +2.4pp, and gate accepts any positive delta with no significance test; TB2 is noisy. (3) Starting harness is a deliberately minimal 3-sentence Deep Agents prompt, so '132% relative gain' is versus a weak baseline; no numerical comparison to hand-tuned harnesses (Terminus-2, mini-SWE-agent, Claude Code) or to Meta-Harness. (4) The released 'final' Qwen harness is almost entirely added prompt text (don't repeat failed commands, check Python modules first, create missing artifacts within 1-2 steps) plus one tool-error-triggered prompt middleware — closer to GEPA/ACE-style prompt optimization than structural harness redesign. (5) No ablations, cost/token accounting, acceptance-rate statistics, or cross-model/cross-benchmark transfer results were accessible in any summary of v3. (6) Code is a partial public re-implementation: single 'Init' commit, only the TB2 Deep Agents harness shipped (no SWE-bench/AppWorld harnesses), diagnosis and proposer LLM calls must be wired by the user via command templates, README says 'more results coming soon'. (7) Authors note the method needs granular verifier outcomes and is bounded by the predefined editable surfaces.
deep_reads.key_insight: Constrain self-modification to a small menu of typed, AST-replaceable harness hooks (prompt slots, subagent policy, skills, middleware, tools, permissions), force each candidate to change exactly one hook tied to a specific mined failure cluster, and admit it only through a train+held-out non-regression gate — this makes same-model self-improvement of the harness tractable and auditable without any stronger external optimizer.
deep_reads.key_results: v1 (TB2 64-task subset, held-out 21 tasks): MiniMax M2.5 40.5%→61.9%, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 23.8%→38.1%, GLM-5 42.9%→57.1%. v3 (9 model x benchmark combos): Terminal-Bench-2.0 MiniMax M2.5 42.2→53.9, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 18.0→36.7 (+104% rel), GLM-5 46.1→57.0; SWE-bench Verified Qwen3.5 19.5→41.5 (+113%), GLM-5 52.0→55.5 (+7%); AppWorld GLM-5 44.4→85.0 (+91%); max claimed relative gain 132% (combo not identified in accessible text). Learned edits are model-specific: MiniMax — early artifact creation and content-tag discipline; Qwen — loop-breakers/no identical retries, dependency checks, a patch_verifier subagent on SWE-bench; GLM-5 — env/path persistence across shell sessions.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Edits restricted to whitelisted hooks in one harness file (evaluator, model, and benchmark are outside the editable surface); one hook per candidate; proposer must justify hook choice and may decline; every candidate and every merged candidate must pass the no-regression gate on both splits before promotion; permissions/interrupt_on hooks exist for human-in-the-loop tool gating; full lineage (branch_state.json, candidate_queue.json, acceptance.json with reasons) is persisted for audit. No sandboxing/safety review of proposed code beyond AST-validity, and no rollback beyond simply not promoting.
open_gaps: No truly held-out test set: the 'heldout' split participates in the acceptance gate, so a framework should add a third, never-consulted split or cross-validation to report unbiased generalization
Acceptance is 'any positive delta over 2 repeats' with no significance/noise model; needs sequential testing, more repeats, or bootstrap CIs before promoting an edit
Linear single-lineage search (one active branch, merged winners); no population/archive, no crossover across branches, no revisiting rejected-but-promising edits
No cross-model or cross-benchmark transfer: harnesses are re-derived per model x benchmark; no experiment applying Qwen's harness to GLM-5 or TB2 edits to SWE-bench

Editable surface is a fixed hand-written hook menu inside one Deep Agents file; the loop cannot invent new hook types, tools with real code, or change control flow/topology beyond adding subagents and prompt middleware
Learned edits are overwhelmingly prompt text; no mechanism to prefer structural changes or to measure which hook family actually drives gains (no ablations)
Diagnosis quality is unvalidated: failure signatures come from the same weak model with no ground-truth check, and clustering is exact-string match on LLM-chosen snake_case labels
No cost accounting or budget control: each candidate costs a full 64-task x 2-repeat benchmark run, making the loop expensive; no cheap proxy eval or early stopping
No baseline against strong hand-tuned harnesses or Meta-Harness numerically, so the value of 'self' vs 'external stronger optimizer' is asserted, not demonstrated
Released code ships only the Terminal-Bench harness and requires users to wire their own diagnosis/proposer LLM commands; SWE-bench and AppWorld loops are not reproducible from the repo
