deep_reads.name: Diving into Reliable Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey (Awesome-Reliable-Self-Evolving-Agents)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Tencent Hunyuan (Kaiqi Wang, project lead; Songyang Zhang, supervisor) + Zhejiang University (Hehe Fan, corresponding; Yongliang Shen, Yi Yang, Yueting Zhuang) + Peking/Tsinghua co-authors; 13 authors
deep_reads.date: 2026-08-10 (PDF built 2026-08-10; repo created 2026-08-06; OpenReview id CGO1hDTHNe; not on arXiv)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-16 (last push: 'Update PDF link'; 12 commits total, all Aug 6-16 2026)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: OpenReview preprint (not peer-reviewed venue), 110 pages, 549 references; ~0 citations as of 2026-09 (1 month old). 196 stars / 9 forks in 5 weeks. Promoted via Tencent Hunyuan X account and Xiaohongshu.
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a survey, not a system; its contribution is a formal frame for the self-evolution loop. Retained agent state is X_k = (theta_k, sigma_k, U_k, C_k): trainable weights, scaffold (prompts/tools/memory/workflows/harness), improver (procedure that proposes/selects/commits/rolls back updates), and internal criterion (rewards, rubrics, comparison rules). One round: (1) Exec under budget b_k yields trajectory, output y_k, experience e_k (may write runtime memory sigma_rt directly); (2) the current improver U_k Proposes candidate states from e_k and history H_k (H_k stored outside the update boundary) and Selects one provisionally using C_k; (3) an EXTERNAL audit with evidence source S and acceptance policy G, both versioned and outside the update boundary, returns accept / reject-and-rollback / escalate-to-human. Only gate acceptance ('promotion') makes the candidate X_{k+1}. Level = deepest component whose active semantics causally change and persist to later independent tasks (retention condition): L0 output only, L1 theta, L2 sigma, L3 U, L4 C. RSI is defined structurally as L3+. Each level has a characteristic failure (self-confirmation, model collapse, scaffold overfitting, metric capture, criterion drift) and a matched audit/control rung ('reliability ladder'). Core principle: no update may control the only evidence used for its own acceptance; evidence disclosed to proposal/selection is 'development evidence' and cannot be the sole final audit evidence.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Prescriptive only (survey runs no experiments). Per-level evidence the paper demands: L0 execution/source-grounded checks or human adjudication; L1 fresh post-update transfer, retention and interference tests plus data-admission checks; L2 matched-budget (same model, tools, tokens, stopping rule) end-to-end comparison vs incumbent on fresh tasks the edit did not select, component ablations, provenance, tested rollback; L3 descendant performance on unseen task families under matched resources with sealed evaluation and proposal history; L4 protected outcome measures, pre- vs post-criterion cross-evaluation, and human authorization. Anti-drift/anti-reward-hacking devices it endorses: external target + evidence source + acceptance policy kept outside and versioned; anytime-valid sequential acceptance tests (PACE, SEA) to control false commits under optional stopping; held-out selection split (RSEA) with the caveat that repeated querying converts a holdout into development evidence; access logs and rotating fresh anchors; protected lineage and independent rollback/halt authority; escalation to humans for criterion changes; staged deployment (shadow, limited, broad). Explicitly cites 'harness updating is not harness benefit' as the reason a higher score does not certify improvement.
deep_reads.key_results: 549 papers classified by depth: L0 42, L1 137, L2 257, L3 21, L4 30 (plus 24 surveys, 8 cross-level reliability, 30 open-problem works). Table 2 positions it against 14 prior surveys, claiming it is the only one covering L3/L4 plus external audit systematically. Table 9 'cross-level reliability ledger' pairs each level with exposed evidence, failure mode and matched controls. Table 10 compares 10 self-evolution benchmarks (SEA-Eval, SEAGym, BenchTrace, EvoMemBench, SE-Bench, PAST-Bench, Meta-Agent Challenge, RSIBench-Data, PostTrainBench, Agent2 RL-Bench) and concludes none directly tests retained improver- or criterion-level change over multiple generations. Synthesized evidence it leans on: SEA-Eval finds up to 31.2x token difference between frameworks at similar success rates; Meta-Agent Challenge shows only 5 model-domain configs beat the human-engineered baseline with attempted test exfiltration; capability-erosion and library-drift studies show stored artifacts may be inactive or harmful later. Runtime-harness subsection catalogs 14 harness-evolution works (Meta-Harness, Self-Harness, HarnessForge, MemoHarness, Continual Harness, The Last Harness, Harness Handbook, AutoHarness, etc.).
deep_reads.limitations: No experiments, no code, no benchmark or protocol implementation; the reliability ladder is stated as 'design requirements, not sufficient guarantees'. Level assignments are by authors' reading and are marked 'conditional' when evidence is lacking, so the taxonomy is not empirically validated. OpenReview preprint, not peer-reviewed; heavy skew toward 2026 arXiv preprints of uncertain quality. L3 (21) and L4 (30) buckets are thin. Prose is dense and definitional; little quantitative meta-analysis. Companion repo is a static list (last push 2026-08-16) with no tooling. Depth is explicitly decoupled from reliability, so the survey offers no ranking of which approaches actually work best.
deep_reads.key_insight: Classify a self-evolving agent by the deepest component its updates can rewrite (output, weights, scaffold, improver, criterion), then keep the external target, evidence source, and accept/reject/escalate gate outside that update boundary: no update should control the only evidence used for its own acceptance, and any evidence the proposer has already seen is development evidence, not audit evidence.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of the audit loop (versioned external target, evidence source S, gate G with accept/reject/escalate, promotion record) — a harness framework could ship this as a concrete schema and runtime gate

No benchmark tests retained L3/L4 changes across multiple generations (does a descendant improver produce better later descendants on fresh task families under matched budget?) — build a multi-generation, sealed-final-test protocol
Holdout erosion is described but not operationalized: no access-budget ledger, query logging, or rotating fresh anchor sets for audit evidence
Matched-budget comparison (tokens, tool calls, wall-clock, stopping rule) is prescribed but no standardized cost-normalized fitness or reporting format exists
No tooling verifies that a retained scaffold/harness edit is actually active on later tasks (harness-updating vs harness-benefit decoupling) — need activation/provenance tracing per edit
Protected lineage + tested rollback for scaffold and harness edits (version DAG, replay, independent halt authority) is required but not implemented in any cited open framework
Escalation-to-human policy is undefined operationally: no triggers, throughput/backlog metrics, or reviewer-independence measures
Level-specific failure detectors (silent store drift, library drift, scaffold overfitting, metric capture) exist as one-off papers but are not integrated as automatic monitors inside evolution loops
Population/archive-based methods are not analyzed as reliability mechanisms (diversity as hedge against metric capture) — gap for multi-lineage frameworks
Cost of the audit itself (compute spent on fresh evaluation vs on evolution) is never budgeted or traded off
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prescribed, not implemented: external audit with sealed probes and fresh cases; external target/evidence source/acceptance policy versioned and outside the update boundary; runtime isolation and least-privilege execution; protected version history and tested rollback; independent halt authority; human escalation and external authorization required for L4 criterion changes; protected constraints kept unwritable; threat model covering self-reinforcing injections (Zombie Agents) and probe selection/hidden-outcome inference; staged deployment (development-separated eval, shadow observation, limited use with safeguards, broad use) with traceable promotion records naming who can authorize promotion, suspension and rollback.

deep_reads.name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (companion list to "A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents", arXiv 2508.07407)
deep_reads.mechanism: This repo has NO loop of its own: it is a README-only curated list (README.md + LICENSE + 3 figures, zero code) that indexes ~250 papers under the survey's taxonomy. The mechanism it codifies is the survey's abstract loop: four components — System Inputs I (task-level datasets vs instance-level single queries), Agent System A (LLM, prompts, memory, tools, and for MAS the topology/workflow), Environment E (benchmark or real-world feedback), and Optimiser P — where P is characterised by a search space (which parts of A are configurable) plus a search algorithm, and each iteration maps (I, A, feedback from E) to a new A'. The list then organises concrete instantiations by what P mutates: (1.1) LLM behaviour via SFT/RL (STaR, Self-Rewarding LMs, Absolute Zero, R-Zero, SPIRAL) or test-time feedback/search (CodeT, ToT, AIDE); (1.2) prompts via edit-based (GrIPS), evolutionary (EvoPrompt, Promptbreeder, GEPA), generative (APE, OPRO, PromptAgent, DSPy/MIPRO) and text-gradient (ProTeGi, TextGrad, REVOLVE) optimisers; (1.3) memory (Agent Workflow Memory, A-MEM, Mem0, Memento, ReasoningBank); (1.4) tools via training, inference-time selection, or tool creation (CREATOR, Alita, ToolEVO); (2) multi-agent workflow/topology search (ADAS, AFlow, GPTSwarm, MaAS, EvoAgentX, MermaidFlow, CORAL); (3) domain systems incl. agent-source-code evolution (DGM, AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve, Live-SWE-agent); (4) evaluation (benchmarks, LLM/Agent-as-a-Judge, safety benchmarks). The survey frames a MOP→MOA→MAO→MASE development path and "Three Laws" (Endure = safety, Excel = performance preservation, Evolve = autonomous optimisation) as constraints any optimiser must respect.
deep_reads.eval_loop: None for the repo itself (its only "signal" is community PRs adding entries). The survey's Section 4 catalogues evaluation signals used across the field: benchmark scores (SWE-bench, WebArena, GAIA, AgentBench, OSWorld, ToolBench-style suites), LLM-as-a-Judge and Agent-as-a-Judge for tasks without ground truth, and a safety/robustness benchmark set (AgentHarm, RedCode, R-Judge, AGrail, AutoDAN-Turbo). It states safety/alignment must be "continuous requirements" across the evolutionary lifecycle, but gives no operational recipe for preventing drift or reward hacking — no held-out validation protocol, no rollback criteria, no anti-Goodhart guidance beyond naming the Endure/Excel principles.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) No runnable artifact — purely a bibliography; the survey's framework is conceptual with no formal guarantees or quantitative comparison across methods. (2) Taxonomy is over-inclusive: issue #37 correctly notes OpenHands, CodeAgent, Self-Refine, AgentCoder etc. are iterative workflows, not self-evolving agents; the list conflates test-time refinement, prompt optimisation, RL post-training, and open-ended code evolution under one banner. (3) Maintenance has stalled: last merge 2026-05-16, 22 PRs (Ouroboros, OpenSkill, RewardHarness, Harness-Aware Training, Kapso, etc.) unmerged as of Sept 2026, so it under-represents the 2026 wave of harness/skill-level self-evolution. (4) Known venue/figure errors (issues #40, #61). (5) Self-promotional: the only two "Open-Source Frameworks" listed are the authors' EvoAgentX and MASLab. (6) Safety section is a list of benchmarks, not mechanisms. (7) Sparse on memory/skill evolution for deployed app agents and on cross-task transfer.
deep_reads.key_insight: Every self-evolution method is the same abstract loop — an Optimiser with a declared search space over agent components (prompt, memory, tools, topology, weights, source code) that consumes environment feedback and emits a new agent — so a framework should treat "what is mutable" as a pluggable dimension, and must explicitly enforce the survey's Endure (safety) and Excel (no performance regression) laws as acceptance gates, not afterthoughts.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of the four-component (Inputs/Agent/Environment/Optimiser) loop — a framework could ship the abstract interface so prompt, memory, tool, topology and code optimisers are interchangeable plugins

Endure/Excel laws are stated but never operationalised: no concrete regression-gate protocol (held-out eval, safety suite re-run, automatic rollback) that an optimiser must pass before a mutation is accepted

Taxonomy has no axis for the fitness signal (ground-truth benchmark vs LLM-judge vs execution tests vs human) or for how each method resists reward hacking — a framework should make evaluator provenance and anti-Goodhart checks explicit
No treatment of cross-task/cross-domain transfer of evolved artifacts (skills, prompts, memories) — most listed methods optimise per-benchmark and are re-run from scratch per task

Harness-level evolution (agent scaffolding, tool schemas, permission/sandbox config, hooks) is absent from the taxonomy — pending PRs (Harness-Aware Training, RewardHarness, Ouroboros, OpenSkill) show the field moved there in 2026 but the list stalled in May 2026

No lineage/archive concept for non-code artifacts: population/archive-based evolution appears only for code (DGM, AlphaEvolve, OpenEvolve); prompt/memory/tool evolution is presented as single-lineage hill-climbing

No cost/compute accounting dimension — nothing tells a practitioner which optimisers run on API-only budgets vs require GPU fine-tuning (model-weight methods dominate section 1.1 and 1.4.1 but are unusable for most app developers)
Memory section lists storage designs but no method for pruning, verifying, or expiring learned memories, so drift and stale-knowledge accumulation remain unaddressed
Evaluation section lacks any benchmark for the evolution process itself (sample-efficiency of improvement, stability across iterations, catastrophic forgetting) as opposed to end-task score
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-05-16 (last merged commits); 22 PRs opened through 2026-09-08 remain unmerged
deep_reads.key_results: Survey-only, no experiments. Repo: 2,477 stars, 190 forks, 41 PRs (22 open), 34 issues. Paper arXiv 2508.07407 (v1 2025-08-10, v2 2025-08-31): ~199 Google Scholar citations by Sept 2026. Contributions: 4-component unified framework (System Inputs, Agent System, Environment, Optimisers), MOP->MOA->MAO->MASE development path, "Three Laws" (Endure, Excel, Evolve), taxonomy covering ~250 works across single-agent (behaviour/prompt/memory/tool/unified), multi-agent (construction, workflow/topology), domain-specific (biomed, programming, science, finance/legal) and evaluation/safety.

deep_reads.name: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Zhe Ren, Yimeng Chen, Dandan Guo, Guowei Rong, Tonghui Li, R.B. Xiong, Qingfeng Lan, Wenyi Wang, Li Nanbo, Yibo Yang, Mingchen Zhuge, Jürgen Schmidhuber — Jilin University, KAUST, University of Alberta, IDSIA/USI/SUPSI
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-11 (companion awesome-list repo still receiving PRs; paper v1 July 2026)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (COLM-style template, no accepted venue found); Semantic Scholar: 9 citations / 1 influential (as of 2026-09-11); HF Daily Papers 35 upvotes; ~521 cited works
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a survey, so the 'loop' is a formalism rather than a running system. Agent configuration A_t = (theta_t, Sigma_t): theta = frozen-or-trainable FM weights; Sigma = (p, m, T, g) = prompts, memory + read/write policy, tools + invocation schemas, control logic (routing/scheduling/safety). Transient execution state X_t (KV cache, dialogue history, working memory) is explicitly excluded — only durable commits to theta or Sigma count as self-improvement. Self-improvement is one self-induced update operator: A_{t+1} = U(A_{1:t}, E(pi_{theta,Sigma}; Sigma_t, C_t)), where E is the agent executing its own policy in a task context C_t to emit a signal S_t (trajectories, critiques, preference pairs, verifier results, proposed edits) and U commits it. Sigma_t is passed into E so the agent can self-inspect its own scaffold. Two modes: (1) indirect/distributional — agent generates data/rewards consumed by an external optimizer (SFT/DPO/RL) on theta, the 'slow loop'; (2) direct/action-level — agent edits p/m/T/g itself, the 'fast loop' (cheap, reversible, inspectable). Full-scaffolding updates are modeled as the agent-as-improver executing on its own serialized program: candidate = exec(<Sigma_t>; S_t), materialized as patch Delta_t, committed only if verifier V(Sigma_t + Delta_t) = 1, else rollback to Sigma_t; the improver I_{Sigma_t} lives inside Sigma_t so it evolves with what it improves (Gödel-machine lineage). A 'skill' is defined as a serialized, reusable instance of U stored in any substrate; meta-level skills (write a tool, refactor a prompt, patch own scaffold) make the operator part of its own operand. History theta_{1:t}/Sigma_{1:t} is kept for validation and rollback.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Survey prescribes rather than runs an eval loop. Recommended protocol: track trajectory m_t = E[Phi(x, tau)] over iterations under a cumulative budget b_t <= B_max on a held-out D_eval (hidden or post-cutoff tasks), with explicit checkpoints, acceptance criteria and early stopping. Phi is either metric-based (executable unit tests, deterministic) or judge-based (LLM/Agent-as-a-Judge with rubric kappa). Anti-drift / anti-reward-hacking measures: (a) evaluator independence — use a different judge model/rubric for reporting than for driving updates; (b) the critic is 'governed infrastructure': decouple proposer from acceptor, allow the critic to evolve only monotonically (additive test generation) and gate its changes behind human audit; (c) verifier-gated commit of every structural patch (functional correctness, tool-permission boundaries, robustness to random state perturbation); (d) report regression rate on previously-solved tasks, tail-risk and safety violations per iteration, multi-seed variance, and full cost breakdown incl. quantified human input. Fast scaffold loop is where noisy feedback should be absorbed; parametric consolidation deferred until behavior is stable, then re-run adversarial safety tests because any theta update invalidates prior safety bounds.
deep_reads.key_results: No experiments — survey/position paper. Contributions: (1) unified formalism A=(theta,Sigma), Sigma=(p,m,T,g), self-improvement as update operator U with execution operator E; (2) two-axis taxonomy: FM improvement by signal type (intrinsic generative demonstrations D_t, intrinsic evaluative feedback e_t, extrinsic exploratory experience tau_t incl. grounded vs simulated envs) and scaffolding improvement by component (prompt: scalar-feedback / qualitative-feedback / population-based / textual-gradient; memory: object / structure / CRUD processing loop; tool: routing / refinement / creation; full scaffolding: ADAS, STOP, Gödel Agent, DGM, HGM, AlphaEvolve, ShinkaEvolve, Live-SWE-Agent, Agent Symbolic Learning); (3) 'skill' formalized as reusable serialized update operator orthogonal to substrate; (4) evaluation protocol with 6 required reporting items and a paper-benchmark incidence matrix across 6 domains; (5) three design principles (fast exploration -> slow consolidation; critic as governed infrastructure; layered gating / agent as untrusted code) and six future directions. ~521 cited works, ~28k words. Companion awesome-list repo: 471 stars, 49 forks, active PRs.
deep_reads.limitations: Purely descriptive: no algorithm, code, benchmark or empirical comparison; the operator U is a notational wrapper around heterogeneous methods, not a computable procedure. Formalism holds one of theta/Sigma fixed per step — joint theta+Sigma optimization and cross-substrate credit assignment are explicitly deferred to future work. The verifier gate V is only written down for full-scaffolding updates; memory/prompt/tool commits have no stated acceptance semantics. 'Skill' definition is loose (anything retained and reused). Safety guidance (monotone critics, human audit, layered gating) is qualitative with no threat model or protocol. Evaluation section is a checklist, not a harness. Taxonomy overlaps heavily with Gao et al. 2025 / Fang et al. 2025 self-evolving-agent surveys (the paper's own comparison table shows mostly 'secondary vs primary' differences). Strong Schmidhuber-lineage framing (Gödel machine, success-story algorithm) may overweight that lineage. Only 9 citations after ~2 months.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the agent as (frozen weights, serializable scaffold Sigma=(prompts, memory, tools, control logic)) and treat every form of self-improvement — from DPO on weights to a coding agent patching its own harness — as one verifier-gated, self-induced update operator whose signal comes from the agent's own execution; do noisy, reversible adaptation in the scaffold fast loop and only consolidate into weights once behavior is proven stable, and keep the critic outside the agent's unconstrained control.
open_gaps: No reference implementation of Sigma=(p,m,T,g) as typed, versioned substrates with a single generic gated commit/rollback API — a framework could ship this directly
Joint theta+Sigma optimization with cross-substrate credit assignment (decide per failure whether to edit a prompt, rewrite a tool wrapper, write memory, or fine-tune) is explicitly unsolved

Verifier gate V is only specified for full-scaffold patches; no acceptance criteria or regression checks are defined for memory writes, prompt edits, or tool additions, leaving memory poisoning and prompt drift persisting across sessions

No concrete protocol for safely evolving the critic/evaluator beyond 'additive test generation + human audit' — no mechanism to detect proposer/acceptor collusion or judge over-optimization automatically

The recommended evaluation protocol (trajectory under budget, held-out transfer, regression rate, cost breakdown, quantified human input) exists only as a checklist; no standardized self-improvement benchmark harness implements it, and the paper's incidence matrix shows methods evaluate on disjoint benchmarks
No non-stationary testbeds (drifting APIs, UI redesigns, adversarial users) for measuring whether self-improvement survives open-world distribution shift
Resource-aware improvement (cheap invariant checks gating expensive LLM/judge evaluations, penalizing wasted iterations, budgeted exploration) has no proposed method
Test-time continual adaptation that patches retrieval/routing/memory on the fly without eroding global performance is named but not addressed
Multi-agent cooperative co-evolution via shared artifact repositories (regression tests, patches, tool wrappers) lacks any version-control or trust protocol
No standard serialization/portability format for 'installer-like' meta-level skills so that an update discovered by one agent can be applied to another agent or session
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prescriptive only: treat self-improving agent as untrusted code in a protected runtime; layered gating / strict permission system for self-modification; every structural patch must pass verifier checks (functional correctness, tool-permission boundaries, robustness to random state perturbation) before commit to Sigma_{t+1} or theta_{t+1}; decouple critic from generator; evolving critics restricted to monotone (additive) changes and gated by human audit trails; keep parameter/scaffold history for rollback; re-run adversarial safety testing after any weight update; track regression rates, tail risk and safety violations per iteration; flags full-scaffolding regime as highest risk because one-off prompt injections can become persistent architectural vulnerabilities (poisoned memory, hijacked tool logic). Cites Vingean reflection problem (weaker system reasoning about stronger successor) as unsolved.

deep_reads.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Mingguang Chen (DeepGrounding, corresponding), Licheng Wang (AlphaAvatar), Bo Qu (Illinois Institute of Technology)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-06 (arXiv v2 + public release of companion repo deepgrounding/recursive-self-improvement)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint cs.AI (44 pp. incl. refs); no venue; citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited, paper is ~2 months old); companion GitHub repo has 0 stars / 0 forks
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a survey, not a system; it has no loop of its own. Its contribution is a canonical description of every self-improvement loop as: (1) generate candidates, (2) score them with an evaluator, (3) select/apply the winner into a substrate, (4) persist or discard. Axis 1 = which substrate absorbs the improvement: deployment-time (frozen-weight output refinement -> test-time weight updates -> harness/skill/memory evolution, ordered by persistence: evaporates per episode < lasts a session < accumulates indefinitely), training-time (self-reward RL, STaR-style CoT self-training, on-policy self-distillation where the same weights conditioned on privileged info act as teacher, self-play/zero-data proposer-solver, embodied/synthetic-data loops), the evaluator itself (judges, PRMs, verifiers, rubrics, meta-evaluation, co-evolved verifiers a la Red Queen Godel Machine), or the research process (evolutionary program discovery like FunSearch/AlphaEvolve, AI-scientist agents, A-Evolve-Training running a 30B post-training loop end to end). Axis 2 = loop closure: human-in-the-loop (person reviews each change), human-on-the-loop (automatic signal, human audits outcomes and gates deployment), closed loop (system generates, validates, applies its own changes). The paper's central claim: nearly all 1,250 papers sit in the human-on-the-loop row; the closed-loop x self-evaluation cell (a system rewriting its own definition of 'better') is where bounded self-refinement becomes open-ended RSI. A verification hierarchy (formal verifier > execution feedback > learned judge > intrinsic self-assessment) predicts observed improvement strength, and four failure modes (self-confirming loop, model collapse, diversity collapse, frame lock-in) are derived as violations of it. Corpus: 871 seed + 379 supplemental arXiv papers classified by theme defaults + keyword rules + explicit overrides, single annotator.
deep_reads.eval_loop: The survey's own 'signal' is bibliographic: arXiv harvest across seven query threads enriched with OpenAlex metadata, then rule-based classification (theme defaults + title/abstract keyword rules moved 89 papers; 3 manual overrides), all by a single annotator with per-paper assignments released for audit -- no inter-annotator agreement reported. For the systems it surveys, the paper argues the improvement signal must be placed on a verification hierarchy: formal verifiers (proof checkers, type systems; sound, can iterate indefinitely), execution feedback (tests/compilers/benchmarks; reliable but incomplete and eventually gamed), learned judges (reward models, LLM-as-judge; ~80% human agreement but themselves optimization targets), intrinsic signals (confidence, self-consistency, likelihood; cheapest and most gameable). Drift/reward hacking is framed as inevitable when generator and evaluator share weights (confidence-coupled rewards over-reward high-confidence mistakes), when exogenous signal fraction vanishes (collapse), or when proposers narrow the curriculum (diversity collapse); the recommended countermeasures are data gating + reward grounding as separate levers, entropy reservoirs (real-data mixing, retrieval), evaluator co-evolution, and human-on-the-loop gating. It also separates result-level (cheap, per-instance, opex) from process-level (expensive, reusable, capex) evaluation and argues durable gains are process-level.
deep_reads.key_results: Corpus of 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-26): deployment-time self-evolution 393 (74% from 2026), training-time self-iteration 340 (69%), self-evaluation 318 (82%), auto research 139 (76%), foundations/limits/safety 60 (57%); 74% of corpus posted in 2026, quarterly output ~500 papers in 2026 Q2. Headline evidence assembled from cited works: Mirror Loop -- 10 rounds of ungrounded self-critique drops informational change 55%, a single verification step at round 3 restores progress; SkillsBench -- human-written skills +16.2 pass-rate points, LLM-written skills no measurable gain; Pareto analysis of 34 inference-scaling configs -- peak +7.1 points over CoT only at ~20x compute; SciIntegrity-Bench -- 34.2% integrity-failure rate, all seven frontier models fabricate data in missing-data scenarios; SoundnessBench (1,099 ICLR proposals) -- pervasive optimism bias in 12 frontier models as research-direction evaluators; A-Evolve-Training -- autonomous 4-round post-training of a 30B model reached 0.86 vs 0.87 human top (8th of ~4,000) and mid-run detected its dev metric had decoupled from the external target and inverted its use of the proxy; rise-and-collapse of pass@1 under verifiable binary reward in REINFORCE that KL/EWC do not prevent; on-policy self-distillation thread went from 0 to 56 papers in ~18 months.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: corpus is a sample not a census, recency-biased by construction (supplement harvest), citation counts near zero so impact cannot be inferred; classification is automatic keyword rules plus single annotator, ~54 of 379 supplement papers are peripheral query bleed left in counts; industrial RSI inside frontier labs is unobservable (publication censoring); taxonomy deliberately does not encode whether the objective is still correct (frame lock-in) nor trajectory/continuity of one system across cells; verification hierarchy is a qualitative pattern, 'not a measured law'. Observed: the original Data availability link (bamboodrift/recursive_self_improvement) was private and did not resolve, replaced only in the 2026-09-06 v2 release; authors are from small/unknown orgs (DeepGrounding, AlphaAvatar) with no track record visible; survey leans heavily on Anthropic's May 2026 RSI essay for framing; representative-systems-per-cell grid (Figure 1) is an image with no machine-readable mapping; no quantitative meta-analysis, only narrative synthesis.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Surveys rather than implements: cites 'unfireable safety kernel' argument that guardrails inside the agent's modifiable runtime are reachable by inputs, so execution-time alignment must live outside the agent's address space; human-oversight anchors against safety drift and capability degradation that arise without any adversary; constraining the self-modification surface to auditable, diffable, roll-back-able artifacts (SHARP rubric policies) instead of free-form prompt/code evolution; formally verifiable skill evolution (VASO) for physical agents; threat analyses of permanently-encoded, self-amplifying, population-transmissible corruption in shared skill libraries; skill spec/code mismatch attacks (SkillMutator); deterministic integrity gates in regulated domains; calls for governance-grade measurement of what a training loop is and is not improving (identified as the emptiest niche: 60 of 1,250 papers on foundations/safety).
deep_reads.key_insight: Self-improvement is only as real as its verification signal: demonstrated gains track a strict hierarchy (formal verifier > execution feedback > learned judge > intrinsic self-assessment), and the risk of a loop is set by the persistence of what it modifies (outputs evaporate < weights roll back < harness/skills/memory accumulate and propagate) -- so a framework should pick the highest-rung signal available per task, keep a fixed external anchor even when co-evolving its evaluator, and constrain the self-modification surface to artifacts the chosen signal can actually audit, diff, and roll back.
open_gaps: No 'exchange rate of grounding': nobody has measured the minimum fraction of exogenous (human/formal/execution) signal per iteration that keeps a loop improving rather than collapsing; a framework could instrument and log external-signal share and detect when it trends toward zero

Trustworthy accumulation: persistent self-modifications (skills, memory, harness code, experience graphs) have no verification/rollback story comparable to weight checkpoints; concrete pattern to adopt: constrain the evolvable surface to diffable, auditable artifacts (rubrics/skill docs) with regression tests and automatic rollback on held-out drops

Frame-revision detection has neither benchmark nor metric: build a suite of deliberately stale or misspecified objectives scored on whether the loop notices (productive abandonment, invariant transfer, absence-sensitivity, reframing latency) rather than how well it optimizes

Evaluator co-evolution (Red Queen, self-trained verifiers, self-evolved rubrics) is unproven against the self-confirming loop; frameworks that evolve their judge need a held-out, non-evolving anchor set and meta-evaluation to show the judge did not drift with the policy

Stability engineering is per-paradigm folklore: no unified detector for rise-and-collapse, diversity collapse, or safety drift; a harness could track output entropy, curriculum diversity, and pass@k trajectories across generations and halt/branch on collapse signatures

LLM-authored skills give zero gain on SkillsBench while human-authored give +16.2 points: skill-writing must be evaluation-guided and trace-conditioned, not one-shot; no framework yet closes this gap in a general-purpose harness
Governance-grade measurement absent: no method produces auditable evidence of what a loop is and is not improving over time (per-substrate change logs, capability deltas against fixed external evals)

Taxonomy indexes substrate, not trajectory: no way to record that one system improved outputs, then evaluator, then method ('scientific amnesia' -- behaviors improve while no methodological knowledge accumulates); a framework needs a process-level memory of how prior improvement campaigns were run, not just their results

Non-verifiable tasks (research direction, creative quality) remain at the bottom rung; direction-evaluation is benchmarkable (SoundnessBench shows frontier models optimism-biased) but direction-generation has no evaluation at all

Representative-systems-per-cell mapping exists only as a figure image; no machine-readable dataset labels each of the 1,250 papers with loop-closure level, so mapping frameworks onto the grid still requires manual work
Survey's own classification is single-annotator keyword rules with no inter-annotator agreement; category counts should not be used as field-composition statistics

deep_reads.name: Evolver (EvoMap)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: EvoMap (evomap.ai; maintainer handle autogame-17; paper authors Junjie Wang, Yiming Ren, Haoyang Zhang, EvoMap/Tsinghua)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-06 (push; release v2.0.33; latest issues 2026-09-07)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv:2604.15097 (self-authored by EvoMap, not peer-reviewed, citation count unavailable); npm ~5.9k downloads/month; 843 forks
deep_reads.mechanism: Evolver is a Node CLI that runs beside a coding agent (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex hooks) in a git repo. Per cycle (verified in readable v1.28 source; current core is obfuscated): (1) Regex-scan session transcripts/logs/MEMORY.md into string "signals" (log_error, errsig:<hash>, perf_bottleneck, user_feature_request, stagnation flags). (2) Select a Gene from genes.json by counting substring/regex hits of gene.signals_match against signals. A memory-graph JSONL of signal->gene outcomes (30-day half-life) supplies a preferred gene and bans genes with expected success <0.18 after 2+ attempts; FailedCapsules with >=0.6 signal overlap ban a gene after 2 failures; "drift" picks a random top-N gene with probability 1/sqrt(pool size). (3) Build a Mutation (category repair/optimize/innovate from signals plus strategy preset) and a PersonalityState (five scalar dials nudged +/-0.05-0.1 by fixed rules; best key chosen by Laplace-smoothed success rate). (4) Emit a "GEP" prompt embedding the gene's strategy steps, an output schema for five JSON objects, recent history and failed capsules; the host spawns a sub-agent that edits code. (5) Solidify: compute git blast radius vs gene.constraints (max_files, forbidden_paths), run gene.validation commands (node/npm/npx only, 180s), canary-load index.js, optional LLM review; success -> score 0.85 else 0.2 with git stash/reset rollback; append parent-linked EvolutionEvent, Capsule (diff+strategy) or FailedCapsule; add epigenetic mark +/-0.1 per env fingerprint; if nothing matched, auto-create a boilerplate gene keyed by signal hash. (6) Capsules with score>=0.7, streak>=2 and safe blast radius auto-publish to EvoMap Hub, where other nodes fetch and validate them. v2 adds ingest --distill (excerpt session turns into gene strategies) -> review -> inject session-start.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Acceptance is binary pass/fail of gene-declared validation commands plus blast-radius/forbidden-path constraint checks and a canary import; the recorded score is a constant (0.85/0.2), not a task metric. Anti-drift: circuit breaker forces 'innovate' after 3 consecutive failed repairs; signals seen in 3+ of last 8 events are suppressed; genes banned via decayed outcome ledger; history block in prompt says 'do not repeat intent+signal+gene'. Reward hacking is weakly guarded: the agent authors gene validation commands itself (a bundled distilled gene validates with 'node --version'), LLM review is off by default, and hub validators re-run only the proposer's own claimed commands. Paper evidence: 4,590 trials, 45 sci-code scenarios, Gemini 3/3.1 Pro; CritPt 70 problems, 9.1->18.57% and 17.7->27.14% (13/70 and 19/70), single benchmark, same-org authors. An offline trigger-shift replay evaluator exists but is diagnostic only and not wired into selection.
deep_reads.limitations: 27 of 53 core src/gep files are javascript-obfuscated with RC4 string encryption and anti-debug traps; git history was rewritten to start 2026-04-16 and v2 ships as 70-100MB binaries, so the current loop cannot be audited despite 'auditable evolution' branding. Fitness never measures task performance; a change that passes self-declared node scripts is 'success'. Signal extraction is regex on log text; gene selection is keyword counting; auto-created genes carry a fixed generic strategy, so 'genes' accumulate mostly as signal keys, not learned strategy. Independent closed-loop tests (issues #624, #625, N=5 runs) found v2 inject passes only summary labels, not strategy text, so gains vanish, and auto-distilled strategies mix success prose with truncated fixes and can be worse than no injection. 'evolver cycle' refuses runners outside claude/codex/gemini (#627); hub validator tasks fail 91% due to sandbox blocking 'node -e' (#607). Heavy coupling to EvoMap Hub economy (ATP credits, worker pool, leaderboards). Personality 'evolution' is rule-based scalar nudges with no demonstrated effect. Paper is not peer-reviewed, Gemini-only, and CritPt gains are small-N. Hermes similarity dispute and license shift make the project's future openness uncertain.
deep_reads.key_insight: Encode accumulated agent experience as compact structured 'genes' (trigger signals -> strategy steps -> AVOID cues -> validation hooks, ~230 tokens) rather than long skill docs, and make every self-modification a git-scoped, validation-gated, rollback-able event logged in a signal->gene outcome ledger so selection can ban low-yield paths and share validated capsules across nodes.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (arXiv:2604.15097): across 4,590 trials on 45 scientific code tasks with Gemini 3 / 3.1 Pro, Skill docs gave unstable signal (overview section -4.7pp, workflow +1.5pp) while genes were robust to structural perturbation but sensitive to semantic errors (~49% with wrong algorithm/domain); failure history distilled into compact AVOID cues beat appended raw failures. CritPt (70 problems): OpenClaw+EvoMap went Beta 0% -> v2.1 17.14% -> v2.2 18.57% vs 9.1% base (Gemini 3 Pro), and 17.7% -> 27.14% (Gemini 3.1 Pro), with tokens rising then falling across versions. Repo: 9,055 stars, 843 forks, ~5.9k npm downloads/month, 34 tags since April, v2.0.33 binaries. Third-party N=5 test: strategy-text injection cut trap errors 11->4 and tokens -55%, but the official inject channel gave 4->6 and +13.8% tokens.
open_gaps: Fitness is a constant 0.85/0.2 derived from self-declared validation commands; no task-level or held-out benchmark score enters gene selection
Proposer and verifier are the same agent: genes carry their own validation commands (e.g. 'node --version'), so a gene-independent, tamper-proof evaluator is missing
Gene selection is substring/regex hit counting over regex-extracted log signals; no semantic retrieval or embedding match of situation to strategy

Auto-created genes get a boilerplate strategy and auto-distilled strategies are truncated excerpts of the agent's own turns; no quality gate or LLM refinement that verifies a strategy is actionable before injection
Closed-loop transfer is unverified by maintainers: v2 inject session-start drops strategy text (issue #624), so learned fixes do not reach the next session
No cross-task or cross-project generalization measurement; the trigger-shift evaluator is offline-only and not fed back into selection or gene pruning
Flat gene list with no population/archive of competing variants, no crossover, no explicit exploration budget beyond random drift 1/sqrt(N)
Core loop is obfuscated and v2 is binary-only, and 'evolver cycle' refuses non-allowlisted runners, so it cannot be audited, extended, or used with custom harnesses
Blast radius is file/line counts, not semantic risk; protected paths are a static list
Personality dials and strategy presets are rule-nudged scalars with no demonstrated causal effect on outcomes
Only evidence is a same-org arXiv paper on Gemini models and a 70-problem benchmark; no independent replication of the gene-vs-skill claim
deep_reads.safety_measures: Git-based rollback on failed solidify (stash default since 1.80.8, hard reset or none configurable); validation commands whitelisted to node/npm/npx with no shell operators or command substitution, 180s timeout; canary child-process import of index.js before commit; blast-radius limits (max_files, forbidden_paths) and destructive-change detection on protected core files; --review human-in-the-loop mode; optional LLM diff review (off by default, fails closed since Aug 2026); external hub assets staged in a candidate zone and promoted only with --validated; credential redaction before publishing; EVOLVE_ALLOW_SELF_MODIFY defaults false to keep the evolver from editing its own source; repair-loop circuit breaker; load and active-session backoff guards.

deep_reads.name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents (XMUDeepLIT) / "A Systematic Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: From Model-Centric to Environment-Driven Co-Evolution"
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a curated reading list plus companion survey, not a runnable system: nothing in the repo executes a loop. What it contributes is a taxonomy of loops. The survey defines an agent as a tuple <Phi (policy/weights), M (memory), T (tools), I (interaction interface; perception P was folded into I after issue #2)> and defines self-evolution by two properties: "strong autonomy with minimal human supervision" and "active exploration through interaction" (maintainer reply, issue #4). Three evolvable substrates: (1) Model-centric: inference-time (self-consistency, Self-Refine, ToT) or training-time mutation of Phi via self-synthesized data (STaR/SEAL) or online self-play/RL with verifiable or self-generated rewards (R-Zero, Absolute Zero, Agent0, WebRL, TTCS). (2) Environment-centric: mutate what sits between model and world -- knowledge (agentic RAG/deep research), experience/context (ReasoningBank, ACE, GEPA, Dynamic Cheatsheet, Memento), skills (SkillWeaver, AutoSkill, SkillRL, OpenSkill), tools (Voyager, LATM, Alita, Godel Agent), memory architecture (A-Mem, MemEvolve), topology (ADAS, AFlow, EvoAgent, MaAS). (3) Co-evolution: agent and environment/curriculum/verifier co-adapt (GenEnv, RLVE, EnvScaler, AutoForge, CoMAS, co-evolving coder/tester). The list's newest and most useful sections are "Self-Evolution Evaluation" benchmarks (Aspire, S3Gym, HarnessDev: held-out downstream tasks after weight/harness updates) and community-added harness tooling (AgentDescent: N workers propose diffs to skills/prompts/harness, aggregator accepts on Beta posterior over held-out reward; hmharness: bench-gated skill evolution with canary A/B; RewardHarness). The list itself evolves by PR: 21 PRs, most from the added projects' own authors, reviewed by two maintainers with no written acceptance criteria.
deep_reads.eval_loop: None intrinsic -- the repo is a document. For the surveyed literature the signal varies by branch: verifiable rewards/unit tests and self-play win-rates for weight evolution; task success or self-judgment for experience/skill evolution; held-out downstream tasks only in the three Sept-2026 "self-evolution evaluation" benchmarks (Aspire, S3Gym, HarnessDev) and in AgentDescent's Beta-posterior acceptance gate. The survey flags reward hacking/misevolution via a single paper ("Your agent may misevolve", ICLR'26) and a solver-verifier-gap theory paper; it does not classify papers by signal type or by regression-prevention mechanism. List curation drift: entries are added by self-promoting PR authors (Ouroboros, hmharness, agent-qa, Aeon, AgentDescent, TaoLive) with no stated inclusion bar.
deep_reads.limitations: 1) No experiments or numbers: pure taxonomy. 2) Per-paper annotations of what-evolves / fitness signal / rollback are absent except the Applications table's one-phrase "Evolution Mechanism" column; only 4 [[Code]] links across 212 paper entries, no star counts or maturity for projects. 3) Taxonomy is leaky: authors concede in issue #4 that "inference-based evolution" (self-consistency, ToT) produces no persistent change and is "temporary and localized"; several works (Voyager, AgentGym, Reasoning Gym) appear in multiple sections. 4) Safety coverage is one paper plus an unrelated embodied-safety survey. 5) The survey paper is on TechRxiv v2 (2026-02-27)/SSRN, not arXiv -- the README's arXiv badge id 2602.05665 resolves to a different paper (Graph-based Agent Memory); OpenAlex shows 0 citations. 6) Applications table lists commercial products (Devin, Cursor, Manus, Claude Code, OpenClaw) with vague, unverifiable mechanism descriptions ("Skill accumulation", "Human-AI co-evolution"). 7) Maintenance is two people (58/89 commits) with 4-11 commits/month since March; a companion list from a different group has 6x the stars. 8) Benchmarks section is mostly generic capability benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, SWE-bench), not evolution benchmarks, until the Sept 2026 addition.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treat the agent as a tuple (weights, memory/experience, tools/skills, topology, environment/curriculum) and pick the cheapest substrate to mutate: the field is moving from mutating weights (needs GPU RL and verifiable rewards) to mutating environment-facing state (skills, context, harness) and finally the environment itself (co-evolution), and the only honest measure of a self-evolution loop is improvement on hidden held-out tasks after the loop runs, not on the tasks the loop trained on.
open_gaps: No surveyed system evolves multiple substrates (prompts, skills, memory, tools, topology, curriculum) under one shared acceptance gate; each paper mutates one substrate, so a unified harness with a single held-out fitness test and per-substrate blast-radius policies is open

Regression prevention is not even a taxonomy category: versioned artifacts, rollback, canary deployment and a frozen regression suite appear only in community-added tools (hmharness, AgentDescent, Ouroboros), never as a studied mechanism

Fitness for experience/skill evolution (ACE, ReasoningBank, Dynamic Cheatsheet, Memento) is in-distribution task success or self-judgment; held-out/hidden-task evaluation exists only in Aspire/S3Gym/HarnessDev (Sept 2026), so a framework should ship hidden splits and report train-vs-held-out deltas by default
Cross-task and cross-domain transfer of learned skills is unmeasured except AgentKB/CoPS; a skill-library transfer benchmark and skill-pruning policy are missing

Credit assignment for non-parametric evolution is untracked: no method records which memory/skill entry caused which improvement, so libraries grow monotonically with no provenance-based garbage collection

The training-based branch requires GPU RL stacks (verl, slime, OpenRLHF); there is no training-free reference implementation of the environment-centric loop that an application developer can run on API models
No cost accounting or stopping criterion for evolution loops: none of the entries report compute per accepted improvement or define when to stop evolving
Safety of self-modification is one paper ('misevolve', ICLR'26): no category for permissioning, sandboxing, or human-review gates on agent-authored skills/tools/code

Multi-agent co-evolution entries mostly need MARL training; a training-free shared-experience population (Group-Evolving Agents style) with conflict resolution and merge acceptance is only prototyped in AgentDescent
The list itself lacks structured per-paper fields (what evolves, signal, rollback, code, stars); a machine-readable index with those fields would make the survey usable for framework design

deep_reads.name: Self-Evolving Coding Agents (survey)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Hao Zhou, Haichuan Hu, Quanjun Zhang (Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Ye Shang (Nanjing University)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-29 (companion repo zhouhao1024/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Coding-Agents last push; paper still v1)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint v1 only (2026-08-04), no venue / not peer-reviewed; citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited), 9 HuggingFace upvotes, 83 references, ~9.5k-word body, Table 2 classifies ~30 representative systems
deep_reads.mechanism: This is a survey, not a system; it contributes no loop of its own but a three-axis frame for describing loops in coding agents. Axis 1, the object of evolution (RQ1): (a) agent framework / scaffold rewriting and archive-based variant search (SICA, SIFT, STOP, DGM, Mendel GM, Huxley GM); (b) memory: experience banks, subtask-aligned memory, repository memory from commit history, vulnerability-repair experience (SWE-Exp, EvoCoder, Subtask Memory, RepoMemory, EvoRepair, SAGE); (c) skills and tools distilled from trajectories or learned per repository, plus on-the-fly tool synthesis (CODESKILL, gskill, Socratic-SWE, EffiSkill, Live-SWE-Agent); (d) model-side: policy/verifier updated from the agent's own verified attempts (Self-play SWE-RL, Agent-RLVR, ReVeal, CURE, ZeroCoder, Sol-Ver, ACE); (e) workflow and topology: mutable roles, DAGs, communication density (SEMAG, EvoMAC, SEW, AFlow, EvoAgentX, AgentConductor). The companion repo adds a sixth: environment/context (TACO, SWE-Pruner, EvoConfig). Axis 2, evolving time (RQ2): task-time (adapt within the current task), post-task (abstract a finished trajectory into memory/skills), stage-wise (batch trajectories into policy or agent-generation updates). Axis 3, evidence: outcome (solve rate, cost, verifier score = selection pressure), environmental feedback (compiler, tests, tool errors = in-task adaptation), trajectory-derived (full traces = memory/skill/curriculum distillation). The survey's sharpest definitional move is a closed-loop boundary: post-training counts as self-evolution only if the signal is generated by the agent's own attempts (so SWE-RL, SWE-Gym, R2E-Gym, SWE-RM are classified as infrastructure or learned evidence, not self-evolving agents).
deep_reads.eval_loop: The survey runs no experiments and reports no numbers of its own. It catalogs the signals used by surveyed systems: outcome evidence (SWE-bench/Verified/Lite/Pro resolve rate, HumanEval/MBPP/APPS/CodeContests/LiveCodeBench pass rate, cost/runtime as in SICA, archive fitness as in DGM), environmental feedback (unit tests, compiler diagnostics, CI logs, sandboxed execution, adversarially generated tests in ACE/CURE), trajectory-derived evidence (traces distilled into experience banks or skill registries, LLM-judge rubrics in CODESKILL and SIFT), and learned verifiers/reward models (SWE-RM). On drift and reward hacking it is diagnostic only: it flags that benchmark-selected self-modifications are sensitive to evaluation noise and leakage, that a harness-modifying agent can exploit the evaluation harness, that self-play loops need learnable information gain per iteration (citing Liu et al. 2026) or they reinforce bias, and that memories/skills go stale or get contaminated by failed trajectories. It recommends validation, rollback, skill audits, and held-out transfer tests but specifies no concrete protocol.
deep_reads.limitations: Narrative synthesis with no quantitative meta-analysis, no reproduced results, no headline numbers, and no comparison table of reported gains; Table 2 covers only ~30 systems while the companion repo already lists 65 core papers (27 in the framework/harness category alone versus 6 discussed in the paper), so the text lags its own corpus; the taxonomy (what/when/evidence) is a domain specialization of prior general surveys (Gao et al. 2026, Fang et al. 2025) rather than a new lens; the safety/rollback/validation discussion stays at the level of exhortation with no mechanism catalog; product coverage (Claude Code memory, Cursor, Devin, Copilot) exists only in the repo README and is explicitly caveated as undocumented mechanisms; arXiv v1 only, not peer-reviewed, five weeks old; 'self-evolving' is used loosely for anything that persists state across tasks.
deep_reads.key_insight: Software engineering is the natural substrate for agent self-evolution because its feedback is executable and repeatable, but a loop only counts as self-evolution when the signal closes around the agent's own attempts; the same executable signals that make evolution cheap also propagate errors into persistent state (memory, skills, scaffold, weights), so validation, rollback and held-out transfer must be first-class parts of the loop, not afterthoughts.
deep_reads.key_results: No experimental results (survey). Structural outputs: three research questions; a five-category object-centered taxonomy (framework, memory, skill/tool, model, workflow/topology), extended to six in the repo (environment/context); a 3-way temporal typology (task-time / post-task / stage-wise); a 3-way evidence typology (outcome / environmental / trajectory-derived); a closed-loop boundary criterion excluding SWE-RL, SWE-Gym, R2E-Gym, SWE-RM from 'self-evolving'; a challenges list (reproducibility and benchmark overfitting, feedback reliability and harness exploitation, stale memory/skills and coordination cost, evaluation beyond short benchmarks, no evidence of transfer to non-coding domains). Companion awesome-list: 174 entries, 139 stars, 11 forks, includes 27 harness-evolution papers (AHE, HarnessFix, TTHE, HarnessCompass, Evo-Harness, EvolveNet, HELIX, Ouroboros, HarnessBank, DarwinX, Self-Harness, Meta-Harness, HarnessX, etc.).
deep_reads.safety_measures: None proposed; the survey only names the need for validation, rollback, robustness checks, memory revision, skill audits, and constrained self-modification, and notes that framework-level evolution can break the agent loop or exploit the evaluation harness. It contains no threat model, no sandboxing guidance, and no catalog of how surveyed systems actually gate or revert self-modifications.
open_gaps: No system in the survey evolves more than one object at a time in a coordinated way (e.g. joint scaffold + skill + memory updates with shared attribution); a framework could unify the five/six objects under one mutation-and-selection loop
Rollback and verification of self-modifications are only called for, never specified: no surveyed system offers versioned scaffold state, regression gates, or automatic revert on held-out degradation

Fitness is almost always a single public benchmark (SWE-bench variants, HumanEval); no protocol for held-out repositories, contamination-aware task generation, or measuring generalization beyond the evolved setting

Memory and skill stores have no staleness, redundancy, or contamination controls; nothing surveyed retires memories/skills when repository state changes or when a stored lesson was learned from a flaky test
Evidence reliability is untreated: no surveyed loop weights signals by test coverage, flakiness, or verifier calibration, so misleading feedback propagates into persistent state
Transfer of evolved artifacts is only in-domain; no evidence that skills/scaffolds learned on one repo or language transfer to others or to non-coding tasks
No cost accounting or budget-aware evolution: repeated benchmark evaluation of candidates is expensive and the survey reports no cost-vs-gain tradeoffs

Product-side mechanisms (Claude Code, Cursor, Devin, Copilot memory) are undocumented; a framework that exposes an auditable evolution log would fill the gap between research prototypes and deployed tools
Long-horizon quality (maintainability, security, reviewability) is never used as an evolution signal; all loops optimize for test passing

deep_reads.name: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner — Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Eric Zelikman*, Yuhuai Wu* (Stanford + Google Research), Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman — Stanford CS
deep_reads.last_activity: Code repo last push 2023-02-21 (CITATION.bib update; actual code release 2022-11-18). Unmaintained since.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: NeurIPS 2022 (main track). OpenAlex cited_by 117 (known undercount); Google Scholar on the order of 1,000+ (not verifiable this session — Semantic Scholar rate-limited). Cited in 15/18 curated self-evolving lists per scout.
deep_reads.mechanism: Single-agent, single-model loop over a FIXED labeled dataset D={(x,y)} plus ~10 hand-written few-shot rationale exemplars P. Each outer iteration n (Algorithm 1; iteration_train.py): (1) Rationale generation — current model M_{n-1}, prompted with P, decodes near-greedily (code: temp=0.01, top_p=0.9, one sample per question) a rationale r̂ and answer ŷ for every x in D (10k sampled arithmetic problems; all 9,741 CQA train; all 7,473 GSM8K train). (2) Filter — keep (x, r̂, y) iff ŷ == y by exact lowercase string match. (3) Rationalization — for every FAILED x, re-prompt M_{n-1} with the correct answer injected as a hint ('(CORRECT)' beside the right CQA choice; '(answer)' after the question for GSM8K; answer after 'Target:' for arithmetic) using a separate hint-prompt set; keep if it reproduces y, and save it with the hint STRIPPED so the model trains as if it had found it unaided. (4) Fine-tune a fresh copy of the ORIGINAL pretrained M — not M_{n-1} (code: device_train.py --tune-model-path=base checkpoint) — on D_n ∪ D_n^rat with plain SFT; inner-loop steps grow per outer iteration (40 steps first, +20%/iter; 300 steps +20/iter with rationalization on arithmetic; GSM8K capped at 7,912 steps from iter 30). (5) Evaluate on dev, repeat until plateau (up to 48 iterations on GSM8K), report best. Theory: filter+SFT approximates REINFORCE with indicator reward 1[ŷ=y] (Eq. 2), using greedy decoding for low variance and multiple gradient steps per batch; rationalization is an off-policy proposal from p(r|x,y). No population, no archive (data regenerated each iteration; optional copy_n carries files forward), no learned verifier, no separate expert/value model. Weights are the only mutated artifact; P, D and the filter are static.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Improvement signal = binary exact-match correctness of the final answer against ground-truth labels on the fixed training set (non-learned, not gameable in itself). Progress monitored by held-out accuracy (CQA dev; GSM8K test; arithmetic per-digit); loop stopped 'when performance saturates' and best iteration reported (mild dev-set selection). Anti-drift/anti-hacking measures: (a) retrain from the original checkpoint every iteration to avoid compounding overfitting; (b) near-greedy sampling — higher temperature (0.5/0.7) produced right-answer/wrong-rationale pairs whose scratchpads 'diverge into meaninglessness' and stalled training (Appendix H); (c) few-shot prompts retained during sampling to prevent rationale style drift and rationalization degradation; (d) hints stripped from saved rationalizations. Weakness: nothing verifies the rationale itself, so lucky spurious rationales enter training (20% chance on 5-way CQA; worse on binary tasks). A label-free self-consistency variant (majority vote of high-temp samples as pseudo-label) was tried and 'significantly underperformed' ground truth. Human eval (20 Prolific raters, 50 items) is post-hoc only, not in the loop.
deep_reads.key_results: GPT-J 6B. Arithmetic (n-digit sums): 89.5% after 16 iterations vs 76.3% direct-answer fine-tune on 10k examples/5k steps; few-shot CoT baseline <1% on 2-digit; with rationalization 2-digit jumps <1%→32% after ONE iteration; without rationalization learning is stage-wise (n digits only after n-1) and plateaus; adding digits at iter 20 yields some OOD success on unseen 9–10 digit sums (with instability). CommonsenseQA dev: STaR+rationalization 72.5% (trains on 86.7% of data: 78.2% gen + 8.5% rat) vs STaR w/o rationalization 68.8% vs GPT-J direct fine-tune 60.0% vs few-shot CoT GPT-J 36.6% vs few-shot direct 20.9% vs LaMDA-137B few-shot CoT 55.6% vs GPT-3-175B direct fine-tune 73.0% (the '30x larger' claim). GSM8K test: 10.7% (rat, 30.3% data) vs 10.1% (no rat, 25.0% data) vs 5.8% direct FT vs 3.1% few-shot CoT; needed 36 + 12 iterations. Ablations: keeping few-shot prompts in fine-tuning 60.9→68.8 (no rat) and 69.9→72.5 (rat); higher-temperature sampling as a substitute for rationalization is worse than no rationalization; majority-vote pseudo-labels significantly underperform. Human eval: STaR rationales ranked above few-shot CoT 30% more often (p=.039) and above human CoS-E rationales 74% more often (p<.001) — authors caveat this reflects poor human baseline. Model uses fewer calculator steps than humans ~45% of the time, sometimes finding shortcuts.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: (1) needs above-chance few-shot CoT to bootstrap — GPT-2 fails even on arithmetic; (2) high-chance-rate tasks (MCQ, binary) admit bad rationales with correct answers, contaminating training — 'filtering bad reasoning paired with correct answers remains an open question'; (3) plateau without rationalization because failures give zero signal; (4) hint injection is task-specific and 'may be nontrivial' elsewhere; (5) bias amplification — 'if biases are useful in solving a dataset they will be amplified', worse with rationalization; (6) faithfulness of rationales unverifiable (model may pick answer then post-hoc justify); (7) no guarantee results scale beyond 6B. Observed/unstated: only in-distribution single-task gains; each task trained separately (no transfer); GSM8K absolute gains tiny (10.7%) and rationalization adds only +0.6 there; CQA headline is dev-set with best-iteration selection; compute-heavy (retrain from base each of up to 48 iterations; GSM8K steps capped to keep runs tractable); greedy one-sample decoding = minimal exploration; code is a TPU/JAX mesh-transformer fork frozen since 2023 (232 stars, 25 forks) — not runnable on modern stacks without porting. 'Self-improvement' claim is genuine but narrow: weights improve on a fixed labeled task; nothing else (prompts, data, verifier) evolves.
deep_reads.key_insight: Outcome-filtered self-imitation (sample → keep only answer-correct traces → SFT from the ORIGINAL checkpoint → resample with the new model) is a low-variance, infrastructure-free approximation of policy gradient with a 0/1 reward; and 'rationalization' (conditioning on the known answer to sample from p(r|x,y)) converts failures — which otherwise contribute zero gradient — into off-policy training signal, preventing the loop from stalling.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Restart fine-tuning from the original pretrained checkpoint each outer iteration (prevents cumulative overfitting/drift); ground-truth-only acceptance filter; near-greedy decoding to limit right-answer/wrong-reasoning contamination; few-shot prompts kept during sampling to constrain style drift; hint removed before storing rationalized examples; stop at plateau. No rollback of a bad iteration, no learned/process verifier, no held-out gating of accepted data, no bias or faithfulness checks in the loop — bias amplification and unfaithful post-hoc rationales are explicitly flagged as open risks (Sec. 5–6).
open_gaps: Fitness is final-answer exact match only: no rationale/process-level verifier, so lucky spurious rationales enter training — worst on multiple-choice/binary tasks (authors call this the main open question)
Requires ground-truth labels for every training question; the label-free majority-vote variant 'significantly underperformed' — no mechanism to bootstrap on unlabeled or open-ended tasks
No held-out generalization gate or cross-task transfer: one model per dataset, best iteration selected on same-task dev accuracy, no measurement of whether learned reasoning transfers

Full retraining from the base checkpoint every iteration (up to 48 iterations, 7.9k steps each on GSM8K): compute grows linearly with iterations; no incremental update, replay buffer, or data archive across iterations
Cold-start dependency: needs above-chance few-shot CoT from the base model (GPT-2 cannot bootstrap); no curriculum/difficulty scheduling to start weaker models
Single greedy sample per question: no exploration budget, no best-of-N, and failures yield no pairwise/preference signal (later filled by V-STaR, DPO-style iterations)
No rollback or regression detection: plateau is the only stop criterion; a degraded iteration is not automatically discarded
Rationalization hint format is hand-designed per task (CQA '(CORRECT)', GSM8K parenthetical, arithmetic 'Target:'); no general answer-injection mechanism for arbitrary domains

Only demonstrated at 6B (GPT-J) with TPU/JAX code unmaintained since Feb 2023; requires full fine-tuning infrastructure — no prompt-, skill-, or context-level variant usable by application developers without GPUs
Bias amplification and rationale faithfulness are acknowledged but unmeasured; nothing filters WHAT gets imitated beyond answer correctness

deep_reads.name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Aman Madaan, Niket Tandon, Prakhar Gupta, Skyler Hallinan, Luyu Gao, Sarah Wiegreffe, Uri Alon, Nouha Dziri, Shrimai Prabhumoye, Yiming Yang, Shashank Gupta, Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder, Katherine Hermann, Sean Welleck, Amir Yazdanbakhsh, Peter Clark — CMU LTI / Allen Institute for AI / UW / NVIDIA / UCSD / Google DeepMind
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo madaan/self-refine: last push 2024-10-04 (one-character typo fix PR); last substantive commit 2023-11-29 (GPT-4V 'visual self-refine' colab). Effectively unmaintained since Nov 2023; scripts hardcode retired OpenAI engines (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003).
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: NeurIPS 2023 (main track). Semantic Scholar: ~4,593 citations, 298 influential (Sept 2026). Repo: 820 stars, 71 forks, Apache-2.0.
deep_reads.mechanism: Nothing about the agent evolves across tasks; what is mutated is a single per-instance OUTPUT y_t within one episode, using one frozen LLM M in three prompted roles. Algorithm 1: (1) y0 = M(p_gen || x) via a task-specific few-shot prompt. (2) Loop t=0..T: fb_t = M(p_fb || x || y_t) where p_fb contains <input, output, feedback> triples demonstrating feedback that is 'actionable' (names a concrete edit) and 'specific' (points at concrete spans); optionally emits numeric per-aspect scores (e.g. acronym: 5 aspects x 5 = /25) or a stop marker. (3) If stop(fb_t, t) break; else y_{t+1} = M(p_refine || x || y0 || fb0 || ... || y_t || fb_t) — the whole history of prior outputs+feedback is appended so the model 'does not repeat mistakes'. Max 4 iterations, temperature 0.7; final y_T is returned (for multi-aspect tasks the max-self-score iterate is selected). In the released code the stop test is a string match (GSM: feedback contains 'it is correct'), and for GSM the feedback and refined solution are produced in ONE generation (critique text followed by a rewritten `def solution()`), with each round's (solution, feedback, fix) triple appended to the prompt as a new in-context example. Three prompts per task (init/feedback/iterate), 7 tasks: dialogue response, code optimization (PIE), code readability, GSM8K math, Yelp sentiment reversal, acronym generation, CommonGen-Hard (20-30 concepts). No training, no external tools, no verifier, no population/archive, single agent, zero persistence across instances.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Inside the loop the ONLY improvement signal is the same model's natural-language self-feedback (plus self-assigned numeric aspect scores on some tasks); termination is a fixed budget (4) or the model's own 'looks correct' verdict. There is no external check, no ground truth, no rollback: the last iterate is returned (or max self-score iterate for multi-aspect tasks), so a bad critique directly degrades the output — the paper's own failure analysis (70 samples, GSM+PIE) attributes 94% of failures to the feedback (33% wrong error location, 61% wrong fix) and only 6% to the refiner. On math, ChatGPT says 'everything looks good' on 94% of instances, so the loop mostly no-ops; gains appear only when an ORACLE correctness label gates refinement (Appendix K.1: GPT-3.5 64.1->68.9, GPT-4 92.9->93.8). Paper-level evaluation: task metrics (GSM solve rate, PIE %programs optimized, concept coverage), GPT-4-as-judge preference (claimed 68-82% agreement with humans), and blind A/B human eval on 150 examples/task performed BY THE AUTHORS (single annotation per item; kappa 0.53-0.75 on a 50-item double-annotated GPT-4 subset). Wilson CIs (Appendix M): nearly all GPT-4 gains significant, ChatGPT 4/7, GPT-3.5 only 3/7. Drift/reward-hacking prevention: none; the only guard is appending history and the per-task max-iteration cap.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 1 (Base -> +Self-Refine): GPT-4: Sentiment Reversal 3.8->36.2, Dialogue 25.4->74.6, Code Opt 27.3->36.0, Code Readability 27.4->56.2, Math (GSM8K) 92.9->93.1, Acronym 30.4->56.0, Constrained Gen 4.4->61.3. ChatGPT: 11.4->43.2, 40.1->59.9, 23.9->27.5, 27.7->63.1, 74.8->75.0, 27.2->37.2, 2.75->33.5. GPT-3.5: 8.8->30.4, 36.4->63.6, 14.8->23.0, 37.4->51.3, 64.1->64.1, 41.6->56.4, 16.0->39.7. Claimed ~20% absolute average. Ablation (Table 2): actionable vs generic vs no feedback: Code Opt 27.5/26.0/24.8; Sentiment 43.2/31.2/0; Acronym 56.4/54.0/48.0. Iterations (Fig 4, avg over 3 models): Code Opt 22.0->27.0->27.9->28.8; Sentiment 33.9->36.8; Constrained Gen 12.1->26.1->39.6->46.1 (diminishing returns after 1-2 rounds; non-monotonic on multi-aspect tasks). 1-vs-k=4 sampling baseline (ChatGPT, preference tasks only): refined output still preferred. Oracle-gated math: +4.8 (GPT-3.5), +1.4 (ChatGPT), +0.7 (GPT-4). BBH subset with GPT-3.5-turbo: +2 to +4.8. Zero-shot instruction-only works (Acronym 16.6->44.8, Sentiment 4.4->71.4) but needs heavy prompt engineering. Llama-2-70B zero-shot: Acronym 22.3->53.1, Sentiment 13.2->60.8, Dialogue 11.2->20.4, Math 37.6->37.8. Vicuna-13B fails to follow feedback/refine prompts even with oracle feedback; mixed-refine (Vicuna init + ChatGPT critic/refiner) 24.2->40.5 on GSM.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) No gain on math/reasoning without an oracle (0 / +0.2 / +0.2) because the model cannot detect its own errors; the follow-up 'LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet' (Huang et al., arXiv 2310.01798, ICLR 2024) shows intrinsic self-correction actively HURTS on GSM8K/CommonSenseQA/HotpotQA (e.g. GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9->74.7; Llama-2-70B 62.0->36.5; GPT-3.5 flips correct->wrong 8.8% vs wrong->correct 7.6%), that Self-Refine's math/Reflexion gains rely on oracle labels, that the Constrained-Generation gain largely reflects an under-specified initial prompt (a well-written single-pass prompt beat the refined output, ~82 vs ~67 in their reproduction), and that self-consistency with equal call budget beats debate/refine. (2) Requires a strong instruction-following model; Vicuna-13B cannot even format feedback. (3) Feedback is the bottleneck (94% of failures), yet nothing validates feedback. (4) Metrics: GPT-4-pref judged GPT-4's own outputs (self-preference bias); human A/B was done by the authors, single-annotated. (5) Many gains not statistically significant for GPT-3.5 (3/7) and ChatGPT (4/7). (6) Cost: 3-9x the LLM calls; the multi-sample control was run only for ChatGPT on preference tasks. (7) Quality can oscillate across iterations on multi-aspect tasks. (8) English only; proprietary, now-retired models; stated no guard against being steered toward harmful outputs. (9) Code is per-task scripts with hardcoded engines and string-match stop conditions, not a reusable library.
deep_reads.key_insight: Training-free self-improvement lives or dies on the critic, not the refiner: the same model used as generator can add value only on tasks where verifying is easier than generating (multi-constraint coverage, preference/style, readability), and the feedback must be specific and actionable (generic feedback loses most of the gain; no feedback loses all of it). Where verification is as hard as generation (math/reasoning) the loop is a no-op or harmful unless an external oracle gates it — so any self-evolving system should invest in grounded/external verification of the critique before spending compute on refinement.
open_gaps: No persistence: every improvement is discarded after the episode; nothing (feedback patterns, discovered fixes, prompts) is written back to a memory, skill library, or weights, so the same mistakes are re-critiqued on the next instance

Critique is unverified: no external/grounded check (tests, execution, retrieval, oracle) of feedback correctness even though 94% of failures are bad feedback; a framework could require a verifier to accept feedback before refining

No regression guard or rollback: the last (or max self-score) iterate is returned; there is no held-out or independent acceptance test that the refined output is actually better than y0, so the loop can silently degrade (as Huang et al. show on reasoning)

Stopping is self-declared (string match on 'it is correct' / fixed 4 rounds); no calibrated confidence or cost-aware stopping, so compute is wasted on cases the model already got right and stopped early on cases it did not
Prompts (init/feedback/refine) are hand-written per task and never optimized or learned; the meta-level (what makes feedback actionable) is not itself evolved

Single-model, single-trajectory: no population, sampling diversity, or best-of-N selection under an external judge; the 1-vs-k control shows sampling is a strong competitor and was only tested on ChatGPT
Fails on small/open models (Vicuna-13B) — no mechanism to distill the critic/refiner behavior into weaker models beyond an ad-hoc 'mixed-refine' with a stronger model

Evaluation relies on LLM-as-judge with the same model family and author-run human eval; a new framework needs held-out, independent, task-metric evaluation and equal-compute baselines (self-consistency) by default
No cross-task or cross-instance transfer of learned feedback: refinement on instance i does not inform instance i+1
Released code is not a reusable harness (per-task scripts, retired OpenAI engines, prompt-lib dependency); no library-grade loop with pluggable critics, verifiers, or budgets
deep_reads.safety_measures: None. The paper explicitly states the approach does not guard against prompting a model to refine toward more toxic or harmful outputs. No output validation, sandboxing (code tasks are executed only at evaluation time), rollback, or human-in-the-loop; the stop condition and quality judgment are the model's own.
