deep_reads.name: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on ML Engineering
deep_reads.org_or_authors: OpenAI (Chan, Chowdhury, Jaffe, Aung, Sherburn, Mays, Starace, Liu, Maksin, Patwardhan, Weng, Madry)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-04-24 (README notice pausing all new leaderboard submissions; last substantive code fix 2026-01-13; original maintainer has left OpenAI and says v2 timeline is 'very unclear')
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv 2410.07095; ICLR 2025 (oral). Semantic Scholar: 388 citations / 43 influential (likely undercount). 258 forks. Leaderboard has ~28 entries from OpenAI, Google CAIR, Meta, Microsoft, Baidu, SJTU, etc.
deep_reads.mechanism: MLE-bench is NOT self-evolving; it is the static fitness function that autoresearch agents evolve against. Nothing in the repo mutates. The loop it defines: (1) `mlebench prepare` downloads 75 Kaggle competitions (3.3 TB, ~2 days) and re-splits each public train set into a custom train/test split because Kaggle's real test labels are unavailable. (2) `run_agent.py` launches one sysbox-isolated Docker container per (competition x seed); the agent sees /home/data + description.md + instructions.txt, must write /home/submission/submission.csv within 24h on 36 vCPU / 440 GB RAM / one 24 GB A10. Test labels live in /private and are unreadable; a Flask endpoint localhost:5000/validate runs the real grader but returns only valid/invalid, never a score. (3) Post-hoc, `mlebench grade` scores the CSV with the competition metric, then `rank_score` maps it onto medal thresholds derived from the original Kaggle leaderboard using kaggle.com/progression rules (e.g. >=1000 teams: gold = rank 10+0.2%, silver = top 5%, bronze = top 10%). Headline metric = any_medal % across competitions, mean +/- SEM over >=3 seeds, reported by Low(22)/Medium/High splits. (4) Extras: a gpt-4o-mini rule-violation detector over agent logs and a Dolos plagiarism check against top Kaggle kernels, both offline and not part of the score. The shipped reference agent is AIDE (500 tree-search steps, debug depth 20, 9h per-step exec timeout): its inner-loop fitness is the agent's OWN validation split, extracted by a feedback LLM; MLE-bench never provides test feedback during the run. Single-agent per container; no archive, population, memory, or cross-competition transfer.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal = deterministic grader on a hidden re-split test set, thresholded against the historical Kaggle leaderboard (bronze/silver/gold). Drift/reward-hacking guards: test labels unreadable in container (/private), format-only validation endpoint, sysbox isolation, >=3 seeds with SEM, an LLM (gpt-4o-mini) rule-violation detector and Dolos plagiarism detector run offline. Guards are demonstrably leaky: >=6 competitions have known test-label leakage (smartphone-decimeter, hubmap, multi-modal-gesture, random-acts-of-pizza, dog-breed via Stanford Dogs) and top agents (Disarray) admitted exploiting them; 'test-set feedback' harnesses (binary bronze-threshold oracle at early termination) were only caught by community review of grading reports and are now segregated purely via a self-disclosure checkbox in the PR template. Paper-validated properties: obfuscating descriptions changed nothing (8.5 vs 8.4%), no correlation between GPT-4o token-familiarity and score, pass@8 doubles o1-preview from 16.9 to 34.1%, 100h vs 24h gives GPT-4o 8.7 -> 11.8%, extra GPU gives no gain.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (Oct 2024): o1-preview + AIDE 16.9% any-medal; GPT-4o AIDE 8.7%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 7.6%, Llama 3.1 405B 3.0%; scaffold matters more than model at the time (gpt-4o: AIDE 8.63 vs OpenHands 4.89 vs MLAB 1.60); pass@8 34.1%. Leaderboard as of 2026-04: Famou-Agent 2.0 (Gemini-3-Pro) 64.44% all / 80.3% Low; AIBuildAI (Claude Opus 4.6) 63.11%; Google CAIR MARS+ 62.67%; MLEvolve 61.33% in 12h (open source); Disarray ensemble 77.78% but segregated for test-set feedback. Low split is near saturation (~80%), High split still ~40-47%. R&D-Agent gpt-5 35.11%, AIRA-dojo o3 31.6%, ML-Master 29.3%. ~4x improvement in 18 months.
deep_reads.limitations: Static, frozen task set with catalogued unfixed bugs; leaderboard submissions paused 2026-04-24 and promised v2 (openai/frontier-evals) does not exist there (only paperbench, swelancer, evmbench). Kaggle-style, well-specified tasks, not open-ended research. Custom test splits mean 'beat Kaggle winners' claims don't transfer. Binary any-medal metric hides score margins; crowded leaderboards (TPS Dec-2021/May-2022, jigsaw) make medals near-random. Prohibitive cost (75 x 24h x 3 seeds on GPU, 3.3 TB). Most leaderboard entries have no source code, and results depend on self-reported compliance. Contamination possible since all competitions are public and pre-2024.
deep_reads.safety_measures: sysbox container runtime for host isolation (OpenHands needed privileged DinD, user must set I_ACCEPT_RUNNING_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINERS); test labels mounted only in /private, agent checks confirm unreadability; agent forbidden from viewing others' solutions or hand-labelling; offline gpt-4o-mini rule-violation detector and Dolos plagiarism detector; leaderboard disclosure checkbox for test-set-signal exposure; leakage-disclaimer column. No runtime enforcement of network egress or external-dataset use.
deep_reads.key_insight: Anchor an agent's fitness to a human population distribution (Kaggle medal thresholds from real leaderboards) rather than to an absolute metric, and keep the true fitness strictly post-hoc so the agent must build its own trustworthy inner-loop validation proxy; this exposed that scaffold/search design, attempts (pass@k) and wall-clock matter far more than raw GPU, but also that any benchmark reused as an optimization target without sealed labels and refreshable tasks gets exploited within ~15 months.
open_gaps: No in-loop reward: the true score is only available after the 24h run, so every autoresearch agent must invent its own validation proxy with no tooling to check that it correlates with the hidden test; a framework could ship a calibrated, query-limited, logged proxy-fitness service

Test-set-feedback harnesses (binary bronze-threshold oracle at early termination) cannot be detected by the benchmark; enforcement is a self-disclosure checkbox, so an attested/sealed evaluation harness with counted, logged label queries is needed

At least 6 competitions have known test-label or external-dataset leakage (smartphone-decimeter, hubmap, multi-modal-gesture, random-acts-of-pizza, dog-breed) and 3 have crowded leaderboards; fixes were never shipped and the leaderboard is frozen, so a contamination-resistant, refreshable, versioned task pool is missing

Fixed 75-task set with the Low split near saturation (~80%) and no held-out generalization set; nothing measures whether skills, memories or prompts learned on one competition transfer to another because every run is a fresh, independent container

Fitness is binary any-medal per competition: no continuous, cross-task-normalized score (e.g. leaderboard percentile) that an evolutionary selection loop could use for fine-grained ranking of variants

Cost is prohibitive (75 x 24h x >=3 seeds on A10 GPUs, 3.3 TB data, ~2 days to prepare); no cheap short-horizon proxy with demonstrated correlation to the full score exists for iterating on agent designs

Cheating detection (gpt-4o-mini over logs, Dolos vs Kaggle kernels) is offline and not part of the score; nothing prevents pulling external labelled data or exploiting benchmark quirks, and top agents openly did both
No process metrics: only wall-clock is reported; LLM calls, tokens, dollar cost and compute-efficiency are not measured, so a 24h multi-model ensemble and a single cheap model are ranked identically

No reproducibility requirement: most leaderboard entries provide no source code and the benchmark cannot re-run submissions; a framework needs reproducible run artifacts (container image + seeds + trajectory logs)
Custom re-split test sets differ from Kaggle's real test sets, so 'beats Kaggle gold' claims on MLE-bench are unverifiable against actual human performance
sources_read: https://github.com/openai/mle-bench/pull/118 (Disarray test-set feedback discussion incl. maintainer comment)

deep_reads.name: MLGym: A New Framework and Benchmark for Advancing AI Research Agents (MLGym-Bench)
deep_reads.mechanism: MLGym is a SWE-Agent-derived harness wrapped in a Gym API, not a self-evolving system. The loop that actually runs: (1) env.reset() spins up a Docker/Podman container with GPU, copies starter code + read-only evaluate.py, executes the task's baseline.py once and caches baseline_scores into the task YAML. (2) A single LLM agent emits one DISCUSSION + one bash/ACI command per step (edit/insert with lint checks, search, goto, literature_search, parse_pdf_url, validate, submit); history is truncated to Last5Observations. (3) `validate` runs evaluate.py on the submission artifact against the real test split and returns "Baseline Score / Evaluation Score" as an observation; the agent iterates on its code/hyperparameters using that number. (4) `submit`, max_steps, cost limit, or error ends the episode; on non-submit exits the last valid artifact is auto-submitted. Crucially, env.step() returns reward=0 always ("Always 0 in current implementation"); the score is only appended to info["score"] for offline analysis. No RL trainer exists in the repo (issue #13: maintainers confirmed none, promised a TorchRL integration by April 2025 that never shipped before the repo went dormant in Aug 2025). The only cross-episode persistence is an optional memory module: memory_write/memory_read tools embed free text with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 into /home/agent/memory.json (top-2 cosine retrieval), and env.close() copies that file back to data/<task>/memory.json so the next run on the same task can load it. What "evolves" in practice is the task solution artifact within an episode and, optionally, a per-task text memory across episodes; the agent scaffold, prompts, tools, and model weights are static.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Per-task evaluate.py (read-only in container) prints JSON metrics on the test split; the same script backs both `validate` (mid-episode feedback) and final scoring, so the improvement signal the agent sees IS the test score (e.g. CIFAR-10 evaluate.py loads uoft-cs/cifar10 split="test"). Baseline is executed at reset and shown to the agent. Across models/tasks, results are aggregated with performance profiles and Area Under Profile (AUP), plus Plackett-Luce and Borda rankings, in two modes: Best Attempt (max over all validate calls) and Best/Last Submission. Anti-drift/reward-hacking measures are thin: evaluation_read_only=true on all 13 task configs, a command blocklist, no interactive shells, cost/step/timeouts. There is no hidden held-out split, so agents can hill-climb the test metric via repeated validate calls, and test labels are reachable from inside the container via HF datasets. Because reward is never fed back into the policy, nothing in the framework itself learns from the signal.
deep_reads.limitations: Claimed vs demonstrated: the README/paper pitch "train agents with RL" is aspirational; the repo contains no RL loop, reward is hard-coded 0, and the promised TorchRL integration never landed (last push 2025-08-10, 9 open issues, dormant ~13 months). Evaluation uses the test split as the validation signal (no hidden split), so scores are optimistic and vulnerable to overfitting/leakage. Tasks are small-scale (1800s training timeout, CIFAR-10/FMNIST/MNLI/House Price/3-SAT/3 gymnax RL tasks/3 game-theory tasks/FineWeb LM/COCO captioning) and the paper itself concludes agents improve baselines "usually by finding better hyperparameters" with no novel hypotheses, algorithms, or architectures (Level 1 of their 0-5 capability ladder). Memory module is a toy (MiniLM embeddings, top-2 retrieval, per-task file) and its effect is not reported in the results tables. Some model runs produce broken outputs (DeepSeek-R1 and Llama-4 -3e13 on Mountain Car). Requires Docker/Podman + NVIDIA GPU + paid API keys; CC-BY-NC 4.0 license blocks commercial use. Single linear trajectory per run: no search, population, or candidate selection (added later by Meta's AIRA-dojo, arXiv 2507.02554).
deep_reads.key_insight: A research-agent benchmark becomes an RL-ready substrate simply by exposing the task score through a `validate` tool inside a Gym step loop with a cached baseline; but exposing the score to the agent without a separate held-out split turns "validation" into test-set hill-climbing, and without wiring reward back into a policy update the "self-evolution" reduces to in-context iteration on a single artifact.
open_gaps: No RL/policy-update loop: env.step() returns reward=0, scores only land in info['score']; no trajectory-to-training pipeline (GRPO/PPO/SFT-on-best) exists despite the README claim

Validation signal equals test-set score (same evaluate.py, test split); no hidden held-out split, so agents can overfit via repeated validate calls and test labels are reachable inside the container via HF datasets

No cross-task or cross-model transfer: memory.json is per-task free text with top-2 MiniLM cosine retrieval; no consolidation into reusable skills/tools, and memory-enabled runs are not reported in results tables
Single agent, one command per step, linear trajectory: no population/archive, tree search, parallel candidates, or selection among solutions (AIRA-dojo added this later)
Agent scaffold is static YAML (prompts, tools, history processor); nothing lets the agent modify or evolve its own harness, tools, or prompts
No regression guard on the artifact: last valid submission is auto-submitted on timeouts/errors, so Last score can be far below Best (e.g. Claude 3.5 Sonnet MS-COCO best 0.298 vs last 0.125)
Fixed set of 13 small tasks (1800s training timeout) with no task generation or curriculum; nothing evaluates Level 2+ (novel methods, paper writing)
Heavy infra: Docker/Podman + NVIDIA GPU + API keys required; CC-BY-NC license; not usable by app developers without GPU hosts
Repo dormant since Aug 2025 with no public leaderboard; results tables are static CSVs regenerated by maintainers only

deep_reads.name: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Mingchen Zhuge*, Wenyi Wang*, Louis Kirsch, Francesco Faccio, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Jürgen Schmidhuber — KAUST AI Initiative + IDSIA (metauto-ai)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-02-05 (last push: 'add bocha web search tool'); last substantive optimizer code change 2024; 2 open issues from 2026-08 (security: PythonReader executes .py attachments, torch.load without weights_only)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICML 2024 Oral (top 1.5%, 144/9473), PMLR 235:62743-62767. Citation count not retrievable this session (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); widely cited as the origin of the agent-as-optimizable-graph line (ADAS, AFlow, MaAS, AgentPrune, G-Designer all build on it) — estimated several hundred.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Every agent is a DAG of operation nodes (LLM call, tool, search); a swarm is a composite graph. The set of potential edges = all ordered node pairs across different agents (+ optional edges to a final decision node); intra-agent edges are frozen.

EDGE LOOP (swarm/optimizer/edge_optimizer): each potential edge i has a logit theta_i (init p=0.5 MMLU, 0.1 crosswords). Per iteration, sample M graphs (M=4 MMLU, 20 crosswords) by walking the edge list in fixed order and adding edge i with prob sigmoid(theta_i) unless it would create a cycle (deterministically skipped). Run each sampled graph on one training question, compute a scalar utility (MMLU: 0/1 majority-vote correctness; crosswords: best-returned-solution word accuracy minus a 0.4 constant or per-problem moving-average baseline). Loss = mean(-log p(G) * (u - baseline)); Adam step on theta (lr 0.1/0.4). 200 iterations for MMLU, ~10 for crosswords. At test time the graph is realized by thresholding probs > 0.5 (MMLU) or sampled from the final distribution (crosswords).

NODE LOOP (swarm/optimizer/node_optimizer, HumanEval): every 4 problems, each OptimizableOperation pulls its last 4 (input, output, feedback) records from GlobalMemory, labels them by unit-test pass. Optionally (a) LLM writes one-sentence diagnoses of each failure then rewrites the node prompt (<=5 sentences, no task specifics), (b) positive examples are added to a max-4 demonstration set. Candidates = {old,new prompt} x {old,new demos}; each candidate is re-scored by re-executing the node on its 10 most recent inputs and counting unit-test passes; argmax is written in place. Appendix D.2 chains node-opt (UCB1 over demo choices) after edge-opt.

Single parameter vector, no population/archive, offline experiment scripts.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Signal is a ground-truth benchmark score on a training split: MMLU dev-set accuracy (eval on first 153 of val), Mini-Crosswords best-state word accuracy on 20 problems (the SAME 20 problems are used to optimize and evaluate), HumanEval unit-test pass (evaluated online on the same stream being learned from). Edge optimization has no acceptance test: theta is updated by REINFORCE gradient every iteration with variance reduction (constant 0.4 baseline or per-problem moving average) — nothing prevents regression except the eventual thresholding. Node optimization is a greedy hill-climb: a candidate prompt/demo set is accepted only if it scores highest when re-run on the node's 10 most recent inputs — but those inputs overlap the examples used to write the candidate, so there is no held-out check against overfitting. A density-matched control (all-edges p=0.125, same expected 32.8 edges, scores 0.510 vs 0.575) is the only anti-'reward-hacking-via-compute' check. No LLM judge is used anywhere; utility must be a verifiable scalar.
deep_reads.key_results: MMLU adversarial (k truthful IO + k adversarial, majority vote, GPT-4-Turbo): fully-connected and random swarms score well below the single-IO baseline; optimized swarm recovers to baseline (~0.83) by pruning adversarial edges; 3T3A optimization cost $5.32/0.9h vs DyLAN $105.93/25.4h (DyLAN 0.8366 vs GPTSwarm 0.8301). MMLU collaborative (7 role-prompted IO agents): +2.1% +/-1.1% over baseline (5 seeds). Mini Crosswords (GPT-3.5-Turbo, 3 agents ToT/Reflexion/CoT, 10 REINFORCE iters, M=20): 0.465 -> 0.575 (+/-0.0275, 3 runs); density-matched control 0.510; same learned edges run with GPT-4-Turbo: 0.800 vs ToT 0.675 (GPT-4) / 0.668 (GPT-4-Turbo re-run); +node-opt after edge-opt: 0.668 (GPT-3.5). HumanEval ReAct agent, demonstration learning: 0.76 -> 0.88 (+/-0.007), gains in first ~5 iterations. GAIA L1/L2/L3 = 30.56/20.93/3.85 (avg 18.45) with 7xToT + self-consistency vs AutoGPT 4.85 avg — but GAIA runs use NO optimization at all. Costs: crosswords edge-opt $77 (50M prompt tokens, GPT-3.5); GPT-4-Turbo eval of one distribution $377; HumanEval w/ opt $28 vs $1.6 without.
deep_reads.limitations: Only inter-agent edges are learned; node set and intra-agent topology are fixed (authors' own stated limitation) — no new nodes, tools, or agents can be invented. Edge parameterization is d independent Bernoulli logits (MRFDist is an empty stub; learned-order mode exists but was disabled in experiments). Adversarial MMLU only recovers to the single-agent baseline; collaborative gain (2.1% +/- 1.1%) is marginal. Crosswords optimizes and evaluates on the same 20 problems; 3 seeds; high variance. Each REINFORCE iteration requires M full swarm rollouts; 7T7A (196 edges) already takes 95 min and the search space is 2^d. Learned theta is task-specific; no transfer across tasks shown. Prompt-rewrite path (learn_prompt) needs a per-node `evaluate` that only CodeReact implements; MetaPromptOptimizer is mostly commented-out dead code; only demonstration learning is reported in the paper. GAIA headline numbers involve no self-improvement — the README tagline 'first self-improving agents' overstates what is demonstrated. Pinned to gpt-4-1106-preview / gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, numpy 1.x; effectively unmaintained since Jan 2025 apart from search-tool PRs; generated Python is executed via PyExecutor with only a timeout.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Essentially none specific to self-modification: DAG acyclicity is enforced at sampling; node candidates are only accepted if they score >= current on the recent window; generated code runs through PyExecutor with a timeout but no sandbox (an open 2026 issue flags PythonReader executing .py attachments and unsafe torch.load). Search space is bounded by construction (fixed nodes, pre-enumerated potential edges), which limits blast radius but is a design constraint rather than a safety mechanism. Impact statement is generic.
deep_reads.key_insight: Factor an agent system into (fixed operation nodes, learnable inter-agent edge probabilities, per-node prompts) so that orchestration becomes a differentiable-in-expectation distribution over DAGs: black-box REINFORCE on a few hundred edge logits, using only end-task score as reward, is enough to discover useful communication topologies (and prune adversarial agents) at ~1/20th the cost of debate/DyLAN-style heuristics — while node-level prompt/demo improvement is decoupled into a local, unit-test-verified hill-climb, sidestepping the combinatorial joint search DSPy faces.
open_gaps: Node/agent set is fixed: cannot add, remove, or invent new nodes, tools, or agents — only pre-enumerated inter-agent edges are learned
Intra-agent topology is frozen; only edges between different agents are optimized (authors' own stated limitation)
Fitness is a training-split benchmark score; Mini Crosswords optimizes and evaluates on the same 20 problems and HumanEval learns online on the eval stream — no held-out generalization test
Learned edge logits are task-specific; no cross-task transfer or reuse of learned topologies/prompts
No archive, population, checkpoint-and-compare, or rollback: a single theta vector is updated in place by REINFORCE with no acceptance test per step
Node prompt/demo acceptance is scored on the same recent inputs used to generate the candidate — no held-out check against overfitting or reward hacking
Utility must be a verifiable scalar (unit test, exact match); no support for LLM-judge, pairwise, or unverifiable-task rewards
Edge and node optimization are run sequentially, not jointly; no shared credit assignment between topology and prompt changes
Cost is not in the objective: each iteration needs M full swarm rollouts (crosswords edge-opt = 50M prompt tokens, $77 on GPT-3.5); no token/latency-aware utility
Independent Bernoulli per edge; conditional/structured edge distributions (MRFDist) are an unimplemented stub, learned node ordering was disabled in experiments
Prompt-rewrite branch requires a per-node `evaluate()` that only the HumanEval CodeReact node implements; MetaPromptOptimizer is largely dead code
Offline experiment scripts only — no runtime loop that improves a deployed agent between real user tasks
Unmaintained since Jan 2025 (except search tools), pinned to 2023 OpenAI models and numpy 1.x; open security issues around executing generated/attached Python and torch.load

deep_reads.name: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
deep_reads.last_activity: 2025-11-04 (last push: travelplanner upload; core search code last touched 2025-06-21)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yu Shang, Yu Li, Keyu Zhao, Likai Ma, Jiahe Liu, Fengli Xu, Yong Li — Tsinghua University FIB Lab
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: ICLR 2025 (poster); arXiv 2410.06153 (v1 Oct 2024, camera-ready v2 ~Feb 2025). Citation count not verifiable this session (Semantic Scholar rate-limited); widely cited in automated-agent-design surveys.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Design space: an agent = one choice per slot from four typed module pools (Planning, Reasoning, ToolUse, Memory), each a Python class with a fixed I/O interface (e.g. Reasoning.__call__(task_description, feedback) -> str) wired into a fixed workflow.py loop. Pools are seeded with ~6 hand-abstracted modules per type from the literature (CoT, ToT, Self-Refine, DEPS, HuggingGPT, Voyager, DILU, Generative, ToolBench...).

Loop (search/agent_search.py, 10 iterations, single current-best agent, greedy):
1. Module evolution: for each module type, an LLM programmer (gpt-4o-mini, T=0.8, JSON) is prompted with that type's archive (thought+code+measured performance of every module so far) plus an interface skeleton and told to "propose an interestingly new module... THINK OUTSIDE THE BOX". One new module per type per iteration.
2. Each new module is smoke-tested in a minimal agent on 50 benchmark episodes; if score > 0 (i.e. it runs) it is appended to the archive and candidate pool, otherwise discarded.
3. Four children = current agent with exactly one slot swapped for the new module; each evaluated on 50 episodes; current agent replaced if strictly better.
4. Module recombination: an LLM proposer (T=0.1) sees task description, natural-language profiles of all candidates, and every (combination, score) pair tested so far, and proposes a full combination; it is again decomposed into four single-slot swaps.
5. Performance predictor: gpt-4o in-context surrogate is given ~85 golden (combination code, score) pairs and predicts scores for the four candidates; only the argmax is actually run (50 episodes); greedy accept.
Archive of modules/scores is persisted per iteration.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Fitness = real environment success rate (ALFWorld `won` flag) on n=50 episodes per candidate, backbone gpt-4o-mini during search; no LLM judge for the fitness itself. Acceptance is strict greedy improvement over the current agent; an archive of all modules and all tested (combination, score) pairs is retained and fed back into the evolution/recombination prompts. An in-context LLM predictor (gpt-4o, T=0) prunes which recombination candidate gets real evaluation (paper: strong rank correlation, cost ~0.025% of full evaluation). Drift/reward-hacking guards are weak: the search-time episodes are drawn from the same split reported as test (ALFWorld eval_out_of_distribution; WebShop fixed_0-499 — raised in issue #18), 50-episode estimates carry ~7pt noise with no re-evaluation or significance test, and new modules are only checked for "runs and scores > 0". Predictor golden set is a static file (alfworld_results.json) and is not updated with newly tested cases.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper: average +17.2% over the best hand-crafted agent across 6 benchmarks (M3Tool +30.6%, ALFWorld +26.1%, SciWorld +20.5%, WebShop +14.1%, TravelPlanner +6.0%, PDDL +6.0%); beats search baselines (random combination, Bayesian optimization, OPRO, ADAS) at lower API cost; predictor shows strong correlation with measured performance while costing as little as 0.025% of full evaluation. Discovered modules: HTSS (ToT + self-consistency + self-refine reasoning), Hier (hierarchical memory), ToolBF (vector retrieval + multi-attempt tool use). Repo ALFWorld archive (single-module tests): SelfRefine reasoning 0.78, Voyager memory 0.78, DILU memory 0.74 vs IO baseline 0.56. Only the ALFWorld search pipeline is wired end-to-end; other tasks have module runners but no automated search.
deep_reads.limitations: Search validated on the evaluation split itself (no held-out test; issue #18). Greedy single-lineage hill-climbing with one-slot mutations; no crossover, no population, no rollback beyond rejection. Fitness ignores cost/latency, so it favors expensive ensembles (HTSS). Fixed four-slot workflow topology and fixed module types; cannot evolve control flow or multi-agent structure. Generated code validated only by "runs and score>0"; LLM output parsed with eval(); module code injected via regex string surgery into source files. Tool-use slot excluded from the released search loop. Predictor golden set is static and never updated during search. Hard-coded to ALFWorld + OpenAI; missing files (alfworld_results.json, base_config.yaml) and no automated pipeline for other tasks per maintainers (issue #16, Aug 2025). Repo is a research artifact: 11 open issues, no Dockerfile, no tests, no license file in repo (README claims Apache-2.0).
deep_reads.safety_measures: Essentially none beyond engineering guards: try/except around benchmark runs (crash => score 0 => module discarded), required-key checks on LLM JSON, generated modules written to a temporary Test class and cleaned up after evaluation. No sandboxing of LLM-generated Python (it is exec'd in-process), eval() on LLM responses, no static analysis, no held-out validation, no cost caps.
deep_reads.key_insight: Constrain automated agent design to a typed modular space with standardized I/O (planning/reasoning/tool-use/memory) so that LLM-generated modules are composable and reusable, and use an LLM as an in-context surrogate over module descriptions plus past (combination, score) pairs to decide which candidates deserve expensive real evaluation.
open_gaps: Fitness is measured on the benchmark test split (ALFWorld eval_out_of_distribution, WebShop fixed_0-499) with no held-out generalization check — a new framework should separate search/validation/test splits and report held-out deltas

Greedy acceptance on 50-episode estimates with no re-evaluation, confidence intervals or significance test — noise can drive accepted 'improvements'; no rollback/regression testing of accepted changes
Only single-slot mutations of one current-best agent: no population, no crossover, no diversity maintenance (module archive != agent archive)
Predictor is a static in-context model over a fixed golden file; it is never refit on newly measured combinations and its calibration is never checked online
Workflow topology (plan -> reason -> tool -> memory loop) and the four module types are fixed; cannot evolve control flow, add module types, or produce multi-agent structures
Generated module code is verified only by 'runs and scores > 0' — no unit tests, static checks, sandboxing; LLM output parsed with eval()
Fitness is single-objective success rate; token cost and latency are ignored, so search drifts toward expensive ensembles
Discovered modules and (combination -> score) knowledge are not transferred across tasks or backbones automatically; every task/backbone starts a fresh search
Tool-use slot is excluded from the released search loop; tool-module evolution is untested end-to-end
Offline batch search (10 iterations) only — no online/continual evolution from deployment traces
Not runnable by app developers: hard-coded ALFWorld + OpenAI, missing config/result files, no Dockerfile, no automated pipeline for the other five tasks

Observations about the space. Signals used: (1) executor/DB/formal verification (AZR, Agent0 tools, SQL-Zero, PSV-Verus) -- the most robust; (2) majority-vote pseudo-labels (TTRL, R-Zero, SQLM, Agent0) -- cheap but degrade with difficulty; (3) proposer difficulty targeting -- learnability reward 1-solve-rate (AZR), uncertainty peak at 50% (R-Zero), hint-based regret (SPADE), Hint-delta predictive shift (G-Zero), student-improvement meta-reward (SOAR); (4) game outcomes in zero-sum/cooperative games (SPIRAL, MARSHAL, SpyRL); (5) external grounding -- web corpus (SPICE, SCOPE), search engine (Dr. Zero, SSP), pretraining corpus + env memory (SPADE); (6) self-evolving rubrics / self-judging (Self-Rewarding LMs, SERPO, SCOPE). What works: asymmetric proposer/solver co-evolution with a verifiable or externally grounded signal; difficulty targeting near 50%; diversity penalties (BLEU repetition penalty, vocabulary dropout); small human anchors (R-Few, Socratic-Zero's 100 seeds); larger models sustain more iterations (AZR 3B/7B/14B +5.7/+10.2/+13.2; R-Zero 0.6B collapses after 1 iter vs 4B after 3). What collapses: pseudo-label accuracy decay (R-Zero 79% -> 63% by iter 3) and iteration-scaling degradation (R-Zero, SQL-Zero 7B); entropy collapse and pass@k plateau -- gains are sharpening bounded by the base model (Understanding Self-play, SvS); proposer reward hacking toward junk-hard or narrow problems (SGS, Vocabulary Dropout, SOAR on intrinsic learnability metrics); judge reward hacking where plausibility rises while accuracy stays flat (0.72->0.94 judge pass vs 0.20 accuracy); correct-answer extinction in majority-vote TTRL; safety 'uh-oh moments' in AZR. The 2026 frontier is moving from proposing tasks to proposing whole environments and skills (SPADE, Skill Self-Play) and to verifier-free open-ended domains (G-Zero, SCOPE, SERPO, RLSVR), with the position paper 2603.02218 giving the unifying diagnosis: loops only evolve when learnable information gain per iteration keeps rising (asymmetric co-evolution, capacity growth, proactive information seeking).

critic.coverage_assessment: The 485-item index is strong and unusually current: it saturates the 2026 arXiv wave on harness evolution, skill libraries, agent memory, Godel-machine lineage (DGM/HGM/Hyperagents/MGM/RQGM), AlphaEvolve replications and applications, self-play-from-zero (AZR/R-Zero/SPIRAL/SPICE/Dr.Zero/Agent0), the karpathy/autoresearch fork ecosystem, and misevolution/reward-hacking safety work. To check completeness I diffed it against 18 curated awesome-lists (lobehub/awesome-rsi, Awesome-AI4AI, Liuziyu77/Awesome-RSI, awesome-agent-evolution, pinkbubblebubble & Picrew awesome-rsi, Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement, D2I awesome-recursive-self-improving-agents, FrontisAI & selfimproving-agent lists, Reliable-Self-Evolving, two awesome-autoresearch lists, awesome-embodied-rsi, ANative/XMU/CharlesQ9 self-evolving lists, Awesome-Agent-Dynamic-Graphs): of ~1,600 distinct arXiv IDs cited across them, ~1,470 are not in the index, but the overwhelming majority are long-tail domain applications ('self-evolving X' for medicine, finance, EDA, recsys, navigation) that are reasonable to exclude. The systematic gaps are: (1) foundational pre-2024 anchors that every list cites (STaR, ReST-EM, Self-Refine, APE/ProTeGi, Self-Instruct, Generative Agents, Quiet-STaR); (2) the AI-R&D evaluation layer (MLE-bench, RE-Bench, MLGym, PaperBench, METR time-horizon) that the indexed autoresearch systems report on; (3) 2024-25 automated agent-design search (GPTSwarm, AgentSquare, MASS, MAS-ZERO, ScoreFlow) between ADAS and the 2026 harness wave; (4) embodied and multimodal self-improvement (SIMA 2, Eureka, RoboCat, Vision-Zero, RISE); (5) weight-level continual learning (SDFT/OPSD line, sparse-memory finetuning, TTT-for-ARC) and intrinsic-reward self-training (INTUITOR); (6) high-star substrates the ecosystem runs on (OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness, Mem0, Agent Lightning); (7) very recent Sept-2026 RSI papers (MetaRSI, Meta^n, SkillAdam, SafeEvolve, J-Zero) and system-level security threat models (Safety in Self-Evolving Systems, Zombie Agents); (8) Sakana's own RHI harness paper and Google's AI co-scientist. Secondary omissions worth a line each: AIRA-dojo (2507.02554), CoEvoSkills (COLM 2026), RewardHarness (2605.08703), ReVeal (ICLR 2026), Forethought's 'software intelligence explosion' analysis and AI 2027 for RSI forecasting, Sakana Evolutionary Model Merge/CycleQD for weight-space evolution. Housekeeping: several index entries are duplicates under different URLs (OpenEvolve x2, ECC x2, Memento x2, EvoAgentX x2, GEPA/ACE/R-Zero paper+repo pairs) and a few star counts look implausible (ECC 256k, Hermes 244k) and should be re-verified.
critic.taxonomy_observations:
Dominant paradigms (approximate share of the 485 items): (a) context-level evolution without weight updates — prompts, playbooks, skills (SKILL.md-style procedural memory), episodic/experience memory (ACE, ReasoningBank, Dynamic Cheatsheet, GEPA/DSPy/TextGrad, SkillOpt/SkillClaw/EvoSkill/MemSkill/WikiSkill/SkillOS, Memento, ReMe, MemEvolve, ALMA) is the largest bucket at roughly 100 items; 2026 made 'skills' the default evolvable artifact for coding agents. (b) Harness/scaffold evolution (Meta-Harness, AHE, three different 'AutoHarness'es, Self-Harness, Continual Harness, HarnessDev, HarnessForge, Co-Harness, HASE, WHALE, TTHE, MemoHarness, HarnessFix, HarnessEvolve, Ecdysis, EvoHarnessBench, Harness Handbook) is ~35 items and almost entirely 2026 — the fastest-growing and most crowded area, with an equally fast counter-literature (Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit, Phantom Guardrails, Budget-Splitting Trap, Rethinking Harness Evolution Evaluation, Harness-Delta Attribution). (c) LLM-driven program/algorithm evolution (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve + ~10 applications, OpenEvolve, ShinkaEvolve, EoH, ReEvo, LLM4AD, CodeEvolve, ThetaEvolve, EvoTune, PACEvolve, DeltaEvolve, TurboEvolve, SMCEvolve) ~45 items: LLM as mutation operator, scalar evaluator as fitness. (d) Self-play / zero-data weight-level self-improvement (AZR, R-Zero, SPIRAL, SPICE, SSP, SvS, STP, PSV, SPIN, Self-Challenging, Dr. Zero, Agent0, TTRL, SEAL, Training-Free GRPO, Co-rewarding, Self-Harmony, SOAR, LURE, G-Zero, PopuLoRA) ~50 items: proposer–solver co-evolution with verifiable rewards on math/code. (e) Self-referential meta-agents (DGM, HGM, Hyperagents/DGM-H, MGM, RQGM, Godel Agent, SICA, STOP, MetaEvolve, MetaSkill-Evolve, Bilevel-Autoresearch, MOSS) ~15: the Godel-machine lineage, mostly benchmarked on SWE-bench/Polyglot. (f) Autoresearch / AI-scientist loops (~45): karpathy/autoresearch and ~15 forks, AI Scientist v1/v2, Agent Lab, AI-Researcher, InternAgent, DeepScientist, Kosmos, R&D-Agent, AIDE, AIRA2, EvoScientist, OpenRSI, PostTrainBench, RSI-Exam, AI4AI-Bench, AutoSOTA — the trend runs from 'write a paper' toward 'improve the training recipe of the model running the loop', i.e. RSI proper. (g) Safety/reliability/misevolution (~35, mostly 2026): Misevolution, SkillMisevo, MemEvoBench, TAME, HackProbe, EVOMAL, EvoSkill Injection, PROCTOR, Blind Curator, Verifier-as-Gatekeeper, plus METR/Anthropic/OpenAI reports. (h) Environment/task synthesis as the evolutionary substrate (~20): AgentGym, EnvScaler, AutoEnv, Agent-World, ToolVerse, EnvCraft, CuES, DreamGym, InfiniteWeb, SWE-smith, R2E-Gym, OpenEnv, DejaQ, BenchEvolver. (i) ~20 surveys/awesome-lists, with at least 12 competing 'awesome' indexes — a sign the field is fragmenting faster than it is consolidating.

What evolves most often, in descending frequency: text artifacts (prompts, context, skills, memory) — cheapest, model-agnostic, portable across Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw; harness code (tools, control flow, hooks, subagent configs) — 2026's object of choice; task-solution programs (AlphaEvolve family); weights via self-generated data (RLVR self-play, on-policy distillation); whole agent source (DGM lineage). Joint co-evolution of weights + harness is a distinct 2026 mini-trend (WHALE, HASE, Co-Harness, HELIX, HarnessForge, 'Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models', SafeEvolve, NeoHorse-1, MetaRSI). Rarely evolved: model architecture (ASI-Arch only), data pipelines (RSIBench-Data), and the evaluator/rubric itself (Double Ratchet, SERPO, EvoRubric, ARISE-RL) — the latter is where several papers now locate the real bottleneck.

Evaluation signals: (1) executable verification dominates — unit tests, compile/run, SWE-bench-style pass@1, formal verification (PSV, STP); (2) fixed benchmark scores used directly as fitness — SWE-bench Verified, Polyglot, Terminal-Bench 2.0, MLE-bench, AlgoTune/ALE, AIME/MATH, ARC-AGI-2, nanoGPT-speedrun val loss; (3) LLM-as-judge, self-judging and self-certainty (TTRL majority vote, Co-rewarding, Self-Harmony, INTUITOR-style confidence) for unverifiable domains — precisely where the index's critique papers (More Convincing Not More Correct, Blind Curator, PROCTOR, Faithful Self-Evolvers) find reward hacking and judge bias; (4) held-out / anytime-valid statistical gating (RSEA, SEA certificates, LIFT, PACE, Falsifiable Release Gates) emerging in mid-2026 as the response to (3); (5) longitudinal compounding metrics (Do Agent Optimizers Compound?, Continual Harness, FinEvo-Bench, SEAGym, EvoHarnessBench, Adaptive Auto-Harness) — new and still thin; (6) token/cost accounting (Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Worth Their Tokens?, METR expenditure horizon) as a rising second axis. Human evaluation is nearly absent.

Crowded areas: harness evolution, skill libraries and skill-misevolution benchmarks, agent memory systems, prompt optimization, autoresearch forks, self-play-from-zero for math/code, AlphaEvolve reimplementations, and meta-lists. Thin or empty areas: weight-level continual learning inside deployed agents (SEAL, MemRL and little else; SDFT/OPSD absent); embodied/robotic RSI (one paper); multimodal/VLM self-evolution (none); 2024-25 automated agent-design search (GPTSwarm/AgentSquare/MASS absent though ADAS/AFlow/MaAS present); AI-R&D capability benchmarks (MLE-bench, RE-Bench, MLGym, PaperBench absent); theory of when self-improvement compounds vs. saturates (only Statistical Limits, Fragility, Simple Baselines, Mutation Without Variation); economics/forecasting of RSI (only MirrorCode); system-level security of self-modifying agents (Zombie Agents, Safety-in-SE absent); and production deployments beyond Databricks/ADK/MLflow. Big-lab presence is uneven: Meta (Hyperagents, SPICE, Dr. Zero, AIRA, DreamGym, Trellis), Sakana, Google DeepMind (AlphaEvolve, ReasoningBank, Evo-Memory, amplio), Alibaba/Tencent/ByteDance and Microsoft are well covered; OpenAI appears only through policy/press items, DeepMind's SIMA 2 and AI co-scientist are missing, and DeepSeek/OpenClaw substrates are missing entirely.
